For the author of the Scholastic History says: [[4:15|whosoever shall kill Cain|Omnis qui occiderit Cain]]: one must supply, *will free him from his labours and misery*. And then is added impersonally, [[4:15|shall be punished sevenfold|Septuplum punietur]], that is, punishment shall be made of him, that is, of Cain, while he lives in punishment until Lamech, the seventh. This exposition agrees with the one cited above in this, that it puts the full stop and end of the sentence at [[4:15|whosoever shall kill Cain|Omnis qui occiderit Cain]], and understands something there, and then expounds [[4:15|shall be punished sevenfold|Septuplum punietur]] of Cain himself. But that it understands *will free him* rather than *shall be gravely punished* follows the exposition by which Cain is said to have said, wishing it: [[4:14|every one therefore that findeth me, shall kill me|Omnis qui invenerit me, occidet me]]. And so it is had in the Gloss: Thou shalt not die quickly, as thou wishest, for [[4:15|shall be punished|punietur]] (impersonally, that is, punishment shall be made of thee) [[4:15|sevenfold|septuplum]], since thou shalt live in torment until the seventh generation, in which thou shalt be slain by Lamech. Therefore, [[4:15|whosoever shall kill|Omnis qui occiderit]]: understand, *will free thee from that torment of a bad conscience*. Thus far the Gloss. By like reasoning, according to the exposition by which Cain is said to have said in fear, [[4:14|every one therefore that findeth me|Omnis qui invenerit me]], after the words [[4:15|whosoever shall kill Cain|Omnis qui occiderit Cain]] there must be understood *shall be gravely punished*. For which reason too there was no need to ascribe that exposition to the Hebrews, as though in this they expounded this letter better than the Catholic doctors.

paras.t: Ex his primo habetur, quod expositio illa quam Rabbi Paulus tam absolute et acriter reprobat, non est taliter reprobanda. Secundo, quod Rabbi Paulus affirmat Deum assecurasse ipsum Cain, quod non occideretur ab aliquo, est contra expositionem catholicorum expositorum communiter, sicut jam patuit. Non enim Deus assecuravit eum de occisione absolute, sed quod non occideretur eo modo quo timuit vel optavit, utpote cito seu a quocumque homine aut bestia occurrente. Ideo Paulus iste inconvenienter infert: Unde non videtur rationabiliter dictum, quod divina assertio frustraretur, quasi illi hoc dicant, qui aiunt ipsum Cain interfectum a Lamech: imo nullus sanæ mentis audet hoc cogitare. Tertio, quod Rabbi Paulus ait, ipsum Cain non esse occisum a Lamech, neque ab alio, non solum est contra commune dictum Catholicorum, sed et contra dictum Hebræorum multorum, ut Lyra allegat. Hieronymus quoque hoc loco ita sentire videtur, ut verba ejus præallegata testantur. Quarto, quod ait, Cain perisse diluvio, non apparet, sic enim vixisset multo plus quam mille annis, quum tamen nullus legatur tamdiu vixisse. Siquidem Mathusalem qui vixit annis nongentis sexaginta novem, obiit ante diluvium anno immediate præcedente, secundum Hieronymum. Mathusalem autem fuit sextus aut septimus post Seth, qui natus est post Cain; imo secundum dictum istud, Cain vixisset plusquam mille et quadringentis annis. Postremo objectionem illam, quod verbum illud, Septuplum punietur, non possit exponi de interfectore ipsius Cain, Rabbi Paulus satis solvit: Frequenter enim contingit, ut ait, quod pro minoribus culpis infligitur major pœna, eo quod homines proniores sunt ad culpas illas minores, quatenus terrore pœnarum retrahantur a vitiis illis. Pœnæ quippe vitæ præsentis non solum sunt supplicia, sed item remedia vitiorum. Hinc quoque secundum jura civilia, major pœna infligitur pro uxoricidio, quam pro matricidio, quum tamen matricidium sit gravius crimen.
paras.en: From these things it is had, first, that the exposition which Rabbi Paul so absolutely and sharply rejects is not to be so rejected. Second, that what Rabbi Paul affirms, that God assured Cain that he would not be killed by anyone, is against the exposition of the Catholic expositors generally, as has now appeared. For God did not assure him against being slain absolutely, but that he would not be slain in the way he feared or wished: namely, quickly, or by any man or beast that met him. Therefore this Paul makes an unfitting inference: Hence it does not seem reasonably said that the divine assertion was made void; as though those who say that Cain was killed by Lamech were saying this: nay, no one of sound mind dares to think it. Third, what Rabbi Paul says, that Cain was not killed by Lamech nor by anyone else, is not only against the common saying of Catholics, but also against the saying of many Hebrews, as Lyra alleges. Jerome too seems to think so in this place, as his words alleged above bear witness. Fourth, what he says, that Cain perished in the flood, is not evident; for so he would have lived much more than a thousand years, though no one is read to have lived so long. For Mathusala, who lived nine hundred and sixty-nine years, died before the flood, in the year immediately preceding it, according to Jerome. Now Mathusala was the sixth or seventh after Seth, who was born after Cain; nay, according to this saying, Cain would have lived more than one thousand four hundred years. Lastly, the objection that the saying [[4:15|shall be punished sevenfold|Septuplum punietur]] cannot be expounded of the slayer of Cain, Rabbi Paul answers well enough: for it often happens, as he says, that a greater punishment is inflicted for lesser faults, because men are more prone to those lesser faults, so that by the terror of punishments they may be drawn back from those vices. For the punishments of the present life are not only penalties but also remedies of vices. Hence too, according to the civil laws, a greater punishment is inflicted for the killing of a wife than for the killing of a mother, although matricide is the graver crime.

paras.t: Posuitque Dominus in Cain signum, ut non interficeret eum omnis qui invenisset eum. Signum istud fuit plaga quædam inflicta ipsi Cain a Deo, ut per plagam illam omnes cognoscerent eum esse punitum, excommunicatum et maledictum a Domino propter innocentis fratris sui occisionem, et ita abstinerent ab interfectione ipsius, quem Deus prohibuit trucidari, et suam prohibitionem declaravit hoc signo: quod signum seu plaga, fuit (ut aliqui dicunt) vehemens capitis tremor. Alii dicunt, quod fuit horribilis tremor omnium membrorum ipsius, et cum hoc impressio quædam in vultu ejus. Porro secundum Strabum, fuit in Cain tremor corporis et agitatio furiatæ mentis. Unde superius ubi nostra translatio habet, Vagus et profugus eris super terram, Septuaginta transtulerunt, Gemens et tremens eris.
paras.en: [[4:15|And the Lord set a mark upon Cain, that whosoever found him should not kill him|Posuitque Dominus in Cain signum, ut non interficeret eum omnis qui invenisset eum]]. This mark was a certain stroke [*plaga*, a blow or affliction] inflicted on Cain by God, so that by that stroke all might know that he had been punished, excommunicated and cursed by the Lord for the killing of his innocent brother, and so might abstain from slaying him, whom God forbade to be slaughtered and whose prohibition He declared by this mark. This mark or stroke was (as some say) a violent trembling of the head. Others say that it was a horrible trembling of all his limbs, and with it a certain impression on his face. Further, according to Strabo, there was in Cain a trembling of the body and an agitation of a maddened mind. Hence above, where our translation has [[4:12|a fugitive and a vagabond shalt thou be upon the earth|Vagus et profugus eris super terram]], the Septuagint translated: *Groaning and trembling shalt thou be*.

paras.t: Egressusque Cain a facie Domini. Corporaliter enim recessit a visibili præsentia angeli, qui ei apparuit in persona Dei, in forma humana. Spiritualiter vero egressus est per mentis aversionem, elongationem, desperationem et indurationem a Deo et a gratiosa ejus præsentia: de quo recessu loquitur Dominus per Osee: Væ eis, quia recesserunt a me. Habitavit profugus in terra ad orientalem plagam Eden. Nomine Eden, intelligitur paradisus terrestris. Itaque Cain recedens a loco habitationis patris sui Adæ, perrexit versus orientem, et profugus cœpit morari ad orientalem plagam paradisi ab ista parte, remote tamen a paradiso, nec amore paradisi perrexit illuc, sed Deo sic ordinante, ad majorem ejus punitionem, ut recordando paradisi delicias magis affligeretur. De hoc Josephus ait : Peragrans Cain multam terram cum uxore sua Calmana, collocatus est in loco, qui Naida appellatur, ubi et filii nati sunt ei. Septuaginta quoque transtulerunt : Habitavit in terra Naid. Circa quod ait Hieronymus : In Hebræo […] dicitur, id est, instabilis et fluctuans et sede incerta. Nec est terra Naid, ut vulgus nostrum putat, sed sensus est, quod juxta sententiam Dei vagus et profugus huc illucque oberravit.
paras.en: [[4:16|And Cain went out from the face of the Lord|Egressusque Cain a facie Domini]]. For bodily he withdrew from the visible presence of the angel who appeared to him in the person of God, in human form; but spiritually he went out by the turning away of his mind, by estrangement, despair and hardening, from God and from His gracious presence: of which departure the Lord speaks through Osee: [[Osee 7:13|Woe to them, for they have departed from me|Væ eis, quia recesserunt a me]]. [[4:16|and dwelt as a fugitive on the earth at the east side of Eden|Habitavit profugus in terra ad orientalem plagam Eden]]. By the name Eden is understood the earthly paradise. And so Cain, withdrawing from the place where his father Adam dwelt, went towards the east, and as a fugitive began to stay at the eastern side of paradise, on that side, yet far from paradise; nor did he go there out of love of paradise, but by God's so ordaining, for his greater punishment, that by remembering the delights of paradise he might be the more afflicted. Of this Josephus says: Cain, wandering over much land with his wife Calmana, settled in a place which is called Naida, where also sons were born to him. The Septuagint too translated: He dwelt in the land of Naid. On which Jerome says: In the Hebrew it is called […], that is, unstable and wavering and of uncertain abode. Nor is there a land Naid, as our common folk think; but the sense is that, according to the sentence of God, he wandered hither and thither as a vagabond and fugitive.

paras.t: Cognovit autem Cain uxorem suam, quæ concepit et peperit Enoch. Uxor Cain, fuit etiam soror sua carnalis. Quocirca sciendum, quod S. Methodius martyr et præsul, quum esset in carcere, Deum rogavit, ut sibi aliquid revelaret de principio mundi et fine ejus. Et quod Deus sibi revelavit, reliquit in scriptis, inter cetera dicens : Adam et Eva de paradiso egressi sunt virgines. Quumque Adam quindecim esset annorum, genuit Cain et sororem ejus Calmana. Post alios quindecim annos natus est ei Abel et soror ejus Delbora. Quamvis autem Adam factus sit in ætate et robore virili quasi esset triginta annorum, tamen quando primo plasmatus est, fuit unius diei, deinde unius anni et duorum ac trium, etc., ascendendo paulatim. Et sicut in Scholastica historia tangitur, potuit ante Cain multos filios genuisse, qui hic tacentur. Et similiter inter Cain et Abel. Juxta Methodium quoque, Abel fuit centum annorum quando occisus est. Itaque sicut ait Methodius, Eva in quolibet partu genuit binos, id est masculum et feminam, quod etiam dicunt Hebræi. Sicque Calmana soror ipsius Cain, fuit uxor ipsius.
paras.en: [[4:17|And Cain knew his wife, and she conceived, and brought forth Henoch|Cognovit autem Cain uxorem suam, quæ concepit et peperit Enoch]]. Cain's wife was also his sister according to the flesh. On this it should be known that St. Methodius, martyr and bishop, when he was in prison, prayed God to reveal to him something about the beginning of the world and its end. And what God revealed to him he left in writing, saying among other things: Adam and Eve went out of paradise virgins. And when Adam was fifteen years old, he begot Cain and his sister Calmana. After another fifteen years Abel was born to him, and his sister Delbora. Now although Adam was made in the age and strength of a grown man, as if he were thirty years old, yet when he was first formed he was one day old, then one year, and two, and three, etc., going up little by little [that is, Adam's years are counted from the day of his creation]. And, as is touched on in the Scholastic History, he may have begotten many sons before Cain, who are passed over in silence here; and likewise between Cain and Abel. According to Methodius, too, Abel was a hundred years old when he was slain. So, as Methodius says, Eve at each birth bore two, that is, a male and a female, which the Hebrews also say. And thus Calmana, Cain's own sister, was his wife.

paras.t: Et ædificavit civitatem ipse Cain non solus, sed simul cum adjutoribus suis, ex suo semine natis ; et vocavit nomen ejus, ex nomine filii sui Enoch, id est Enochiam, secundum Josephum. Hanc civitatem Cain ædificavit, non statim aut immediate post nativitatem primogeniti sui, sed quum multi fuissent ex se nati. De hoc loquitur Augustinus diffuse quintodecimo de Civitate Dei, ostendens quod primi homines illi tamdiu vivendo poterant valde multiplicari, quum filii Israel sic multiplicati fuerint in Ægypto infra modicum tempus. Præterea Josephus ait : Cain rapinis et violentia opes congregans, suos ad latrocinia et luxuriam invitabat, simplicitatemque vitæ humanæ adinventione mensurarum ac ponderum permutavit, atque ad calliditatem et corruptionem perduxit, terminos terræ posuit primus, civitates quoque muravit, et timens eos quos læsit, suos in urbibus congregavit. Rabbi Paulus autem testatur, quod Cain primo invenit prudentiam politicam. Ad quod dicendum videtur, quod quum vitiosis, teste Philosopho, non insit prudentia, ipse pravissimus Cain prudentiam veram non habuit, nec invenit, nec urbes instituit propter commune bonum, sed sicut prætactum est, ob finem perversum ; sed habuit aliquid simile veræ prudentiæ, sicut et ceteri impii, utpote vulpinam versutiam. Iterum dicit, quod ex quo terra nullum fructum dedit ipsi Cain, idcirco reliquit agriculturam, quam primo elegit. Et ipse ac sua posteritas studuit artibus mechanicis inveniendis, quæ ad hominum convictum sunt utiles. Verumtamen sicut ex præhabita expositione innotuit, non est intelligendum, quod terra nullum fructum protulit Cain, sed minorem quam alii.
paras.en: [[4:17|and he built a city|Et ædificavit civitatem]]: Cain himself, not alone but together with his helpers, born of his own seed; [[4:17|and called the name thereof by the name of his son Henoch|et vocavit nomen ejus, ex nomine filii sui Enoch]], that is, Enochia, according to Josephus. Cain built this city not at once or immediately after the birth of his firstborn, but when many had been born of him. Augustine speaks of this at length in the fifteenth book of the City of God, showing that those first men, living so long, could multiply very greatly, since the children of Israel were so multiplied in Egypt within a short time. Moreover Josephus says: Cain, gathering wealth by plunder and violence, invited his own to robbery and lust; and he changed the simplicity of human life by the invention of measures and weights, and led it to craftiness and corruption; he was the first to set boundaries to the land; he also walled cities, and, fearing those whom he had injured, gathered his own into towns. Rabbi Paul [Paul of Burgos, whose Additions to Lyra's Postill Denis often cites], again, testifies that Cain first invented political prudence. To this it seems we must say that since, as the Philosopher [Aristotle] witnesses, prudence is not found in the vicious, Cain, most wicked as he was, neither had nor invented true prudence, nor founded cities for the common good, but, as was touched on before, for a perverse end; yet he had something like true prudence, as the other ungodly have too, namely a fox's cunning. He says further that, because the earth gave Cain no fruit, he therefore left husbandry, which he had chosen at first; and he and his posterity applied themselves to inventing the mechanical arts, which are useful for men's living together. Yet, as appeared from the exposition given before, it is not to be understood that the earth bore no fruit for Cain, but less than for others.

paras.t: Porro Enoch genuit Irad, et Irad genuit Maviael, et Maviael genuit Mathusael, et Mathusael genuit Lamech. Qui accepit uxores duas : nomen uni Ada, et nomen alteri Sella. Lamech iste qui septimus fuit ab Adam, tam pravus fuit, quod primus bigamiam induxit, duas accipiendo uxores sine dispensatione divina, contra Dei decretum et legem naturæ, ac morem laudabilem, qui habet vim legis. In prima quippe institutione matrimonii, facta est unica uxor unico viro. Et Deus per Adam decrevit ac dixit : Erunt duo in carne una. Sicque Lamech cum secunda uxore adulterium perpetravit, quia non fuit veraciter uxor : juxta quem modum usque in præsens adulterant Saraceni, qui plures ducunt uxores, sicut hoc plenius demonstravi in libro quem edidi contra Alcoranum, id est librum legis eorum. Guillelmus quoque Parisiensis idem testatur in libro de Fide et legibus. Refert Josephus, quod Lamech ex duabus suis uxoribus habuit filios septem et septuaginta.
paras.en: [[4:18|And Henoch begot Irad, and Irad begot Maviael, and Maviael begot Mathusael, and Mathusael begot Lamech,|Porro Enoch genuit Irad, et Irad genuit Maviael, et Maviael genuit Mathusael, et Mathusael genuit Lamech]] [[4:19|Who took two wives: the name of the one was Ada, and the name of the other Sella.|Qui accepit uxores duas : nomen uni Ada, et nomen alteri Sella]] This Lamech, who was the seventh from Adam, was so wicked that he was the first to bring in bigamy [that is, having two wives at once], taking two wives without divine dispensation, against God's decree and the law of nature, and against laudable custom, which has the force of law. For in the first institution of marriage one wife was made for one man. And God decreed through Adam, and said: [[Gen 2:24|they shall be two in one flesh|Erunt duo in carne una]]. And so Lamech committed adultery with the second wife, since she was not truly his wife; in which way the Saracens commit adultery to this present day, who marry several wives, as I have shown more fully in the book I published against the Alcoran, that is, the book of their law. William of Paris also testifies the same in his book On Faith and Laws. Josephus relates that Lamech had seventy-seven sons by his two wives.

paras.t: Genuitque Ada Jabel, qui fuit pater habitantium in tentoriis atque pastorum. Iste Jabel vocatur pater habitantium in tentoriis et pastorum, quoniam fuit magister eorum, et præcipuus inter eos, quantum ad multa. Invenit namque artem faciendi portatilia, hoc est tentoria seu portatiles domus pastorum : quæ tentoria pastores secum ferebant tempore opportuno, quando pergere voluerunt ad alia pascua. Ordinavitque pecorum greges, et characteribus seu signis distinxit eos ab invicem. Sed et greges ovium ab hœdorum gregibus separavit, tam secundum qualitatem, videlicet unicolores a multicoloribus, quam secundum ætatem, ut agniculos a maturioribus. Consideravit quoque commixtiones pecorum certis temporibus faciendas, prout in Scholastica fertur historia.
paras.en: [[4:20|And Ada brought forth Jabel: who was the father of such as dwell in tents, and of herdsmen.|Genuitque Ada Jabel, qui fuit pater habitantium in tentoriis atque pastorum]] This Jabel is called the father of such as dwell in tents and of herdsmen, since he was their master, and the chief among them in many things. For he invented the art of making things that can be carried, that is, tents or portable houses for herdsmen; which tents the herdsmen carried with them at the fitting time, when they wished to move on to other pastures. And he ordered the herds of cattle, and marked them off from one another with brands or signs. He also separated the flocks of sheep from the herds of goats, both by kind, namely the one-coloured from the many-coloured, and by age, as the lambs from the older ones. He also considered how the matings of the cattle should be made at certain times, as is related in the Scholastic History.

paras.t: Et nomen fratris ejus Jubal, quem genuit Ada ex Lamech. Ipse Jubal fuit pater canentium in cithara et organo, hoc est magister et princeps utentium atque ludentium in his musicis instrumentis, quoniam primo invenit musica instrumenta, ut aliqui dicunt ; et inventor musicæ secundum Glossam. Verumtamen auctor Scholasticæ historiæ refert, quod non fuit inventor musicorum instrumentorum, quæ diu postea sunt inventa, sed quod fuit inventor consonantiarum, ut labor pastoralis hoc relevaretur solatio, et quasi in delicias verteretur. Denique, ut recitant Rabanus et præfata Historia, ex quo Jubal iste percepit ipsum Adam prophetasse de duplici judicio mundi, uno per aquam, alio per ignem : ideo scripsit musicæ artem in duabus columnis, et in qualibet totam, hoc est, in columna marmorea, quæ non dissolveretur diluvio, et in columna latericia, quæ non dissolveretur incendio. Istud ex Josepho sumptum est, qui etiam narrat columnam illam marmoream adhuc in terra Syriaca esse. Verumtamen Josephus recitat istud aut simile huic de filiis Seth, ut infra dicetur.
paras.en: [[4:21|And his brother's name was Jubal|Et nomen fratris ejus Jubal]], whom Ada bore to Lamech. [[4:21|he was the father of them that play upon the harp and the organs|Ipse Jubal fuit pater canentium in cithara et organo]], that is, the master and prince of those who use and play these musical instruments, since he first invented musical instruments, as some say; and he was the inventor of music, according to the Gloss. Yet the author of the Scholastic History relates that he was not the inventor of musical instruments, which were invented long afterwards, but that he was the inventor of harmonies [consonantiæ: the concords of sounds], so that the herdsmen's labour might be relieved by this solace and turned, as it were, into delight. Lastly, as Rabanus and the said History recount, since this Jubal had learned that Adam had prophesied a twofold judgment of the world, one by water, the other by fire, he wrote the art of music on two pillars, the whole of it on each: that is, on a pillar of marble, which would not be dissolved by the flood, and on a pillar of brick, which would not be dissolved by the fire. This is taken from Josephus, who also tells that the marble pillar is still in the land of Syria. Yet Josephus tells this, or something like it, of the sons of Seth, as will be said below.

paras.t: Sella quoque genuit ex Lamech Tubalcain, qui fuit malleator et faber in cuncta opera æris et ferri, id est, ad faciendum omnia quæ fiunt ex ære et ferro. Hic enim primus invenit artem ferrariam, atque ut Josephus scribit, alios docuit artem istam, et res bellicas fecit, et fortitudine cunctos excellens, res bellicas decenter exercuit. Aliqua quoque ad oculorum concupiscentiam spectantia, scilicet sculpturas et picturas invenit. De hoc in Scholastica refertur historia, quod isto Tubalcain fabricante ex ære et ferro, et sculpturas in metallis faciente, præfatus frater ejus Jubal delectatus sono malleorum, consideravit et excogitavit ex ponderibus malleorum proportiones et consonantias musicæ quæ nascuntur ex illis. Quam inventionem Græci Pythagoræ attribuunt fabulose. Denique Tubalcain iste excogitavit ex opere fruticum operari in metallis. Quum enim frutices incendisset in pascuis, venæ metallorum fluxerunt et eruperunt in rivulos suos, et laminæ inde sublatæ, referebant figuras locorum in quibus jacuerant. Soror vero Tubalcain fuit Noema, quæ dicitur invenisse artem variæ texturæ. Et aliqui dicunt, quod invenit lanificium, ad faciendum vestes ex lana, quum homines antea induerentur animalium pelles, sicut induti erant a Deo primi parentes.
paras.en: [[4:22|Sella also brought forth|Sella quoque genuit]] by Lamech [[4:22|Tubalcain, who was a hammerer and artificer in every work of brass and iron|Tubalcain, qui fuit malleator et faber in cuncta opera æris et ferri]], that is, for making all things that are made of brass and iron. For he first invented the smith's art, and, as Josephus writes, taught others this art and made the things of war, and, excelling all in strength, practised the things of war with skill. He also invented some things that pertain to the concupiscence of the eyes, namely carvings and paintings. Of this it is related in the Scholastic History that while this Tubalcain was working in brass and iron and making carvings in metal, his brother Jubal, mentioned above, delighted by the sound of the hammers, considered and worked out from the weights of the hammers the proportions and harmonies of music that arise from them. This discovery the Greeks, fabulously, attribute to Pythagoras. Further, this Tubalcain thought out from what happened to brushwood how to work in metals. For when he had set fire to the brushwood in the pastures, the veins of the metals melted and burst out into little streams of their own, and the plates taken up from there bore the shapes of the places in which they had lain. [[4:22|And the sister of Tubalcain|Soror vero Tubalcain]] was [[4:22|Noema|Noema]], who is said to have invented the art of varied weaving. And some say that she invented the working of wool, for making garments of wool, since men had before been clothed in the skins of animals, as our first parents had been clothed by God.

paras.t: Refert hic Lyra, quod Hebræi dicunt præfatum Jabel fecisse tentoria ad ponendum in eis idola, et quod Jubal canebat in instrumentis musicis coram idolis illis, eadem venerando : ex quo infert, quod isti qui descenderunt de Cain, fuerunt malitiosi : quod quamvis sit verum, tamen dictum illud Hebræorum videtur contrariari communi dicto doctorum, dicentium quod idololatria post diluvium cœpit, nec ante fuit, propter recentem memoriam creationis mundi, ex qua cunctis innotuit unitas veri Dei. Præterea Rabbi Paulus ait hoc loco, quod Lamech adinvenit tres artes pro filiis suis, videlicet artem faciendi tentoria, artem faciendi musica instrumenta, et artem ferrariam ad arma bellica fabricanda. Sed istud videtur contrariari textui, verbisque Josephi et doctoribus catholicis præallegatis. Nempe si Lamech invenisset has artes, inventio harum artium non adscriberetur filiis ejus, nec unus eorum vocaretur pater habitantium in tentoriis atque pastorum, alter vero pater canentium cithara, etc.
paras.en: Here Lyra relates that the Hebrews say that the aforesaid Jabel made tents to set idols in, and that Jubal sang on musical instruments before those idols, worshipping them; from which he infers that those who descended from Cain were wicked. Which, though it is true, yet that saying of the Hebrews seems to contradict the common saying of the doctors, who say that idolatry began after the flood and was not before it, because of the fresh memory of the creation of the world, from which the unity of the true God was known to all. Moreover Rabbi Paul says at this place that Lamech invented three arts for his sons, namely the art of making tents, the art of making musical instruments, and the smith's art for forging weapons of war. But this seems to contradict the text, and the words of Josephus and of the catholic doctors cited before. For if Lamech had invented these arts, the invention of these arts would not be ascribed to his sons, nor would one of them be called [[4:20|the father of such as dwell in tents, and of herdsmen|pater habitantium in tentoriis atque pastorum]], and the other [[4:21|the father of them that play upon the harp|pater canentium cithara]], etc.

paras.t: Dixitque Lamech uxoribus suis, Adæ et Sellæ : Audite vocem meam, o uxores Lamech, auscultate sermonem meum, id est, auribus corporis et cordis diligenter advertite verba mea, quæ nunc magni ponderis erunt: quoniam occidi virum, id est, sagittando interfeci Cain in vulnus meum, hoc est ad mei ipsius dolorem et conscientiæ meæ remorsum, et adolescentulum occidi in livorem meum, hoc est zelo furoris et rancoris contra juvenem illum concepto. Septuplum ultio dabitur de Cain, id est, ego ipse graviter valde puniar, eo quod occiderim Cain, juxta sensum in isto articulo præinductum ; de Lamech vero septuagies septies, id est, si quis occiderit me, quasi incomparabiliter plus punietur pro suo peccato quo me sponte occideret, quam ego puniri promerui, qui sine proposito meo, et nescienter occidi Cain, non ex invidia aliqua; et de ejus occisione vehementissime doleo, tantumque dolui, quod adolescentulum interfeci, ob hoc, quod ex ejus erronea directione ipsum Cain occidi.
paras.en: [[4:23|And Lamech said to his wives Ada and Sella|Dixitque Lamech uxoribus suis, Adæ et Sellæ]]: [[4:23|Hear my voice, ye wives of Lamech|Audite vocem meam, o uxores Lamech]], [[4:23|hearken to my speech|auscultate sermonem meum]], that is, attend carefully with the ears of body and of heart to my words, which will now be of great weight: [[4:23|for I have slain a man|quoniam occidi virum]], that is, I have killed Cain with an arrow, [[4:23|to the wounding of myself|in vulnus meum]], that is, to my own sorrow and the remorse of my conscience, [[4:23|and a stripling|et adolescentulum]] I have slain [[4:23|to my own bruising|in livorem meum]], that is, out of a zeal of fury and rancour conceived against that youth [livor means both a bruise and spite; Denis takes it in the second sense]. [[4:24|Sevenfold vengeance shall be taken for Cain|Septuplum ultio dabitur de Cain]], that is, I myself shall be very gravely punished for having slain Cain, in the sense brought forward earlier in this article; [[4:24|but for Lamech seventy times sevenfold|de Lamech vero septuagies septies]], that is, if anyone kills me, he will be punished almost beyond comparison more for his sin in killing me of set purpose than I have deserved to be punished, who slew Cain without intending it and unknowingly, not out of any envy; and I grieve most vehemently over his killing, and I grieved so much that I slew the stripling, because it was through his mistaken direction that I slew Cain.

paras.t: Probabile reor, quod quum Lamech occidisset Cain, timuit ab aliquo posterorum ipsius Cain interfici, in ultionem sanguinis Cain, eo quod Cain erat post Adam primus et communis pater totius plebis illius malevolæ. Ideo Lamech dixit hæc verba, ad reprimendum omnes illos a sui occisione. Aliqui autem dicunt, quod uxores istius Lamech, tractabant eum valde male in senio suo : ideo protulit verba hæc ad earum terrorem, ne auderent eum ita affligere. Et sicut in Scholastica habetur historia, Hebræi hoc dicunt, et quamvis quidam hoc reprobet, rationes tamen ejus facillime solvi possent, nec dignum arbitror circa hoc immorari.
paras.en: I think it probable that, when Lamech had slain Cain, he feared being killed by one of Cain's descendants in vengeance for Cain's blood, since Cain was, after Adam, the first and common father of all that malevolent people. Therefore Lamech spoke these words, to restrain them all from killing him. Some, however, say that this Lamech's wives treated him very badly in his old age; therefore he uttered these words to frighten them, that they might not dare to afflict him so. And, as is found in the Scholastic History, the Hebrews say this; and although someone rejects it, yet his reasons could very easily be answered, nor do I think it worth dwelling on this.

paras.t: Rursus Lyra adducit hic aliam expositionem, dicendo quod uxores Lamech refugiebant ejus concubitum, eo quod occidisset Cain et adolescentulum, quem quidam Hebræi dicunt fuisse Tubalcain filium suum : propter quod metuebant, quod si conciperent ex Lamech, proles nascitura esset a Deo plaganda. Hinc Lamech excusando se dixit : Quoniam occidi virum, etc., juxta sensum præhabitum. Deinde consolando uxores suas, adjecit : Septuplum ultio dabitur de Cain, etc. ; quasi diceret : Si Cain, qui invidiose occidit Abel, non fuit interfectus usque ad septimam generationem ; multo fortius ego, qui ignoranter occidi Cain, non puniar in prole mea usque ad generationes multo plures, vel usque in generationes sine termino. Sed huic expositioni objicitur, quia secundum eam, verbum hoc Lamech fuisset in se falsum. Ipse enim in prole sua fuit punitus diluvio diu ante septimam generationem post eum, imo tota sua progenies periit ante illam. Non autem videtur, quod Scriptura ista canonica tam ponderose recitasset unum mendacium Lamech, præsertim quum recitatio illius non videatur utilis aliunde.
paras.en: Again, Lyra brings forward here another exposition, saying that Lamech's wives shunned lying with him because he had slain Cain and the stripling, who, some Hebrews say, was Tubalcain his son; on which account they feared that, if they conceived by Lamech, the offspring to be born would be stricken by God. Hence Lamech, excusing himself, said: [[4:23|for I have slain a man|Quoniam occidi virum]], etc., in the sense given before. Then, consoling his wives, he added: [[4:24|Sevenfold vengeance shall be taken for Cain|Septuplum ultio dabitur de Cain]], etc.; as if to say: If Cain, who slew Abel out of envy, was not killed until the seventh generation, much more shall I, who slew Cain unknowingly, not be punished in my offspring until many more generations, or until generations without end. But against this exposition it is objected that, according to it, this word of Lamech would have been false in itself. For he was punished in his offspring by the flood long before the seventh generation after him; indeed his whole progeny perished before it. And it does not seem that this canonical Scripture would have recounted so weightily a lie of Lamech, especially since the recounting of it does not seem useful in any other way.

paras.t: Præterea Rabbi Paulus improbat hanc ipsam expositionem. Id quoque quod recitatum est de uxoribus Lamech, quod ejus vitabant concubitum, non habet auctoritatem aut certitudinem ex Scripturis, nec ex dictis authenticis. Hinc Rabbi Paulus aliam ponit, et approbat expositionem quam Rabbi Moysi adscribit, dicenti quod uxores Lamech videntes fieri diversa opera ex ære et ferro, formidabant quod ex arte illa introducerent arma ad vulnerandum et occidendum ; ideo Lamech retraxit eas ab isto timore, dicens : Occidi virum in vulnus meum ; quasi diceret : Possum occidere in vulnere aut livore sine armis. Verum hæc expositio videtur valde impropria, ut scilicet verbum istud præteriti temporis, Occidi, exponatur per istud complexum, Possum occidere. Hinc prima quam posui, expositio aptior mihi videtur.
paras.en: Moreover Rabbi Paul disapproves this very exposition. And what was recounted about Lamech's wives, that they avoided lying with him, has no authority or certainty from the Scriptures, nor from authentic sayings. Hence Rabbi Paul puts forward and approves another exposition, which he ascribes to Rabbi Moses, who says that Lamech's wives, seeing various works being made of brass and iron, feared that from that art men would bring in weapons for wounding and killing; therefore Lamech drew them away from this fear, saying: [[4:23|I have slain a man to the wounding of myself|Occidi virum in vulnus meum]]; as if to say: I can kill by wound or bruise without weapons. But this exposition seems very improper, namely that this word of past time, Occidi [I have slain], should be expounded by this phrase, Possum occidere [I can kill]. Hence the first exposition that I gave seems to me more fitting.

paras.t: Quocirca sciendum, quia ut dicunt auctor Scholasticæ historiæ, Glossa, et Rabanus, Lamech vir sagittarius exstitit et venator, ac diu vivendo incurrit oculorum caliginem ; ideo duxit secum adolescentem, qui sibi monstravit bestias sagittandas, qui videns Cain jacentem retro fruteta, putavit bestiam esse ; sicque ex directione adolescentis, Lamech direxit sagittam in Cain, et eum occidit. Quo cognito, ita accensus est ira contra adolescentem, quod verberavit eum usque ad mortem. Cain autem ita hinc inde latebat, eo quod abominabilis et in timore jugiter fuit. Lamech quoque venabatur et bestias sagittabat, non ut earum carnibus vesceretur, quoniam ante diluvium non erat manducatio carnium, sed pro sua delectatione et usu pellium ad vestitum.
paras.en: On this it should be known that, as the author of the Scholastic History, the Gloss and Rabanus say, Lamech was an archer and a hunter, and from living long fell into dimness of the eyes; therefore he took with him a youth who showed him the beasts to shoot; and he, seeing Cain lying behind the thickets, thought he was a beast; and so, at the youth's direction, Lamech aimed an arrow at Cain and killed him. When he learned this, he was so kindled with anger against the youth that he beat him to death. Now Cain lay hidden here and there in this way because he was abominable and was continually in fear. Lamech, too, hunted and shot beasts, not to feed on their flesh, since before the flood there was no eating of flesh, but for his own delight and for the use of their skins for clothing.

paras.t: Deinde describitur, qualiter generatio electorum quorumdam processit ex Adam, quum subditur : Cognovit quoque adhuc Adam uxorem suam ; et peperit filium, vocavitque nomen ejus Seth, quod uno modo interpretatur positio, et ita accipitur hic. Nam subditur : Dicens, ipsa uxor Adæ : Posuit mihi Deus semen aliud pro Abel, id est, alium filium, scilicet istum Seth, contulit mihi Deus succedentem in locum Abel, quem interfecit Cain.
paras.en: Then it is described how the generation of certain of the elect proceeded from Adam, when there follows: [[4:25|Adam also knew his wife again|Cognovit quoque adhuc Adam uxorem suam]]: [[4:25|and she brought forth a son, and called his name Seth|et peperit filium, vocavitque nomen ejus Seth]], which in one way is interpreted placing, and so it is taken here. For there follows: [[4:25|saying|Dicens]], that is, Adam's wife: [[4:25|God hath given me another seed for Abel|Posuit mihi Deus semen aliud pro Abel]] [posuit, literally "hath placed", where the Douay-Rheims has "hath given": hence the name Seth, "placing"], that is, another son, namely this Seth, God has granted me to succeed in Abel's place, [[4:25|whom Cain slew|quem interfecit Cain]].

paras.t: Circa hoc in Scholastica historia fertur : Dicit Strabus, quod Adam post mortem Abel, vovit non se amplius cogniturum uxorem. Verumtamen Strabus recitative magis quam assertive hoc ait : Ferunt, inquiens, post mortem Abel vovisse Adam, se ultra uxorem non cogniturum, nec filium generaturum : sed Deo jubente per angelum, fregit votum ut Dei Filius de ea nascetur et homo redimeretur. De Cain enim nasci non debuit. Verumtamen Josephus scribit quod Abel extincto, et Cain ejecto, amor generationis vehementer angebat Adam. Istud autem quod dicitur de voto seu proposito Adæ de continendo in reliquum, reprobat Rabbi Paulus. Sed dicendum, quod dictum illud satis probabile est ex duobus. Primo, ex vehementissimo mœrore, quem de Abel occisione concepit. Non enim solummodo doluerunt ipse et Eva de Abel interfectione, sed etiam ineffabiliter de tanto maleficio proprii filii, scilicet Cain ; et ideo potuerunt cogitare, melius esse non generare, quam in filiis genitis talia fieri ac videre. Et timuerunt, ne talia de cetero fierent. Sciebant equidem verum esse quod diu postmodum scriptum est : Bonum est mori sine filiis, quam post se relinquere filios nequam. Secundo, quia habetur in textu, quod Adam erat centum et triginta annorum dum genuit Seth. Ex quo elicitur, quod post occisionem Abel diu continuit, saltem secundum computationem Septuaginta interpretum atque Methodii, nisi dicatur alios genuisse inter Abel et Seth, quos Scriptura non exprimit.
paras.en: On this it is related in the Scholastic History: Strabus says that Adam, after the death of Abel, vowed that he would not know his wife any more. Yet Strabus says this by way of report rather than of assertion: They say, he says, that after Abel's death Adam vowed that he would no longer know his wife nor beget a son; but at God's bidding, given through an angel, he broke the vow, so that the Son of God might be born of her and man be redeemed. For He was not to be born of Cain. Yet Josephus writes that when Abel was dead and Cain cast out, the desire for offspring vehemently pressed upon Adam. Now this that is said of Adam's vow or resolve to be continent for the rest of his life Rabbi Paul rejects. But it must be said that the saying is probable enough on two grounds. First, from the most vehement grief that he conceived over Abel's slaying. For he and Eve grieved not only over Abel's killing, but also unspeakably over so great a crime of their own son, namely Cain; and so they could have thought it better not to beget than to see such things done among the children begotten. And they feared that such things might happen again. For they knew the truth of what was written long afterwards: [[Ecclus 16:4|it is better to die without children, than to leave ungodly children|Bonum est mori sine filiis, quam post se relinquere filios nequam]] [Denis quotes freely; the Vulgate has utile est mori sine filiis, quam relinquere filios impios]. Second, because it is found in the text that Adam was a hundred and thirty years old when he begot Seth. From which it is gathered that after Abel's slaying he was continent for a long time, at least according to the reckoning of the Septuagint translators and of Methodius, unless it be said that he begot others between Abel and Seth whom Scripture does not mention.

paras.t: Denique Lyra refert, quod Hebræi dicunt ipsum Lamech convenisse conjuges suas coram Adam, qui erat pater et judex eorum, eo quod nollent sibi misceri. Quumque Adam vellet eas inducere, ut redderent debitum viro suo, dixerunt ad Adam : Castiga primo te ipsum, quoniam diu continuisti ab Eva. Tunc Adam cognovit conjugem suam. Ista fabula stulta est, et manifeste mendosa. Jam enim expositum est, quod secundum doctores catholicos et Hebræos atque Josephum, Lamech ex senectute incurrit oculorum caliginem, antequam interfecit Cain et adolescentem, propter quod factum, dicunt Hebræi isti uxores Lamech abhorruisse ejus concubitum : sicque Lamech fuisset antiquus atque cæcutiens, antequam Adam genuit Seth, quem genuit quum esset centum triginta annorum, quæ ætas fuit tunc adhuc juvenilis. Sicque Lamech fuisset senior ipso Adam. Rursus generatio Cain non potuit protendi usque ad septimam generationem ante nativitatem Seth, seu antequam Adam fuit centum triginta annorum, præsertim quia homines tunc multis annis vixerunt antequam genuerunt. Sed ad hoc quidam respondet, quasi salvando fabulam Hebræorum, quod filii Cain erant luxuriosi, ideo festinabant accipere conjuges. Sicque antequam Adam esset centum triginta annorum, poterant usque ad septimam generationem venire. Quod si verum esset, generatio illa fuisset adhuc multiplicata per plurimos gradus ac numeros ante diluvium : quod est contra doctores sanctos, et contra textum, qui genealogiam Cain terminat in filiis Lamech.
paras.en: Lastly, Lyra relates that the Hebrews say that Lamech brought his wives before Adam, who was their father and judge, because they would not lie with him. And when Adam wished to induce them to render the debt [that is, the marriage debt, the conjugal union owed to a spouse] to their husband, they said to Adam: First chastise thyself, for thou hast long abstained from Eve. Then Adam knew his wife. This fable is foolish and plainly false. For it has already been set out that, according to the catholic doctors and the Hebrews and Josephus, Lamech in old age fell into dimness of the eyes before he slew Cain and the youth, on account of which deed, these Hebrews say, Lamech's wives shrank from lying with him; and so Lamech would have been old and half-blind before Adam begot Seth, whom he begot when he was a hundred and thirty years old, which age was then still youthful. And so Lamech would have been older than Adam himself. Again, Cain's line could not have stretched to the seventh generation before the birth of Seth, or before Adam was a hundred and thirty years old, especially since men then lived many years before they begot. But to this someone replies, as if to save the Hebrews' fable, that Cain's sons were lustful and therefore hastened to take wives; and so, before Adam was a hundred and thirty years old, they could have come as far as the seventh generation. If this were true, that line would have multiplied further through very many degrees and numbers before the flood: which is against the holy doctors, and against the text, which ends the genealogy of Cain with the sons of Lamech.

paras.t: Sed et Seth natus est filius, id est, ipse Seth ex conjuge sua genuit filium, quem vocavit Enos : quod nomen interpretatur, homo seu vir ; et optime conveniebat homini huic, qui rationabiliter ac virtuose se habuit, quia subjungitur : Iste cœpit invocare nomen Domini. Non est dubium quin Adam et Eva, et Abel quamdiu vixit, Seth quoque quotidie ac devote invocaverint Deum ; sed iste dicitur specialiter cœpisse Dominum invocare, quoniam cum præcipua devotione hoc fecit, et forte cum specialibus orationibus et ritibus, cærimoniisque decentibus.
paras.en: [[4:26|But to Seth also was born a son|Sed et Seth natus est filius]], that is, Seth himself begot a son by his wife, [[4:26|whom he called Enos|quem vocavit Enos]]: which name is interpreted man [homo seu vir: man, or a man in the full sense]; and it suited this man excellently, who bore himself reasonably and virtuously, for there follows: [[4:26|this man began to call upon the name of the Lord|Iste cœpit invocare nomen Domini]]. There is no doubt that Adam and Eve, and Abel as long as he lived, and Seth too, called upon God daily and devoutly; but this man is said in a special way to have begun to call upon the Lord, because he did it with especial devotion, and perhaps with special prayers and rites and becoming ceremonies.

paras.t: Circa hoc refert Lyra, in Hebræo haberi, Tunc cœpit invocare nomen Domini, propter quod Judæi exponunt hanc invocationem de idololatria, quia (ut dicunt) tunc aliqui inceperunt nomen Dei attribuere creaturis, videlicet soli, lunæ, ac idolis ; non tamen ab isto devoto Enos, sed a filiis Cain ei contemporaneis, factum est hoc. Istud autem stolide dictum est, quoniam invocatio nominis Dei semper in bono accipitur ; nec sequitur, si tunc idololatria cœpit, quod tunc cœpit invocare nomen Domini, sed potius nomen diaboli, quoniam ab idololatris, etiamsi hoc nesciant, invocatur. Verumtamen S. Hieronymus ait : Plerique Judæorum arbitrantur, quod tunc primo in nomine et similitudine Domini fabricata sint idola. Circa quod aliqui dicunt, et in Scholastica historia tangitur, quod Enos iste excogitavit et fecit imagines ad Dei honorem, et excitandam memoriæ humanæ pigritiam, non ut coleret illas. Ex hoc tamen ut dicitur, alii quidam sumpserunt occasionem erroris. Jam autem superius dictum est, et Thomas in secunda secundæ testatur, quod in prima mundi ætate non fuit idololatria, sed unius Dei solius notitia, ex recenti creationis mundi memoria.
paras.en: On this Lyra relates that the Hebrew has: Then [[4:26|began to call upon the name of the Lord|Tunc cœpit invocare nomen Domini]]; for which reason the Jews expound this calling upon of idolatry, because (as they say) some then began to attribute the name of God to creatures, namely to the sun, the moon and idols; yet this was done not by this devout Enos but by the sons of Cain who were his contemporaries. But this is said foolishly, since the calling upon of God's name is always taken in a good sense; nor does it follow, if idolatry began then, that one then began to call upon the name of the Lord, but rather the name of the devil, since he is called upon by idolaters, even if they do not know it. Yet St. Jerome says: Most of the Jews think that then for the first time idols were fashioned in the name and likeness of the Lord. On this some say, and it is touched on in the Scholastic History, that this Enos devised and made images to the honour of God, and to stir up the sluggishness of human memory, not that he might worship them. Yet from this, as is said, certain others took occasion of error. But it was said above, and Thomas testifies in the Secunda Secundæ [the second part of the second part of his Summa], that in the first age of the world there was no idolatry, but the knowledge of the one God alone, from the fresh memory of the creation of the world.

paras.t: Circa præhabita Josephus scribit : Seth ad ætatem discretionis perveniens, virtutibus studuit ; et quum esset vir egregius, imitatores sui filios dereliquit, qui disciplinam rerum cœlestium, et ornamentum earum primitus invenerunt : et ne perirent quæ invenerunt, quum prædixisset Adam exterminationem omnium rerum, unam per ignem, aliam per aquam, fecerunt duas columnas, unam ex lateribus, aliam ex lapidibus, in ambabus quæ invenerant, conscribentes ; ut si constructa ex lateribus exterminaretur imbribus, lapidea permanens, præberet hominibus scripta cognoscere : quæ lapidea permanet hactenus in Syria.
paras.en: On the foregoing Josephus writes: Seth, coming to the age of discretion, applied himself to the virtues; and since he was an excellent man, he left sons who imitated him, who first discovered the learning of heavenly things and their order [ornamentum, Josephus's kosmos: the arrangement of the heavenly bodies]; and lest what they had discovered should perish, since Adam had foretold the destruction of all things, one by fire, the other by water, they made two pillars, one of bricks, the other of stones, writing on both what they had discovered; so that, if the one built of bricks were destroyed by the rains, the one of stone, remaining, might let men know what was written: which one of stone remains to this day in Syria.

4.title: Elucidatio spiritualis ac mystica ejusdem capituli
4.title_en: Spiritual and mystical explanation of the same chapter

paras.t: Adam cognovit uxorem suam. Per Adam intelligitur Christus; per Evam, primitiva illa Ecclesia ex Judaismo nata, quæ Christo adhuc corporaliter in mundo inter homines conversanti adhæsit. Hanc Christus cognovit, quando post suam ascensionem eidem Spiritum Sanctum misit, ejusque donis Ecclesiam illam exuberantissime fecundavit, ita quod tunc concepit et peperit Cain, hoc est, Judaicum populum spiritualiter regeneravit in Christo, quando in die sancto Pentecostes, beatissimus princeps Apostolorum Petrus tria millia, et paulo post quinque millia Judæorum convertit, atque quotidie plurimi Judæorum in omni Judæa, Galilæa, atque Samaria convertebantur ad Christum, et baptizabantur. Unde Ecclesia ista primitiva, tunc gratulans, dixit: Possedi hominem per Deum, hoc est, divina virtute subjeci Christo et mihi per fidem ac evangelicam legem populum istum Judaicum, qui comparatione gentilium, dignus erat homo vocari, hoc est rationalis, unum Deum colendo.
paras.en: [[4:1|Adam knew|Adam cognovit]] [[4:1|his wife|uxorem suam]]. By Adam is understood Christ; by Eve, that primitive Church born of Judaism, which cleaved to Christ while He still lived bodily in the world among men. Christ knew her when, after His ascension, He sent the Holy Ghost upon her, and made that Church most abundantly fruitful with His gifts, so that she then [[4:1|conceived and brought forth Cain|concepit et peperit Cain]]: that is, she spiritually regenerated the Jewish people in Christ, when on the holy day of Pentecost the most blessed prince of the Apostles, Peter, converted three thousand of the Jews[[Acts 2:41||]], and a little later five thousand[[Acts 4:4||]], and daily a great many of the Jews in all Judea, Galilee and Samaria were converted to Christ and baptized. Hence that primitive Church, rejoicing then, said: [[4:1|I have gotten a man through God|Possedi hominem per Deum]]; that is, by the power of God I have made this Jewish people subject to Christ and to myself through faith and the law of the Gospel, a people which, in comparison with the gentiles, was worthy to be called *man*, that is, rational, since it worshipped the one God.

paras.t: Rursus peperit fratrem ejus Abel. Per Abel intelligitur plebs gentilis, ad Christum per primitivam Ecclesiam illam conversa, cujus conversio cœpit in glorioso Cornelio centurione et congregatis cum eo, quos præfatus Archiapostolus Christo incorporavit, sicut in Actibus Apostolorum testatur: Vos, inquiens, scitis quomodo Deus primum elegit per os meum ex gentibus assumere populum nomini suo.
paras.en: Again, [[4:2|she brought forth his brother Abel|peperit fratrem ejus Abel]]. By Abel is understood the gentile people converted to Christ through that primitive Church, whose conversion began in the glorious centurion Cornelius and those gathered with him[[Acts 10:1||]], whom the aforesaid chief Apostle incorporated into Christ, as he testifies in the Acts of the Apostles: “You know,” he says, “how God first chose by my mouth to take from the Gentiles a people to his name”[[Acts 15:7||]] [Denis joins Peter's words at Acts 15:7 with those of James at Acts 15:14, “how God first visited to take of the Gentiles a people to his name”].

paras.t: Fuit autem Abel pastor ovium: id est, multi ex gentilitate conversi, facti sunt evangelicæ legis prædicatores, et aliorum prælati, fideliumque pastores, qui fideles sunt oves Christi, de quibus prædixit: Alias oves habeo quæ non sunt ex hoc ovili. Et Cain agricola: id est, conversi ex Judaismo, laboraverunt ut aliquos ex Synagoga, quæ erat ager ac vinea Dei, ad Christum converterent. Fuit quoque Abel pastor ovium, id est cultor simplicitatis ovinæ et innocentiæ. Cain autem agricola, id est cultor agri interioris, videlicet proprii cordis. Vel agricola fuit, quoniam multi ex Synagoga conversi, adhuc circa legalia observanda erant intenti, quemadmodum in Actibus Apostolorum sanctus Jacobus loquitur Paulo: Vides, frater, quot millia crediderunt in Judæis, et omnes æmulatores legis sunt.
paras.en: [[4:2|And Abel was a shepherd|Fuit autem Abel pastor ovium]]: that is, many converted from among the gentiles were made preachers of the law of the Gospel, and prelates over others, and shepherds of the faithful, who are the sheep of Christ, of whom He foretold: [[John 10:16|other sheep I have that are not of this fold|Alias oves habeo quæ non sunt ex hoc ovili]]. [[4:2|and Cain a husbandman|Et Cain agricola]]: that is, those converted from Judaism laboured to convert to Christ some from the Synagogue, which was the field and vineyard of God. Again, [[4:2|Abel was a shepherd|Fuit quoque Abel pastor ovium]], that is, one who cultivated the simplicity and innocence of sheep; [[4:2|Cain a husbandman|Cain autem agricola]], that is, one who tilled the inner field, namely his own heart. Or he was a husbandman because many converted from the Synagogue were still intent on keeping the observances of the law, as St James says to Paul in the Acts of the Apostles: [[Acts 21:20|Thou seest, brother, how many thousands|Vides, frater, quot millia]] [[Acts 21:20|among the Jews that have believed: and they are all zealous for the law|crediderunt in Judæis, et omnes æmulatores legis sunt]].

paras.t: Factum est autem post multos dies, ut offerret Cain de fructibus terræ munera Domino: hoc est, multi ex Judæis conversis adhuc obtulerunt Deo carnalia sacrificia legis.
paras.en: [[4:3|And it came to pass after many days, that Cain offered, of the fruits of the earth, gifts to the Lord|Factum est autem post multos dies, ut offerret Cain de fructibus terræ munera Domino]]: that is, many of the converted Jews still offered to God the carnal sacrifices of the law.

paras.t: Abel quoque obtulit de primogenitis gregis sui et de adipibus eorum: id est, plebs ex gentilitate conversa, et aliis præsidens, multos excellentiores ex gregibus sibi commissis, induxit ad hoc, quod per palmam martyrii se ipsos Domino devotissime obtulerunt. Rursus, Abel seu populus iste christifidelis, obtulit Deo primogenita gregis sui, id est, quidquid in virtutibus et actibus suis virtuosis præcipuum fuit, divinæ pietati et gratiæ Dei, non viribus suis, adscripsit. Et de adipibus, id est, spirituali fervore et opulentia divinorum charismatum obtulit Deo sacrificium laudis et observantiam mandatorum: siquidem sacrificium salutare, respicere in mandatis. Et Dominus ait: Sacrificium laudis honorificabit me.
paras.en: [[4:4|Abel also offered of the firstlings of his flock, and of their fat|Abel quoque obtulit de primogenitis gregis sui et de adipibus eorum]]: that is, the people converted from among the gentiles, set over others, led many of the more excellent from the flocks entrusted to them to offer themselves most devoutly to the Lord by the palm of martyrdom. Again, Abel, or that Christian people, offered to God the firstlings of his flock: that is, whatever was foremost in its virtues and virtuous acts it ascribed to the divine goodness and the grace of God, not to its own strength. And of the fat: that is, with spiritual fervour and a wealth of divine gifts it offered to God the sacrifice of praise and the keeping of the commandments; for indeed [[Ecclus 35:2|it is a wholesome sacrifice to take heed to the commandments|sacrificium salutare, respicere in mandatis]]. And the Lord says: [[Ps 49:23|The sacrifice of praise shall glorify me|Sacrificium laudis honorificabit me]].

paras.t: Et respexit Dominus ad Abel et ad munera ejus: quoniam plebs ista christifidelis ex gentilitate electa, fuit acceptissima Deo in se et in actibus ac sacrificiis suis sanctis.
paras.en: [[4:4|and the Lord had respect to Abel, and to his offerings|Et respexit Dominus ad Abel et ad munera ejus]]: for that Christian people, chosen from among the gentiles, was most acceptable to God in itself and in its holy acts and sacrifices.

paras.t: […] Cain vero et ad munera illius non respexit. Hoc intelligendum est de Judæis illis conversis, qui tandem pertinaciter asseruerunt legalia simul cum Evangelio esse servanda: qui hæretici facti, Deo displicuerunt cum sacrificiis suis. Ideo populus iste […] et concidit vultus ejus. Ut enim in Actibus legitur, quidam de hæresi Pharisæorum eorum qui crediderant, surrexerunt, dicentes: Quia oportet circumcidi, et servare legem Moysis, quod etiam alii multi ex Judæis conversis dixerunt: sicut ibidem habetur: Descendentes quidam a Judæa Antiochiam, docebant fratres, quia nisi circumcidamini, non potestis salvi fieri. Quum autem Apostoli cum consilio suo determinassent oppositum, irati sunt illi. Hinc Dominus ait de populis istis Malachiæ: Non est mihi voluntas in vobis, et munus non suscipiam de manu vestra: Ab ortu enim solis usque ad occasum, magnum est nomen meum in gentibus, et in omni loco sacrificatur et offertur nomini meo oblatio munda. Quod ad litteram dictum est de Sacramento, sacrificioque altaris.
paras.en: […] [[4:5|to Cain and his offerings he had no respect|Cain vero et ad munera illius non respexit]]. This is to be understood of those converted Jews who in the end stubbornly maintained that the observances of the law were to be kept together with the Gospel: having become heretics, they displeased God with their sacrifices. Therefore that people […] [[4:5|and his countenance fell|et concidit vultus ejus]]. For, as we read in the Acts, certain of the sect of the Pharisees, of those who had believed, rose up, saying: [[Acts 15:5|They must be circumcised|Quia oportet circumcidi]], and [[Acts 15:5|observe the law of Moses|servare legem Moysis]] [the margin note here cannot be read; the passage is Acts 15:5], which many others of the converted Jews said too, as is told in the same place: [[Acts 15:1|some, coming down from Judea|Descendentes quidam a Judæa]] to Antioch, [[Acts 15:1|taught the brethren: That, except you be circumcised|docebant fratres, quia nisi circumcidamini]], [[Acts 15:1|you cannot be saved|non potestis salvi fieri]]. And when the Apostles in their council had decided the contrary, these men were angry. Hence the Lord says of these peoples through Malachias: [[Mal 1:10|I have no pleasure in you|Non est mihi voluntas in vobis]], [[Mal 1:10|and I will not receive a gift of your hand|et munus non suscipiam de manu vestra]]: [[Mal 1:11|For from the rising of the sun even to the going down, my name is great among the Gentiles, and in every place there is sacrifice, and there is offered to my name a clean oblation|Ab ortu enim solis usque ad occasum, magnum est nomen meum in gentibus, et in omni loco sacrificatur et offertur nomini meo oblatio munda]]. This was said, in its literal sense, of the Sacrament and sacrifice of the altar.

paras.t: Dixitque Dominus ad eum: Quare iratus es? Sic Dominus per sanctos Apostolos increpavit et docuit Judæos illos, in suis erroribus pertinaces, quorum facies concidit, quando videbant omnem gratiam Dei a Synagoga ad Christifideles transferri, et gentiles sibi præferri ac præfulgere in donis Spiritus Sancti atque miraculis. Nonne si bene egeris, credendo et obtemperando apostolicis documentis. Vel, juxta Septuaginta, Nonne si recte offeras, recte autem non dividas, peccasti? Recte obtulerunt Judæi isti, quando tempore opportuno obtulerunt legalia: sed recte non diviserunt, dum sub tempore evangelicæ legis ac gratiæ asseruerunt cærimonialia legis præcepta oportere servari, etiam Evangelio divulgato, atque ab his qui ex gentibus erant conversi. Denique qui agit bonum ex genere, recte offert; sed non recte dividit, nisi cum discretione et debitis circumstantiis agat hoc, utpote loco et tempore congruo ac recta intentione, imo et exclusione vitiorum, ne prava bonis admisceantur. Propter quod dixit Apostolus: Rationabile obsequium vestrum. Et Deus per Jeremiam: Si separaveris pretiosum a vili, quasi os meum eris. Nisi istud impleverimus, culpabiles sumus, etiam si bona agere videamur.
paras.en: [[4:6|And the Lord said to him: Why art thou angry?|Dixitque Dominus ad eum: Quare iratus es?]] So the Lord, through the holy Apostles, rebuked and taught those Jews who were stubborn in their errors, whose face fell when they saw the whole grace of God being transferred from the Synagogue to the faithful of Christ, and the gentiles preferred to themselves and shining before them in the gifts of the Holy Ghost and in miracles. [[4:7|If thou do well, shalt thou not receive|Nonne si bene egeris]]: by believing and obeying the teachings of the Apostles. Or, according to the Seventy: “If thou offer rightly, but dost not rightly divide, hast thou not sinned?” Those Jews offered rightly when they offered the observances of the law at the fitting time; but they did not rightly divide, when in the time of the law of the Gospel and of grace they maintained that the ceremonial precepts of the law must be kept, even after the Gospel had been spread abroad, and kept even by those converted from the gentiles. Further, whoever does what is good in its kind [that is, an act good in its object, apart from its circumstances and intention] offers rightly; but he does not rightly divide unless he does it with discretion and with due circumstances, that is, in a fitting place and time and with a right intention, and indeed with vices shut out, lest evil be mixed with good. For this reason the Apostle said: [[Rom 12:1|your reasonable service|Rationabile obsequium vestrum]]. And God through Jeremias: If [[Jer 15:19|thou wilt separate the precious from the vile, thou shalt be as my mouth|separaveris pretiosum a vili, quasi os meum eris]]. Unless we fulfil this, we are blameworthy, even if we seem to do good.

paras.t: Sub te erit appetitus ejus, et tu dominaberis illius. Hoc loco edocemur a Domino, superare nosmetipsos ac proprio animo dominari, passionesque refrenare, et sensitivam partem rationi tenere subjectam, sicque omnia ponere sub ordine divini amoris. Regnum enim cælorum vim patitur, et violenti rapiunt illud.
paras.en: [[4:7|but the lust thereof shall be under thee|Sub te erit appetitus ejus]], [[4:7|and thou shalt have dominion over it|et tu dominaberis illius]]. In this place we are taught by the Lord to overcome ourselves and to rule our own mind, to curb the passions and keep the sensitive part [that is, the senses and the appetites that follow them] subject to reason, and so to set all things under the order of divine love. For [[Matt 11:12|the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent bear it away|Regnum enim cælorum vim patitur, et violenti rapiunt illud]].

paras.t: Dixitque Cain ad Abel fratrem suum: Egrediamur foras; id est, populus iste Judaicus credens et legalia servans, provocavit conversos ex gentibus ad disputationis conflictum. Quumque essent in agro sæculi hujus, consurrexit Cain adversus fratrem suum Abel, et interfecit eum. Quum enim Judæi non potuissent ratione et Scripturarum allegatione Catholicis prævalere, cœperunt eos corporaliter persequi ac necare. Et in hoc hæretici atque increduli fuerunt concordes, quamvis in aliis discordarent.
paras.en: [[4:8|And Cain said to Abel his brother: Let us go forth abroad|Dixitque Cain ad Abel fratrem suum: Egrediamur foras]]: that is, that Jewish people, believing and keeping the observances of the law, challenged those converted from the gentiles to a contest of disputation. [[4:8|And when they were in the field|Quumque essent in agro]] of this world, [[4:8|Cain rose up against his brother Abel, and slew him|consurrexit Cain adversus fratrem suum Abel, et interfecit eum]]. For when the Jews could not prevail over the Catholics by reason and by citing the Scriptures, they began to persecute them in the body and to kill them. And in this the heretics and the unbelievers were of one mind, though they disagreed in other things.

paras.t: Et ait Dominus ad Cain: Ubi est Abel frater tuus? Sic Dominus reprehendit persecutores fidelium, quorum sanguinem requirit et vindicat de persecutoribus eorumdem. Qui respondit: Nescio. Numquid custos fratris mei sum ego? Judæi namque persecutores Catholicorum in primitiva Ecclesia, non fatebantur se reos ab interfectione fidelium, nec arbitrabantur illorum curam pertinere ad se, sed potius reputabant se obsequium Deo præstare in persecutione et interfectione credentium, sicut Salvator prædixit: Venit hora, ut omnis qui interficit vos, arbitretur obsequium se præstare Deo.
paras.en: [[4:9|And the Lord said to Cain: Where is thy brother Abel?|Et ait Dominus ad Cain: Ubi est Abel frater tuus?]]? So the Lord rebukes the persecutors of the faithful, whose blood He requires and avenges of their persecutors[[Matt 23:34||]][[Matt 23:35||]]. [[4:9|And he answered: I know not: am I my brother's keeper?|Qui respondit: Nescio. Numquid custos fratris mei sum ego?]]? For the Jews who persecuted the Catholics in the primitive Church did not confess themselves guilty of killing the faithful, nor did they think that the care of them belonged to them; rather they reckoned that they were doing God a service in persecuting and killing the believers, as the Saviour foretold: [[John 16:2|the hour cometh, that whosoever killeth you will think that he doth a service to God|Venit hora, ut omnis qui interficit vos, arbitretur obsequium se præstare Deo]].

paras.t: Dixitque Dominus ad eum: Quid fecisti? Vox sanguinis fratris tui clamat ad me de terra. Hoc Dominus per prædicatores evangelicæ legis dixit illis perversis Judæis. Hinc enim in Apocalypsi habetur: Animæ interfectorum clamabant voce magna: Usquequo Domine, sanctus et verus, non judicas et non vindicas sanguinem nostrum de his qui habitant in terra? Denique istud generaliter accipi potest de omnibus injuste et inordinate occisis. Unde loquitur Isaias: Revelabit terra sanguinem suum, et non operiet ultra interfectos suos. Et sanctus Job ait: Terra, ne operias sanguinem meum.
paras.en: [[4:10|And he said|Dixitque]] the Lord [[4:10|to him: What hast thou done?|ad eum: Quid fecisti?]] [[4:10|the voice of thy brother's blood crieth to me from the earth|Vox sanguinis fratris tui clamat ad me de terra]]. This the Lord said to those perverse Jews through the preachers of the law of the Gospel. Hence we read in the Apocalypse: the souls of the slain [[Apoc 6:10|cried with a loud voice|clamabant voce magna]]: [[Apoc 6:10|How long, O Lord (Holy and True), dost thou not judge and revenge our blood on them that dwell on the earth?|Usquequo Domine, sanctus et verus, non judicas et non vindicas sanguinem nostrum de his qui habitant in terra?]]? Further, this can be taken generally of all who are slain unjustly and wrongfully. Hence Isaias says: [[Is 26:21|the earth shall disclose her blood, and shall cover her slain no more|Revelabit terra sanguinem suum, et non operiet ultra interfectos suos]]. And holy Job says: [[Job 16:19|O earth, cover not thou my blood|Terra, ne operias sanguinem meum]].

paras.t: Nunc igitur maledictus eris super terram. Hoc clare impletum est in Judæis illis perversis, qui ob persecutionem suam in Christum et ejus discipulos, temporaliter et æternaliter, corporaliter et spiritualiter a Deo et hominibus maledicti sunt: quia ut ait Apostolus, Ira Dei pervenit super eos usque in finem. De quibus locutus est Psalmista Deo: Effunde super eos iram tuam, et furor iræ tuæ comprehendat eos. Denique etiam in Alcorano Mahometi habetur, quod Judæi a Deo relicti sunt, eo quod Jesum non receperunt pro Christo eis promisso. Sarraceni quippe fatentur, quod Jesus Nazarenus sit Christus in lege et Prophetis promissus, ac summus Propheta, sed negant deitatem ipsius. Mahometus namque fuit instructus a Sergio monacho Nestoriano hæretico. Nestorius autem hæresiarcha et inimicus Dei, dixit Christum esse hominem purum.
paras.en: [[4:11|Now therefore cursed shalt thou be upon the earth|Nunc igitur maledictus eris super terram]]. This was plainly fulfilled in those perverse Jews who, for their persecution of Christ and His disciples, are cursed by God and by men, in time and in eternity, in body and in spirit; for, as the Apostle says, [[1 Thess 2:16|the wrath of God is come upon them to the end|Ira Dei pervenit super eos usque in finem]]. Of them the Psalmist spoke to God: [[Ps 68:25|Pour out thy indignation upon them: and let thy wrathful anger take hold of them|Effunde super eos iram tuam, et furor iræ tuæ comprehendat eos]]. Indeed, even in the Koran of Mahomet it is said that the Jews are forsaken by God because they did not receive Jesus as the Christ promised to them. For the Saracens confess that Jesus of Nazareth is the Christ promised in the law and the Prophets, and the greatest Prophet, but they deny His godhead. For Mahomet was instructed by Sergius, a Nestorian monk and heretic; and Nestorius, a heresiarch and enemy of God, said that Christ was a mere man.

paras.t: Quum operatus fueris eam, non dabit tibi fructus suos. Hoc fuit impletum in Judæis, quando propter impietatem suam in Christum, a Romanis vastati sunt, et terra eorum undique demolita. Spiritualius autem loquendo, quando terram suam, id est corpora sua, exercuerunt in observantiis legis, non recte credendo in Christum, corpora eorum nullum protulerunt fructum virtutum, sed putredinem vitiorum.
paras.en: [[4:12|When thou shalt till it, it shall not yield to thee its fruit|Quum operatus fueris eam, non dabit tibi fructus suos]]. This was fulfilled in the Jews when, for their impiety against Christ, they were laid waste by the Romans and their land was destroyed on every side. Speaking more spiritually: when they exercised their earth, that is, their bodies, in the observances of the law, not believing rightly in Christ, their bodies brought forth no fruit of virtues, but the rottenness of vices.

paras.t: Vagus et profugus eris super terram, seu gemens et tremens, secundum aliorum translationem. Nil certius isto. Judæi enim undique sunt dispersi, et dura captivitate premuntur, atque sub Christianorum adversariorum suorum tenentur imperio, sub quo gemunt et tremunt. Unde Danieli Gabriel angelus ait de ipsis: Non erit populus Christi qui eum negaturus est, et finis ejus vastitas, et usque ad finem perseverabit desolatio.
paras.en: [[4:12|a fugitive and a vagabond shalt thou be upon the earth|Vagus et profugus eris super terram]]; or, *groaning and trembling*, according to the translation of others [the Septuagint reads “groaning and trembling shalt thou be upon the earth”]. Nothing is more certain than this. For the Jews are scattered everywhere and weighed down by a hard captivity, and are held under the rule of the Christians, their adversaries, under which they groan and tremble. Hence the angel Gabriel says of them to Daniel: [[Dan 9:26|the people that shall deny him shall not be his|Non erit populus Christi qui eum negaturus est]] [Denis has “shall not be Christ's people”], [[Dan 9:26|and the end thereof shall be waste|et finis ejus vastitas]], [[Dan 9:27|and the desolation shall continue even to the consummation, and to the end|et usque ad finem perseverabit desolatio]] [the margin gives only Dan. ix, 26; this last clause is from v. 27].

paras.t: Dixitque Cain ad Dominum: Major est iniquitas mea, quam ut veniam merear. Hoc competit infideli populo Judæorum, qui licet se neget profugum a terra promissionis, et vagum per mundum propter Christi occisionem, et primitivæ Ecclesiæ persecutionem, fatetur tamen se perpetrasse crimen tam grande, ut veniam nequeant impetrare, ita quod liberentur ab ista captivitate. Verumtamen captivitatem suam populus iste deplorat, dicendo: Ecce ejicis me a facie terræ patrum meorum, et a facie tua abscondar. Sed inter hæc metuit mortem temporalem magis quam Dei offensam, et propriarum animarum interitum: ideo ait: Omnis qui invenerit me, occidet me.
paras.en: [[4:13|And Cain said to the Lord: My iniquity is greater than that I may deserve pardon|Dixitque Cain ad Dominum: Major est iniquitas mea, quam ut veniam merear]]. This fits the unbelieving people of the Jews, who, though it denies that it is a fugitive from the land of promise and a vagabond through the world on account of the slaying of Christ and the persecution of the primitive Church, yet confesses that it has committed so great a crime that they cannot obtain pardon so as to be freed from this captivity. Yet this people bewails its captivity, saying: [[4:14|Behold thou dost cast me out|Ecce ejicis me]] [[4:14|from the face of the earth|a facie terræ]] of my fathers, [[4:14|and from thy face I shall be hid|et a facie tua abscondar]]. But amid all this it fears temporal death more than offending God and the ruin of its own souls; therefore it says: [[4:14|every one therefore that findeth me, shall kill me|Omnis qui invenerit me, occidet me]].

paras.t: Dixitque ei Dominus: Nequaquam ita fiet, sed omnis qui occiderit Cain, septuplum punietur. Non enim vult Deus ut incredulus Judæorum populus penitus occidatur, nec quisquam eorum est occidendus, eo quod patres eorum Christum occiderunt, et persecuti sunt ejus primitivam Ecclesiam. Si tamen aliunde meruerint mortem, possunt occidi. Qui vero sine causa rationabili occiderit quemquam eorum, septuplum, id est, valde dure et perfecte punietur, tanquam homicida crudelis. Non enim est miseris et afflictis illis addenda afflictio sine causa idonea, sed pro eorum conversione orare debemus.
paras.en: [[4:15|And the Lord said to him: No, it shall not so be: but whosoever shall kill Cain, shall be punished sevenfold|Dixitque ei Dominus: Nequaquam ita fiet, sed omnis qui occiderit Cain, septuplum punietur]]. For God does not will that the unbelieving people of the Jews be killed off altogether, nor is any one of them to be killed because their fathers killed Christ and persecuted His primitive Church. But if on other grounds they have deserved death, they may be put to death. Whoever kills any of them without reasonable cause shall be punished sevenfold, that is, very severely and fully, as a cruel murderer. For affliction is not to be added to those wretched and afflicted men without a fitting cause; rather we ought to pray for their conversion[[Jas 5:16||]].

paras.t: Posuitque Dominus in Cain signum, id est in populo illo incredulo, ut non interficeret eum omnis qui invenisset eum. Hoc signum est prophetia per multos sanctos veteris Testamenti prænuntiata de reservatione Judæorum in vita usque in sæculi finem, ut ex eorum adspectu inducantur Christiani ad considerationem divinæ justitiæ, ad recordationem quoque passionis dominicæ, atque ad confirmationem fidei christianæ, quæ ex illorum tam diuturna derelictione clare probatur, ex quorum etiam libris probamus quæ credimus. Ideo scriptum est: Ne occidas eos, nequando obliviscantur populi mei.
paras.en: [[4:15|And the Lord set a mark upon Cain|Posuitque Dominus in Cain signum]], that is, upon that unbelieving people, [[4:15|that whosoever found him should not kill him|ut non interficeret eum omnis qui invenisset eum]]. This mark is the prophecy, foretold by many holy men of the Old Testament, that the Jews would be kept alive until the end of the world, so that by the sight of them Christians might be led to consider the justice of God, to call to mind the Lord's passion, and to be confirmed in the Christian faith, which is clearly proved by their being forsaken for so long, and from whose own books, too, we prove what we believe. Therefore it is written: [[Ps 58:12|slay them not, lest at any time my people forget|Ne occidas eos, nequando obliviscantur populi mei]] [the psalm's number in the margin cannot be read; the verse is Ps 58:12].

paras.t: […] Cain a facie Domini, id est a Deo ejectus ac derelictus populus ille habitavit profugus ad orientalem plagam Eden. Per Eden, intelligitur Ecclesia Christi: per orientalem plagam ejus, doctrina legis et Prophetarum, ex qua tanquam ex oriente, orta est lux sapientiæ salutaris universæ militanti Ecclesiæ. In hac itaque plaga habitavit ac habitat usque nunc perfidus populus Hebræorum, in quantum aliqualem habent cognitionem Scripturarum illarum, atque in ea quotidie student, Scripturasque illas habent et veras credunt. Porro ejectionem ipsius Cain repræsentat Ecclesia, sanguinarios excommunicando, præcipue cum candelis accensis, quoniam vitam hominum exstinxerunt.
paras.en: […] [[4:16|Cain went out from the face of the Lord|Cain a facie Domini]], that is, that people, cast out and forsaken by God, [[4:16|dwelt as a fugitive on the earth at the east side of Eden|habitavit profugus ad orientalem plagam Eden]]. By Eden is understood the Church of Christ; by its eastern side, the teaching of the law and the Prophets, from which, as from the east, the light of saving wisdom has risen upon the whole Church militant. In this side, then, the faithless people of the Hebrews has dwelt and dwells until now, inasmuch as they have some knowledge of those Scriptures and study in them daily, and possess those Scriptures and believe them true. Further, the casting out of Cain is represented by the Church when she excommunicates men of blood, especially with lighted candles [which are put out at the end of the rite], since they have put out the life of men.

paras.t: Præterea omnis qui per mortale peccatum a facie Dei egreditur, mentem suam avertendo a Creatore, habitat profugus a mystica unitate Ecclesiæ, vagus quoque instabilisque in terra, quantum ad corpus diaboli pertinet: et corde instabiles sunt, passionibusque subduntur, et undique evagantur a Deo iniqui. In circuitu etenim impii ambulant, qui sunt tanquam mare fervens, quod non potest quiescere, et tanquam pulvis quem projicit ventus a facie terræ.
