paras.t: Et paulo post addit Origenes : Quantum ad necessitatem pluviarum atque diluvii spectat, nulla poterat tam conveniens et congrua forma arcæ dari, quam ut e summo velut ex tecto quodam in angustum culmen educto diffunderet imbrem cadentem, et per ima in aquis quadrata stabilitate consistens, nec impulsu ventorum, nec impetu fluctuum, nec inquietudine animalium, quæ intrinsecus erant, inclinari posset aut mer[…] Hæc consonare videtur quod ait Meninus, et habetur in Glossa : Congrue arca in summo, velut tecto quodam angusto, cacuminata est, ut imbrium ruinas diffunderet.
paras.en: And a little after Origen adds: As far as the need of the rains and of the flood is concerned, no shape could have been given to the ark so suitable and fitting as this: that from the top, as from a roof drawn up to a narrow ridge, it should shed the falling rain, and that, standing below in the waters with the steadiness of a square, it could not be tipped over by the thrust of the winds, nor by the force of the waves, nor by the restlessness of the animals that were within, nor sunk […] [the Latin breaks off at *mer…*, plainly *mergi*, ‘be sunk’; what follows is lost]. With this seems to agree what Meninus says, which is found in the Gloss: Fittingly the ark was brought to a peak at the top, as by a narrow roof, so as to shed the downpour of the rains.

paras.t: Verumtamen Hugo de S. Victore in libro de Arca Noe, verba Origenis sic objicit : Sententiæ Origenis plura refragari videntur. Primo, quia hæc forma quam assignat, non videtur ad natandum esse idonea. Constat namque arcam tam magnam, tot animalibus cibariisque onustam, non potuisse supernatare, venientibus aquis, quin pro magna parte sui premeretur deorsum in aquis, ut docet experientia in navibus onera magna gestantibus. Si ergo arca statim ab imo contrahi cœpit, ita ut latera ejus hinc inde se inclinantia non repellerent, sed reciperent fluctus intumescentes, et non tam aqua arcam, quam arca aquam portaret, quomodo fieri poterat, ut non tota statim ad ima descenderet ? Rursum, quum Dominus dicit, Pones ostium in latere deorsum, per latus deorsum, videtur significare parietem lateralem, ad differentiam lateris quod sursum erat in tecto, in quo fortassis fenestra posita erat ; et quum iterum infra dicitur, Aperuit Noe tectum arcæ, satis consequenter innuit, ipsam arcam deorsum habuisse parietes, quibus superpositum fuit tectum, quod erat contiguum supremæ mansioni in qua homines erant. Propter has et hujusmodi alias causas, videtur nobis quod in arca parietes erant erecti in quatuor partibus, in quibus tectum superpositum in cacumine suo contrahebatur ad cubiti unius mensuram. Hæc Hugo.
paras.en: Hugh of St Victor, however, in his book on the Ark of Noe, objects to Origen's words thus: Many things seem to tell against Origen's opinion. First, that this shape which he gives does not seem fit for floating. For it is plain that an ark so great, laden with so many animals and so much food, could not have floated on the coming waters without being pressed down into the water for a great part of itself, as experience teaches in ships that carry great loads. If, then, the ark began to draw in at once from the bottom, so that its sides, leaning inward on either hand, did not thrust back the swelling waves but took them in, and the ark bore the water rather than the water the ark, how could it be that the whole of it did not at once go to the bottom? Again, when the Lord says, [[6:16|the door of the ark thou shalt set in the side|Pones ostium in latere deorsum]] [Hugh reads *in latere deorsum*, ‘in the side below’; the Douay-Rheims takes *deorsum* with the chambers that follow, ‘with lower, middle chambers’], by the side below he seems to mean a side wall, as distinct from the side which was above, in the roof, in which perhaps the window was placed; and when it is said again further on, [[Gen 8:13|Noe opening the covering of the ark|Aperuit Noe tectum arcæ]] [the margin gives Gen. viii, 6, where Noe opens the window; the covering is opened at Gen 8:13], it implies, consistently enough, that the ark itself had walls below, on which was set the roof [*tectum*, the Douay-Rheims' ‘covering’], which was next to the uppermost room, in which the men were. For these and other causes of this kind it seems to us that in the ark walls were raised on the four sides, and the roof set on them was drawn in at its peak to the measure of one cubit. Thus far Hugh.

paras.t: Qui iterum ait : In parietibus hujus arcæ foris facti erant nidi sive mansiunculæ quasi affixi ad ipsos parietes, quorum nidorum aditus seu introitus patebat extrinsecus, ipso pariete intus integro permanente, erantque facti hi nidi pro bestiis, quæ nec semper in aqua, nec semper in arida degere possunt, ut sunt luter, vituli quoque marini.
paras.en: He says again: On the walls of this ark, on the outside, there were made nests or little rooms [*mansiunculæ*, the word of v. 14], fixed as it were to the walls themselves, whose openings or entrances lay open to the outside, the wall itself remaining whole within; and these nests were made for the beasts which can live neither always in the water nor always on dry land, such as the otter, and seals too [*vituli marini*, ‘sea-calves’].

paras.t: Præterea Hugo scribit de ista materia alia quædam, quæ vel stare non possunt, vel ego non intelligo ea, quod facilius concedi potest. Etenim ait : Cujus altitudinis fuerint parietes arcæ, non dicit auctoritas : sed quantum conjicimus, altitudo parietum usque ad fundum quartæ mansionis extendebatur. Quomodo verum est hoc ? Si verum est quod superius dixit, tectum fuisse supremæ mansioni contiguum, parietes namque extendebantur usque ad tectum, ergo altitudo parietum pertingebat usque ad quintam mansionem. Deinde ait : Si quæratur, an æqualis fuit altitudo singularum mansionum, an non, nos ex auctoritate probare non possumus. Interim vero quod auctoritati non exstat contrarium, postulamus nobis concedi. Volumus enim sic distinguere, ut primæ mansioni demus in altitudine quatuor cubitos, secundæ quinque, tertiæ sex, quartæ septem, quintæ et supremæ octo. Et sic altitudo parietum habuit quindecim cubitos, et totidem altitudo tecti. Istud non videtur, quia secundum hoc quarta et quinta mansiones fuissent sub tecto. Secundum expositores autem omnes mansiones erant infra tectum, prout in figuris arcæ, quæ secundum duplicem expositionem dupliciter pingitur, describitur. Denique, si tectum fuisset tantæ altitudinis sicut parietes, capacitas seu spatium intra arcam, fuisset per hoc multum minoratum. Rursus, præhabitum est, quod secundum expositionem, quæ textui et præsertim Septuaginta translationi consonantior est, mansio tertia, quarta et quinta, fuerunt æque altæ, quoniam locus in quo erant situatæ, fuit tricameratus per transversum.
paras.en: Hugh also writes on this matter certain other things which either cannot stand, or else I do not understand them, which is the easier to grant. For he says: Of what height the walls of the ark were, authority does not say; but as far as we can guess, the height of the walls reached up to the floor of the fourth room. How is this true? If what he said above is true, that the roof was next to the uppermost room, then, since the walls reached up to the roof, the height of the walls reached up to the fifth room. Then he says: If it is asked whether the height of the several rooms was equal or not, we cannot prove it from authority; but meanwhile we ask that what is not contrary to authority be granted us. For we wish to divide it thus: to give the first room four cubits in height, the second five, the third six, the fourth seven, the fifth and uppermost eight. And so the height of the walls was fifteen cubits, and the height of the roof as many. This does not seem right, because on this reckoning the fourth and fifth rooms would have been under the roof [that is, within the sloping roof itself]. But according to the expositors all the rooms were below the roof, as is shown in the pictures of the ark, which is painted in two ways according to the twofold exposition. Lastly, if the roof had been as high as the walls, the capacity or space within the ark would have been much lessened by it. Again, it was said before that, according to the exposition that agrees better with the text and especially with the Septuagint translation, the third, fourth and fifth rooms were of equal height, since the place in which they stood was divided crosswise into three chambers [*tricameratus*, ‘three-chambered’; compare the *tristega*, ‘third stories’, of v. 16].

paras.t: Præterea his quæ Hugo dixit de nidis, consonat quod ait Glossa : quæ in aqua et terra communiter vivunt, sicut lutri, vitulique marini, extra arcam habebant loculos præparatos, in quibus recipi poterant velut in arida. De avibus quoque marinis et fluvialibus idem dicendum est. Hæc Glossa, quæ et Augustino adscribitur.
paras.en: Further, with what Hugh said of the nests agrees what the Gloss says: The creatures that live in water and on land alike, such as otters and seals, had little places made ready outside the ark, in which they could be received as on dry land. The same is to be said of sea birds and river birds. Thus the Gloss, which is also ascribed to Augustine.

paras.t: Amplius circa istud. Trecentorum cubitorum erat longitudo arcæ, scribit Lyra : Aliqui dicunt, quod cubiti isti fuerunt geometrici. Sed tunc occurrit dubium, qualiter ædificium tantæ magnitudinis fieri poterat. Hebræi autem dicunt, quod erant cubiti usuales. Sed dubium tunc occurrit, quomodo tot animalia et cibaria poterant contineri in arca. Istud tamen dubium videtur mihi minus quam primum. Hæc Lyra. Sed sicut ex verbis Augustini jam patuit, minor est difficultas dubii illius prioris. Sciendum quoque, quod aliqui dicunt arcam habuisse triginta cubitos in altitudine infra tectum seu præter altitudinem tecti. Unde in Scholastica historia dicitur, quod arca dicitur habuisse triginta cubitos in altitudine, intelligendum est in corpore ejus, id est, a fundo usque ad tabulatum. Impossibile enim esset, operturam ejus non plus ascendisse, et ligna triginta cubitorum tantam longitudinem ac latitudinem operire. Verumtamen verbum hoc satis obscurum videtur.
paras.en: Further on this. On the words [[6:15|The length of the ark shall be three hundred cubits|Trecentorum cubitorum erat longitudo arcæ]], Lyra writes: Some say that these cubits were geometrical. But then the doubt arises how a building of such size could have been made. The Hebrews, however, say that they were ordinary cubits. But then the doubt arises how so many animals and so much food could be held in the ark. Yet this doubt seems to me smaller than the first. Thus far Lyra. But, as has already appeared from Augustine's words, the difficulty of that earlier doubt is the smaller. It should be known too that some say the ark had thirty cubits in height below the roof, that is, not counting the height of the roof. Hence it is said in the Scholastic History that where the ark is said to have had thirty cubits in height, this is to be understood of its body, that is, from the bottom up to the deck [*tabulatum*, the boarding on which the roof rested]. For it would be impossible that its covering rose no higher, and that timbers of thirty cubits should cover so great a length and breadth. Yet this saying seems rather obscure.

paras.t: Circa præhabita quæritur primo, cur Scriptura ista nil dicat de loco ad quem superfluitates animalium descenderunt. Secundo, an animalia quibus naturale est carnibus vesci, vescebantur eis in arca. Tertio, an animalia commiscebantur in arca. Quarto, an absolute de universis animalium speciebus fuerint ibi individua aliqua. Quinto de potu animalium, quando fuerunt in arca, et quis proposuit eis quotidie necessaria vitæ. Sexto, qualiter devenerunt ad Noe, et quomodo ingressa sunt arcam.
paras.en: On what has been said, it is asked, first, why this Scripture says nothing of the place to which the animals' waste went down. Second, whether the animals whose nature it is to eat flesh ate it in the ark. Third, whether the animals mated in the ark. Fourth, whether there were there some individuals of absolutely every species of animal. Fifth, of the animals' drink while they were in the ark, and who set before them each day what they needed for life. Sixth, how they came to Noe, and how they went into the ark.

paras.t: Ad primum horum Origenes respondet : Opportune siluit Scriptura de loco ad fimum animalium reservato, quia de hoc sufficienter docuit ipsius consequentiæ ratio, id est, ex his quæ de animalium mansionibus cibariisque scribuntur, satis consequens fuit ac evidens, quod inferius fuit hujusmodi locus. Et quia ad spiritualem intelligentiam minus digne poterat coaptari, merito ergo Scriptura siluit inde : quia hoc ipsum, quod scilicet siluit inde, rationes suas magis adaptat intellectibus allegoricis.
paras.en: To the first of these Origen replies: Scripture fittingly kept silence about the place set aside for the animals' dung, because the reasoning of what follows taught enough about it; that is, from what is written of the animals' rooms and their food it followed clearly and plainly enough that such a place was the lowest. And since it could not so becomingly be fitted to the spiritual understanding, Scripture was right, then, to keep silence about it: for this very thing, namely that it kept silence about it, suits its reasons the better to the allegorical senses.

paras.t: Ad secundum quoque Origenes sic ait: Necessarium videbatur, ut his bestiis, quibus natura dedit carnibus vesci, introducta sint extrinsecus animalia, quorum vescentes carnibus, conservare vitam valeant gratia reparandæ posteritatis. Aliis vero alia servarentur alimenta, quæ naturalis usus deposcit. Porro Augustinus de hoc aliter sentit, dicendo: Solet quosdam movere quæstio de generibus escarum, quæ ibi habere poterant animalia, quæ non nisi carnibus vesci putantur: utrum animalia quibus vescerentur, erant ibi ultra numerum in Scriptura taxatum sine transgressione præcepti, an quod magis credendum est, potuerunt ibi esse præter carnes aliqua alia alimenta, quæ omnibus communia exsistant. Novimus enim quam multa animalia, quibus caro cibus est, quæ pomis frugibusque vescuntur, et maxime fico atque castaneis. Quid ergo mirum, si Noe vir justus et sapiens, cuique animalium generi aptam alimoniam sine carnibus præparavit atque recondidit? Quid est autem quo vesci non cogeret fames? Aut quid non suave ac salubre facere posset Deus? Qui etiam dedisset illis faciliter vivere sine cibis, nisi conveniret impletioni figuræ tanti mysterii, ut pascerentur. Hæc Augustinus. Et istud verius reor. Quæ enim in arca erant, fuerunt (ut apparet) assecurata a morte quamdiu manebant in ea. Hinc Glossa, itemque Scholastica historia istud sequuntur.
paras.en: To the second, too, Origen speaks thus: It seemed necessary that for those beasts to which nature has given to eat flesh, animals should be brought in from outside, by eating whose flesh they could preserve their life for the sake of restoring their posterity; while for the others other foods were kept, such as natural use demands. Augustine, however, thinks otherwise of this, saying: Some are wont to be troubled by the question of the kinds of food which those animals could have there that are thought to eat nothing but flesh: whether animals for them to eat were there beyond the number fixed in Scripture, without transgression of the command, or, as is rather to be believed, there could be there, besides flesh, some other foods common to all. For we know how many animals whose food is flesh also eat fruit and grain, and especially figs and chestnuts. What wonder, then, if Noe, a just and wise man, prepared and stored up for each kind of animal suitable nourishment without flesh? And what is there that hunger would not drive them to eat? Or what could God not make sweet and wholesome? He who would even have granted them to live easily without food, had it not suited the fulfilment of the figure of so great a mystery that they should be fed. Thus far Augustine. And this I think the truer view. For the creatures that were in the ark were (as it appears) made safe from death as long as they remained in it. Hence the Gloss, and likewise the Scholastic History, follow this view.

paras.t: Ad tertium Andreas expositor et alii quidam dicunt, quod bruta prolificabant in arca. Alii dicunt, quod propter generalem mundi afflictionem et desolationem non fuit tunc tempus voluptuosæ commixtionis, quoniam Dominus de ingressu in arcam loquens, seorsum nominavit viros, seorsumque feminas, quemadmodum in exordio sequentis capituli innotescit. Quasi diceret: Tempore tribulationis ab amplexibus est cessandum, prout in Scholastica habetur historia. Ad quod allegari potest, quod imminente subversione Ninivæ, rex et principes Ninivæ præceperunt ut homines et jumenta, boves et pecora non gustent quidquam nec pascantur, et aquam non bibant.
paras.en: To the third, Andrew the expositor [Andrew of St Victor] and certain others say that the beasts bred in the ark. Others say that, because of the general affliction and desolation of the world, it was then no time for pleasurable union, since the Lord, speaking of the entry into the ark, named the men apart and the women apart, as is made known at the beginning of the next chapter [the Lord's words in this order stand at v. 18 of this chapter, ‘thou and thy sons, and thy wife, and the wives of thy sons’; the next chapter repeats the order in the story, Gen 7:7]; as if he were saying: In a time of tribulation one must refrain from embraces, as is found in the Scholastic History. In support of this it may be alleged that when the overthrow of Ninive was at hand, the king and princes of Ninive commanded: [[Jon 3:7|Let neither men nor beasts, oxen, nor sheep taste anything: let them not feed, nor drink water|homines et jumenta, boves et pecora non gustent quidquam nec pascantur, et aquam non bibant]].

paras.t: Ad quartum Augustinus respondet: Quod autem scrupulosissime quæri solet de minutissimis bestiolis, non solum quales sunt mures et stelliones, verum etiam quales sunt locustæ, scarabei, muscæ ac pulices, annon fuerunt in numero majori in arca quam in textu taxatur. Sic admonendi sunt qui hoc quærunt, sic intelligendum esse quod Dominus ait, Quæ repunt super terram, ut necesse non fuerit conservari in arca, quæ in aquis vivere queunt, non solum mersa, ut pisces, verum etiam supernatantia, sicuti multæ aves. Deinde quum ait, Masculus et femina, profecto intelligitur quod ad reparandam speciem dicit hoc, ac per hoc non fuisse necesse, ut ibi essent ea quæ possunt sine concubitu de materiis aut rerum corruptionibus nasci. Aut si in arca fuerunt, sicut in domibus esse solent, potuerunt ibi esse absque omni numero definito ac certo. Aut si sacratissimum mysterium, quod agebatur tantæ rei figura et etiam facti veritate, aliter non posset impleri, nisi omnia ibi essent numero certo in textu expressa, quæ in aqua vivere nequeunt, non fuit hoc cura ipsius Noe, filiorumque ejus, sed Dei. Non ergo fuerunt in arca quæ sexu carent. Quædam vero de quibuslibet rebus sine concubitu ita nascuntur, ut postea concumbant ac generent, sicut muscæ. In aliis nil maris et feminæ est, sicut in apibus. Alia sic habent sexum, ut non habeant fetum, ut muli et mulæ, de quibus mirum est si fuerint in arca: quæ tamen fuerunt in arca, si hoc ad mysterium pertinebat; nam masculum habent et feminam.
paras.en: To the fourth Augustine replies: As for the question asked with the greatest scrupulousness about the tiniest little creatures, not only such as mice and lizards [*stelliones*, spotted lizards], but also such as locusts, beetles, flies and fleas, whether they were not in the ark in greater number than is fixed in the text: those who ask this are to be told that what the Lord says, [[6:20|every thing that creepeth on the earth|Quæ repunt super terram]], is to be so understood that there was no need to keep in the ark those that can live in the waters, not only those that live under the water, like fishes, but also those that float upon it, like many birds. Then, when he says, [[6:19|of the male sex, and the female|Masculus et femina]], it is certainly understood that he says this for the restoring of the species, and therefore that there was no need for those things to be there which can be born without mating from matter or from the corruption of things; or, if they were in the ark, as they are wont to be in houses, they could have been there without any fixed and definite number. Or, if the most sacred mystery that was being enacted, both by the figure of so great a thing and by the truth of the deed, could not be fulfilled otherwise than by all the creatures that cannot live in water being there in the definite number given in the text, this was not the care of Noe himself and his sons, but of God. Those, then, that lack sex were not in the ark. Some, however, are born of all sorts of things without mating, yet so that afterwards they mate and breed, like flies. In others there is nothing of male and female, as in bees. Others have sex, yet so as to bear no young, like mules, male and female: it is a wonder if these were in the ark; yet they were in the ark, if this belonged to the mystery, for they have male and female.

paras.t: Ad quintum dicendum, quod nomine cibi intelligitur sanctus Noe tam sibi ac suis, quam irrationalibus providisse de necessario potu. Qualiter autem brutis ministrabantur necessaria victui, determinate exponere reor difficile. Quomodo enim octo homines qui erant in arca, potuerunt tot brutis anteponere alimenta. Si autem supernaturale auxilium necessarium fuit, non defuit.
paras.en: To the fifth it must be said that under the name of food [the food of v. 21] holy Noe is understood to have provided the necessary drink both for himself and his own and for the beasts. But how the beasts were served with what they needed for living I think it hard to set out definitely. For how could the eight men who were in the ark set food before so many beasts? But if supernatural help was needed, it was not lacking.

paras.t: Ad sextum Augustinus respondet, quod non hominis actu, sed Dei nutu, omnia irrationalia illa, etiam aves, venerunt ad Noe, et ingressa sunt arcam sponte: quod angelico obsequio creditur factum, quemadmodum in exordio adducta sunt ad Adam in paradiso, ut videret quid vocaret ea.
paras.en: To the sixth Augustine replies that it was not by the act of man but at the bidding of God that all those beasts, the birds too, came to Noe and went into the ark of their own accord; which is believed to have been done by the service of angels, just as in the beginning they were brought to Adam in paradise, [[Gen 2:19|to see what he would call them|ut videret quid vocaret ea]].

6.title: Expositio spiritualis ejusdem capituli
6.title_en: Spiritual exposition of the same chapter

paras.t: Concorditer dicunt doctores, quod per Noe Dominus Jesus Christus signetur. Nec solum per Noe intelligitur Christus secundum quod homo, sed etiam ut est Deus. Quemadmodum enim totius humani generis post diluvium exsistentis, Noe exstat principium, sic Christus secundum quod Deus, est causale principium universorum quæ sunt et vivunt sub sole. Præterea per ætatem sexcentorum annorum, recte significatur æternitas Christi, propter numeri perfectionem. Quemadmodum ergo Noe quum esset quingentorum annorum, genuit Sem, Cham et Japhet, sic Christus in sua æternitate consistens, condidit tria hominum genera in hoc mundo, videlicet gentilem, qui fuit sub lege naturæ: Hebraicum, qui fuit sub lege scripta: christianum, qui est sub lege gratiæ.
paras.en: The doctors say with one accord that by Noe is signified the Lord Jesus Christ. And by Noe is understood Christ not only according as He is man, but also as He is God. For just as Noe stands as the beginning of the whole human race that existed after the flood, so Christ, according as He is God, is the causal principle of all things that are and live under the sun. Moreover, by the age of six hundred years the eternity of Christ is rightly signified, because of the perfection of the number. As, then, Noe, when he was five hundred years old, begot Sem, Cham and Japhet, so Christ, abiding in His eternity, founded three kinds of men in this world: namely the gentile, which was under the law of nature; the Hebrew, which was under the written law; and the Christian, which is under the law of grace.

paras.t: Quumque cœpissent homines multiplicari super terram, hoc est, ultra modum et solitum plurimi essent, quod videtur fuisse sub monarchia Romanorum, quando inaudita pax fuit in terra, præliisque cessantibus, homines quasi arena sunt multiplicati. Videntes filii Dei filias hominum quod essent pulchræ, acceperunt uxores sibi ex omnibus quas elegerant. Illis quippe temporibus temporali prosperitate undique arridente, etiam illi qui fuerunt boni in lege naturali aut scripta, carnales effecti sunt, id est, lascivis curiosisque juncti sunt feminis, propter quod Spiritus Sanctus recessit ab eis. Ex illorum quoque connubio geniti sunt gigantes, id est homines animosi, ambitiosi, et magni ac præpotentes in oculis suis, aut etiam in exterioribus rebus: quorum omnium pravitatem indesinentem, atque ad omnia scelera pronitatem considerans Dominus, quasi pœnitens quod illos fecisset: Delebo, inquit, hominem, id est, istos æterna morte damnabo, usque ad animantia, hoc est, homines rurales, brutales, indomitos, simul cum illis damnationi adjiciam.
paras.en: And when [[6:1|men began to be multiplied upon the earth|Quumque cœpissent homines multiplicari super terram]], that is, were very many, beyond measure and beyond what was usual; which seems to have been under the monarchy of the Romans, when there was an unheard-of peace on earth, and, wars ceasing, men were multiplied as the sand. [[6:2|The sons of God seeing the daughters of men, that they were fair, took to themselves wives of all which they chose|Videntes filii Dei filias hominum quod essent pulchræ, acceperunt uxores sibi ex omnibus quas elegerant]]. For in those times, when temporal prosperity smiled on every side, even those who had been good under the natural or the written law became carnal, that is, were joined to wanton and curious women; for which cause the Holy Ghost departed from them. Of their union too were born giants, that is, men high-spirited, ambitious, and great and mighty in their own eyes, or even in outward things. And the Lord, considering the unceasing depravity of them all and their proneness to every crime, as if repenting that He had made them, [[6:7|I will destroy|Delebo]], says he, [[6:7|man|hominem]], that is, I will condemn these to eternal death, [[6:7|even to beasts|usque ad animantia]], that is, men rustic, brutish and untamed I will cast into damnation together with them.

paras.t: Noe vero invenit gratiam coram Domino: id est, Christus acceptissimus fuit Patri æterno, imo Christus secundum naturam humanam plus placuit et carior fuit superbeatissimæ Trinitati, quam ceterorum universitas electorum. Et genuit tres filios. Per istos tres filios, quos genuit Christus adhuc inter homines conversans in terris, intelligi possunt tres ordines hominum quos convertit, videlicet ordo Apostolorum, chorus septuaginta duorum discipulorum, et reliquorum in eum credentium multitudo.
paras.en: [[6:8|But Noe found grace before the Lord|Noe vero invenit gratiam coram Domino]]: that is, Christ was most acceptable to the eternal Father; nay, Christ according to His human nature was more pleasing and dearer to the most blessed Trinity than the whole company of the other elect. [[6:10|And he begot three sons|Et genuit tres filios]]. By these three sons, whom Christ begot while He still dwelt among men on earth, may be understood the three orders of men whom He converted: namely the order of the Apostles, the company of the seventy-two disciples, and the multitude of the rest who believed in Him.

paras.t: Quumque vidisset Deus terram esse corruptam, omnis quippe caro corruperat viam suam super terram. Tunc enim vitia carnalia ac spiritualia, præsertim idololatria, vehementissime invaluerunt, imo et scelera contra naturam in multis. Dixit ad Noe, id est ad Christum: Finis universæ carnis venit coram me, id est, reproborum carnalium horum iniquitates non feram diutius, sed disperdam eos cum terra, hoc est cum operibus suis carnalibus ac terrenis: secundum quod Deus in veteri Testamento per Prophetas prædixit de populo Judæorum, aliisque diversis linguis ac gentibus. Unde Jeremias ait Judæis: Non poterat vos Dominus ultra sustinere propter malitiam studiorum vestrorum. Nempe ut in libro de Doctrina christiana loquitur Augustinus, Deus a quolibet peccatore dignatur certum aliquod pondus seu certam mensuram excessuum tolerare: qua mensura impleta, non suffert diutius. Propter quod infra testatur: Nondum impletæ sunt iniquitates Amorrhæorum.
paras.en: [[6:12|And when God had seen that the earth was corrupted|Quumque vidisset Deus terram esse corruptam]], [[6:12|for all flesh had corrupted its way upon the earth|omnis quippe caro corruperat viam suam super terram]]. For then carnal and spiritual vices, idolatry above all, grew most violently strong; nay, in many even crimes against nature. [[6:13|He said to Noe|Dixit ad Noe]], that is, to Christ: [[6:13|The end of all flesh is come before me|Finis universæ carnis venit coram me]], that is, I will no longer bear the iniquities of these carnal reprobates, but [[6:13|I will destroy them with the earth|disperdam eos cum terra]], that is, with their carnal and earthly works: according as God in the Old Testament foretold through the Prophets of the people of the Jews, and of various other tongues and nations. Whence Jeremias says to the Jews: [[Jer 44:22|the Lord could no longer bear, because of the evil of your doings|Non poterat vos Dominus ultra sustinere propter malitiam studiorum vestrorum]]. For, as Augustine says in the book On Christian Doctrine, God deigns to bear from any sinner a certain weight or a certain measure of excesses; and when that measure is filled, He bears no longer. For which cause it is testified below: [[Gen 15:16|as yet the iniquities of the Amorrhites are not at the full|Nondum impletæ sunt iniquitates Amorrhæorum]].

paras.t: Fac tibi arcam de lignis lævigatis, id est, electos a me et vasa misericordiæ, converte per te ac tuos discipulos, atque ex eis Ecclesiam construe, extra quam nullus salvetur, ne totum hominum genus damnetur. Hinc de Christo Zacharias prædixit: Ecce vir, Oriens nomen ejus, et ædificabit templum Domino. De qua Ecclesia Christus fatetur: Erit unus pastor et unum ovile. Itemque: Nemo venit ad Patrem nisi per me. Hanc arcam Christus ædificavit, conjungendo electos per fidem et caritatem, sicque efficiendo ex eis unum mysticum corpus, cujus ipse est caput. Hinc enim ait: Supra hanc petram, id est fidei firmitatem, seu supra me ipsum, ædificabo Ecclesiam meam. Christus quippe non solum est caput Ecclesiæ, influendo fidelibus vitam gratiæ ac motum justæ conversationis, sed etiam fundamentum, cujus pietati et veritati innituntur fideles, et a quo fundantur et firmantur seu stabiliuntur in cognitione et gratia Dei. Unde protestatus est Paulus: Fundamentum aliud nemo ponere potest, præter id quod positum est, quod est Christus Jesus. Denique arca ista versatur et movetur in hoc mari magno, utpote in hoc sæculo nequam inter tribulationum et tentationum procellas, quibus sæpe agitantur fideles. Sed inter eas ipse Dominus omnium et Salvator, regit, dirigit, et conservat eamdem, atque ad portum salubris quietis gratiæ in præsenti, ac salutis æternæ gloriæ in futuro eam perducit. Et sicut exeuntes in arca Noe, per lignum arcæ et aquas diluvii sunt salvati a morte temporali: sic existentes in Ecclesia, per lignum crucis et aquas Baptismi salvantur a supplicio infernali. Ideo beatissimus princeps Apostolorum: In arca, inquit, octo animæ salvatæ sunt per aquam, sic et vos salvos facit similis formæ Baptismus. Est quoque Ecclesia ex lævigatis lignis, id est firmis et justis hominibus ædificata, qui recte vocantur ligna quadrata, polita, imputribilia, quum sint in æternum victuri, virtutibus decorati, atque in omni eventu constantes, et recti instar quadrati, quod quocumque projiciatur, stat firmiter et erectum.
paras.en: [[6:14|Make thee an ark of timber planks|Fac tibi arcam de lignis lævigatis]] [the Latin is *of smoothed timbers*, which Denis explains below], that is, convert through thyself and thy disciples those chosen by me, the vessels of mercy, and build of them the Church, outside which no one is saved, lest the whole race of men be damned. Hence Zacharias foretold of Christ: [[Zach 6:12|BEHOLD A MAN, THE ORIENT IS HIS NAME|Ecce vir, Oriens nomen ejus]], [[Zach 6:12|and shall build a temple to the Lord|et ædificabit templum Domino]]. Of which Church Christ declares: [[John 10:16|there shall be one fold and one shepherd|Erit unus pastor et unum ovile]]. And again: [[John 14:6|No man cometh to the Father, but by me|Nemo venit ad Patrem nisi per me]]. This ark Christ built by joining the elect together through faith and charity, and so making of them one mystical body, whose head He Himself is. Hence He says: [[Matt 16:18|upon this rock|Supra hanc petram]], that is, the firmness of faith, or upon myself, [[Matt 16:18|I will build my church|ædificabo Ecclesiam meam]]. For Christ is not only the head of the Church, pouring into the faithful the life of grace and the movement of a righteous life, but also its foundation, on whose mercy and truth the faithful rest, and by whom they are founded and made firm or established in the knowledge and grace of God. Whence Paul protested: [[1 Cor 3:11|other foundation no man can lay, but that which is laid: which is Christ Jesus|Fundamentum aliud nemo ponere potest, præter id quod positum est, quod est Christus Jesus]]. Lastly, this ark is tossed and driven about on this great sea, that is, in this wicked world, amid the storms of tribulations and temptations by which the faithful are often shaken. But amid them the Lord and Saviour of all Himself rules, directs and preserves it, and brings it to the haven of the wholesome rest of grace in the present, and of the eternal salvation of glory in the future. And as those who were in the ark of Noe were saved from temporal death by the wood of the ark and the waters of the flood, so those who are in the Church are saved from the punishment of hell by the wood of the cross and the waters of Baptism. Therefore the most blessed prince of the Apostles says: In the ark, [[1 Pet 3:20|eight souls, were saved by water|octo animæ salvatæ sunt per aquam]]; so [[1 Pet 3:21|baptism, being of the like form, now saveth you also|sic et vos salvos facit similis formæ Baptismus]]. The Church is also built of smoothed timbers, that is, of steadfast and just men, who are rightly called squared, polished, incorruptible timbers, since they are to live for ever, adorned with virtues, constant in every event, and upright like a square block, which, whichever way it is thrown, stands firm and erect.

paras.t: Mansiunculas in ea facies. Mansiunculæ istæ sunt particulares Ecclesiæ, diversæ quoque religiones et ordines. Item variæ distinctiones virtutum ac meritorum, et varia dona cœlestium gratiarum, in quibus requiescunt fideles. De quibus Dominus per Isaiam fatetur: Sedebit populus meus in pulchritudine pacis et in tabernaculis fiduciæ et in requie opulenta. Et rursus: Vade, populus meus, intra in cubicula tua, abscondere parumper donec transeat indignatio mea. His mansiunculis correspondent mansiones in patria, id est, diversi gradus præmiorum cœlestium, de quibus Salvator: In domo, inquit, Patris mei mansiones multæ sunt. Et bitumine linies eam intrinsecus et extrinsecus. Per bitumen quod ferventissime atque fortissime nectit, sancta caritas, qua nihil ferventius, nihil robustius, nilque indissolubilius colligat, designatur. Tunc ergo Ecclesia intus et extra linitur bitumine, quando fideles se corde et opere diligunt, dum omne quod agunt, ex Dei amore procedit, dum universi per dilectionem uniuntur in Deo, ita ut dicere queant, Quis nos separabit a caritate Dei? dumque solliciti sunt servare unitatem spiritus in vinculo pacis. Ideo Paulus hortatur: Super omnia caritatem habete, quod est vinculum perfectionis.
paras.en: [[6:14|thou shalt make little rooms in the ark|Mansiunculas in ea facies]]. These little rooms are the particular Churches, and also the various religious institutes and orders; likewise the various distinctions of virtues and merits, and the various gifts of heavenly graces, in which the faithful rest. Of these the Lord declares through Isaias: [[Is 32:18|my people shall sit in the beauty of peace, and in the tabernacles of confidence, and in wealthy rest|Sedebit populus meus in pulchritudine pacis et in tabernaculis fiduciæ et in requie opulenta]]. And again: [[Is 26:20|Go, my people, enter into thy chambers|Vade, populus meus, intra in cubicula tua]], [[Is 26:20|hide thyself a little for a moment, until the indignation pass away|abscondere parumper donec transeat indignatio mea]]. To these little rooms correspond the mansions in the fatherland, that is, the different degrees of heavenly rewards, of which the Saviour says: [[John 14:2|In my Father's house|In domo]], says he, [[John 14:2|there are many mansions|Patris mei mansiones multæ sunt]]. [[6:14|and thou shalt pitch it within and without|Et bitumine linies eam intrinsecus et extrinsecus]]. By pitch, which binds most fervently and most strongly, is signified holy charity, than which nothing binds more fervently, nothing more strongly, nothing more indissolubly. The Church, then, is pitched within and without when the faithful love one another in heart and in deed, when all that they do proceeds from the love of God, when all are united in God through love, so that they can say: Who [[Rom 8:35|shall separate us from the love|nos separabit a caritate]] of God? [Denis has *of God* where the Apostle here has *of Christ*], and while they are careful [[Eph 4:3|to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace|servare unitatem spiritus in vinculo pacis]]. Therefore Paul exhorts: [[Col 3:14|above all these things have charity, which is the bond of perfection|Super omnia caritatem habete, quod est vinculum perfectionis]].

paras.t: Et sic facies eam: Trecentorum cubitorum erit longitudo arcæ. Longitudo Ecclesiæ, est diurna atque longanimis spes Christifidelium, quæ trecentorum est cubitorum, id est perfectæ durationis ab exordio conversionis usque ad beatificum finem, ad omnes pertinens Christianos, fide Trinitatis superbeatissimæ insignitos. Universitas autem fidelium per centenarium designatur, dum Christus in Evangelio loquitur: Quis ex vobis homo qui habet centum oves, etc.? Quoniam ergo universitas ista ex summa Trinitate subsistit, longitudinemque dierum æternitatis sortitur, recte longitudo ipsius per centenarium triplicatum exprimitur. Quinquaginta cubitorum latitudo ejus. Per latitudinem intelligitur caritas ad omnia se extendens, quam oportet quinquaginta cubitorum consistere, utpote tantæ exsistentiæ ac vigoris, ut ad quinquagesimum annum remissionis omnium peccatorum, requiemque æternæ felicitatis, in qua omnia bona omissa, plenissime et supereminenter restituuntur, pertingat. Et triginta cubitorum altitudo illius. Altitudo Ecclesiæ est contemplatio fidei in hac vita, quæ per observantiam decem præceptorum pertingit ad beatificæ gloriam visionis. In qua quidquid hic promeremur, triplicatum recipimus, sicut Judex ipse testatur: Mensuram bonam et confertam et coagitatam et supereffluentem dabunt in sinum vestrum.
paras.en: [[6:15|And thus shalt thou make it|Et sic facies eam]]: [[6:15|The length of the ark shall be three hundred cubits|Trecentorum cubitorum erit longitudo arcæ]]. The length of the Church is the long-lasting and long-suffering hope of the faithful of Christ, which is of three hundred cubits, that is, of perfect duration from the beginning of conversion to the blessed end, belonging to all Christians, who are marked with faith in the most blessed Trinity. For the whole body of the faithful is signified by the number one hundred, when Christ says in the Gospel: [[Luke 15:4|What man of you that hath an hundred sheep|Quis ex vobis homo qui habet centum oves]], etc.? Since, then, this whole body has its being from the supreme Trinity, and is allotted length of days in eternity, its length is rightly expressed by the hundred tripled. [[6:15|the breadth of it fifty cubits|Quinquaginta cubitorum latitudo]]. By the breadth is understood charity extending itself to all things[[1 Cor 13:7||]], which must be of fifty cubits, that is, of such being and vigour that it reaches to the fiftieth year [that is, the year of jubilee, Lev 25:10] of the remission of all sins, and to the rest of eternal happiness, in which all good things given up are restored most fully and superabundantly. [[6:15|and the height of it thirty cubits|Et triginta cubitorum altitudo illius]]. The height of the Church is the contemplation of faith in this life, which through the observance of the ten commandments reaches to the glory of the beatific vision [thirty being ten tripled]. In that vision we receive tripled whatever we merit here, as the Judge Himself testifies: [[Luke 6:38|good measure and pressed down and shaken together and running over shall they give into your bosom|Mensuram bonam et confertam et coagitatam et supereffluentem dabunt in sinum vestrum]].

paras.t: Fenestram in arca facies. Per fenestram ipsa fides seu donum sapientiæ rite accipitur, per quam cœlestia intuemur, lumenque gratiæ et splendorem virtutum atque deinde claritatem luminis gloriæ obtinebimus. Et in uno cubito consummabis summitatem ejus, id est, vertex Ecclesiæ tantus erit, tam strictus et arduus, ut uni soli, videlicet Christo capiti Ecclesiæ, competat. Hic etenim vertex est suprema perfectio propria soli Christo. Ostium autem arcæ pones in latere deorsum. Ostium Ecclesiæ est ipsemet Christus, qui ait: Ego sum ostium ovium. Posuit autem se ipsum in latere Ecclesiæ deorsum, quia totius humilitatis præbuit se exemplum, et universis exhibuit se paratum, ita ut cunctis per eum pateret ingressus in sanctam Ecclesiam. Posuit quoque se in latere Ecclesiæ, applicando se pie non solum justis, sed etiam ceteris. Rursus ostium Ecclesiæ est fides, per quam primo in Ecclesiam fit ingressus, seu sacramentum Baptismi, qui est regeneratio spiritualis, ceterorumque janua sacramentorum, vel Pœnitentiæ sacramentum, quod est secunda post naufragium tabula, et primus post lapsum ingressus: quæ omnia omnibus patent tanquam in latere deorsum locata. Postremo ostium in latere deorsum, est vulnus lateri Christi infixum, de quo sacramenta profluxerunt Ecclesiæ. Cœnacula et tristega facies in ea. Cœnacula sunt officia prælatorum atque doctorum, quorum est corda multitudinis subditorum ac vulgi multiplici cibo spiritualiter reficere, sicut per Jeremiam asserit Deus: Dabo vobis pastores juxta cor meum, et pascent vos scientia et doctrina. Tristega sunt tres status ac gradus fidelium, utpote incipientium, proficientium, et perfectorum; seu virginum, viduarum, et conjugatorum. In quibus unusquisque juxta suæ vocationis exigentiam conquiescit.
paras.en: [[6:16|Thou shalt make a window in the ark|Fenestram in arca facies]]. By the window is fitly understood faith itself, or the gift of wisdom, through which we behold heavenly things, and shall obtain the light of grace and the splendour of the virtues, and then the brightness of the light of glory. [[6:16|and in a cubit shalt thou finish the top of it|Et in uno cubito consummabis summitatem ejus]], that is, the summit of the Church will be such, so narrow and so steep, that it befits one alone, namely Christ, the head of the Church. For this summit is the supreme perfection proper to Christ alone. [[6:16|and the door of the ark thou shalt set in the side|Ostium autem arcæ pones in latere]] below [Denis reads *in latere deorsum*, "in the side below", taking *deorsum* with the door; the margin gives the variant *ex latere*, "from the side"]. The door of the Church is Christ Himself, who says: [[John 10:7|I am the door of the sheep|Ego sum ostium ovium]]. And He set Himself in the side of the Church below, because He offered Himself as an example of all humility, and showed Himself ready for all, so that through Him entrance into holy Church lay open to all. He set Himself also in the side of the Church by kindly drawing near not only to the just but to the rest as well. Again, the door of the Church is faith, through which entrance is first made into the Church; or the sacrament of Baptism, which is spiritual regeneration and the gate of the other sacraments; or the sacrament of Penance, which is the second plank after shipwreck, and the first entrance after a fall: all of which lie open to all, as if placed in the side below. Lastly, the door in the side below is the wound driven into the side of Christ, from which the sacraments of the Church flowed forth. [[6:16|middle chambers, and third stories shalt thou make it|Cœnacula et tristega facies in ea]]. The middle chambers [*cœnacula*, properly dining rooms] are the offices of prelates and doctors, whose part it is to refresh spiritually with manifold food the hearts of the multitude of their subjects and of the common people, as God declares through Jeremias: [[Jer 3:15|I will give you pastors according to my own heart, and they shall feed you with knowledge and doctrine|Dabo vobis pastores juxta cor meum, et pascent vos scientia et doctrina]]. The third stories are the three states and degrees of the faithful, namely of beginners, of the proficient, and of the perfect; or of virgins, widows and the married; in which each one rests according to what his calling requires.

paras.t: Ecce ego adducam aquas diluvii super terram, et interficiam omnem carnem. Per diluvium illud intelligit spiritualiter Origenes futurum in fine mundi exterminium omnimodum terræ per ignem, quo omnia viventia in hac terra penitus exstinguentur.
paras.en: [[6:17|Behold, I will bring the waters of a great flood upon the earth|Ecce ego adducam aquas diluvii super terram]], [[6:17|to destroy all flesh|et interficiam omnem carnem]]. By that flood Origen understands spiritually the utter destruction of the earth by fire that is to come at the end of the world, by which all living things on this earth will be wholly extinguished.

paras.t: Ponamque fœdus meum tecum. Hoc est, fœdus summæ amicitiæ inter Patrem et Filium, de quo in Filii baptizatione et transfiguratione locutus est Pater: Tu es Filius meus dilectus. Et ingredieris arcam tu et filii tui, uxor tua et uxores filiorum tuorum tecum. Christus namque fuit in ipsa Ecclesia, quemadmodum ait ad Patrem: In medio Ecclesiæ laudabo te. Ad discipulos quoque: Ego, ait, in medio vestrum sum sicut qui ministrat. Filii autem Christi fuerunt ejus discipuli, de quibus per Isaiam testatur: Ecce ego et pueri mei quos dedit mihi Dominus. Uxor Christi, quæ cum ipso intravit Ecclesiam, est congregatio ex Judaismo ad evangelicam legem per Christum conversa. Uxores filiorum Christi, sunt particulares Ecclesiæ ab Apostolis et apostolicis viris conversæ, et bene rectæ, quæ omnes universalem introierunt Ecclesiam.
paras.en: [[6:18|And I will establish my covenant with thee|Ponamque fœdus meum tecum]]. That is, the covenant of supreme friendship between the Father and the Son, of which the Father spoke at the Son's baptism and transfiguration: [[Mark 1:11|Thou art my beloved Son|Tu es Filius meus dilectus]]. [[6:18|and thou shalt enter into the ark, thou and thy sons, and thy wife, and the wives of thy sons with thee|Et ingredieris arcam tu et filii tui, uxor tua et uxores filiorum tuorum tecum]]. For Christ was within the Church itself, as He says to the Father: [[Ps 21:23|in the midst of the church will I praise thee|In medio Ecclesiæ laudabo te]]. And to the disciples also: I, says he, [[Luke 22:27|am in the midst of you, as he that serveth|in medio vestrum sum sicut qui ministrat]]. The sons of Christ were His disciples, of whom He testifies through Isaias: [[Is 8:18|Behold I and my children, whom the Lord hath given me|Ecce ego et pueri mei quos dedit mihi Dominus]]. The wife of Christ, who entered the Church with Him, is the congregation converted by Christ from Judaism to the law of the Gospel. The wives of the sons of Christ are the particular Churches converted by the Apostles and apostolic men, and well ordered, all of which have entered the universal Church.

paras.t: Et ex cunctis animantibus universæ carnis bina induces in arcam, ut vivant tecum, masculini sexus et feminini, hoc est, ex omni genere hominum quosdam utriusque sexus convertes et tibi incorporabis, ut vivant tecum modo per gratiam, et in cœlis per gloriam.
paras.en: [[6:19|And of every living creature of all flesh, thou shalt bring two of a sort into the ark, that they may live with thee: of the male sex, and the female|Et ex cunctis animantibus universæ carnis bina induces in arcam, ut vivant tecum, masculini sexus et feminini]], that is, of every kind of men thou shalt convert some of either sex and incorporate them into thyself, that they may live with thee now through grace, and in heaven through glory.

paras.t: Tolles igitur tecum, ex omnibus escis quæ mandi possunt, id est, omni genere spiritualium ferculorum implebis Ecclesiam, scilicet sacramentis, scripturis, doctrinis, variisque donis et gratiis Spiritus Sancti, et actibus virtuosis. Et erunt tam tibi quam illis in escam, id est spiritualem refectionem. His etenim reficiuntur suaviter et vere salubriter mentes fidelium, quorum profectus et salus est refectio Salvatoris, cui quum incorporantur fideles, quasi comeduntur ab ipso, quando per conversionem ad ipsum, efficiuntur membra ipsius, quod per ignem caritatis peragitur.
paras.en: [[6:21|Thou shalt take unto thee of all food that may be eaten|Tolles igitur tecum, ex omnibus escis quæ mandi possunt]], that is, thou shalt fill the Church with every kind of spiritual dishes, namely with sacraments, scriptures, doctrines, and the various gifts and graces of the Holy Ghost, and with virtuous acts. [[6:21|and it shall be food for thee and them|Et erunt tam tibi quam illis in escam]], that is, spiritual refreshment. For by these the minds of the faithful are refreshed sweetly and truly wholesomely; and their progress and salvation is the refreshment of the Saviour, into whom, when the faithful are incorporated, they are as it were eaten by Him, when through conversion to Him they are made His members; which is done through the fire of charity.

paras.t: Fecit igitur Noe omnia quæ præceperat illi Deus: id est, Christus secundum naturam assumptam Patri per omnia obedivit, quemadmodum ait: Sicut mandatum dedit mihi Pater, sic facio.
paras.en: [[6:22|And Noe did all things which God commanded him|Fecit igitur Noe omnia quæ præceperat illi Deus]]: that is, Christ, according to the nature He assumed, obeyed the Father in all things, as He says: [[John 14:31|as the Father hath given me commandments, so do I|Sicut mandatum dedit mihi Pater, sic facio]].

paras.t: Insuper de hac spirituali expositione arcæ loquitur Augustinus: Mensura longitudinis, latitudinis et altitudinis arcæ, significat corpus humanum, in cujus veritate Christus venit ad homines. Longitudo quippe corporis humani a vertice usque ad vestigia, sexies tantum habet, quantum latitudo, quæ est ab uno latere ad aliud latus: et decies tantum, quantum altitudo, id est profunditas, cujus altitudinis mensura est a latere usque ad ventrem: ut si metiaris hominem jacentem supinum seu pronum, sexies tantum longus est a capite usque ad calcaneum, quam latus est a dextera in sinistram, seu a sinistra in dexteram: et decies tantum longus est, quantum altus a terra in qua jacet. Dicitur autem arca inferius bicamerata, quia ex Judæis et gentilibus est collecta, et continet illos in se; superius vero tricamerata propter fidem, spem et caritatem. Aut propter fructum centesimum, sexagesimum atque tricesimum. Vel propter tres filios Noe, ex quorum semine nati sunt omnes Ecclesiæ filii. Insuper quod ea quæ de arca sunt scripta, sunt spiritualiter de Ecclesia exponenda, probat ex hoc Augustinus, quod Deus jussit de animalibus mundis septena et septena duci in arcam: de immundis vero, bina et bina, quum tamen munda possent reparari per bina et bina, sicut immunda; et quoniam Deus potuit omnia reparare eo modo quo condidit ea. Hæc Augustinus.
paras.en: Moreover, Augustine speaks of this spiritual exposition of the ark: The measure of the length, breadth and height of the ark signifies the human body, in the reality of which Christ came to men. For the length of the human body, from the crown of the head to the soles of the feet, is six times its breadth, which is from one side to the other, and ten times its height, that is, its depth, the measure of which height is from the side to the belly: so that if you measure a man lying on his back or on his face, he is six times as long from head to heel as he is broad from right to left or from left to right, and ten times as long as he is high from the ground on which he lies. The ark is said to be of two chambers below, because it is gathered from Jews and gentiles and holds them within it; and of three chambers above because of faith, hope and charity. Or because of the fruit a hundredfold, sixtyfold and thirtyfold[[Matt 13:8||]] [the margin note here is unreadable; the reference is to the parable of the sower, Matt 13:8, 23]. Or because of the three sons of Noe, from whose seed all the sons of the Church are born. Moreover, Augustine proves that what is written of the ark is to be expounded spiritually of the Church from this: that God commanded the clean animals to be brought into the ark by sevens and sevens, but the unclean by twos and twos, although the clean could have been restored by twos and twos just as well as the unclean; and since God could have restored all things in the way in which He made them. Thus far Augustine.

paras.t: Præterea Gregorius dicit: Arca in inferioribus fuit lata, in superioribus vero angusta, atque in summitate sua ad unius cubiti mensuram pervenit. Inferius enim quadrupedia et reptilia, superius vero aves et homines creditur habuisse. Ibi lata, ubi bestiæ; ibi angusta, ubi homines erant. Hæc verba Gregorii, consonare videntur verbis Origenis supradictis de figura seu forma arcæ, quod ab imo forma cœperat contrahi. Deinde addit Gregorius: Arca in summis angustatur usque ad cubitum unum, quoniam in Ecclesia quanto aliqui fuerint sanctiores, tanto sunt pauciores, qui in summo perducuntur ad illum, qui solus sine comparatione natus est Sanctus in terra.
paras.en: Further, Gregory says: The ark was broad in its lower parts but narrow in its upper parts, and at its top came to the measure of one cubit. For below it is believed to have held the four-footed beasts and the creeping things, but above the birds and men. It was broad where the beasts were, narrow where the men were. These words of Gregory seem to agree with the words of Origen given above on the figure or shape of the ark, that from the bottom its shape began to narrow. Then Gregory adds: The ark narrows at the top to one cubit, because in the Church the holier some are, the fewer they are, who at the summit are brought to Him who alone, beyond compare, was born Holy on earth.

paras.t: Ait quoque Hugo de S. Victore: Trecentorum cubitorum longitudo designat sæculum præsens, quod tribus decurrit temporibus, scilicet tempore legis naturalis, tempore legis scriptæ, et tempore gratiæ, per quæ sancta Ecclesia a principio mundi tendit ad patriam. Quinquaginta cubitorum latitudo, universos fideles significat, qui sub uno capite Christo sunt constituti. Nam quinquaginta constant ex septies septem, qui numerus universitatem fidelium signat, uno adjuncto quod Christum significat, qui est caput Ecclesiæ et finis desideriorum nostrorum, propter quod arca in uno cubito consummatur. Porro altitudo cubitorum triginta designat triginta libros sacræ Scripturæ, videlicet viginti duos veteris Testamenti, et octo novi, in quibus summa omnium continetur, quæ propter Ecclesiam suam Deus fecit aut faciet. Centum anni quibus ædificata est arca, significant tempus gratiæ quo Ecclesia est formata. Hæc Hugo.
paras.en: Hugh of St. Victor also says: The length of three hundred cubits signifies the present world, which runs its course in three times, namely the time of the natural law, the time of the written law, and the time of grace, through which holy Church tends from the beginning of the world towards the fatherland. The breadth of fifty cubits signifies all the faithful, who are set under one head, Christ. For fifty is made up of seven times seven, a number which signifies the whole body of the faithful, with one added, which signifies Christ, who is the head of the Church and the end of our desires; for which reason the ark is finished in one cubit. Further, the height of thirty cubits signifies the thirty books of sacred Scripture, namely twenty-two of the Old Testament and eight of the New, in which is contained the sum of all that God has done or will do for His Church. The hundred years in which the ark was built signify the time of grace in which the Church was formed. Thus far Hugh.

paras.t: Postremo juxta tropologiam, per arcam exprimitur mentis nostræ secretum, in quo ab inquietudine mundi et tentationum quiescere et latere debemus. Hujus arcæ ostium est exitus ad opera bona: fenestra vero, ingressus est ad meditandum ac contemplandum. Mansiones hujus arcæ, sunt diversa genera cogitationum. In hac arca omnia intellectualiter continentur et spiritualia alimenta habentur. Verum hæc prosequi prohibet brevitas, cui insudo.
paras.en: Lastly, according to the tropological sense [that is, the moral sense, concerning the soul], by the ark is expressed the secret place of our mind, in which we ought to rest and lie hidden from the unrest of the world and of temptations. The door of this ark is the going out to good works; the window is the going in to meditate and contemplate. The rooms of this ark are the various kinds of thoughts. In this ark all things are contained in the understanding, and spiritual food is had. But the brevity at which I labour forbids me to pursue these things.

7.title: Expositio litteralis capituli septimi: Dixitque Dominus ad eum
7.title_en: Literal exposition of the seventh chapter: “And the Lord said to him”

paras.t: Consequenter describitur exsecutio divinæ comminationis de adductione diluvii. Dixitque Dominus ad eum, scilicet ad Noe: Ingredere tu et omnis domus tua, id est omnes domestici tui, videlicet uxor tua et filii tui, eorumque conjuges, in arcam. Verumtamen ingressionis hujus præceptum implevit Noe, non statim quando Dominus locutus est verba hæc, sed tempore opportuno, ut paulo post scribitur. Te enim vidi justum coram me, id est veraciter virtuosum, in tantum ut propter te parcam domesticis tuis: in generatione hæc. Hoc in præcedentis capituli expositione dupliciter explanatum est.
paras.en: Next is described the carrying out of the divine threat of bringing on the flood. [[7:1|And the Lord said to him|Dixitque Dominus ad eum]], that is, to Noe: [[7:1|Go in, thou and all thy house|Ingredere tu et omnis domus tua]], that is, all thy household, namely thy wife and thy sons and their wives, [[7:1|into the ark|in arcam]]. Yet Noe fulfilled this command to go in not at once, when the Lord spoke these words, but at the fitting time, as is written a little later. [[7:1|for thee I have seen just before me|Te enim vidi justum coram me]], that is, truly virtuous, so much so that for thy sake I will spare thy household[[Gen 6:18||]]: [[7:1|in this generation|in generatione hæc]]. This was explained in two ways in the exposition of the preceding chapter.

paras.t: Ex omnibus animantibus mundis tolle septena et septena, masculum et feminam. Verumtamen istud videtur obscurum, idcirco doctores in ejus expositione diversificantur. Quidam enim exponunt sic: Ex omnibus animantibus mundis, id est ex qualibet specie specialissima animalium mundorum, accipe septem mares et totidem feminas: et isti dicunt, quod ex qualibet specie tali fuerunt in arca quatuordecim individua, et hoc videtur textus prætendere, dicens, Septena et septena, masculum et feminam: quasi dicat, Septem et septem, ita quod septem sint mares, septemque feminæ: quod etiam verba textus paulo post sequentia, insinuare videntur, sicut patebit. De animantibus vero immundis tolle duo et duo, masculum et feminam, id est bina et bina seu quatuor, secundum istos, ita quod duo erunt masculi et duæ feminæ, ex omni hujusmodi specie. Sed et de volatilibus cœli septena et septena, masculum et feminam, hoc est quatuordecim juxta sensum de animalibus mundis inductum. Ut salvetur semen super faciem universæ terræ, id est, ut animalia ista post diluvium reparent specierum suarum ruinam, et generando multiplicent suarum individua specierum ubique terrarum.
paras.en: [[7:2|Of all clean beasts take seven and seven, the male and the female|Ex omnibus animantibus mundis tolle septena et septena, masculum et feminam]]. Yet this seems obscure, and so the doctors differ in expounding it. For some expound it thus: Of all clean beasts, that is, of every most specific species [that is, every lowest species, below which there are only individuals] of clean animals, take seven males and as many females; and these say that of every such species there were fourteen individuals in the ark. And the text seems to put this forward when it says, Seven and seven, the male and the female: as if to say, Seven and seven, so that seven be males and seven females; which the words of the text that follow a little later also seem to suggest, as will appear. [[7:3|But of the beasts that are unclean|De animantibus vero immundis]] take [[7:3|two and two, the male and the female|duo et duo, masculum et feminam]] [the Douay-Rheims puts these words at the start of v. 3; in the Vulgate they close v. 2], that is, two and two, or four, according to these, so that there will be two males and two females of every such species. [[7:3|Of the fowls also of the air seven and seven, the male and the female|Sed et de volatilibus cœli septena et septena, masculum et feminam]], that is, fourteen, in keeping with the sense given for the clean animals. [[7:3|that seed may be saved upon the face of the whole earth|Ut salvetur semen super faciem universæ terræ]], that is, so that after the flood these animals might repair the ruin of their species, and by generating multiply the individuals of their species all over the earth.

paras.t: Circa hoc quæri potest, an de qualibet specie avium fuerunt individua tot in arca, et cur non distinguit Moyses inter aves, vocando aliquas mundas, quasdam vero immundas, potissimum quum secundum legem quædam aves fuerunt immundæ, quædam mundæ. Ad istud non legi responsionem, nec vidi quæstionem hanc motam, idcirco eam determinare non audeo, nec incerta pro certis in expositione Scripturæ scribere volo. Qui autem vult dicere, quod distinctio fuit inter aves quantum ad munditiam et immunditiam, et quantum ad numerum, sicut de animalibus dictum est, dicere potest quod Moyses brevitati studens, non distinxit inter aves: sed de solis septenis et septenis introducendis in arcam, locutus est, intelligendo per ista septena aves mundas: quia quod de animalibus terræ jam dixerat, quantum ad distinctionem et numerum varium, de avibus quoque intelligi voluit. Qui vero superficiem litteræ sequitur, dicere habet, quod de qualibet specie avium non fluvialium et sexum utrumque ad generandum habentium, septena et septena in arcam deducta sunt, id est quatuordecim secundum istam expositionem, et forsitan totidem de avibus fluvialibus generativis, in nidos præfatos arcæ affixos. Et quod propter mysterium non fit distinctio inter aves cœli, sicut inter bestias terræ, utpote propter mysticam significationem infra tangendam. Denique expositioni huic consonare videtur quod paulo post subditur: De animantibus mundis et immundis et de volucribus duo et duo ingressa sunt in arcam ad Noe, masculus et femina. Ex quo (ut apparet) consequitur, quod ea quæ introierunt, ingressa sunt omnia combinata, atque in numero pari, sive in quaternario sive in quatuordenario, ita quod non introierunt septem tantum de animalibus mundis: sic namque septimum intrasset non combinatum, et masculus sine femella, contra quod rursus in isto capitulo subditur: Ingressa sunt ad Noe in arcam bina et bina ex omni carne, in qua erat spiritus vitæ: et quæ ingressa sunt, masculus et femina introierunt. Unde in præcedenti capitulo scriptum est: De volucribus et jumentis et ex omni reptili terræ secundum genus suum, bina de omnibus ingredientur tecum.
paras.en: On this it may be asked whether of every species of birds there were so many individuals in the ark, and why Moses does not distinguish among the birds, calling some clean and others unclean, especially since under the Law some birds were unclean and some clean. To this I have not read an answer, nor have I seen this question raised; and so I do not dare to settle it, nor do I wish to write uncertain things as certain in expounding Scripture. But whoever wishes to say that there was a distinction among the birds as to cleanness and uncleanness, and as to number, as was said of the beasts, can say that Moses, studying brevity, did not distinguish among the birds, but spoke only of sevens and sevens to be brought into the ark, meaning by these sevens the clean birds: for what he had already said of the beasts of the earth, as to the distinction and the differing number, he wished to be understood of the birds too. But whoever follows the surface of the letter has to say that of every species of birds that are not river birds [that is, water-fowl, which could live outside on the waters] and that have both sexes for generating, seven and seven were brought into the ark, that is, fourteen according to this exposition; and perhaps as many of the river birds that generate, into the nests mentioned above, fixed to the ark. And that no distinction is made among the birds of the air, as among the beasts of the earth, because of a mystery, namely because of a mystical signification to be touched on below. Lastly, what is added a little later seems to agree with this exposition: [[7:8|of beasts clean and unclean, and of fowls|De animantibus mundis et immundis et de volucribus]] [[7:9|Two and two went in to Noe into the ark, male and female|duo et duo ingressa sunt in arcam ad Noe, masculus et femina]]. From which (as appears) it follows that those that went in all went in paired, and in an even number, whether by fours or by fourteens, so that it was not merely seven of the clean animals that went in: for then the seventh would have gone in unpaired, and a male without a female; against which it is added again in this chapter: [[7:15|Went in to Noe into the ark, two and two of all flesh, wherein was the breath of life|Ingressa sunt ad Noe in arcam bina et bina ex omni carne, in qua erat spiritus vitæ]]: [[7:16|And they that went in, went in male and female|et quæ ingressa sunt, masculus et femina introierunt]]. Hence in the preceding chapter it is written: [[Gen 6:20|Of fowls according to their kind, and of beasts in their kind, and of every thing that creepeth on the earth according to its kind: two of every sort shall go in with thee|De volucribus et jumentis et ex omni reptili terræ secundum genus suum, bina de omnibus ingredientur tecum]].

paras.t: Hanc expositionem tenet Andreas expositor, et concordant Hebræi, ut legi. Origenes quoque hoc sentit: Bina, inquiens, et bina, hoc est bini masculi et binæ feminæ de immundis animalibus. Hoc enim indicat sermo repetitus. Ex mundis vero septena et septena, quod est paria septena, in arcam dicuntur inducta. Idem Augustinus insinuare videtur, dicens: Dicunt quidam quantitatem arcæ non potuisse capere tam multa animalium genera in utroque sexu, videlicet bina de immundis, septena de mundis. Ad quod Augustinus ita respondet, ut non neget tantam animalium multitudinem in utroque sexu ibi fuisse, sed arcam fuisse majorem, quam prima facie littera sonare videtur.
paras.en: This exposition is held by Andrew the expositor [that is, Andrew of Saint Victor], and the Hebrews agree, as I have read. Origen too thinks so, saying: Two and two, that is, two males and two females of the unclean animals; for the repeated word shows this. But of the clean, seven and seven, that is, seven pairs, are said to have been brought into the ark. Augustine seems to suggest the same, saying: Some say that the size of the ark could not hold so many kinds of animals in both sexes, namely two of the unclean and seven of the clean. To which Augustine answers in such a way that he does not deny that so great a multitude of animals in both sexes was there, but says that the ark was larger than the letter seems at first sight to sound.

paras.t: His autem objiciunt alii, quod arca fuisset nimis gravata et occupata tanta animalium et avium pluralitate. Item quod ad multiplicationem et reparationem animalium et avium non erat necessaria pluralitas tanta. Hi itaque litteram sic exponunt: Ex omnibus animantibus mundis tolles septena et septena, masculum et feminam, id est septem de isto animalium genere, et septem de illo, sicque de singulis, ita quod ibi sint tria masculini generis, et tria feminini, septimum vero ut immoletur Deo post egressum ab arca. De animantibus vero immundis duo et duo, id est, de quolibet illorum genere duo. Et simili modo exponunt quod de avibus dicitur, septena et septena. Porro quod sequitur, Bina et bina ingressa sunt, masculus et femina, sic exponunt, quod combinatio illa intelligitur tantum de animalibus quæ erant ad prolificandum reposita. Hanc expositionem sequitur Rabanus, Glossa, et Scholastica historia: prima tamen videtur consonantior textui, et argumenta in oppositum facta, faciliter solverentur.
paras.en: But others object to these that the ark would have been too much weighed down and filled with so great a number of animals and birds; also that so great a number was not needed for the multiplying and restoring of the animals and birds. So these expound the letter thus: [[7:2|Of all clean beasts take seven and seven, the male and the female|Ex omnibus animantibus mundis tolles septena et septena, masculum et feminam]], that is, seven of this kind of animal and seven of that, and so of each, so that there be three of the male sex and three of the female, and the seventh to be sacrificed to God after the going out from the ark. [[7:3|But of the beasts that are unclean two and two|De animantibus vero immundis duo et duo]], that is, two of each kind of them. And in like manner they expound what is said of the birds, seven and seven. Further, what follows, [[7:9|Two and two went in|Bina et bina ingressa sunt]], [[7:9|male and female|masculus et femina]], they expound thus: that this pairing is understood only of the animals that were kept for breeding. This exposition is followed by Rabanus, the Gloss and the Scholastic History; yet the first seems more in keeping with the text, and the arguments made against it would easily be answered.

paras.t: Sed jam adhuc oritur quæstio duplex. Prima, quæ animalia vocentur munda, quæ item immunda. Secunda, cur inducta sunt plura, et tam multo plura de mundis, quam de immundis. Ad primam est duplex responsio. Una, quod ea dicuntur munda et ea immunda, quæ post diluvium tempore legis Mosaicæ reputata sunt munda sive immunda. Secunda, quod illa dicuntur immunda, quæ naturaliter sunt esui humano inepta: munda vero, quæ naturaliter sunt apta ad edendum. Insuper in Glossa tangitur responsio tertia, in qua fertur: Omnia munda sunt naturaliter, sed comparatione melioris naturæ, quædam dicuntur immunda, sicut Bos melior est leone, quoniam magis necessarius atque utilior est homini propter quem creata sunt omnia. Ad secundum respondetur, secundum Augustinum, quod principaliter causa illius rei est mystica significatio, quæ tangetur sequenti articulo. Potest et alia ratio assignari, quod munda animalia idcirco fuerunt plura, ut Noe egressus de arca, haberet quod immolaret, et item ut ipse et qui secum fuerunt, haberent ad manducandum, quia post diluvium concessus est esus carnium. Has causas Rabanus tangit. Glossa quoque adjungit, quod ideo munda animalia erant plura, ut plura essent, quæ facto diluvio hominibus prodessent ac deservirent, quam quæ possent nocere, et ita est usque ad præsens.
paras.en: But now a twofold question arises. First, which animals are called clean, and which unclean. Second, why more were brought in, and so many more of the clean than of the unclean. To the first there is a twofold answer. One, that those are called clean and those unclean which after the flood, in the time of the Law of Moses, were reckoned clean or unclean. The second, that those are called unclean which by nature are unfit for human food, and those clean which by nature are fit to be eaten. Besides, a third answer is touched on in the Gloss, where it is said: All things are clean by nature, but by comparison with a better nature some are called unclean; as the ox is better than the lion, since it is more necessary and more useful to man, for whose sake all things were created. To the second it is answered, according to Augustine, that the chief cause of this thing is a mystical signification, which will be touched on in the following article. Another reason too can be given: that the clean animals were more numerous so that Noe, on going out of the ark, might have something to sacrifice, and also so that he and those who were with him might have something to eat, since after the flood the eating of flesh was granted. Rabanus touches on these causes. The Gloss also adds that the clean animals were more numerous so that, once the flood was over, there might be more that would profit and serve men than that could harm them; and so it is to this day.

paras.t: Adhuc enim et post dies septem ego pluam super terram quadraginta diebus et quadraginta noctibus, et delebo omnem substantiam quam feci de superficie terræ, id est, omnia viva in terra occidam. Tunc quoque terræ nascentia sunt destructa, arboresque eversæ. Denique usque in præsens inveniuntur corpora arborum magna et longa sub terra, quæ aliqui opinantur ex diluvio sic dejecta ac derelicta. Aliqua etenim ligna quasi imputribilia manent in terra, ipsaque terra interim in pluribus locis est inalterata. Dicunt quoque Hebræi, ut refert Lyra, quod septem isti dies, quibus differebat diluvium, fuerunt dies deplorationis ipsius Mathusalem, quem dicunt ante hos dies obiisse, atque in hoc honoratum a Deo propter suam justitiam.
paras.en: [[7:4|For yet a while, and after seven days, I will rain upon the earth forty days and forty nights: and I will destroy every substance that I have made, from the face of the earth|Adhuc enim et post dies septem ego pluam super terram quadraginta diebus et quadraginta noctibus, et delebo omnem substantiam quam feci de superficie terræ]], that is, I will kill all living things on the earth. Then too the things growing from the earth were destroyed, and the trees overthrown. Indeed, to this day great and long trunks of trees are found under the earth, which some think were thrown down and left so by the flood. For some timbers remain in the earth as if incorruptible, while the earth itself in many places is unaltered [the transcription marks this word as doubtful]. The Hebrews also say, as Lyra relates, that these seven days by which the flood was put off were the days of mourning for Mathusala, who they say died before these days, and was in this honoured by God for his justice.

paras.t: Fecit ergo Noe omnia quæ mandaverat ei Dominus. Eratque Noe sexcentorum annorum quando aquæ diluvii inundaverunt super terram. Ex quo patet, quod centum annis fuit occupatus in fabrica arcæ, quia (ut dictum est in principio sexti capituli), quingentorum erat annorum, quum Dominus ei jussit facere arcam. Patet quoque, quod primogenitus ejus fuit centum annorum quando intravit arcam: quia quum esset quingentorum annorum, cœpit generare hos tres qui secum ingressi sunt. Dicunt autem doctores, quod infra annos quibus fabricata est arca, prædixit hominibus ortum diluvii, eosque ad pœnitentiam hortabatur, qui indurati, non crediderunt nec acquieverunt. Circa quod refert Lyra, quod homines illi induratissimi dixerunt ad Noe, quod interficerent eum si introiret arcam, ne eis submersis, superviveret ipse cum suis. Sed Rabbi Paulus dicit esse fictitium, quum in Scripturis non habeat fundamentum.
paras.en: [[7:5|And Noe did all things which the Lord had commanded him|Fecit ergo Noe omnia quæ mandaverat ei Dominus]]. And Noe was [[7:6|six hundred years old, when the waters of the flood overflowed the earth|sexcentorum annorum quando aquæ diluvii inundaverunt super terram]]. From which it is plain that he was busy for a hundred years building the ark, since (as was said at the beginning of the sixth chapter) he was five hundred years old when the Lord bade him make the ark. It is plain also that his firstborn was a hundred years old when he went into the ark, since when Noe was five hundred years old he began to beget these three who went in with him. Now the doctors say that within the years in which the ark was built he foretold to men the coming of the flood and exhorted them to penance; but they, hardened, neither believed nor gave heed. On which Lyra relates that those most hardened men told Noe that they would kill him if he went into the ark, lest when they were drowned he should survive with his own. But Rabbi Paul [that is, Paul of Burgos, a convert from Judaism who wrote additions to Lyra] says this is made up, since it has no foundation in the Scriptures.

paras.t: Et ingressus est Noe et filii ejus, uxor ejus et uxores filiorum ejus cum eo in arcam. Seorsum viri, seorsumque feminæ dicuntur arcam ingressi, ad innuendum quod in arca commixti non sunt: infra vero leguntur simul egressi, quum dicitur, Egressus est Noe et uxor ejus: quia ut Salomon ait, Tempus amplexandi, et tempus longe fiendi ab amplexibus. Ingressi sunt in arcam, propter aquas diluvii, ne mergerentur. Sicque ingressi sunt, quando aqua cœpit multiplicari.
paras.en: [[7:7|And Noe went in and his sons, his wife and the wives of his sons with him into the ark|Et ingressus est Noe et filii ejus, uxor ejus et uxores filiorum ejus cum eo in arcam]]. The men are said to have gone into the ark apart, and the women apart, to hint that they did not come together in the ark; but below they are read to have gone out together, when it is said, [[Gen 8:18|Noe went out|Egressus est Noe]], and his wife [so Denis gives it; the verse reads: So Noe went out, he and his sons: his wife, and the wives of his sons with him]: because, as Solomon says, there is [[Eccles 3:5|A time to embrace, and a time to be far from embraces|Tempus amplexandi, et tempus longe fiendi ab amplexibus]]. They went into the ark [[7:7|because of the waters of the flood|propter aquas diluvii]], lest they be drowned. And so they went in when the water began to increase.
