For the Lord, through the holy angels and virtuous men, afflicts the demons and their prince grievously and in many ways, curbing them, overcoming them and mocking them, because they do not cease so to tempt the Church of Christ; and at length their misery will be greatly increased, when, according to the oracle of Isaias, [[Is 24:22|they shall be gathered together as in the gathering of one bundle|congregabuntur congregatione unius fasciis]], [[Is 24:22|and they shall be shut up there in prison|et claudentur in carcere]]. [[12:18|And Pharao called Abram|Vocavitque Pharao Abram]], etc. This comes about when the devil sees and confesses himself overcome by the members of Christ, and lets the victors go in peace, that they may serve Christ.

paras.t: Postremo Abram juxta tropologiam designat unumquemque fidelem, cui jubet aut consulit Christus, ut egrediatur de terra sua, relinquendo propter ipsum omnia exteriora: et de cognatione sua, relinquendo propinquos; et de domo patris sui, deserendo domesticos: quatenus ad nihil horum inordinate afficiatur, imo et se ipsum abneget, vincat, mortificet, et sedens in claustro, levet se super se contemplando divina; veniatque in terram quam Dominus ei monstrat, sanctam ingrediendo religionem, atque ad patriam festinando cælestem, ut faciat eum in gentem magnam, alios ædificando, et convertendo per ipsum, et benedicat et dando centuplum in præsenti, et vitam gloriæ in futuro.
paras.en: Lastly, according to the tropological sense [that is, the moral sense, which concerns the conduct of the soul], Abram signifies each of the faithful, whom Christ commands or counsels to go forth out of his country, leaving all outward things for his sake; and from his kindred, leaving his relations; and out of his father's house, forsaking those of his household: so that he be inordinately attached to none of these; nay, that he deny himself, conquer and mortify himself, and, sitting in the cloister, lift himself above himself[[Lam 3:28||]] [the margin refers to Lamentations 3:28, in the Vulgate *Sedebit solitarius … quia levavit super se*, "he shall sit solitary … because he hath lifted himself above himself"; the Douay-Rheims has "he hath taken it up upon himself"] in contemplating divine things; and that he come into the land which the Lord shews him, by entering holy religion [that is, the religious life under vows] and hastening to the heavenly fatherland; so that the Lord may make him a great nation, edifying and converting others through him, and may bless him, giving a hundredfold in the present life, and the life of glory in the world to come.

13.title: Expositio litteralis capituli tertiidecimi: Ascendit ergo Abram de Ægypto
13.title_en: Literal exposition of the thirteenth chapter: And Abram went up out of Egypt

paras.t: Ascendit ergo Abram de Ægypto, quæ in decliviori est situ quam regio Chanaan, ipse et uxor ejus, et omnia quæ habebat, et Lot cum eo, ad australem plagam terræ Chanaan. Erat autem dives valde in possessione auri et argenti. Reversusque est per iter quo venerat, id est per quod Ægyptum intraverat a meridie. Reversusque est, inquam, a meridie, id est plaga meridiana, vel ab Ægypto, quæ respectu terræ Chanaan, est versus meridiem, in Bethel, urbem præfatam. Ait quidam, quod in Hebræo habetur, Reversus est per mansiones quibus venerat: quod exponendo, affirmat, quod Abram, quando intravit Ægyptum, non habebat sufficientem pecuniam ad solvendum in hospitiis suas expensas: idcirco per eadem revertebatur hospitia, ut solveret debita quæ ibi contraxit. Istud fabulosum videtur, nec apparentiam habet, quum Deus promiserit Abræ benedictionem in spiritualibus ac temporalibus, antequam exivit a Mesopotamia ad terram promissionis, nec unquam fuit tam pauper, ut non haberet tantillum pecuniæ, qua solveret in via suas expensas. Erat quoque ignotus in illis hospitiis, idcirco non habet apparentiam quod dedissent ei dilationem solutionis expensarum, nisi forsan sub pignore.
paras.en: [[13:1|And Abram went up out of Egypt|Ascendit ergo Abram de Ægypto]], which lies lower than the country of Chanaan, [[13:1|he and his wife, and all that he had, and Lot with him|ipse et uxor ejus, et omnia quæ habebat, et Lot cum eo]] [[13:1|into the south|ad australem plagam]] of the land of Chanaan. [[13:2|And he was very rich in possession of gold and silver.|Erat autem dives valde in possessione auri et argenti.]] [[13:3|And he returned by the way, that he came|Reversusque est per iter quo venerat]], that is, by the way by which he had entered Egypt from the south. And he returned, I say, [[13:3|from the south|a meridie]], that is, from the southern quarter, or from Egypt, which with respect to the land of Chanaan lies toward the south, [[13:3|to Bethel|in Bethel]], the city named above. A certain writer says that the Hebrew has: He returned by the stages by which he had come [mansiones: the halts or lodgings of a journey]; and expounding this, he affirms that Abram, when he entered Egypt, did not have money enough to pay his expenses at the inns, and therefore went back by the same inns to pay the debts he had run up there. This seems a fable and has no likelihood, since God had promised Abram a blessing in things spiritual and temporal before he went out of Mesopotamia to the land of promise; nor was he ever so poor as not to have even a little money with which to pay his expenses on the road. He was also unknown at those inns, and so it is not likely that they would have allowed him to put off paying his expenses, unless perhaps against a pledge.

paras.t: Facta est rixa inter pastores gregum Abram et Lot: quia ut habetur in littera, uterque eorum habuit pecora multa, diversorumque generum, et tabernacula pro se et pertinentibus sibi, videlicet pro suis domesticis et jumentis. Nec poterat eos capere terra, ut habitarent simul. Poterat utique terra Chanaan capere eos, sed non ita, ut pacifice simul manerent, videlicet sine contentione pastorum suorum, quorum unusquisque festinavit meliora pascua præoccupare, nec cesserunt sibi ad invicem, quum essent homines imperfecti. Eo autem tempore Chananæus et Pherezæus, id est populi Chananæorum ac Pherezæorum, qui nati fuerunt ex filiis Chanaan filii Cham, habitabant in terra illa. Hoc interponit Scriptura, secundum Rabbi Paulum, ad innuendum quod causa separationis Abræ a Lot fuit, quoniam Abram timuit quod habitatores terræ illius videntes tantam opulentiam suam ac sui nepotis, spoliarent aut expellerent se et Lot a terra illa. Alii dicunt, quod Abram timuit posse ex contentionibus pastorum litem moveri coram infidelibus illis judicibus.
paras.en: [[13:7|there arose a strife between the herdsmen of Abram and of Lot|Facta est rixa inter pastores gregum Abram et Lot]]: because, as the text has it, each of them had many beasts, and of different kinds, and tents for himself and for those belonging to him, namely for his household and his cattle. [[13:6|Neither was the land able to bear them, that they might dwell together|Nec poterat eos capere terra, ut habitarent simul]]. The land of Chanaan could indeed hold them, but not so that they might stay together in peace, that is, without strife among their herdsmen, each of whom hurried to seize the better pastures first; nor did they give way to one another, since they were imperfect men. [[13:7|And at that time the Chanaanite and the Pherezite|Eo autem tempore Chananæus et Pherezæus]], that is, the peoples of the Chanaanites and the Pherezites, who were born of the sons of Chanaan the son of Cham, [[13:7|dwelled in that country|habitabant in terra illa]]. Scripture puts this in, according to Rabbi Paul [Paul of Burgos, a converted rabbi whose Additions accompany Lyra], to hint that the cause of Abram's parting from Lot was that Abram feared that the inhabitants of that land, seeing so much wealth of his own and of his nephew's, would rob them or drive himself and Lot out of that land. Others say that Abram feared that the herdsmen's quarrels might lead to a lawsuit before those infidel judges.

paras.t: Dixit ergo Abram ad Lot: Ne, quæso, sit jurgium inter me et te, et inter pastores meos et tuos: fratres enim sumus, id est multum propinqui. Timuit itaque Abram ne ex occasione contentionis pastorum suorum etiam inter eos oriretur contentio, quæ inter domesticos tanto detestabilior est, quanto mutua pax eorum est appetibilior. Ecce universa terra coram te est, id est, terram istam præsentialiter vides: idcirco considerare potes quæ pars ejus aptior tibi sit. Recede a me, obsecro. Melius namque est, salva caritate et pace, corporaliter separari et seorsum morari, quam cum caritatis et pacis detrimento simul et corpore habitare. Si tu ad sinistram ibis, ego dexteram tenebo; si tu dexteram elegeris, ego ad sinistram pergam. In his verbis apparet eximia bonitas Abræ, utpote caritas, mansuetudo, pietas, et humilitas ejus, quia quum esset tam sublimiter major ac eruditior, tamen in omnibus detulit suo nepoti, electionem dans ei, et communi providens paci. Ex quo Abræ facto, secundum Augustinum, fortassis effecta est laudabilis ista consuetudo, quod quando aliquid terrenum est inter homines dividendum, major dividat, et minor eligat.
paras.en: [[13:8|Abram therefore said to Lot: Let there be no quarrel, I beseech thee, between me and thee, and between my herdsmen and thy herdsmen: for we are brethren|Dixit ergo Abram ad Lot: Ne, quæso, sit jurgium inter me et te, et inter pastores meos et tuos: fratres enim sumus]], that is, very near of kin. So Abram feared that, from the occasion of their herdsmen's strife, strife might arise between themselves too; and among those of one household this is the more detestable, the more desirable their mutual peace is. [[13:9|Behold the whole land is before thee|Ecce universa terra coram te est]], that is, thou seest this land present before thee: therefore thou canst consider which part of it suits thee better. [[13:9|depart from me, I pray thee|Recede a me, obsecro]]. For it is better, with charity and peace kept safe, to be parted in body and live apart, than to dwell together in body to the loss of charity and peace. [[13:9|if thou wilt go to the left hand, I will take the right: if thou choose the right hand, I will pass to the left|Si tu ad sinistram ibis, ego dexteram tenebo; si tu dexteram elegeris, ego ad sinistram pergam]]. In these words appears the surpassing goodness of Abram, namely his charity, meekness, kindness and humility: for though he was so far the greater and the more learned, yet he deferred to his nephew in everything, giving him the choice and providing for their common peace. From this deed of Abram, according to Augustine, there perhaps arose that praiseworthy custom that, when something earthly is to be divided among men, the greater divides and the lesser chooses [major, minor: the greater and the lesser, or the elder and the younger].

paras.t: Elevatis itaque Lot oculis, vidit omnem circa regionem Jordanis, id est, circumquaque adspiciens, consideravit regionem suam circa Jordanem, quæ tunc fuit regio Pentapolis; quæ universa rigabatur aquis Jordanis, opportune extra fluentis, aut etiam pluviis, antequam subverteret Dominus Sodomam et Gomorrham, sicut paradisus Domini, hoc est, sicut paradisus irrigatur fonte ac fluvio existente in eo, et sicut Ægyptus irrigatur Nilo, venientibus in Segor, id est in adspectu eorum, qui ab Ægypto vadunt in urbem, Segor vocatam, circa quod iter terra Ægypti est pulchra ac fertilis valde. Elegitque sibi Lot regionem circa Jordanem, hoc est, in aliqua parte regionis illius habitare elegit; et recessit ab oriente, id est plaga orientali, in qua erat cum Abram, quæ respectu regionis quam elegit Lot ad inhabitandum, fuit orientalis; divisique sunt alterutrum a fratre suo, id est, unus eorum recessit ab altero sibi propinquo. Lot vero moratus est in oppidis quæ erant circa Jordanem, hoc est in urbibus Pentapolis, et habitavit in Sodomis, id est civitatibus Sodomorum, præsertim in Sodoma, quæ erat principalis inter quinque urbes illas præfatas. Ex quo videtur, quod successive habitavit in pluribus oppidorum illorum, nisi forte plurale pro singulari ponatur, juxta modum loquendi quo aliquid attribuitur multitudini, quia convenit uni aut alicui parti ejus. Estque probabile, quod Lot paulatim experiens impietatem oppidanorum illorum, recessit ab una urbe ad aliam, æstimans habitatores unius meliores habitatoribus alterius urbis, si tamen in diversis oppidis illis successive moratus est.
paras.en: [[13:10|And Lot lifting up his eyes, saw all the country about the Jordan|Elevatis itaque Lot oculis, vidit omnem circa regionem Jordanis]], that is, looking all around, he surveyed the country about the Jordan that lay before him, which was then the country of the Pentapolis [the five cities of the plain]; [[13:10|which was watered throughout|quæ universa rigabatur]] by the waters of the Jordan, flowing out over the land in due season, or else by rains, [[13:10|before the Lord destroyed Sodom and Gomorrha, as the paradise of the Lord|antequam subverteret Dominus Sodomam et Gomorrham, sicut paradisus Domini]], that is, as paradise is watered by the spring and river that is in it, [[13:10|and like Egypt|et sicut Ægyptus]] is watered by the Nile, [[13:10|as one comes to Segor|venientibus in Segor]], that is, in the sight of those who go from Egypt to the city called Segor, along which road the land of Egypt is very fair and fertile. [[13:11|And Lot chose to himself the country about the Jordan|Elegitque sibi Lot regionem circa Jordanem]], that is, he chose to dwell in some part of that country; [[13:11|and he departed from the east|et recessit ab oriente]], that is, from the eastern quarter where he had been with Abram, which lay to the east with respect to the country Lot chose to live in; [[13:11|and they were separated one brother from the other|divisique sunt alterutrum a fratre suo]], that is, one of them withdrew from the other, his near kinsman. [[13:12|Lot abode in the towns, that were about the Jordan|Lot vero moratus est in oppidis quæ erant circa Jordanem]], that is, in the cities of the Pentapolis, [[13:12|and dwelt in Sodom|et habitavit in Sodomis]] [the Latin, in Sodomis, is plural], that is, in the cities of the Sodomites, and especially in Sodom, which was the chief of those five cities named above. From this it seems that he lived in several of those towns one after another, unless perhaps the plural is put for the singular, after the manner of speaking by which something is attributed to a multitude because it belongs to one, or to some part, of it. And it is likely that Lot, finding out little by little the wickedness of the townsfolk, moved from one city to another, thinking the inhabitants of one better than those of the other, if indeed he did live in several of those towns in turn.

paras.t: Præterea quæritur, cur Lot quum esset vir justus, elegit habitationem inter pessimos Sodomitas. Ad quod dicendum, quod aliqui adscribunt hoc imperfectioni ipsius, et dicunt nonnulli eum pejoratum ex cohabitatione illorum: quod non videtur consonare verbis dignissimi principis Apostolorum, qui in sua secunda scribit Canonica: Adspectu et auditu Lot justus erat, habitans inter eos qui de die in diem animam justi iniquis operibus cruciabant. Ideo dici potest, quod forte non scivit tantam facinorositatem eorum, quando inter eos habitare elegit ac cœpit. Vel dispensatione et ordinatione divina id factum est, ut virtus Lot magis exercitaretur et ostenderetur per illorum pravitatem nequissimam, quatenus ejus exemplo discamus non perverti ab impiis, sed et ut Sodomitæ ejus virtutibus ædificarentur.
paras.en: Further, it is asked why Lot, being a just man, chose to dwell among the most wicked Sodomites. To this it must be said that some ascribe it to his imperfection, and some say that he grew worse from living with them: which does not seem to agree with the words of the most worthy prince of the Apostles, who writes in his second canonical Epistle: [[2 Pet 2:8|in sight and hearing|Adspectu et auditu]] Lot [[2 Pet 2:8|was just, dwelling among them who from day to day vexed the just soul with unjust works|justus erat, habitans inter eos qui de die in diem animam justi iniquis operibus cruciabant]]. It can be said, then, that perhaps he did not know how great their villainy was when he chose and began to dwell among them. Or else this was done by God's dispensation and ordinance, so that Lot's virtue might be the more exercised and shown forth through their most wicked depravity, that by his example we may learn not to be perverted by the wicked, and also that the Sodomites might be edified by his virtues.

paras.t: Homines autem Sodomitæ pessimi erant, etc., de quorum sceleribus infra dicetur.
paras.en: [[13:13|And the men of Sodom were very wicked|Homines autem Sodomitæ pessimi erant]], etc.: of their crimes more will be said below.

paras.t: Dixitque Dominus ad Abram postquam divisus est ab eo Lot. Abram quippe in aliena habitans terra, antiquam habuit consolationem ex cohabitatione Lot nepotis ac socii sui: idcirco dum amore virtutum separasset eum a se, meruit consolationem divinam accipere, et etiam quia contentiones jam erant a domo sua sublatæ. Leva oculos tuos in directum, et vide a loco in quo nunc es, ad aquilonem et meridiem, ad orientem et occidentem, id est ad quatuor plagas terræ Chanaan in qua stas. Omnem terram quam conspicis, id est universam terram Chanaan, cujus partem nunc vides oculo corporali, tibi dabo, id est posteris tuis. Ideo expositorie subditur: et semini tuo, videlicet filiis Israel, usque in sempiternum, id est per spatium valde longum, vel usque in finem mundi, nisi peccando meruerint eam amittere. Tales namque promissiones intelliguntur sub conditione. Verum ut ait B. Stephanus, Deus non dedit Abrahæ hereditatem in terra illa nec passum pedis.
paras.en: [[13:14|And the Lord said to Abram, after Lot was separated from him|Dixitque Dominus ad Abram postquam divisus est ab eo Lot]]. For Abram, living in a foreign land, had long had the comfort of living with Lot, his nephew and companion: therefore, since for love of virtue he had parted him from himself, he deserved to receive God's comfort; and also because strife had now been taken away from his house. [[13:14|Lift up thy eyes|Leva oculos tuos]] straight before thee [in directum: these words are in Denis's text, not in the Clementine Vulgate], [[13:14|and look from the place wherein thou now art, to the north and to the south, to the east and to the west|et vide a loco in quo nunc es, ad aquilonem et meridiem, ad orientem et occidentem]], that is, to the four quarters of the land of Chanaan in which thou standest. [[13:15|All the land which thou seest|Omnem terram quam conspicis]], that is, the whole land of Chanaan, part of which thou now seest with the bodily eye, [[13:15|I will give to thee|tibi dabo]], that is, to thy posterity. Therefore it is added by way of explanation: [[13:15|and to thy seed|et semini tuo]], namely the children of Israel, [[13:15|for ever|usque in sempiternum]], that is, for a very long time, or until the end of the world, unless by sinning they deserve to lose it. For such promises are understood under a condition. But, as blessed Stephen says, God [[Acts 7:5|gave him no inheritance in it: no, not the pace of a foot|non dedit Abrahæ hereditatem in terra illa nec passum pedis]].

paras.t: Faciamque semen tuum sicut pulverem terræ, id est, innumerabiliter eos multiplicabo. Si quis hominum potest numerare pulverem terræ, semen quoque tuum numerare poterit; quasi dicat: Tam innumerabilis erit posteritas tua, ut pulvis terræ. Hæc tamen hyperbolica locutio est, utpote per excessum dicta, ad insinuandum magnitudinem rei, seu vehementem multitudinem posterorum Abrahæ patriarchæ, sicut ad Joseph Pharao dixit: Absque oris tui imperio nullus movebit manum aut pedem in omni terra Ægypti: juxta quem modum etiam de electis et amicis Dei fertur in Psalmo, Dinumerabo eos, et super arenam multiplicabuntur. Et si ista promissio verificari potest in sola multiplicatione filiorum Israel, quanto magis si eis addantur Ismaelitæ ac aliæ nationes magnæ et multæ ex filiis Abrahæ nati, de quibus infra habebitur? Surge ergo, et perambula terram in longitudine et latitudine sua, quia daturus sum eam tibi: ut scias magnitudinem beneficii mei, et futuram multitudinem sobolis tuæ, atque ut obediendo mihi in ista perambulatione terræ, merearis gratiam ampliorem, aut etiam hujus promissi impletionem.
paras.en: [[13:16|And I will make thy seed as the dust of the earth|Faciamque semen tuum sicut pulverem terræ]], that is, I will multiply them beyond number. [[13:16|if any man be able to number the dust of the earth, he shall be able to number thy seed also|Si quis hominum potest numerare pulverem terræ, semen quoque tuum numerare poterit]]; as if to say: Thy posterity shall be as numberless as the dust of the earth. Yet this is a hyperbolical way of speaking, that is, said by way of excess, to suggest the greatness of the thing, or the very great multitude of the descendants of the patriarch Abraham; as Pharao said to Joseph: [[Gen 41:44|without thy commandment no man shall move hand or foot in all the land of Egypt|Absque oris tui imperio nullus movebit manum aut pedem in omni terra Ægypti]]; after which manner it is also said in the Psalm of God's elect and friends: [[Ps 138:18|I will number them, and they shall be multiplied above the sand|Dinumerabo eos, et super arenam multiplicabuntur]]. And if this promise can be made good in the multiplying of the children of Israel alone, how much more if to them are added the Ismaelites and the other nations, great and many, born of the sons of Abraham, of whom more will be said below? [[13:17|Arise and walk through the land in the length, and the breadth thereof|Surge ergo, et perambula terram in longitudine et latitudine sua]], [[13:17|for I will give it to thee|quia daturus sum eam tibi]]: that thou mayest know the greatness of my benefit and the future multitude of thy offspring, and that by obeying me in this walking through the land thou mayest merit a fuller grace, or even the fulfilment of this promise.

paras.t: Movens igitur Abram tabernaculum suum, id est secum deferens illud, venit cum uxore et domesticis atque pecoribus suis, et habitavit juxta convallem Mambre, hoc est viri sic dicti, a quo vallis illa cognominata est, ita quod Mambre fuit cum fratribus suis Abræ confœderatus, ut patebit sequenti capitulo. Intelligendum est tamen, quod obedientissimus Abram statim divinum istud implevit præceptum. Est quoque hæc convallis in Hebron; id est juxta Hebron. Ædificavitque ibi altare Domino, eisdem de causis, ob quas et alibi, sicut jam patuit.
paras.en: [[13:18|So Abram removing his tent|Movens igitur Abram tabernaculum suum]], that is, carrying it with him, [[13:18|came|venit]] with his wife and household and his beasts, [[13:18|and dwelt by the vale of Mambre|et habitavit juxta convallem Mambre]], that is, of the man so called, after whom that valley was named; and Mambre, with his brothers, was Abram's confederate, as will appear in the next chapter. It is to be understood, moreover, that Abram, being most obedient, fulfilled this command of God at once. This vale is also [[13:18|in Hebron|in Hebron]], that is, near Hebron. [[13:18|and he built there an altar to the Lord|Ædificavitque ibi altare Domino]], for the same reasons as elsewhere, as has already been shown.

paras.t: Præterea, juxta spiritualem intelligentiam, per ascensum Abræ et conjugis ac domesticorum ipsius ab Ægypto ad plagam australem, significatur ascensio Christi et fidelium ejus ad orientem lucis æternæ ac patriam Beatorum, in qua ferventissimus calor est Solis justitiæ. Per divitias vero ipsorum in argento et auro, spiritualis opulentia Catholicorum in omni virtute et gratia, præsertim in caritate et sapientia, designatur. Per rixas demum pastorum Abram et Lot, intelligitur contentio, quæ est inter justos et injustos prælatos, seu inter catholicos et hæreticos propter greges eis subjectos: quoniam justi et catholici præsidentes maxime dolent, dum vident populum Dei ab impiis perfidisve prælatis negligi, scandalizari, ac male doceri et decipi. Amplius, exemplo Abræ discamus esse solliciti servare unitatem spiritus in vinculo pacis, nec solum superioribus cedere ac parere, sed et inferioribus humiliter loqui, pie deferre, et omnem contentionis, iræ, impatientiæ, cupiditatis inquietudinem evitare: quod et religiosis summe est necessarium, quum sanctus testetur Hieronymus: Nulla vita deterior est, quam corpore simul manere, et animo dissentire. Et vere infelices sunt, quibus non unum, sed diversum cor est.
paras.en: Further, according to the spiritual understanding, by the going up of Abram with his wife and household from Egypt to the southern quarter is signified the ascension of Christ and his faithful to the rising of eternal light [orientem: the east, or the rising of the sun] and the homeland of the Blessed, where the heat of the Sun of justice is most fervent. By their riches in silver and gold is denoted the spiritual wealth of Catholics in every virtue and grace, especially in charity and wisdom. By the strife of the herdsmen of Abram and Lot, lastly, is understood the contention that exists between just and unjust prelates, or between Catholics and heretics, over the flocks subject to them: for just and Catholic rulers grieve most when they see God's people neglected, scandalized, badly taught and deceived by wicked or faithless prelates. Moreover, by Abram's example let us learn to be [[Eph 4:3|careful to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace|solliciti servare unitatem spiritus in vinculo pacis]], and not only to give way to our superiors and obey them, but also to speak humbly to our inferiors, to defer to them kindly, and to avoid all the unrest of contention, anger, impatience and covetousness. This is supremely necessary for religious too [religious: members of religious orders], since holy Jerome testifies: No life is worse than to stay together in body and disagree in mind. And truly unhappy are they who have not one heart, but different hearts.

paras.t: Insuper promissio Abræ facta de multiplicatione sobolis suæ, multo præclarius est impleta in multiplicatione fidelium christianorum, qui juxta Apostolum ad Galatas, per fidem sunt filii Abrahæ. Semini quoque Abrahæ, utpote Christo secundum naturam humanam, data est in sempiternum, non solum Chanaan terra, sed totus orbis terrarum: cujus semen, id est plebs christiana instar pulveris innumerabilis facta est. Unde Pater ait ad Christum: Postula a me, et dabo tibi gentes hæreditatem tuam, et possessionem tuam terminos terræ. Constat item quod Christus per prædicatores suos gloriosos Apostolos, terram in longitudine ac latitudine perambulavit.
paras.en: Moreover, the promise made to Abram of the multiplying of his offspring has been fulfilled far more gloriously in the multiplying of the Christian faithful, who, according to the Apostle writing to the Galatians, are children of Abraham through faith[[Gal 3:7||]]. To the seed of Abraham also, namely to Christ according to his human nature, there has been given for ever not only the land of Chanaan but the whole world; and his seed, that is, the Christian people, has become like the dust, beyond number. Hence the Father says to Christ: [[Ps 2:8|Ask of me, and I will give thee the Gentiles for thy inheritance, and the utmost parts of the earth for thy possession|Postula a me, et dabo tibi gentes hæreditatem tuam, et possessionem tuam terminos terræ]]. It is likewise clear that Christ, through his preachers the glorious Apostles, walked through the land in its length and breadth.

14.title: Elucidatio litteralis capituli quartidecimi: Factum est autem in illo tempore
14.title_en: Literal explanation of the fourteenth chapter: And it came to pass at that time

paras.t: FACTUM est autem in illo tempore. In isto capitulo describitur fidelitas Abræ, et constantia ejus ac fortitudo, quorum occasione recitatur hic bellum inter gentilium reges peractum, nec est difficultas in littera. Factum est, inquit, ut Amraphel rex Sennaar, id est Chaldææ seu Babylonis; atque ut Lyra refert, Hebræi communiter dicunt, quod Amraphel iste fuit Nemrod, quem dicunt fuisse binomium. Quod si verum est, vixisset Nemrod iste valde diu. Fuit enim filius Chus filii Cham, qui Cham fuit filius Noe, a quo Abram decimus fuit. Et Arioch rex Ponti, et Chodorlahomor rex Elamitarum. Sicut in Scholastica historia dicitur, jam dominandi libido in tantum processerat, quod pene quælibet civitas habuit regem. Quorum plurimi subditi erant alicui regi majori, et tandem omnes monarchæ alicui, ac primum monarchæ Assyriorum. Et Thadal rex Gentium, id est, qui rex Gentium appellatur, vel propter multitudinem gentium sibi subditarum, vel quia in ejus dominio erant homines plurium nationum.
paras.en: [[14:1|And it came to pass at that time|FACTUM est autem in illo tempore]]. In this chapter are described the faithfulness of Abram, and his constancy and fortitude; on the occasion of these a war waged among kings of the Gentiles is here related, and there is no difficulty in the letter. [[14:1|And it came to pass|Factum est]], he says, [[14:1|that Amraphel, king of Sennaar|ut Amraphel rex Sennaar]], that is, of Chaldea or Babylon. And, as Lyra reports, the Hebrews commonly say that this Amraphel was Nemrod, who they say had two names. If that is true, this Nemrod would have lived a very long time: for he was the son of Chus, the son of Cham, and Cham was the son of Noe, from whom Abram was the tenth. [[14:1|and Arioch, king of Pontus, and Chodorlahomor, king of the Elamites|Et Arioch rex Ponti, et Chodorlahomor rex Elamitarum]]. As is said in the Scholastic History, the lust of lordship had by then gone so far that almost every city had its king. Most of these were subject to some greater king, and at length all of them to some monarch, and first of all to the monarch of the Assyrians. [[14:1|and Thadal, king of nations|Et Thadal rex Gentium]], that is, he who is called king of nations, either because of the multitude of nations subject to him, or because there were men of many nations in his dominion.

paras.t: Inirent bellum contra Bara regem Sodomorum, et ceteros quatuor qui in littera exprimuntur: qui quinque regnaverunt in quinque urbibus regionis quæ vocatur Pentapolis, a πέντε, quod est quinque, et πόλις, civitas, inter quos rex Sodomorum dicitur fuisse principalis. Pro eo autem quod nostra translatio habet, Contra Sennaab regem Adamæ, dicit Lyra in Hebræo haberi, Regem Balæ; estque Bala nomen civitatis, quæ alio nomine dicitur Segor. Sed non apparet sic esse, quum in littera alius rex Balæ introducatur, nec aliter essent quinque reges, de quibus hic sermo. Adama quoque fuit alia urbs quam Bala. Omnes isti, videlicet quinque reges Pentapolis, convenerunt in vallem Silvestrem, quæ præcedenti capitulo appellatur vallis Illustris: quæ nunc est mare Salis, id est, post subversionem Pentapolis, facta et vocata est lacus salsissimus et mare Mortuum, quoniam nullus piscis in eo vivere potest, propter spissitudinem et ineptitudinem aquæ illius, quæ tam spissa et sordida est, ut pannus in ea potius inquinetur quam lavetur.
paras.en: [[14:2|Made war against Bara, king of Sodom|Inirent bellum contra Bara regem Sodomorum]], and the other four who are named in the letter. These five reigned in the five cities of the region called Pentapolis, from πέντε, which is “five,” and πόλις, “city”; among them the king of Sodom is said to have been the chief. Where our translation has [[14:2|against Sennaab, king of Adama|Contra Sennaab regem Adamæ]], Lyra says that the Hebrew has “the king of Bala”; and Bala is the name of a city which by another name is called Segor. But it does not appear to be so, since in the letter another king of Bala is brought in, and otherwise there would not be the five kings of whom the passage speaks. Adama, too, was a different city from Bala. [[14:3|All these|Omnes isti]], namely the five kings of the Pentapolis, [[14:3|came together into the woodland vale|convenerunt in vallem Silvestrem]], which in the preceding chapter is called the illustrious vale: [[14:3|which now is the salt sea|quæ nunc est mare Salis]], that is, after the overthrow of the Pentapolis it was made, and was called, a lake most salt and the Dead Sea, since no fish can live in it, because of the thickness and unfitness of its water, which is so thick and foul that a cloth is rather soiled in it than washed.

paras.t: Deinde subjungitur causa prælii hujus. Duodecim enim annis servierant quinque reges prædicti, Chodorlahomor regi Elamitarum, qui subjugaverat eos sibi, ita quod dederunt ei tributum duodecim annis: et in tertiodecimo anno recesserunt ab eo per rebellionem, non per loci mutationem, de quo recessu Joram rex Israel loquitur in quarto Regum libro, Moab recessit a me.
paras.en: Next the cause of this battle is added. For [[14:4|twelve years|Duodecim enim annis]] the five kings aforesaid [[14:4|had served|servierant]] [[14:4|Chodorlahomor|Chodorlahomor]], king of the Elamites, who had subjugated them, so that they paid him tribute for twelve years: [[14:4|and in the thirteenth year they revolted from him|et in tertiodecimo anno recesserunt ab eo]], by rebellion, not by a change of place. Of such a revolt Joram, king of Israel, speaks in the fourth book of Kings: [[4 Kings 3:7|Moab is revolted from me|Moab recessit a me]].

paras.t: Igitur quartodecimo anno venit Chodorlahomor, et reges qui cum eo erant, percusseruntque Raphaim, id est quosdam fortes seu gigantes natos de Raphaim, aut Raphaim nominatos, in Astaroth, hoc est in loco sic nuncupato; et Carnaim et Zuzim cum eis, id est nationes sic appellatas, quæ erant terribiles et robustæ, secundum Hieronymum, occiderunt cum præfatis gigantibus Raphaim; et Emim, id est populum sic vocatum, in Save Cariathaim, hoc est, in civitate seu loco sic dicto occiderunt, et Chorræos in montibus Seir, id est gentem sic nominatam, habitantem in montibus Seir, quæ gens infra vocatur Horræi, usque ad campestria Pharan, id est urbis sic nuncupatæ, quæ est in solitudine. Reversique sunt quatuor reges prædicti, et venerunt usque ad fontem Misphat, id est ad locum fontis illius, in quo loco Deus postea produxit filiis Israel aquam de petra: ideo subditur, ipsa est Cades, quia sic dictus est locus ille alio nomine, de quo loco infra habebitur. Et secundum Hieronymum, vocatur fons Judicii, quoniam Deus judicavit populum Israel contra se murmurantem, vel, ut alii dicunt, Moysen et Aaron, qui fuerunt ibi increduli Deo, videlicet ad aquas Contradictionis, propter quod Deus tulit contra eos sententiam, quod non ingrederentur terram promissionis. Quidam dicit, quod vocetur fons Judicii, quoniam judices terræ illius convenerunt ibi ad determinandum judicia. Sed mirum si in loco isto deserto convenerunt ad judicandum. Et percusserunt omnem regionem Amalecitarum, id est populum regionis illius, in qua postea habitaverunt Amalecitæ, qui tempore hujus belli nondum fuerunt nati: et Amorrhæum, hoc est populum Amorrhæorum, natum ex Amorrhæo filio Chanaan, filii Cham, ut dictum est capitulo decimo: qui habitabat in Asasonthamar, id est in loco sic nominato, qui in libro Paralipomenon vocatur Engaddi, secundum quosdam.
paras.en: [[14:5|And in the fourteenth year came Chodorlahomor, and the kings that were with him|Igitur quartodecimo anno venit Chodorlahomor, et reges qui cum eo erant]]: [[14:5|and they smote the Raphaim|percusseruntque Raphaim]], that is, certain strong men or giants born of Raphaim, or called Raphaim, *in Astaroth*, that is, in a place so named; *and Carnaim* [Denis reads Astaroth and Carnaim as two names; the Douay-Rheims has the one name Astarothcarnaim] [[14:5|and the Zuzim with them|et Zuzim cum eis]], that is, nations so called, which according to Jerome were fearsome and strong, they slew together with the aforesaid giants, the Raphaim; [[14:5|and the Emim|et Emim]], that is, a people so called, [[14:5|in Save of Cariathaim|in Save Cariathaim]], that is, in a city or place so called, they slew; [[14:6|And the Chorreans in the mountains of Seir|et Chorræos in montibus Seir]], that is, a nation so named, dwelling in the mountains of Seir, which nation is called below the Horites, [[14:6|even to the plains of Pharan|usque ad campestria Pharan]], that is, of the city so called, [[14:6|which is in the wilderness|quæ est in solitudine]]. [[14:7|And they returned|Reversique sunt]], the four kings aforesaid, [[14:7|and came to the fountain of Misphat|et venerunt usque ad fontem Misphat]], that is, to the site of that fountain, in which place God afterwards brought forth water from the rock for the children of Israel. Therefore it is added, [[14:7|the same is Cades|ipsa est Cades]], because that place is so called by another name; of this place more will be said below. And according to Jerome it is called the fountain of Judgment, because God judged the people of Israel when they murmured against him; or, as others say, because he judged Moses and Aaron, who were unbelieving towards God there, namely at the waters of Contradiction, for which God passed sentence against them that they should not enter the land of promise[[Num 20:12||]]. Someone says that it is called the fountain of Judgment because the judges of that land gathered there to determine judgments. But it would be strange if they gathered in this desert place to judge. [[14:7|and they smote all the country of the Amalecites|Et percusserunt omnem regionem Amalecitarum]], that is, the people of that country in which the Amalecites afterwards dwelt, who at the time of this war were not yet born; [[14:7|and the Amorrhean|et Amorrhæum]], that is, the people of the Amorrheans, born of Amorrheus the son of Chanaan, the son of Cham, as was said in chapter ten; [[14:7|that dwelt in Asasonthamar|qui habitabat in Asasonthamar]], that is, in a place so named, which in the book of Paralipomenon is called Engaddi, according to some.

paras.t: Quæri potest, cur præfati quatuor reges, qui venerunt ad pugnandum contra quinque reges Pentapolis, interfecerunt tot alios populos. Ad quod aliqui dicunt, quod populi illi fuerunt adversarii trium regum qui venerunt cum prædicto rege Elamitarum, qui adjuvit eos ad dejiciendum adversarios eorumdem, deinde adjuverunt eum contra reges Pentapolis. Scriptura autem non exprimit illud, ut dicunt, quia non concernit facta Abræ et Lot.
paras.en: It may be asked why the four kings aforesaid, who came to fight against the five kings of the Pentapolis, killed so many other peoples. To this some say that those peoples were enemies of the three kings who came with the aforesaid king of the Elamites; he helped them to put down their enemies, and then they helped him against the kings of the Pentapolis. But Scripture does not set this down, they say, because it does not concern the deeds of Abram and Lot.

paras.t: Et egressi sunt rex Sodomorum, etc. Hic recitatur qualiter in valle Silvestri congressi sunt quinque reges Pentapolis contra quatuor reges prædictos. Et terga verterunt, cecideruntque ibi. Porro in textu statim ante hæc verba habetur, Vallis autem Silvestris habebat puteos multos bituminis: et ita quod dictum est, Cecideruntque ibi, exponunt quod rex Sodomorum, et rex Gomorrhæ cum multis de suo exercitu fugientes, corruerunt in puteos illos, a quibus tamen exisse dicuntur, vel humano vel divino auxilio. Nam paulo post subditur, quod rex Sodomorum venit obviam Abræ post hæc. Potest tamen exponi, quod quidam ex eorum populo sint occisi in valle illa. Et qui remanserunt, fugerunt ad montem, id est, qui a quatuor regibus illis occisi non sunt, ad loca confugerunt montana. Denique vallis ista habebat bituminis puteos, vel quia ex foveis illis erumpebat et tollebatur bitumen, vel quia inde accipiebatur materia ex qua cæmentum sive bitumen fiebat. Tulerunt autem omnem substantiam Sodomorum, etc.: necnon et Lot et omnem substantiam ejus, etc. Hoc fecerunt quatuor reges victores horum quinque regum, quemadmodum moris est in bello, diripere spolia devictorum.
paras.en: [[14:8|And the king of Sodom|Et egressi sunt rex Sodomorum]], etc. Here it is related how in the woodland vale the five kings of the Pentapolis joined battle with the four kings aforesaid. And they [[14:10|turned their backs, and were overthrown there|terga verterunt, cecideruntque ibi]]. Now in the text, just before these words, stands: [[14:10|Now the woodland vale had many pits of slime|Vallis autem Silvestris habebat puteos multos bituminis]]; and so what is said, [[14:10|and were overthrown there|Cecideruntque ibi]] [the Latin *ceciderunt* is literally “they fell”], they explain thus: that the king of Sodom and the king of Gomorrha, fleeing with many of their army, fell into those pits, from which, however, they are said to have come out, by human or by divine help; for a little later it is added that after this the king of Sodom came out to meet Abram. Yet it can also be explained that some of their people were slain in that vale. [[14:10|and they that remained, fled to the mountain|Et qui remanserunt, fugerunt ad montem]], that is, those who were not slain by those four kings fled to the mountain country. Further, this vale had pits of slime [*bitumen*, pitch], either because bitumen burst forth from those hollows and was taken from them, or because from there was taken the material of which cement or bitumen was made. [[14:11|And they took all the substance of the Sodomites|Tulerunt autem omnem substantiam Sodomorum]], etc.: [[14:12|And Lot also|necnon et Lot]] [[14:12|and his substance|et omnem substantiam ejus]], etc. This the four kings did, the victors over these five kings, as the custom is in war, to carry off the spoils of the vanquished.

paras.t: Et ecce unus qui evaserat de prælio, ut quidam de exercitu regis Sodomorum, nuntiavit Abram Hebræo, id est ex semine Heber nato. Ex quo patet, quod Judæi et Israelitæ dicuntur Hebræi non ab Abram, quasi Abræi, sed ab Heber, ut dictum est. Iste fugiens a prælio, scivit Lot esse nepotem Abræ, ipsumque Abram esse virum potentem et sapientem: ideo nuntiavit ei captivitatem et adversitatem sui nepotis. Qui Abram habitavit in valle Mambre Amorrhæi, id est in valle quæ nomen accepit a viro nomine Mambre, qui fuerat Amorrhæus; itaque in valle Mambre Amorrhæi fratris Eschol et fratris Aner, quia hi duo viri, videlicet Eschol et Aner, fuerunt fratres carnales istius Mambre. Hi enim pepigerant fœdus cum Abram, id est, pactum amicitiæ secum inierant. Ubi quæri potest, cur vir ille fidelis cum infidelibus illis pepigerit pactum tale. Respondetur, quod ex quo inter illos demorabatur, poterat in licitis et honestis cum ipsis contrahere fœdus, præsertim quatenus hac occasione traheret eos ad cultum unius Dei. Quod et forsitan antea fecit, quamvis Scriptura non referat hoc.
paras.en: [[14:13|And behold one, that had escaped|Et ecce unus qui evaserat]] from the battle, as it were one of the army of the king of Sodom, [[14:13|told Abram the Hebrew|nuntiavit Abram Hebræo]], that is, born of the seed of Heber. From this it is plain that the Jews and Israelites are called Hebrews not from Abram, as though Abreans, but from Heber, as has been said. This man, fleeing from the battle, knew that Lot was Abram's nephew, and that Abram himself was a powerful and wise man; therefore he told him of the captivity and misfortune of his nephew. [[14:13|who dwelt in the vale of Mambre the Amorrhite|Qui Abram habitavit in valle Mambre Amorrhæi]], that is, in the vale that took its name from a man named Mambre, who had been an Amorrhite; thus in the vale of Mambre the Amorrhite, [[14:13|the brother of Escol, and the brother of Aner|fratris Eschol et fratris Aner]], because these two men, namely Eschol and Aner, were brothers in the flesh of this Mambre. [[14:13|for these had made a league with Abram|Hi enim pepigerant fœdus cum Abram]], that is, they had entered into a pact of friendship with him. Here it may be asked why that faithful man made such a pact with those unbelievers. The answer is that, since he was living among them, he could make a league with them in things lawful and honest, especially so that by this occasion he might draw them to the worship of the one God; which perhaps he had already done before, though Scripture does not relate it.

paras.t: Quod quum audisset Abram, captum videlicet Lot fratrem suum, numeravit expeditos vernaculos suos, hoc est, numerando alumnavit servos suos ad pugnam aptos, trecentos decem et octo. Ex quo patet quam magnus et dives vir fuerit. Accepit etiam secum tres fratres prælatos sibi confœderatos, de quibus probabile est, quod et ipsi non paucos de suis famulis et propinquis secum assumpserint. Et persecutus est eos, scilicet quatuor reges prænominatos, usque Dan, id est usque ad fontem nomine Dan qui est unus duorum fontium ex quibus emanat Jordanis. Circa quod ait Glossa: Ex duobus fontibus non multum a se distantibus, rivus in unum collectus, vocatur Jordanis. Nam alter fons Jor dicitur. Interea Abram persecutus est reges istos, non quod reges a facie ejus fugerunt, imo nihil sciverunt de ejus adventu. Et divisis sociis, id est vernaculis suis in tres turmas partitis, ut ex tribus locis hostes invaderet. Sic et Gedeon trecentos viros suos divisit in totidem partes. Vel, divisis sociis, id est vernaculis suis separatis a tribus fratribus illis et eorum auxiliariis, irruit super eos nocte, utpote improvise, et percussit eos, id est, dormientes invasit ac trucidavit, usque Hoba, id est locum sic dictum, et Phœnicem urbem, quæ est ad lævam, id est sinistram, Damasci. Quum enim plurimi excitati fugam arriperent, persecutus est, et fugientes prostravit, quia præ securitate incauta erant paulo ante inebriati, et prorsus inepti ad prælium.
paras.en: [[14:14|Which when Abram had heard, to wit, that his brother Lot was taken|Quod quum audisset Abram, captum videlicet Lot fratrem suum]], [[14:14|he numbered of the servants born in his house|numeravit expeditos vernaculos suos]], that is, by numbering them he mustered his servants fit for battle [the printed word is *alumnavit*, perhaps for *adunavit*, “gathered”], [[14:14|three hundred and eighteen, well appointed|trecentos decem et octo]]. From this it is plain how great and rich a man he was. He also took with him the three brothers mentioned before, his confederates, of whom it is likely that they too took with them not a few of their own servants and kinsmen. [[14:14|and pursued them|Et persecutus est eos]], namely the four kings named before, [[14:14|to Dan|usque Dan]], that is, as far as the spring called Dan, which is one of the two springs from which the Jordan flows. On this the Gloss says: From two springs not far from one another a stream gathered into one is called the Jordan; for the other spring is called Jor [so that the two names together make *Jordan*]. Abram, then, pursued these kings; not that the kings fled from before his face; on the contrary, they knew nothing of his coming. [[14:15|And dividing his company|Et divisis sociis]], that is, his servants being parted into three bands, so that he might fall upon the enemy from three places. So too Gedeon divided his three hundred men into as many parts[[Judg 7:16||]]. Or, [[14:15|dividing his company|divisis sociis]], that is, his servants being separated from those three brothers and their auxiliaries: [[14:15|he rushed upon them in the night|irruit super eos nocte]], that is, unexpectedly, [[14:15|and defeated them|et percussit eos]], that is, he fell upon them asleep and slaughtered them, [[14:15|as far as Hoba|usque Hoba]], that is, the place so called, and the city of Phoenicia, [[14:15|which is on the left hand|quæ est ad lævam]], that is, on the left side, [[14:15|of Damascus|Damasci]]. For when very many of them were roused and took to flight, he pursued them and laid the fugitives low, since in their careless security they had shortly before been drinking deep, and were altogether unfit for battle.

paras.t: Reduxitque omnem substantiam et Lot, mulieres quoque, quas reges illi ex urbibus Pentapolis secum duxerunt captivas, et populum captum, qui erat de exercitu quinque regum. Egressus est autem rex Sodomorum in occursum ejus, videlicet Abræ, postquam reversus est a cæde, id est occisione seu percussione regum quatuor prædictorum. Egressus est, inquam, in occursum ei in valle Save, id est sic appellata, quæ est vallis Regis: nam alio nomine dicta est vallis Regis, ab aliquo rege quicumque fuerit ille, propter aliquod speciale quod rex iste in valle illa commisit aut habuit, aut aliquid tale.
paras.en: [[14:16|And he brought back all the substance, and Lot|Reduxitque omnem substantiam et Lot]], [[14:16|the women also|mulieres quoque]], whom those kings had led away captive with them from the cities of the Pentapolis, [[14:16|and the people|et populum]] taken captive, which was of the army of the five kings. [[14:17|And the king of Sodom went out to meet him|Egressus est autem rex Sodomorum in occursum ejus]], namely Abram, [[14:17|after he returned from the slaughter|postquam reversus est a cæde]], that is, the killing or smiting, [[14:17|of the kings|regum]], the four aforesaid. He went out, I say, to meet him [[14:17|in the vale of Save|in valle Save]], that is, so called, [[14:17|which is the king's vale|quæ est vallis Regis]]; for by another name it was called the King's vale, from some king, whoever he was, because of something special that this king did or had in that vale, or some such thing.

paras.t: Et vero Melchisedech rex Salem, id est civitatis, quæ postea Jerusalem est vocata, proferens panem et vinum, non ad reficiendum ipsum Abram et populum ejus, ut dicunt infideles Judæi, quoniam Abram et populus ejus portaverunt secum spolia et victualia regum quos occiderant, ita quod cibariis abundabant; sed protulit panem et vinum, ad offerendum Domino pro gratiarum actione de victoria Abræ concessa. Propter quod subditur: Erat enim sacerdos Dei summi. In lege enim naturæ primogeniti erant sacerdotes. Et interdum sacerdotium transferebatur a primogenito ad posterius natum, sicut et jus primogenituræ ex inspiratione et ordinatione divina. Sacerdotium quoque Melchisedech fuit figura sacerdotii Christi, ut infra tangetur. Benedixit ei, videlicet Abræ tanquam major minori, imprecando ei bona: et ait: Benedictus Abram Deo excelso, id est, ad laudem et gloriam Dei sublimis, est Abram benedictus et laude dignus, seu Domino deputatus; et benedictus Deus excelsus. Deus autem essentialiter benedictus est, tanquam in se ipso perfectus et sanctus, et omni bono nomine superdignissimus, omnis etiam benedictionis et gratiæ causa. Quo protegente, id est auxiliante et defendente te, o Abram, hostes in manibus tuis sunt, id est, subjecti sunt tibi et victi a te. Et dedit ei decimas ex omnibus, id est, Abram dedit Melchisedech regi decimas, de omnibus spoliis aut etiam aliis rebus tanquam majori ac sacerdoti. Denique, ut in Scholastica historia fertur, tunc primo leguntur decimæ datæ. Primitiæ vero ab Abel Deo oblatæ leguntur.
paras.en: [[14:18|But Melchisedech, the king of Salem|Et vero Melchisedech rex Salem]], that is, of the city which was afterwards called Jerusalem, [[14:18|bringing forth bread and wine|proferens panem et vinum]], not to refresh Abram himself and his people, as the unbelieving Jews say, since Abram and his people carried with them the spoils and victuals of the kings whom they had slain, so that they had food in plenty; but he brought forth bread and wine to offer them to the Lord in thanksgiving for the victory granted to Abram. For this reason it is added: [[14:18|for he was the priest of the most high God|Erat enim sacerdos Dei summi]]. For in the law of nature the firstborn were priests; and sometimes the priesthood was transferred from the firstborn to one born later, as was the right of the firstborn too, by divine inspiration and ordinance. The priesthood of Melchisedech, moreover, was a figure of the priesthood of Christ, as will be touched on below. [[14:19|Blessed him|Benedixit ei]], namely Abram, as the greater blesses the less, praying good things upon him: [[14:19|and said: Blessed be Abram by the most high God|et ait: Benedictus Abram Deo excelso]], that is, to the praise and glory of God on high Abram is blessed and worthy of praise, or devoted to the Lord; [[14:20|And blessed be the most high God|et benedictus Deus excelsus]]. Now God is blessed in his essence, as perfect and holy in himself, and supremely worthy of every good name, and the cause too of all blessing and grace. [[14:20|by whose protection|Quo protegente]], that is, by whose help and defence, O Abram, [[14:20|the enemies are in thy hands|hostes in manibus tuis sunt]], that is, they are subject to thee and conquered by thee. [[14:20|And he gave him the tithes of all|Et dedit ei decimas ex omnibus]], that is, Abram gave King Melchisedech tithes of all the spoils, or of other things too, as to his superior and to a priest. Lastly, as is related in the Scholastic History, this is the first time that tithes are read of as given; but firstfruits are read of as offered to God by Abel.

paras.t: Dixit autem rex Sodomorum, qui egressus fuit obviam Abræ, ad honorandum eum, et ad regratiandum ei, quod adversarios a quibus ipse victus erat, prostravit et spolia retulit: Da mihi animas, hoc est, captivos restitue mihi, qui de populo meo sunt, ut revertantur ad propria: cetera tolle tibi, id est, substantiam seu spolia reserva pro te et auxiliaribus tuis. Qui respondit ei: Levo manum meam ad Deum excelsum possessorem cæli et terræ, id est, per Deum omnium creatorem ac dominum, elevata manu, juro: et dicunt quod iste fuit modus jurandi: quod a filo subtegminis usque ad corrigiam caligæ non accipiam, id est, penitus nihil, quantumlibet parvum, sumam, ex omnibus quæ tua sunt, id est, tua erant antequam succubuisti, et ea perdidisti in bello, vel quæ adhuc tua sunt de jure aut facto; ne dicas, Ego ditavi Abram, hoc est, ne inde te jactes et mihi improperes. Nec ex superbia dixit hoc Abram, sed quoniam Deus ei promiserat, quod benediceret ei in omnibus, ideo noluit suam locupletationem adscribi hominibus. Exceptis his quæ comederunt juvenes, id est, vernaculi mei qui pugnaverunt, quorum expensas jam factas ex spoliis, non persolvo nec reddo: et partibus virorum, hoc est spoliis seu stipendiis quæ juste debentur viris Amorrhæis, qui venerunt mecum, videlicet Aner, Eschol et Mambre. Isti accipiant partes suas, quæ jure prælii eis debentur. Circa quod ait Glossa: Abram vir justus manus suas excutit ab omni munere. In quo ostenditur, quod bella a fidelibus non cupiditate, sed caritate et æquitate committenda sunt. Stipendia quoque militantium excipit, et partes eorum qui secum pugnaverunt, partim justitiam suam demonstrans, partim stipendia legitime pugnantibus debita non abnuens.
paras.en: [[14:21|And the king of Sodom said|Dixit autem rex Sodomorum]], who had gone out to meet Abram, to honour him and to thank him for having laid low the enemies by whom he himself had been beaten, and for having brought back the spoils: [[14:21|Give me the persons|Da mihi animas]] [literally “souls”], that is, give me back the captives who are of my people, that they may return to their homes; [[14:21|and the rest take to thyself|cetera tolle tibi]], that is, keep the goods or spoils for thyself and for thy auxiliaries. [[14:22|And he answered him: I lift up my hand to the Lord God the most high, the possessor of heaven and earth|Qui respondit ei: Levo manum meam ad Deum excelsum possessorem cæli et terræ]], that is, with my hand raised I swear by God, the creator and lord of all; and they say that this was the manner of swearing: [[14:23|That from the very woof thread unto the shoe latchet|quod a filo subtegminis usque ad corrigiam caligæ]] [[14:23|I will not take|non accipiam]], that is, I will take nothing at all, however small, [[14:23|of any things that are thine|ex omnibus quæ tua sunt]], that is, that were thine before thou wast beaten and lost them in the war, or that are still thine by right or in fact; [[14:23|lest thou say: I have enriched Abram|ne dicas, Ego ditavi Abram]], that is, lest thou boast of it and cast it in my teeth. Nor did Abram say this out of pride, but because God had promised him that he would bless him in all things; therefore he would not have his enrichment ascribed to men. [[14:24|Except such things as the young men have eaten|Exceptis his quæ comederunt juvenes]], that is, my servants who fought, whose expenses, already met out of the spoils, I do not pay back or restore; [[14:24|and the shares of the men|et partibus virorum]], that is, the spoils or wages justly owed to the Amorrhite men, [[14:24|that came with me|qui venerunt mecum]], namely [[14:24|Aner, Escol, and Mambre: these shall take their shares|Aner, Eschol et Mambre. Isti accipiant partes suas]], which are owed them by the right of war. On this the Gloss says: Abram, a just man, [[Is 33:15|shaketh his hands from all bribes|manus suas excutit ab omni munere]]. In this it is shown that wars are to be waged by the faithful not out of greed, but out of charity and equity. He also excepts the wages of those who served under him, and the shares of those who fought with him, partly showing his own justice, partly not refusing the wages owed to those who fight lawfully.

paras.t: Præterea de isto Melchisedech scribit Hieronymus, quod Hebræi dicunt eum fuisse Sem filium Noe; et omnes primogenitos a Noe usque ad Aaron, sacerdotes fuisse, qui in conviviis et oblationibus populo benedicebant.
paras.en: Moreover, of this Melchisedech Jerome writes that the Hebrews say he was Sem, the son of Noe; and that all the firstborn from Noe down to Aaron were priests, who blessed the people at feasts and offerings.

paras.t: In Scholastica quoque habetur historia, quod aliqui dicunt, a præfata victoria Abræ et remissione captivorum quos reduxit, annum jubilæum habuisse initium, et quod ideo institutus est quinquagesimus, quia Lot tunc erat quinquagenarius. Vel, quia quinquaginta anni fluxerunt, ex quo Dominus erat Abræ locutus, quando egrediebatur de Haran. Verumtamen verius dici videtur, quod annus jubilæus et quinquagenarius fuit primo divinitus per Moysen institutus, atque in hoc facto Abræ præfiguratus. Nec istud de annis Lot seu tempore allocutionis illius divinæ ad Abram, certitudinem habet.
paras.en: In the Scholastic History, too, it is said that some hold that the year of jubilee had its beginning from the aforesaid victory of Abram and the release of the captives whom he brought back; and that it was fixed at the fiftieth year for this reason, that Lot was then fifty years old; or because fifty years had passed since the Lord had spoken to Abram when he was going out from Haran. Yet it seems truer to say that the year of jubilee, the fiftieth year, was first instituted by God through Moses, and was prefigured in this deed of Abram. Nor is there any certainty in what is said of Lot's years, or of the time of that divine address to Abram.

paras.t: Præterea de excellentia Melchisedech et sacerdotio ejus, et qualiter Christus dicitur sacerdos factus in æternum, secundum ordinem Melchisedech, multa scribit Apostolus in epistola ad Hebræos, inter cetera dicens: Præcursor pro nobis introivit Jesus secundum ordinem Melchisedech, pontifex factus in æternum. Hic enim Melchisedech rex Salem, sacerdos Dei summi, cui et decimas omnium divisit Abraham, qui Melchisedech interpretatur rex justitiæ: deinde autem et rex Salem, quod est rex pacis; sine patre, sine matre, sine genealogia, neque initium dierum, neque finem habens, assimilatus autem Filio Dei, manet sacerdos in perpetuum. Quocirca pensandum, quia ut scribit Thomas in tertia parte Summæ suæ, quæstione 21. In officio sacerdotis duo considerantur: primum est ipsa oblatio: secundum, sacrificii consummatio, per quam hi pro quibus sacrificium immolatur, effectum sacrificii consequuntur. Effectus autem sacrificii Christi, quo obtulit se ipsum in ara crucis, est consecutio felicitatis æternæ. Passus est enim pro nobis, propter bona futura, cœlestia et æterna. Ideo sacerdotium Christi vocatur æternum. Et item idcirco, quoniam aliud sacerdotium non succedet ei in vita præsenti.
paras.en: Moreover, of the excellence of Melchisedech and his priesthood, and of how Christ is said to have been made [[Ps 109:4|a priest for ever according to the order of Melchisedech|sacerdos factus in æternum, secundum ordinem Melchisedech]], the Apostle writes much in the epistle to the Hebrews, saying among other things: [[Heb 6:20|the forerunner Jesus is entered for us, made a high priest for ever according to the order of Melchisedech|Præcursor pro nobis introivit Jesus secundum ordinem Melchisedech, pontifex factus in æternum]]. [[Heb 7:1|For this Melchisedech was king of Salem, priest of the most high God|Hic enim Melchisedech rex Salem, sacerdos Dei summi]], [[Heb 7:2|To whom also Abraham divided the tithes of all|cui et decimas omnium divisit Abraham]], who, Melchisedech, [[Heb 7:2|by interpretation is king of justice|interpretatur rex justitiæ]]: [[Heb 7:2|and then also king of Salem, that is, king of peace|deinde autem et rex Salem, quod est rex pacis]]; [[Heb 7:3|Without father, without mother, without genealogy, having neither beginning of days nor end of life, but likened unto the Son of God, continueth a priest for ever.|sine patre, sine matre, sine genealogia, neque initium dierum, neque finem habens, assimilatus autem Filio Dei, manet sacerdos in perpetuum]]. Hence it is to be considered that, as Thomas writes in the third part of his Summa, question 21 [the passage is in question 22, article 5], in the office of a priest two things are considered: first, the offering itself; second, the consummation of the sacrifice, by which those for whom the sacrifice is offered obtain the effect of the sacrifice. Now the effect of the sacrifice of Christ, by which he offered himself on the altar of the cross, is the attainment of eternal happiness; for he suffered for us for the sake of good things to come, heavenly and eternal. Therefore the priesthood of Christ is called eternal; and also for this reason, that no other priesthood will succeed it in the present life.

paras.t: Præterea sacerdotium Christi et sacerdotium evangelicæ legis, in multis excellit sacerdotium veteris legis, quoniam aufert peccata, et æternaliter manet: quod significatum est per sacerdotium Melchisedech, qui decimas sumpsit ab Abram, in cujus lumbis quodammodo decimatus est Levi seu legalis sacerdos. Unde sacerdotium Christi, dicitur secundum ordinem Melchisedech, propter eminentiam veri sacrificii quod est Christus, seu Sacramentum altaris super sacrificia legis Mosaicæ. Sacrificium enim Melchisedech, quod fuit oblatio panis et vini, in Ecclesia continuatur et consummatur usque ad finem mundi. Et quantum ad hoc, sacerdotium Melchisedech perfectius præfiguravit sacerdotium Christi, quam sacerdotium illud legale. Verumtamen advertendum, quia ut tactum est, in sacerdotio Christi duo pensantur, puta oblatio, oblationisque effectus. Quantum ad primum, sacerdotium legale magis perfecte præfiguravit sacerdotium Christi, quam sacerdotium Melchisedech, quia in sacrificiis legis fiebat effusio sanguinis, sicut et Christus se offerendo sanguinem suum fudit pro nobis. Sed quoad effectum quemdam oblationis Christi, qui est mystica unitas Ecclesiæ, sacerdotium Melchisedech magis perfecte præfiguravit sacerdotium Christi. Obtulit namque Melchisedech panem et vinum, per quæ unitas Ecclesiæ designatur, quam Christus per fidem caritatemque colligit. Propterea sub speciebus panis et vini, sacrificium Christi atque Ecclesiæ frequentatur.
paras.en: Moreover, the priesthood of Christ and the priesthood of the law of the Gospel excel the priesthood of the old law in many ways, since it takes away sins and abides for ever. This was signified by the priesthood of Melchisedech, who took tithes from Abram, in whose loins Levi, that is, the priest of the law, was in a manner tithed[[Heb 7:9||]][[Heb 7:10||]]. Hence the priesthood of Christ is said to be according to the order of Melchisedech because of the pre-eminence of the true sacrifice, which is Christ, or the Sacrament of the altar, over the sacrifices of the Mosaic law. For the sacrifice of Melchisedech, which was the offering of bread and wine, is continued and consummated in the Church until the end of the world. And in this respect the priesthood of Melchisedech prefigured the priesthood of Christ more perfectly than that legal priesthood did. Yet it must be noted that, as was touched on, two things are weighed in the priesthood of Christ, namely the offering and the effect of the offering. As to the first, the legal priesthood prefigured the priesthood of Christ more perfectly than the priesthood of Melchisedech, because in the sacrifices of the law there was a shedding of blood, just as Christ too, in offering himself, shed his blood for us. But as to a certain effect of Christ's offering, which is the mystical unity of the Church, the priesthood of Melchisedech prefigured the priesthood of Christ more perfectly. For Melchisedech offered bread and wine, by which is signified the unity of the Church, which Christ gathers together through faith and charity. Therefore the sacrifice of Christ and of the Church is frequently offered under the species of bread and wine.

paras.t: Amplius, ipse Melchisedech, dicitur sine patre et matre ac genealogia, non habens dierum initium neque finem, quoniam in Scriptura non legitur initium aut finis genealogiæ ipsius. Sed contra hoc objici potest, quoniam pari ratione et ceteri, quorum genealogiæ exordium ac finis non describuntur, dicerentur sine patre et matre, et non habentes finem initiumve dierum. Præterea dictum est, communiterque tenetur, quod Melchisedech fuit Sem filius Noe. Genealogia vero Sem, et initium ac finis vitæ suæ, in Genesi describuntur. Et respondendum quoad primum, quod ceterorum de quibus ait Scriptura canonica, aliquo modo in ipsis Scripturis describitur, aut insinuatur genealogia. Et ita non est de patriarcha Melchisedech. Ad secundum communiter respondetur, quod genealogia Melchisedech, non describitur sub nomine isto Melchisedech, quamvis describatur sub nomine Sem. Contra quod denuo objici posset, quod propter diversitatem nominum non fit in re significata mutatio: idcirco non sequitur, quod genealogia illius viri in Scripturis non exprimatur, quamvis non exprimatur sub nomine isto Melchisedech, imo potius sequitur quod exprimatur, quia sub nomine isto Sem recitatur. Ad quod poterit responderi, quod Melchisedech dicitur sine genealogia et sine patre ac matre, ac sine principio et fine, propter nimiam ejus antiquitatem post diluvium, quæ tanta exstiterat, quod nullus contemporaneus ei, noverat tam principium ejus quam finem, seu parentes ejus ac mortem, sensitiva et præsentiali cognitione.
paras.en: Further, Melchisedech himself is said to be without father and mother and genealogy, having neither beginning of days nor end, because in Scripture no beginning or end of his genealogy is read. But against this it can be objected that by the same reasoning others too, the beginning and end of whose genealogy are not described, would be said to be without father and mother, and to have neither end nor beginning of days. Moreover, it has been said, and it is commonly held, that Melchisedech was Sem, the son of Noe; but the genealogy of Sem, and the beginning and end of his life, are described in Genesis. To the first, it must be answered that of the others of whom canonical Scripture speaks, the genealogy is in some way described, or hinted at, in the Scriptures themselves; and it is not so with the patriarch Melchisedech. To the second it is commonly answered that the genealogy of Melchisedech is not described under this name Melchisedech, although it is described under the name Sem. Against this it could again be objected that a difference of names makes no change in the thing signified; therefore it does not follow that the genealogy of that man is not given in the Scriptures, even though it is not given under this name Melchisedech; rather it follows that it is given, since it is recorded under this name Sem. To this it can be answered that Melchisedech is said to be without genealogy, and without father and mother, and without beginning and end, because of his very great age after the flood, which was so great that no one contemporary with him had known both his beginning and his end, that is, his parents and his death, by the knowledge of sense and of presence [that is, as an eyewitness].

paras.t: Insuper, Melchisedech vocatus est nomine isto Melchisedech, quod interpretatur rex justitiæ, quum antea vocaretur Sem, propter opportunum regimen quo præfuit suis. Et item rex Salem, id est rex pacis, quia in præcipua pace regnavit. Postremo, quia Melchisedech fuit rex Salem seu Jerusalem, quæ est in terra Chanaan, dicunt quidam doctores quod terra Chanaan ordinatione divina et institutione ipsius Noe, pertinuit ad posteros Sem ac filios Israel.
paras.en: Furthermore, Melchisedech was called by this name Melchisedech, which is interpreted king of justice, whereas before he was called Sem, because of the fitting rule with which he governed his people; and likewise king of Salem, that is, king of peace, because he reigned in singular peace. Lastly, because Melchisedech was king of Salem, or Jerusalem, which is in the land of Chanaan, certain doctors say that the land of Chanaan belonged, by divine ordinance and by the appointment of Noe himself, to the descendants of Sem and the children of Israel.

14.title: De spirituali ejusdem capituli quartidecimi intelligentia
14.title_en: On the spiritual understanding of the same fourteenth chapter

paras.t: Pugna quatuor infidelium regum, contra quinque perfidos reges, in primis designat, quod inter ambitiosos et superbos semper sunt jurgia ; quod item iniqui raro concordant ad invicem, imo contra se mutuo præliantur frequenter. Et rursus, quod etiam vitia quædam impugnant se invicem, quemadmodum gula instigat ad esum ac potum superfluum, vana gloria interdum retrahit inde desiderio laudis humanæ. Idem quoque designat, quod quatuor peccata præcipua, quæ quatuor virtutibus cardinalibus exstant contraria, utpote intemperantia, timor inordinatus, indiscretio, injustitia, impugnant quinque hominis sensus, seu potius hominem interiorem per quinque sensus exteriores.
paras.en: The battle of the four unbelieving kings against the five faithless kings signifies, in the first place, that among the ambitious and [[Prov 13:10|the proud there are always contentions|superbos semper sunt jurgia]]; again, that the wicked seldom agree with one another, but rather often make war on each other. And further, that even certain vices fight against one another: as gluttony urges to excessive eating and drinking, while vainglory sometimes draws a man back from it out of desire for human praise. It signifies also that four chief sins, which stand opposed to the four cardinal virtues, namely intemperance, inordinate fear, indiscretion [*indiscretio*, want of discernment, the vice opposed to prudence] and injustice, assail the five senses of man, or rather the inner man through the five outward senses.

paras.t: In hujuscemodi autem pugna interdum etiam aliqui electi et boni, qui designantur per Lot, captivantur vinculis impietatis, corruendo in vitiorum consensum et actum. Quod alius tale malum evadens, et victo compatiens, denuntiat Abræ Hebræo, id est viro contemplativo seu prædicatori devoto, qui virtutibus mox armatus, insequitur invisibiles hostes, et orando seu prædicando reducit ad viam salutis virum bonum qui erat seductus, omnemque substantiam ejus reportat, dum ei cooperatur ad recuperandum spiritualia gratiæ dona quæ perdidit : quibus cognitis, Melchisedech, id est quicumque magnus prælatus, graditur in occursum hujusmodi reductoris benedicitque Deo, et gratias agit ei pro eo, quod dedit suo ministro victoriam contra invisibiles hostes.
paras.en: In a battle of this kind, moreover, sometimes even some of the elect and the good, who are signified by Lot, are taken captive in the bonds of ungodliness, falling into consent to vices and into the deed. This, another who escapes such an evil and has compassion on the one overcome makes known to [[14:13|Abram the Hebrew|Abræ Hebræo]], that is, to a contemplative man or a devout preacher; who, armed at once with the virtues, pursues the invisible enemies, and by praying or preaching leads back to the way of salvation the good man who had been led astray, and brings back all his substance, while he works with him to recover the spiritual gifts of grace which he had lost. When these things are known, [[14:18|Melchisedech|Melchisedech]], that is, any great prelate, goes out to meet such a one who has brought him back, and blesses God, and gives him thanks for having given his minister the victory over the invisible enemies.

paras.t: Occurrit quoque ei rex Sodomorum. Per quod figuratur, quod homini virtuoso frequenter se ingerit vanæ gloriæ et elationis tentatio de opere notabiliter bono ac arduo. Cui vir justus respondere debet cum Abram : Non accipiam ex omnibus quæ tua sunt, id est, in nullo tibi consentiam.
paras.en: Also [[14:17|the king of Sodom went out to meet him|Occurrit quoque ei rex Sodomorum]]. By this is figured that the temptation of vainglory and elation often thrusts itself upon a virtuous man over some work notably good and arduous. To which the just man ought to answer with Abram: [[14:23|I will not take of any things that are thine|Non accipiam ex omnibus quæ tua sunt]], that is, in nothing will I consent to thee.

paras.t: Denique per hoc quod rex Sodomorum dixit ad Abram, Da mihi animas, cetera tolle tibi : insinuatur quod diabolus rex filiorum superbiæ, non aliud quærit finaliter, nisi animas hominum, et cetera eis permittit, dummodo animas rapere permittatur.
paras.en: Lastly, by this, that [[14:21|the king of Sodom said to Abram|rex Sodomorum dixit ad Abram]]: [[14:21|Give me the persons, and the rest take to thyself|Da mihi animas, cetera tolle tibi]] [*animas*, literally ‘the souls’, which is how Denis takes it], it is suggested that the devil, [[Job 41:25|king over all the children of pride|rex filiorum superbiæ]], seeks in the end nothing else but the souls of men, and leaves them the rest, so long as he is allowed to carry off their souls.

paras.t: Insuper per bellum Abræ, qui de fide et obedientia specialiter commendatur, datur intelligi quod virtutes contra vitia jugiter præliantur, præfataque quatuor vitia, imo et universa peccata per fidem formatam et obedientiam sanctam vincantur. Propter quod ait Apostolus : In omnibus sumentes scutum fidei, in quo possitis omnia tela nequissimi ignea exstinguere. Discipulus quoque quem diligebat Jesus : Hæc est, inquit, victoria quæ vincit mundum, fides nostra.
paras.en: Moreover, by the war of Abram, who is especially commended for his faith and obedience, we are given to understand that the virtues ceaselessly do battle against the vices, and that the four vices aforesaid, and indeed all sins, are overcome by formed faith [that is, faith informed by charity] and holy obedience. Wherefore the Apostle says: [[Eph 6:16|In all things taking the shield of faith, wherewith you may be able to extinguish all the fiery darts of the most wicked one|In omnibus sumentes scutum fidei, in quo possitis omnia tela nequissimi ignea exstinguere]]. And the disciple whom Jesus loved: [[1 John 5:4|this is|Hæc est]], he says, [[1 John 5:4|the victory which overcameth the world: Our faith|victoria quæ vincit mundum, fides nostra]].

15.title: Expositio litteralis capituli quintidecimi: His itaque transactis, factus est sermo Domini ad Abram
15.title_en: Literal exposition of the fifteenth chapter: Now when these things were done, the word of the Lord came to Abram

paras.t: His itaque transactis, factus est sermo Domini ad Abram per visionem, hoc est allocutionem internam, imaginariam adspectionem, seu exteriorem atque sensibilem apparitionem in vigilia factam, per modum sæpe prætactum, Noli timere, inordinato, carnali, aut humano timore. Abram. Qui in terra aliena habitavit ut peregrinus, victis tot regibus, poterat formidare, ne impugnaretur a successoribus et propinquis regum illorum, atque ut aliqui dicunt, verebatur, ne grandis illa victoria, qua vicit quatuor reges, esset tota merces suæ justitiæ. Sed non apparet, quod vir tantæ illuminationis, putaverit temporalem et exteriorem illum triumphum, esse condignum et sufficiens præmium actuum meritoriorum, et vere virtuosorum. Abram autem ex multis revelationibus scivit se esse in statu salutis.
paras.en: [[15:1|Now when these things were done, the word of the Lord came to Abram by a vision|His itaque transactis, factus est sermo Domini ad Abram per visionem]], that is, by an inward speaking, an imaginary seeing [that is, a vision formed in the imagination], or an outward and sensible appearance made while he was awake, in the manner often touched on already: [[15:1|Fear not|Noli timere]], with an inordinate, carnal or human fear, [[15:1|Abram|Abram]]. For he dwelt as a pilgrim in a strange land and, having conquered so many kings, could dread being attacked by the successors and kinsmen of those kings; and, as some say, he feared that that great victory, in which he conquered four kings, might be the whole reward of his justice. But it does not seem likely that a man of such enlightenment thought that temporal and outward triumph a worthy and sufficient reward for meritorious and truly virtuous acts. Abram, moreover, knew from many revelations that he was in the state of salvation.

paras.t: Ego protector tuus sum contra visibiles et invisibiles hostes tuos, ut vel ad mortale peccatum induci non poteris, vel si inductus fueris, tamen finaliter non peribis. Denique Deus protector est omnium in se sperantium, ac diligentium eum, qui tamen interdum vincuntur et cadunt: quod non est ex defectu divinæ protectionis, sed ex infirmitate et negligentia eorumdem. Sunt autem diversi gradus protectionis divinæ. Nam Virginem gloriosam protexit non solum ab omni mortali, sed item ab omni veniali peccato: sanctificatos autem in utero, et confirmatos in gratia, protexit dumtaxat ab omni mortali, ne laberentur in illud. Indiguit autem Abram protectione divina, præcipue quoniam in medio idololatrarum ac pessimorum tunc morabatur, ne cum perversis illis perverteretur. Et merces tua magna nimis, hoc est, magnum valde præmium tibi paratum est pro obedientia tua et ceteris tuis virtutibus. Porro merces illa magna nimis, non poterat esse temporale aut exterius bonum dumtaxat, quum illud non sit sufficiens præmium operis virtuosi, sed beatifica deitatis fruitio, quæ est incomparabile bonum, et quodammodo infinitum, utpote infiniti increatique boni immediata, secura, et sempiterna possessio.
paras.en: [[15:1|I am thy protector|Ego protector tuus sum]] against thy enemies visible and invisible, so that either thou shalt not be able to be led into mortal sin, or, if thou art led into it, thou shalt nevertheless not perish in the end. Indeed God is [[Ps 17:31|the protector of all that trust in him|protector est omnium in se sperantium]] [the margin's reference to the Psalm cannot be read; the words are those of Ps 17:31], and of those who love Him; who nevertheless are sometimes overcome and fall: and this is not from any defect of the divine protection, but from their own weakness and negligence. Now there are different degrees of the divine protection.
