paras.en: [[16:10|And again he said: I will multiply thy seed exceedingly, and it shall not be numbered for multitude|Et rursum: Multiplicans, inquit, multiplicabo semen tuum, et non numerabitur præ multitudine]]. This will be fulfilled at the end of the world, when the Synagogue will be converted to the Lord by the preaching of Enoch and Elias[[Mal 4:5||]].

paras.t: Ac deinceps: Ecce, ait, concepisti et paries filium, vocabisque nomen ejus Ismael. Synagoga in hac sua captivitate atque miseria videtur agere aliquid boni, unum verum Deum aliquo modo colendo et invocando, et in Scripturis veteris Testamenti se occupando, aut alia opera ex suo genere bona agendo, pro quibus in hac vita suam consequitur qualemcumque retributionem, et datur ei a Deo carnalis quædam fecunditas, pro qua Deum precatur, quæ per Ismael designatur. Denique soboles hujus incredulæ Synagogæ, instar Ismaelis, crudelis est, ita quod manus ejus est contra omnes, et manus omnium contra eam. Judæi namque increduli, ex suis prædecessoribus per propagationem naturæ et imitationem malitiæ nati, non obstante omni eorum calamitate et vastitate, hominibus se præferunt universis, et omnes alias gentes earumque leges despiciunt, præsumentes se solos pertinere ad Dominum. De quibus dixit Apostolus quod Deo non placent, et cunctis hominibus adversantur: sicque figunt tabernacula sua e regione universorum fratrum suorum, quoniam ex Scripturis suis præsumunt se posse omnibus suis adversariis disputando spiritualiter prævalere.
paras.en: [[16:11|And again: Behold, said he, thou art with child, and thou shalt bring forth a son: and thou shalt call his name Ismael|Ac deinceps: Ecce, ait, concepisti et paries filium, vocabisque nomen ejus Ismael]]. The Synagogue in this her captivity and misery seems to do some good, worshipping and calling upon the one true God after a fashion, and busying herself with the Scriptures of the Old Testament, or doing other works good in their kind [that is, good in what is done, though not done in grace and so not meritorious]; for these she obtains in this life some reward or other, and there is given her by God a certain carnal fruitfulness, for which she prays to God; and this is signified by Ismael. Finally, the offspring of this unbelieving Synagogue is cruel like Ismael, so that [[16:12|his hand will be against all men, and all men's hands against him|manus ejus est contra omnes, et manus omnium contra eam]]. For the unbelieving Jews, born of their forebears by the propagation of nature and the imitation of their malice, in spite of all their calamity and desolation, prefer themselves to all men, and despise all other nations and their laws, presuming that they alone belong to the Lord. Of them the Apostle said that they [[1 Thess 2:15|please not God, and are adversaries to all men|Deo non placent, et cunctis hominibus adversantur]]; and so they pitch their tents [[16:12|over against all his brethren|e regione universorum fratrum suorum]], since they presume that out of their Scriptures they can prevail spiritually over all their adversaries in disputation.

paras.t: Vocavit autem Agar nomen Domini qui loquebatur ad eam, Tu Deus qui vidisti me. Synagoga nempe usque in præsens jactat se a Deo præcipue adspici, illuminari ac dirigi, neminemque esse in statu salutis, nisi filios suos, se quoque Deum contemplari per creaturas affirmat, dicendo: Profecto hic vidi posteriora videntis me. Allegorice vero per posteriora Dei, intelliguntur incarnatio, humanitas, passio, et cetera Christi mysteria, quæ Patres veteris Testamenti per fidem et prophetiæ gratiam contemplabantur.
paras.en: [[16:13|And she called the name of the Lord that spoke unto her: Thou the God who hast seen me|Vocavit autem Agar nomen Domini qui loquebatur ad eam, Tu Deus qui vidisti me]]. For the Synagogue boasts even to the present day that she is especially looked upon, enlightened and directed by God, and that no one is in the state of salvation save her own children; she affirms too that she contemplates God through creatures, saying: [[16:13|Verily, here have I seen the hinder parts of him that seeth me|Profecto hic vidi posteriora videntis me]]. But allegorically, by the hinder parts of God are understood the incarnation, the humanity, the passion and the other mysteries of Christ, which the Fathers of the Old Testament contemplated by faith and by the grace of prophecy.

paras.t: Propterea appellavit puteum illum, puteum Viventis et videntis me. Synagoga quippe Scripturam suam, cui nec vere credit, quam nec recte intelligit, vehementer extollit, et sapientialem ac saluberrimam esse fatetur, ita ut specialissime reputetur fons et puteus Dei omnia intuentis substantialiterque viventis. Circa quod ait sanctus doctor Hieronymus: Puteus iste significat doctrinam novæ ac veteris legis: quam doctrinam Conditor noster, vita viventium spesque morientium, intuitu propriæ miserationis dedit mortalibus, ut edocti et a vitiis correcti, digni inveniantur visione deitatis perpetua. Ad quam, ut tangit Glossa, Deum toto corde et proximos tanquam nos ipsos sinceriter diligendo, suspirare semper debemus, et festinare ad eam cum omni gratiarum actione, contemplando assidue posteriora, hoc est præfata Christi mysteria salvatoris, utpote quæ, quanta, et qualia pro nostra salute assumpsit, fecit, ac pertulit Unigenitus Patris æterni, sectando quoque indesinenter vestigia ejus.
paras.en: [[16:14|Therefore she called that well, the well of him that liveth and seeth me|Propterea appellavit puteum illum, puteum Viventis et videntis me]]. For the Synagogue vehemently extols her Scripture, which she neither truly believes nor rightly understands, and declares it to be full of wisdom and most wholesome, so that it is held in a most special way to be the fountain and well of God, who beholds all things and lives by his very substance. On this the holy doctor Jerome says: This well signifies the doctrine of the new and of the old law; which doctrine our Maker, the life of the living and the hope of the dying, gave to mortals out of regard for his own mercy, that, being taught and corrected of their vices, they may be found worthy of the everlasting vision of the Godhead. To this vision, as the Gloss touches on, we ought ever to sigh, loving God with our whole heart and our neighbours as ourselves sincerely, and to hasten to it with all thanksgiving, contemplating assiduously the hinder parts, that is, the aforesaid mysteries of Christ the Saviour, namely what things, how great and of what kind the Only-begotten of the eternal Father took upon him, did and endured for our salvation; following also unceasingly in his steps[[1 Pet 2:21||]] [the margin note is partly unreadable, showing only "I Pe"; 1 Pet 2:21, "that you should follow his steps", fits].

17.title: Elucidatio litteralis capituli septimidecimi: Postquam vero nonaginta et novem annorum esset
17.title_en: Literal explanation of the seventeenth chapter: And after he began to be ninety and nine years old

paras.t: QUANTUM Abram patriarcha crevit ætate, tantum crevit in beneficiis Dei et omni virtute, sicut describitur consequenter: Postquam vero nonaginta et novem annorum esse cœperat, apparuit ei Dominus, dixitque ad eum: Ego Dominus omnipotens. Quasi dicat: Facile mihi est adimplere quæcumque voluero, et quæ tibi promisero. Qualiter facta sit visio ista, Scriptura non exprimit: an scilicet fuerit imaginaria et in somno exhibita, an potius sensibilis et in vigilia facta. Porro ex circumstantia textus, magis videtur quod facta sit, sicut et præcedentes, per angelum in humana specie apparentem, atque in persona Dei loquentem. Ambula coram me, id est, secundum beneplacitum meum vive, ut conversatio tua per approbationem inspiciatur a me. Unde alia translatio habet: Complace coram me. Vel, Ambula coram me, id est, tam reverenter et timorate conversare in meo conspectu, ac si jugiter cerneres me præsentem, hoc est, ubique et semper cogita me præsentem, et omnia intuentem, et juxta exigentiam considerationis istius habe te coram me: et esto perfectus, prout perfectio viatoribus competere potest: quæ perfectio potissime sita est in actu caritatis divinæ, ut scilicet Deus toto corde sinceriter diligatur, omni inordinata affectione circa creata exclusa, quatenus homo nec se ipsum, nec aliud quodcumque creatum diligat, nisi in Deo et secundum Deum.
paras.en: As much as the patriarch Abram grew in age, so much did he grow in the benefits of God and in every virtue, as is next described: [[17:1|And after he began to be ninety and nine years old, the Lord appeared to him: and said unto him: I am the Almighty God|Postquam vero nonaginta et novem annorum esse cœperat, apparuit ei Dominus, dixitque ad eum: Ego Dominus omnipotens]] [Denis reads *Dominus omnipotens*, "the almighty Lord", where the Vulgate has *Deus omnipotens*]. As if to say: It is easy for me to fulfil whatever I will, and whatever I shall promise thee. How this vision took place Scripture does not state: that is, whether it was imaginary [that is, formed in the imagination, not seen with the bodily eyes] and shown in sleep, or rather sensible [that is, perceived by the senses] and made while he was awake. But from the circumstances of the text it seems rather that it took place, like the preceding ones, through an angel appearing in human form and speaking in the person of God. [[17:1|walk before me|Ambula coram me]], that is, live according to my good pleasure, so that thy manner of life may be looked upon by me with approval. Hence another translation has: Be pleasing before me. Or, [[17:1|walk before me|Ambula coram me]], that is, live as reverently and fearfully in my sight as if thou didst continually see me present; that is, everywhere and always think of me as present and beholding all things, and bear thyself before me as that thought requires: [[17:1|and be perfect|et esto perfectus]], so far as perfection can belong to wayfarers[[Matt 5:48||]] [that is, to men still on the way in this life, not yet in the heavenly fatherland]: which perfection consists above all in the act of divine charity, namely that God be loved sincerely with the whole heart, every inordinate affection for created things being shut out, so that a man love neither himself nor any other created thing except in God and according to God.

paras.t: Ponamque fœdus meum inter me et te, id est, amicitiæ pactum et promissionem, seu recens circumcisionis mandatum ac legem, inter me et te constituam ac firmabo: et multiplicabo te vehementer nimis, hoc est, valde innumerabiliter multos faciam generari ex filiis tuis: quod constat impletum in Judæis, qui descenderunt ex Abraham per Isaac; et Idumæis, qui ex Abraham sunt per Esau nati; et Sarracenis, qui ex eodem sunt orti per Ismaelem; imo et aliæ plures gentes descenderunt ex Abraham, ut infra habetur. Cecidit Abram pronus in faciem, humiliando se majestati divinæ quantum valebat, et regratiando ei ex intimo corde super beneficiis et promissis ipsius.
paras.en: [[17:2|And I will make my covenant between me and thee|Ponamque fœdus meum inter me et te]], that is, I will set up and confirm between me and thee a pact of friendship and a promise, or the new command and law of circumcision: [[17:2|and I will multiply thee exceedingly|et multiplicabo te vehementer nimis]], that is, I will cause very many, beyond number, to be born of thy sons: which plainly was fulfilled in the Jews, who descended from Abraham through Isaac; and in the Idumeans, who are born of Abraham through Esau; and in the Saracens, who sprang from him through Ismael; indeed many other nations also descended from Abraham, as is told below. [[17:3|Abram fell flat on his face|Cecidit Abram pronus in faciem]], humbling himself before the divine majesty as much as he could, and giving him thanks from the bottom of his heart for his benefits and promises.

paras.t: Dixitque ei Deus: Ego sum, et pactum meum tecum. Quasi dicat: Sicut ego sum invariabiliter et infallibiliter Veritas ipsa, qui solus plene et incircumscriptibiliter sum, sic pactum præfatum ratum erit, et tecum fixum manebit. Erisque pater multarum gentium, quæ post mortem tuam nascentur successive ex filiis tuis. Nec ultra vocabitur nomen tuum Abram, quod interpretatur pater excelsus, et dicitur Abram ab ABBA, quod est pater, et RAM, quod interpretatur excelsus: quod nomen potest competere viro sublimi, quamvis perpauci nascantur ex eo, et cito deficiat posteritas ejus; sed appellaberis Abraham, quod interpretatur pater multarum, et subauditur, gentium. Idcirco ratio hujus immutationis et novæ appellationis subjungitur: quia patrem multarum gen[…], id est, facere te decrevi patrem populorum multorum. Est enim pater cunctorum fidelium spiritualis, quemadmodum ad Romanos et Galatas docet Apostolus. Est quoque pater carnalis multorum gentium ex suis filiis genitarum, ut factum est, plenius patebat.
paras.en: [[17:4|And God said to him: I am, and my covenant is with thee|Dixitque ei Deus: Ego sum, et pactum meum tecum]]. As if to say: As I am, unchangeably and unfailingly, Truth itself, who alone am fully and without bounds, so the aforesaid covenant shall be ratified and shall remain fixed with thee. [[17:4|and thou shalt be a father of many nations|Erisque pater multarum gentium]], which after thy death shall be born one after another of thy sons. [[17:5|Neither shall thy name be called any more Abram|Nec ultra vocabitur nomen tuum Abram]], which is interpreted *high father*: Abram is so called from *ABBA*, which is *father*, and *RAM*, which is interpreted *high*: a name that can fit a lofty man, even if very few are born of him and his posterity soon fails; [[17:5|but thou shalt be called Abraham|sed appellaberis Abraham]], which is interpreted *father of many*, *nations* being understood. Therefore the reason for this change and new name is added: [[17:5|because|quia]] [[17:5|a father of many|patrem multarum]] […], that is, I have decreed to make thee the father of many peoples. For he is the spiritual father of all the faithful, as the Apostle teaches in the Epistles to the Romans and the Galatians[[Rom 4:11||]][[Gal 3:7||]] [the two margin notes here cannot be read; these verses are the likeliest]. He is also the father according to the flesh of many nations begotten of his sons, as was done, and was made more fully plain.

paras.t: Regesque ex te egredientur, non immediate, sed mediate, id est, ex posteris tuis reges nascentur, quia prælatæ gentes habuerunt ex semine suo plurimos reges; et statuam pactum meum jam dictum inter […], id est, ordinabo atque præcipiam ut pactum istud observetur a te et posteris tuis in generationibus suis, fœdere sempiterno, id est perpetua pactione seu ritu jugiter duraturo; ut sim Deus tuus et seminis tui post te, id est, quatenus ego qui sum omnium Deus jure creationis et universalis imperii, sim specialiter Deus tuus et posterorum tuorum fidem tuam sequentium, per specialem provisionem, pietatem et gratiam mei circa te et illos, atque per fidem et cultum, quibus a te et illis colar ac honorabor.
paras.en: [[17:6|and kings shall come out of thee|Regesque ex te egredientur]], not immediately but mediately, that is, kings shall be born of thy descendants, since the aforesaid nations had very many kings of their own seed; [[17:7|And I will establish my covenant|et statuam pactum meum]] already spoken of, [[17:7|between|inter]] […], that is, I will ordain and command that this covenant be kept by thee and thy descendants [[17:7|in their generations, by a perpetual covenant|in generationibus suis, fœdere sempiterno]], that is, by a perpetual pact or a rite lasting continually; [[17:7|to be a God to thee, and to thy seed after thee|ut sim Deus tuus et seminis tui post te]], that is, so that I, who am the God of all by right of creation and of universal rule, may be in a special way thy God and the God of thy descendants who follow thy faith, through my special providence, kindness and grace towards thee and them, and through the faith and worship with which I shall be worshipped and honoured by thee and them.

paras.t: Circa hoc quæritur, qualiter Deus dicatur pactum istud statuisse ad Abraham et posteros ejus fœdere sempiterno, quum istud de præcepto circumcisionis intelligatur, ut paulo post in isto habetur capitulo, quod præceptum in evangelicæ legis promulgatione finem accepit. Ad hoc Augustinus respondet, quod in tali locutione, æternum, pro sæculo sumitur. Sæculum vero accipitur multis modis. Porro Thomas super quartum Sententiarum: Æternum, inquit, hic pro sæculo capitur, quod habet finem, sed finis ejus non est nobis determinatus. Vel dicendum, quod circumcisio corporalis potuit esse in fœdus æternum, quantum ad suum significatum, et quantum ad id quod ei succedit, quemadmodum fides dicitur a quibusdam semper manere ratione beatificæ visionis quæ ei succedit in patria. Hinc super illud, Fœdere sempiterno, habetur in Glossa, quia aliquid sempiternum significabat. Quid autem significaverit, mox dicetur.
paras.en: Here it is asked how God is said to have established this covenant with Abraham and his descendants by a perpetual covenant, since it is understood of the precept of circumcision, as is found a little later in this chapter, a precept which came to an end when the law of the Gospel was promulgated. To this Augustine answers that in such a form of speech *eternal* is taken for *an age* [Latin *sæculum*, a long but limited span of time]. And *an age* is taken in many senses. Thomas, on the fourth book of the Sentences, says: *Eternal* is here taken for *an age*, which has an end, but its end is not fixed for us. Or it must be said that bodily circumcision could be for an eternal covenant as regards what it signified and as regards what succeeds it, as faith is said by some to remain always by reason of the beatific vision which succeeds it in the fatherland. Hence on the words [[17:7|by a perpetual covenant|Fœdere sempiterno]] the Gloss says: because it signified something everlasting. What it signified will be said shortly.

paras.t: Daboque tibi et semini tuo post te terram peregrinationis tuæ omnem, scilicet terram Chanaan, in possessionem æternam. Hic rursus æternum pro sæculo, cujus diuturnus et ignotus est finis, accipitur. Propter quod ait Augustinus: Scriptura vocat æternum, cujus finis non constituitur, aut quod ita sit, ut non sit deinceps faciendum, quantum ad facientis pertinet curam aut potestatem. Vel vocatur possessio ista æterna, secundum Glossam, quia æternum aliquid, utpote cœlestis patriæ habitatio, figuratur per eam. Porro, quod terra ipsa non sit ipsi Abrahæ data ad possidendum, per actualem exhibitionem, sed per certam promissionem, in suis posteris adimplendam, dictum est sæpe.
paras.en: [[17:8|And I will give to thee, and to thy seed|Daboque tibi et semini tuo]] after thee [[17:8|the land of thy sojournment, all|terram peregrinationis tuæ omnem]], namely the land of Chanaan, [[17:8|for a perpetual possession|in possessionem æternam]]. Here again *eternal* is taken for *an age*, whose end is long off and unknown. Therefore Augustine says: Scripture calls eternal that whose end is not fixed, or what is so that it need not be done again, as far as it belongs to the care or power of him who does it. Or, according to the Gloss, this possession is called eternal because something eternal, namely the dwelling in the heavenly fatherland, is figured by it. Moreover, it has often been said that the land itself was not given to Abraham himself to possess by being actually handed over, but by a sure promise, to be fulfilled in his descendants.

paras.t: Circa hæc scribit quidam: Promissiones istæ, frequenter factæ sunt Abrahæ, semper tamen procedendo in expressiorem et majorem promissionem. Quemadmodum enim natura et ars in operibus suis procedunt de imperfecto ad perfectum, ita est in processu divinarum revelationum et promissionum. Ad quod dicendum, quod quamvis interdum sic sit in processu divinarum revelationum et promissionum, non tamen semper: imo frequenter est aliter, quoniam omnipotentia et libertas Altissimi nullis legibus stringitur, nullis terminis coarctatur. Unde quum Christus octo beatitudines prædicaret, primæ beatitudini summum præmium, scilicet regnum cœlorum promisit: Beati, inquit, pauperes spiritu, quoniam ipsorum est regnum cœlorum. Imo exordium prædicationis Christi Præcursorisque sui hoc fuit: Pœnitentiam agite, appropinquabit enim regnum cœlorum. Paulus quoque apostolus in principio suæ conversionis, statim ad tertium raptus est cœlum, et summam sortitus est revelationem.
paras.en: On these things a certain writer says: These promises were often made to Abraham, yet always proceeding to a more explicit and greater promise. For as nature and art proceed in their works from the imperfect to the perfect, so it is in the course of divine revelations and promises. To which it must be said that although it is sometimes so in the course of divine revelations and promises, yet not always: indeed it is often otherwise, since the omnipotence and freedom of the Most High is bound by no laws and confined by no limits. Hence when Christ preached the eight beatitudes, he promised the highest reward, namely the kingdom of heaven, to the first beatitude: [[Matt 5:3|Blessed|Beati]], he says, [[Matt 5:3|are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven|pauperes spiritu, quoniam ipsorum est regnum cœlorum]]. Indeed the beginning of the preaching of Christ and of his Precursor was this: [[Matt 4:17|Do penance, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand|Pœnitentiam agite, appropinquabit enim regnum cœlorum]] [the Precursor's preaching in the same words is at Matt 3:2]. Paul the apostle too, at the beginning of his conversion, was straightway caught up to the third heaven[[2 Cor 12:2||]] and received the highest revelation.

paras.t: Consequenter describitur, qualiter circumcisionis præceptum sit datum. Dixit iterum Deus ad Abraham: Et tu ergo custodies, id est, tibi præcipio ut custodias pactum meum, videlicet circumcisionis præceptum, et semen tuum post te in generationibus suis, etc. Circumcidetur ex vobis omne masculinum, et circumcidetis carnem præputii vestri, id est, circumcidi permittetis seu facietis, ita quod abscidetur extremitas illa membri virilis, ut sit in signum fœderis inter me et vos, id est, quatenus circumcisio ista sit in testimonium atque indicium amicabilis fœderis initi inter me et vos, utpote quod ego sum specialiter Deus vester, et vos populus meus, hoc circumcisionis signaculo tanquam charactere certo, divisus et discretus a ceteris gentibus.
paras.en: Next it is described how the precept of circumcision was given. [[17:9|Again God said to Abraham: And thou therefore shalt keep|Dixit iterum Deus ad Abraham: Et tu ergo custodies]], that is, I command thee to keep [[17:9|my covenant|pactum meum]], namely the precept of circumcision, [[17:9|and thy seed after thee in their generations|et semen tuum post te in generationibus suis]], etc. [[17:10|All the male-kind of you shall be circumcised|Circumcidetur ex vobis omne masculinum]], [[17:11|And you shall circumcise the flesh of your foreskin|et circumcidetis carnem præputii vestri]], that is, you shall let it be circumcised or have it done, so that the end of the male member is cut off, [[17:11|that it may be for a sign of the covenant between me and you|ut sit in signum fœderis inter me et vos]], that is, so that this circumcision may be a testimony and token of the covenant of friendship entered into between me and you, namely that I am in a special way your God, and you my people, set apart and distinguished from the other nations by this seal of circumcision as by a sure mark.

paras.t: In his verbis tria sunt tacta, ad circumcisionem spectantia. Unum est sexus masculinus, aliud determinatio membri, tertium est causa finalis, cur fiebat circumcisio, ut scilicet per eam populus Dei a populo infideli distingueretur; quartum subjungitur, utpote determinatio temporis quo fieri debuit: Infans octo dierum circumcidetur in vobis. Omne masculinum in generationibus vestris, tam vernaculus, id est servus in domo natus in servitute, quam emptitius, id est emptus seu emptione adeptus, circumcidetur, quia ad vestram spectat familiam: et quicumque fuerit de stirpe vestra circumcidetur, quamdiu manserit in vestra familia. Aliqui textus habent: Et quicumque non fuerit de stirpe vestra. Et tunc sensus est, quod etiam alieni a vestra cognatione, circumcidendi sint, antequam in vestram societatem, legem seu ritum suscipiantur.
paras.en: In these words three things touching circumcision are mentioned. One is the male sex, another the determination of the member, the third the final cause [that is, the end or purpose] for which circumcision was done, namely that by it the people of God might be distinguished from the unbelieving people; a fourth is added, namely the determination of the time when it was to be done: [[17:12|An infant of eight days old shall be circumcised among you|Infans octo dierum circumcidetur in vobis]]. [[17:12|every manchild in your generations|Omne masculinum in generationibus vestris]], [[17:12|he that is born in the house|tam vernaculus]], that is, a servant born in the house in servitude, [[17:12|as well as the bought servant|quam emptitius]], that is, one bought or acquired by purchase, [[17:12|shall be circumcised|circumcidetur]], since he belongs to your household: [[17:12|and whosoever|et quicumque]] is [[17:12|of your stock|de stirpe vestra]] shall be circumcised, as long as he remains in your household. Some texts have: [[17:12|and whosoever is not of your stock|Et quicumque non fuerit de stirpe vestra]] [this second reading, with *not*, is that of the Clementine Vulgate and the Douay-Rheims]. And then the sense is that even those who are strangers to your kindred are to be circumcised before they are received into your fellowship, law or rite.

paras.t: Eritque pactum meum in carne vestra, id est, præceptum istud circumcisionis in corpore vestro implebitur, atque in eo apparebit signum pacti istius seu ejus effectus per amputationem pelliculæ membri præfati: in fœdus æternum, juxta sensum præhabitum.
paras.en: [[17:13|And my covenant shall be in your flesh|Eritque pactum meum in carne vestra]], that is, this precept of circumcision shall be fulfilled in your body, and in it shall appear the sign of this covenant, or its effect, by the cutting away of the skin of the aforesaid member: [[17:13|for a perpetual covenant|in fœdus æternum]], in the sense given above.

paras.t: Masculus, cujus præputii caro circumcisa non fuerit, delebitur anima illa de populo suo, id est, masculus ille a numero electorum populi sui separabitur, nec computabitur inter sanctos: quod intelligendum est de masculis ad semen et familiam Abrahæ pertinentibus, quibus dumtaxat dabatur istud præceptum, […] ritum fecit, id est, præceptum istud circumcisionis violavit, si fuit adultæ ætatis, et ex negligentia aut contemptu omisit circumcisionem accipere; vel si fuit infantulus, præceptum seu pactum meum in ipso, non ab ipso, factum est irritum, quia non est servatum in eo, et ita ex aliorum negligentia occasionaliter subsecuta est perditio talis infantis non circumcisi, nisi ei aliunde subveniatur. Circa hæc multæ et magnæ dubitationes occurrunt, quæ infra in speciali tangentur articulo.
paras.en: [[17:14|The male whose flesh of his foreskin shall not be circumcised, that soul shall be destroyed out of his people|Masculus, cujus præputii caro circumcisa non fuerit, delebitur anima illa de populo suo]], that is, that male shall be separated from the number of the elect of his people and shall not be counted among the saints: which is to be understood of the males belonging to the seed and household of Abraham, to whom alone this precept was given, […] [[17:14|hath broken|ritum fecit]], that is, he has violated this precept of circumcision, if he was of adult age and through negligence or contempt failed to receive circumcision; or if he was a little infant, my precept or covenant has been made void in him, not by him, because it was not kept in him; and so through the negligence of others the loss of such an uncircumcised infant followed as by occasion, unless help came to him from elsewhere. On these things many great doubts arise, which will be touched on below in a special article.

paras.t: Denique in Scholastica historia dicitur: Servus primo dictus est a servando. Victores enim victos hostes, quos reservabant ad vitam, servos vocabant. Verna autem aut vernaculus, dicitur qui nutritus est domi. Emptitius, qui in persona propria emptus est. Originarius vero, qui servus est glebæ, puta colonus.
paras.en: Lastly, it is said in the Scholastic History: *Servus* [slave] was first so called from *servare* [to preserve]. For victors called *servi* the conquered enemies whom they kept alive. *Verna* or *vernaculus* [home-born] is said of one reared in the house; *emptitius* [bought], of one bought in his own person; and *originarius* [one bound by birth], of one who is a serf of the soil, that is, a tenant farmer.

paras.t: Deinde describitur immutatio nominis Sarai. Dixit quoque Deus ad Abraham: Sarai uxorem tuam non vocabis Sarai, sed Saram. Circa hæc scribit Hieronymus: Dicunt Hebræi, quod Deus ex nomine suo tetragrammato, litteram HE addidit Abræ et Sarai. Nec mirandum quod quum apud Latinos et Græcos videatur a littera addita, littera HE addita asseratur. Hebræum etenim idioma consuevit h scribere, et a legere, sicut et econtrario, consuevit h pronuntiare, et a scribere. Errant quoque, qui dicunt mutationem nominis Saræ sic factam, quia quum prius scriberetur per duo r, modo scribitur per unum r, aut econverso. Sed quum prius diceretur Sarai, quod interpretatur princeps mea, quasi princeps unius gentis futura, dicta est Saraa, id est princeps absolute, quasi omnium gentium princeps futura, utpote universorum spiritualis mater fidelium. Porro secundum Augustinum, Sara interpretatur virtus: et ideo sic vocata est, quia divina virtute concepit. Unde Apostolus ad Hebræos: Fide, inquit, Sara virtutem accepit, etc. Itaque, sicut propter mysticam significationem mutavit Deus nomen Abræ, ita et Sarai.
paras.en: Next the change of Sarai's name is described. [[17:15|God said also to Abraham: Sarai thy wife thou shalt not call Sarai, but Sara|Dixit quoque Deus ad Abraham: Sarai uxorem tuam non vocabis Sarai, sed Saram]]. On this Jerome writes: The Hebrews say that God added the letter *HE* from his own name of four letters [the Tetragrammaton] to Abram and to Sarai. Nor need one wonder that, though among the Latins and Greeks the letter *a* seems to be added, the letter *HE* is said to be added. For the Hebrew tongue is wont to write *h* and read *a*, and conversely to pronounce *h* and write *a*. They also err who say that Sara's name was changed in this way, that whereas it was formerly written with two *r*'s it is now written with one, or the other way round. But whereas she was formerly called Sarai, which is interpreted *my princess*, as one who was to be princess of one nation, she was called Saraa, that is, *princess* absolutely, as one who was to be princess of all nations, namely the spiritual mother of all the faithful. Further, according to Augustine, Sara is interpreted *virtus* [power, strength]: and she was so called because she conceived by divine power. Hence the Apostle says to the Hebrews: [[Heb 11:11|By faith|Fide]], he says, Sara [[Heb 11:11|received strength|virtutem accepit]], etc. [the Latin *virtus* is both the meaning of her name and the "strength" she received]. And so, as God changed Abram's name for a mystical meaning, so too Sarai's.

paras.t: Et benedicam ei, videlicet Saræ, multiplicando et perficiendo in ea dona gratiæ meæ, supernaturalem quoque fecunditatem et præstando. Et ex illa dabo tibi filium cui benedicturus sum in spiritualibus ac temporalibus utpote Isaac. Quasi dicat: Copiosius benedicam ei, quam Ismaeli aut aliis filiis, quos post Isaac generabis. Eritque in nationes, id est, diversæ tribus et nationes nascentur ex eo, videlicet duodecim tribus Jacob, et Idumæi per Jacob et Esau: et reges populorum orientur ex eo, quia tam filii Israel, quam Idumæi, habuerunt reges ex se ipsis.
paras.en: [[17:16|And I will bless her|Et benedicam ei]], namely Sara, by multiplying and perfecting in her the gifts of my grace, and also by granting her a supernatural fruitfulness. [[17:16|and of her I will give thee a son, whom I will bless|Et ex illa dabo tibi filium cui benedicturus sum]] in spiritual and temporal things, namely Isaac. As if to say: I will bless him more abundantly than Ismael or the other sons whom thou shalt beget after Isaac. [[17:16|and he shall become nations|Eritque in nationes]], that is, various tribes and nations shall be born of him, namely the twelve tribes of Jacob and the Idumeans, through Jacob and Esau: [[17:16|and kings of people shall spring from him|et reges populorum orientur ex eo]], since both the children of Israel and the Idumeans had kings from among themselves.

paras.t: Cecidit Abraham in faciem, id est, Deo humiliter se prostravit, regratiando eidem, et admirando super magnitudine misericordiæ Dei ad se: et risit, non irridendo divina promissa, sed ex prætacta pia admiratione atque ex gaudio spirituali; dicens in corde suo, non disceptando aut discredendo, sed applaudendo promissioni divinæ: Putasne centenario nascetur filius, et Sara nonagenaria pariet? Quasi dicat: Mirabile istud est; et quamvis per naturam fieri nequeat, tamen cum gaudio credo, quod ego jam centenarius, ex conjuge mea Sara nonagenaria filium procreabo. Quod autem non dixit hæc, nec ea quæ consequuntur, ex incredulitate, constat ex verbis Apostoli ad Romanos, dicentis: Non consideravit corpus suum emortuum, quum fere centum esset annorum, nec emortuam vulvam Saræ.
paras.en: [[17:17|Abraham fell upon his face|Cecidit Abraham in faciem]], that is, he humbly prostrated himself before God, giving him thanks and marvelling at the greatness of God's mercy towards him: [[17:17|and laughed|et risit]], not mocking the divine promises, but out of the devout wonder just mentioned and out of spiritual joy; [[17:17|saying in his heart|dicens in corde suo]], not disputing or disbelieving, but applauding the divine promise: [[17:17|Shall a son, thinkest thou, be born to him that is a hundred years old? and shall Sara that is ninety years old bring forth?|Putasne centenario nascetur filius, et Sara nonagenaria pariet?]] As if to say: This is a marvel; and though it cannot happen by nature, yet I believe with joy that I, now a hundred years old, shall beget a son of my wife Sara at ninety. That he did not say these things, nor those that follow, out of unbelief is clear from the words of the Apostle to the Romans, who says: [[Rom 4:19|Neither did he consider his own body, now dead (whereas he was almost an hundred years old), nor the dead womb of Sara|Non consideravit corpus suum emortuum, quum fere centum esset annorum, nec emortuam vulvam Saræ]].

paras.t: Dixitque ad Dominum: Utinam Ismael vivat coram te. Quasi dicat: Magnum reputo, si Ismael jam natus non moriatur ante tempus. De majoribus tamen promissionibus non diffido. Et possunt hæc verba ita exponi: Utinam Ismael spiritualiter vivat virtuose conversando, ne male agendo, sit spiritualiter mortuus coram te, sicut qui impie vivunt. Unde secundum Glossam dixit hoc, desiderando ut filii carnis reputarentur in semine, hoc est, ut posteri Ismaelis inter electos filios computarentur.
paras.en: [[17:18|And he said to God|Dixitque ad Dominum]] [Denis reads *ad Dominum*, "to the Lord"]: [[17:18|O that Ismael may live before thee|Utinam Ismael vivat coram te]]. As if to say: I count it a great thing if Ismael, already born, does not die before his time. Yet I do not distrust the greater promises. These words can also be explained thus: O that Ismael may live spiritually by living virtuously, lest by doing evil he be spiritually dead before thee, like those who live wickedly. Hence, according to the Gloss, he said this desiring that the children of the flesh might be counted for the seed, that is, that the descendants of Ismael might be numbered among the elect sons.

paras.t: Et ait Deus ad Abraham: Sara uxor tua pariet tibi filium, vocabisque nomen ejus Isaac. Circa quod ait Hieronymus: Isaac risus interpretatur, ideo filius iste vocatus est Isaac, non de risu Saræ, sed de risu Abrahæ, qui ex gaudio hujus promissi filii risit. Nam post præenuntiationem nominis hujus legitur Sara risisse, ut patebit. Et constituam pactum meum illi in fœdus sempiternum, et semini ejus post eum, id est, tam filio tuo Isaac quam posteris ejus, injungam observantiam hujus præcepti de circumcisione, ut servent illud in sæculum, juxta expositionem inductam; specialiter autem ad posteros Isaac per Jacob, hoc est, ad duodecim tribus Israel, circumcisio pertinebat, ut infra dicetur.
paras.en: [[17:19|And God said to Abraham: Sara thy wife shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name Isaac|Et ait Deus ad Abraham: Sara uxor tua pariet tibi filium, vocabisque nomen ejus Isaac]]. On which Jerome says: Isaac is interpreted *laughter*; therefore this son was called Isaac, not from Sara's laughter but from the laughter of Abraham, who laughed for joy at this promised son. For it is after the name was foretold that Sara is read to have laughed, as will appear[[Gen 18:10||]]. [[17:19|and I will establish my covenant with him for a perpetual covenant, and with his seed after him|Et constituam pactum meum illi in fœdus sempiternum, et semini ejus post eum]], that is, both on thy son Isaac and on his descendants I will lay the observance of this precept of circumcision, that they may keep it for an age, according to the explanation given; but circumcision belonged in a special way to the descendants of Isaac through Jacob, that is, to the twelve tribes of Israel, as will be said below.

paras.t: Super Ismael quoque exaudivi te, ita quod vivet coram me, sicut rogasti. Circa quod scribit Lyra: Ex hoc dicunt Hebræi, et verum videtur, quod Ismael finivit vitam in bono, id est in statu salutis, seu caritate. Hoc enim Abraham postulavit, dicendo: Utinam Ismael vivat coram te! Verumtamen quidam Sanctorum aliter sentire videntur, præfataque verba multipliciter possunt exponi. In Glossa quoque habetur super verba sequentia: Ecce benedicam ei, in temporalibus, non promissione æterna. Sed de re ista nihil assero. Sarraceni vero dicunt Ismaelem fuisse prophetam Dei, et sanctum virum, suosque posteros docuisse cultum unius Dei, ut in Alcorano Mahometi habetur. Verum liber iste sacrilegus atque mendosus est, quamvis aliqua vera contineantur in eo. Et augebo et multiplicabo eum valde, in posteris suis. Duodecim duces generabit, id est duodecim filios qui erunt capitanei et principes duodecim tribuum suarum.
paras.en: [[17:20|And as for Ismael I have also heard thee|Super Ismael quoque exaudivi te]], so that he shall live before me, as thou hast asked. On which Lyra writes: From this the Hebrews say, and it seems true, that Ismael ended his life in good, that is, in the state of salvation, or in charity. For this is what Abraham asked, saying: [[17:18|O that Ismael may live before thee|Utinam Ismael vivat coram te]]! Yet some of the Saints seem to think otherwise, and the aforesaid words can be explained in many ways. In the Gloss too it is said on the words that follow, [[17:20|Behold, I will bless him|Ecce benedicam ei]]: in temporal things, not by an eternal promise. But on this matter I assert nothing. The Saracens indeed say that Ismael was a prophet of God and a holy man, and taught his descendants the worship of the one God, as is found in Mahomet's Alcoran. But that book is sacrilegious and full of lies, although some true things are contained in it. [[17:20|and increase, and multiply him exceedingly|Et augebo et multiplicabo eum valde]], in his descendants. [[17:20|he shall beget twelve chiefs|Duodecim duces generabit]], that is, twelve sons who shall be the captains and princes of his twelve tribes.

paras.t: Quumque finitus esset sermo loquentis cum eo, id est, quum Deus præinducta verba terminasset, loquendo cum Abraham in subjecta creatura, videlicet per angelum in forma visibili apparentem, ut tangit Glossa, ascendit Deus ab Abraham, hoc est, invisibilem se præbuit, et repente disparendo, ad cœlum reversus est. Quod totum adscribitur Deo, quia angelus sic disparens, repræsentavit Dei personam.
paras.en: [[17:22|And when he had left off speaking with him|Quumque finitus esset sermo loquentis cum eo]], that is, when God had finished the words set down above, speaking with Abraham in a creature subject to him, namely through an angel appearing in visible form, as the Gloss touches on, [[17:22|God went up from Abraham|ascendit Deus ab Abraham]], that is, he made himself invisible and, vanishing suddenly, went back to heaven. All this is ascribed to God because the angel, so vanishing, represented the person of God.

paras.t: Deinde describitur, quam prompte et indilate Abraham implevit divinum præceptum, quia eodem die quo et ista præcepta sunt, circumcidit filium suum Ismaelem, et omnes domesticos suos atque se ipsum: in quo commendatur maxima et ferventissima obedientia ejus, quia et se ipsum circumcidit in tanta ætate. Attenditur quoque ex isto, quam laudabiliter rexit universam familiam suam, quia omnes obediebant ei in re ista tam ardua, credideruntque Abrahæ. In quo innotescit, quantæ auctoritatis fuerit apud illos. Ex quibus littera residua patet.
paras.en: Next it is described how promptly and without delay Abraham fulfilled the divine precept, since on the same day on which these precepts were given he circumcised his son Ismael, and all his household, and himself: in which is commended his very great and most fervent obedience, since he circumcised even himself at so great an age. It is also seen from this how admirably he ruled his whole household, since all obeyed him in so hard a matter and believed Abraham. In which it is made known how great his authority was among them. From these things the rest of the text is clear.

paras.t: Postremo, ex tenore hujus præcepti circumcidunt se Saraceni. Et quoniam pater eorum Ismael tredecim erat annorum quando circumcisus est, circumcidunt pueros suos in tertiodecimo anno vitæ ipsorum. Ex quo constat, quod nec divinum in hoc observant præceptum, quoniam Deus jussit, ut infans octo dierum circumcideretur.
paras.en: Lastly, the Saracens circumcise themselves on the strength of this precept. And because their father Ismael was thirteen years old when he was circumcised[[17:25||]], they circumcise their boys in the thirteenth year of their life. From which it is clear that they do not keep the divine precept even in this, since God commanded that [[17:12|An infant of eight days old|infans octo dierum]] should be circumcised.

17.title: Introductio et solutio quæstionum concernentium præsens capitulum septimumdecimum
17.title_en: Introduction, and solution of the questions concerning the present seventeenth chapter

paras.t: Circa præhabitum textum de circumcisione Abrahæ jussa, quæritur primo, cur Deus eam præcepit. Ad hoc Thomas super quartum Sententiarum, distinctione I, respondet: Circumcisio primo et principaliter necessaria fuit ad expressiorem significationem. Quemadmodum enim oportuit secundum processum temporis crescere fidei explicationem, ita et sacramentalium signorum distinctionem. Porro circumcisio expresse significavit ablutionem originalis peccati: primo, quantum ad membrum generationis, per quod originale transfunditur. Secundo, quantum ad pœnam quæ erat in circumcisione contra delectationem concupiscentiæ, in qua præcipue viget vis fomitis. Tertio, quantum ad sanguinis effusionem, in qua Christi passio designatur, per quam satisfaciendum erat pro originali. Et quantum ad hanc circumcisionis utilitatem, sic definitur: Circumcisio est signaculum curationis ab originali. Ex consequenti quoque fuit alia circumcisionis utilitas, puta distinctio populi fidelis ab infideli, propter fidem ejus cui circumcisio data est primo. Sicque Damascenus eam definiens: Circumcisio, inquit, est signum determinans seu distinguens Israel a gentibus, cum quibus conversabatur.
paras.en: Concerning the text set out above on the circumcision commanded to Abraham, it is asked first why God commanded it. To this Thomas, on the fourth book of the Sentences, distinction 1, answers: Circumcision was necessary first and chiefly for a more express signification. For just as, with the passing of time, the unfolding of the faith had to grow, so too had the distinction of the sacramental signs. Now circumcision expressly signified the washing away of original sin: first, as regards the member of generation, through which original sin is passed on; secondly, as regards the pain there was in circumcision, set against the delight of concupiscence, in which the force of the *fomes* [that is, the tinder of sin: the inclination to evil left in fallen nature] is chiefly strong; thirdly, as regards the shedding of blood, in which the passion of Christ is signified, through which satisfaction was to be made for original sin. And as regards this use of circumcision, it is defined thus: Circumcision is the seal of healing from original sin. In consequence there was also another use of circumcision, namely the distinguishing of the faithful people from the unbelieving, on account of the faith of him to whom circumcision was first given. And so Damascene, defining it, says: Circumcision is a sign marking off, or distinguishing, Israel from the gentiles among whom it lived.

paras.t: Habuit etiam circumcisio mysticam significationem. Primo, moralem, quoniam erat signum castitatis servandæ. Deinde allegoricam, quoniam significavit purgationem per Christum futuram. Tertio, quasi anagogicam, in quantum significabat depositionem corruptibilitatis carnis et sanguinis in resurrectione futura. Hinc asserit Alcuinus: Circumcisionis pactum dabatur in signum, ne misceretur semen Abrahæ gentibus; et quia significavit naturæ renovationem post Baptismum. Servos quoque vernaculos atque emptitios, imo et omnes Abrahæ domesticos præcepit Dominus circumcidi, ad innuendum quod gratia redemptionis Christi pertineret ad omnes.
paras.en: Circumcision also had a mystical signification. First, a moral one, since it was a sign of the chastity to be kept. Next, an allegorical one, since it signified the cleansing that was to come through Christ. Thirdly, a quasi-anagogical one, inasmuch as it signified the putting off of the corruptibility of flesh and blood in the resurrection to come. Hence Alcuin asserts: The covenant of circumcision was given for a sign, that the seed of Abraham should not be mingled with the gentiles; and because it signified the renewal of nature after Baptism. The Lord also commanded the servants, both those born in the house and those bought, and indeed all of Abraham's household, to be circumcised, to intimate that the grace of Christ's redemption would reach to all.

paras.t: Secundo quæritur, cur Deus circumcisionem instituit tempore Abrahæ, ante legem scriptam per Moysen datam. Respondetur, quod lex proprie concernit communitatem, non unam personam dumtaxat: idcirco non debuit dari, nisi populo fideli adunato. Hinc oportuit populum fidelem prius congregari, ab aliisque distingui, quam lex Dei sibi daretur. Hæc autem congregatio et distinctio per aliquod signum fieri debuit, et Deo jubente per circumcisionis signaculum factum est: ideo ante legislationem circumcisio data est. Convenienter quoque hoc factum est tempore Abrahæ, quando genus humanum ex infectione originalis peccati usque ad profundissimum corruit vitiorum, puta ad idololatriam, et vitia contra naturam. Sicque tunc maxime indigebat remedio, et cognitione futuræ purgationis per Christum: idcirco tunc congruebat manifestam fieri promissionem de semine nascituro, in quo omnes gentes benedicerentur, et a vitiis mundarentur. Tunc etiam decent signa castitatis dari contra corruptissimam concupiscentiam carnis. Ideo Abrahæ primo data est circumcisio in signum paternitatis, tanquam ei ex quo nasciturus erat Christus vitiorum destructor, atque in signum fidei ac distinctionis ab infidelibus, et in signum munditiæ observandæ.
paras.en: Secondly it is asked why God instituted circumcision in the time of Abraham, before the written law given through Moses. The answer is that law properly concerns a community, not one person only; and so it ought not to have been given except to a faithful people gathered together. Hence the faithful people had first to be gathered together and set apart from the others before the law of God was given to it. Now this gathering and setting apart had to be done by some sign, and at God's command it was done by the seal of circumcision: therefore circumcision was given before the giving of the law. It was fitting, too, that this should be done in the time of Abraham, when the human race, from the infection of original sin, had fallen into the very depths of vice, namely into idolatry and sins against nature. And so it then stood most in need of a remedy, and of the knowledge of the cleansing to come through Christ: therefore it was fitting then that the promise should be made plain of the seed to be born, in whom all nations should be blessed and cleansed from their vices. Then too it was fitting that signs of chastity should be given against the most corrupt concupiscence of the flesh. Therefore circumcision was first given to Abraham as a sign of fatherhood, as to him of whom Christ, the destroyer of vices, was to be born; and as a sign of faith and of separation from unbelievers; and as a sign of the cleanness to be kept.

paras.t: Tertio quæritur, quomodo circumcisio data est in remedium contra originale peccatum, quum Abraham ante circumcisionis institutionem fuerit ab originali mundatus, eo modo quo alii boni tempore legis naturæ. Respondetur, quod quantum ad Abraham, data non fuit propter purgationem ab originali, sed quantum ad posteros ejus: imo quantum ad Abraham et circumcisos cum eo, purgatos ab originali, fuit a principio data in distinctionem; quantum vero ad alios, principaliter in purgationem.
paras.en: Thirdly it is asked how circumcision was given as a remedy against original sin, since Abraham had been cleansed from original sin before circumcision was instituted, in the way that other good men were in the time of the law of nature. The answer is that as regards Abraham it was not given for cleansing from original sin, but as regards his posterity: rather, as regards Abraham and those circumcised with him, who were already cleansed from original sin, it was given from the beginning as a mark of distinction; but as regards the others, chiefly for cleansing.

paras.t: Quarto quæritur, quum originale peccatum sit generalis infirmitas, atque infectio omnium hominum, quare circumcisionis præceptum datum non fuit cunctis hominibus, sed Abrahæ, et domesticis ac posteris ejus solum. Respondetur, quod quum Christus sit sanctus sanctorum, et universorum sanctificator ac salvator, oportuit populum illum, ex quo ipse fuerat incarnandus, multis privilegiis et prærogativis ornari, et præcipua purificatione pollere. Quoniam ergo ex semine Abrahæ incarnari elegit, ideo ei et posteris ejus, præsertim filiis Israel, præceptum hoc dedit, non solum in purgationem ab originali, sed etiam in distinctionem a populo infideli. Nec tamen ceteris populis defuit remedium originalis peccati. Nam illud quod fuit in lege naturæ, habebant.
paras.en: Fourthly it is asked why, since original sin is a general infirmity and infection of all men, the precept of circumcision was not given to all men, but only to Abraham and his household and posterity. The answer is that, since Christ is [[Dan 9:24|the Saint of saints|sanctus sanctorum]], and the sanctifier and saviour of all, it was fitting that the people from which he was to become incarnate should be adorned with many privileges and prerogatives, and be strong in a special purification. Since, then, he chose to become incarnate of the seed of Abraham, he gave this precept to him and to his posterity, especially the children of Israel, not only for cleansing from original sin but also for distinction from the unbelieving people. Yet the other peoples did not lack a remedy for original sin; for they had that which there was in the law of nature.

paras.t: Quinto quæritur, cur mulieribus non est circumcisio data, quum et ipsæ originali peccato infectæ sint, et a muliere originale peccatum habuerit ortum. Respondetur, quod originale peccatum quoad culpam atque reatum, descendit a primo parente in posteros: sed quoad pœnalitates, a femina: quum pater sit principalis et efficiens causa in generatione, mater vero ministratrix materiæ. Quum ergo circumcisio data sit contra originale ad tollendum culpam, non autem ad auferendum carnis pœnas et corruptionem, constat quod masculis danda fuit, non feminis. Feminæ vero alio remedio purgabantur ab originali, videlicet fide parentum, quantum ad infantulas, seu propria fide, loquendo de adultis, ante ab ipso peccato non expurgatis. Insuper, quamvis prima ista transgressio incepit a femina, vir tamen fuit causa transfusionis originalis peccati. Nam si ipse non peccasset, originale peccatum non fuisset transfusum: idcirco secundum Apostolum, Per unum hominem peccatum intravit in mundum.
paras.en: Fifthly it is asked why circumcision was not given to women, since they too are infected with original sin, and original sin had its beginning from a woman. The answer is that original sin, as regards the guilt and the liability to punishment, comes down from the first father to his posterity, but as regards its penalties, from the woman: since the father is the principal and efficient cause in generation, while the mother supplies the matter. Since, then, circumcision was given against original sin to take away the guilt, not to remove the penalties and corruption of the flesh, it is plain that it was to be given to males, not to females. Women, for their part, were cleansed from original sin by another remedy, namely by the faith of their parents in the case of little girls, or by their own faith, speaking of grown women not cleansed of that sin before. Moreover, although that first transgression began with the woman, yet the man was the cause of the passing on of original sin; for had he not sinned, original sin would not have been passed on. Therefore, according to the Apostle, [[Rom 5:12|by one man sin entered into this world|Per unum hominem peccatum intravit in mundum]].

paras.t: Sexto quæritur, cur Dominus jussit, ut octavo die vitæ infantuli circumcisio fieret, et utrum determinatum tempus illud fuit de necessitate circumcisionis. Ad hæc Thomas respondet, quod circumcisio fuit res præcepta, et etiam sacramentum. Octavus itaque dies, fuit de necessitate circumcisionis, quantum ad obligationem præcepti: propter quod reus fuit transgressionis, qui illo die non circumcidit infantem circumcidendum. Non autem fuit determinatum tempus istud de necessitate circumcisionis, quantum ad efficaciam sacramenti: quia et alio tempore facta, habuit suum sacramentalem effectum, quemadmodum et Baptismus, quamvis aliqua ad solennitatem ejus spectantia omittantur. Præterea litteralis ratio hujus determinati temporis, fuit, secundum Rabbi Moysen, quoniam infans septem primis diebus est tantæ teneritudinis, sicut in utero matris, ideo ante octavum diem ferre non aut vix poterat circumcisionem. Est quoque mystica ratio, quam Magister quarto libro assignat, videlicet ad insinuandum, quod per Christi resurrectionem octavo die factam, circumcidimur a peccatis. In resurrectione quoque communi hoc die futura, per petram Christum omnis ab electis abscindetur corruptio.
paras.en: Sixthly it is asked why the Lord commanded that circumcision be done on the eighth day of the infant's life, and whether that fixed time was of the necessity of circumcision. To this Thomas answers that circumcision was a thing commanded, and also a sacrament. The eighth day, therefore, was of the necessity of circumcision as regards the obligation of the precept: for which reason he who did not circumcise on that day an infant who was to be circumcised was guilty of transgression. But that fixed time was not of the necessity of circumcision as regards the efficacy of the sacrament: for when done at another time too, it had its sacramental effect, just as Baptism does even when some things belonging to its solemnity are left out. Further, the literal reason for this fixed time was, according to Rabbi Moses [that is, Moses Maimonides], that for the first seven days an infant is as tender as in its mother's womb, and so before the eighth day it could not, or could hardly, bear circumcision. There is also a mystical reason, which the Master [Peter Lombard, the Master of the Sentences] gives in the fourth book: namely, to intimate that by the resurrection of Christ, which took place on the eighth day, we are circumcised from our sins. And in the general resurrection too, which is to be on this day, all corruption will be cut away from the elect by the rock, Christ [circumcision was done with knives of stone (Jos 5:2), and "the rock was Christ" (1 Cor 10:4)].

paras.t: Septimo quæritur, quid fiebat de parvulis ante octavum diem defunctis, et an necessitate imminente poterat circumcisio anticipari, et dies octavus præveniri. Ad hæc quidam dixerunt, quod infantuli ante octavum diem defuncti peribant, sicut nunc pueri non baptizati, et quod non licuit tempus præveniri illud præfixum. Hanc opinionem tangit Magister, et auctoritatem Bedæ allegat pro ea, dicentis: Qui nunc in Evangelio terribiliter atque salubriter clamat, Nisi quis renatus fuerit, etc., terribiliter dudum clamavit: Anima cujus præputii caro circumcisa non fuerit, peribit de populo suo. His verbis addit Magister: Forte tamen ingruente necessitate mortis, circumcidebant pueros suos ante octavum diem sine peccato. Porro Hugo de S. Victore ait, quod non licuit tempus anticipari, nec oportebat; quia ut dicit, illis qui moriebantur ante diem octavum valuit contra originale illud remedium quod fuit in lege naturæ: quod confirmatur, primo per Judæos hucusque viventes, qui octavum diem in circumcidendo nunquam præveniunt. Secundo, quoniam nullum animal offerebatur Domino ante diem octavum. Tertio, quoniam super illud Proverbiorum, Unigenitus eram coram matre mea, asserit Glossa, quod primus filius Bethsabee non computatur, quia ante octavum diem defunctus, non fuit nominatus, nec circumcisus. Nempe in circumcisione nomen puero imponebatur, sicut nunc in Baptismo, quoniam Deus mutavit Abrahæ nomen, quando circumcisionis præceptum eidem injunxit. De his quoque qui in deserto […] diu manserunt, dicendum quod dispensatum fuit cum illis quoniam ignorabant quando castra movenda erant: et quandiu seorsum manebant, non oportebat eis signum distinctionis a ceteris gentibus adhiberi.
paras.en: Seventhly it is asked what became of little ones who died before the eighth day, and whether, when necessity pressed, circumcision could be brought forward and the eighth day anticipated. To this some have said that infants who died before the eighth day perished, as children not baptized do now, and that it was not lawful to anticipate that appointed time. The Master touches on this opinion, and cites for it the authority of Bede, who says: He who now in the Gospel cries out, terribly and wholesomely, [[John 3:5|unless a man be born again|Nisi quis renatus fuerit]], etc., cried out terribly long ago: The soul [[17:14|whose flesh of his foreskin shall not be circumcised|cujus præputii caro circumcisa non fuerit]], [[17:14|shall be destroyed out of his people|peribit de populo suo]] [Bede's wording is "the soul … shall perish from his people"]. To these words the Master adds: Perhaps, however, when the danger of death pressed upon them, they circumcised their children before the eighth day without sin. Hugh of St Victor, however, says that it was not lawful to anticipate the time, nor was it needful; because, as he says, for those who died before the eighth day the remedy that there was in the law of nature availed against original sin. This is confirmed, first, by the Jews living to this day, who never anticipate the eighth day in circumcising. Secondly, because no animal was offered to the Lord before the eighth day. Thirdly, because on that verse of Proverbs, I was [[Prov 4:3|as an only son in the sight of my mother|Unigenitus eram coram matre mea]], the Gloss asserts that the first son of Bethsabee is not counted, because, having died before the eighth day[[2 Kings 12:18||]], he was neither named nor circumcised. For in circumcision a name was given to the child, as now in Baptism, since God changed Abraham's name when he laid on him the precept of circumcision. As for those who stayed […] a long time in the desert, it must be said that they were dispensed, since they did not know when the camp was to be moved; and as long as they dwelt apart, there was no need for the sign of distinction from the other nations to be applied to them.

paras.t: Octavo quæritur, an ante circumcisionem suffecit parvulis contra originale fides parentum, aut aliorum. Respondetur, quod originale est peccatum naturæ humanæ, quæ reparari non potuit, nisi per Christum: ideo nunquam remittebatur originale peccatum, nisi per quamdam relationem et continuationem ejus, qui curandus fuit, ad Christum: quod fiebat per fidem. Ideo fides mediatoris fuit semper efficax ad curandum ab originali: in adultis videlicet fides propria, in aliis fides aliena. Verumtamen quidam dixerunt, quod non sufficiebat fides sine protestatione fidei, facta per aliquod exterius signum: ita tamen, quod parvulis sufficiebat fides aliena cum exteriori signo ab aliis facto; adultis autem, fides propria cum signo ab eis facto. Alii dicunt, quod pro parvulis sufficiebat sola fides sine omni exteriori signo, non ipse habitus fidei, sed motus ejus relatus ad salutem pueri ex interiori quadam vi fidei, quicumque fuerit ille, qui professionem seu actum fidei suæ hoc modo referret ad puerum, quamvis hoc amplius pertinuerit ad parentes, per quos originale puer contraxerat, atque ad quos pueri cura spectabat: et istud verius reputatur, quia Gregorius dicit, Quod apud nos valet aqua Baptismi, hoc apud veteres egit pro parvulis sola fides, pro majoribus virtus sacrificii, pro his vero qui ex stirpe Abrahæ prodierunt, circumcisionis mysterium.
paras.en: Eighthly it is asked whether, before circumcision, the faith of the parents or of others sufficed for little ones against original sin. The answer is that original sin is a sin of human nature, which could not be repaired except through Christ; and so original sin was never remitted except through a certain relating and joining to Christ of him who was to be healed, and this was done by faith. Therefore faith in the Mediator was always effective for healing from original sin: in adults, namely, their own faith; in others, the faith of another. Yet some have said that faith did not suffice without a profession of faith made by some outward sign; in such a way, however, that for little ones the faith of another sufficed, with an outward sign made by others, and for adults their own faith, with a sign made by themselves. Others say that for little ones faith alone sufficed, without any outward sign: not the habit of faith itself [that is, the abiding disposition of faith, as distinct from its act], but its movement, referred to the child's salvation by a certain inward power of faith, whoever it might be that referred the profession or act of his faith to the child in this way, although this belonged more to the parents, through whom the child had contracted original sin, and to whom the care of the child belonged. And this is held to be the truer view, because Gregory says: What the water of Baptism does among us, that was done among the ancients by faith alone for little ones, by the power of sacrifice for older persons, and for those who came forth from the stock of Abraham, by the mystery of circumcision.

paras.t: Nono quæritur, an in adultis ad remissionem originalis, requirebatur ultra fidem propriam sacrificium aut aliquid tale. Ad hoc Thomas super quartum respondet: Sacramenta et sacrificia legis naturæ non obligabant ex divino præcepto, sed celebrabantur ex voto seu beneplacito proprio, prout unicuique ratio sua dictavit, ut fidem suam alias profiteretur signo exteriori ad Dei honorem, secundum quod habitus caritatis inclinat ad actus exteriores. Quemadmodum ergo sufficit ad salutem interior actus caritatis quando non adest facultas exterius operandi: sic adultis in lege naturæ sufficiebat sola interior fidei actio, quum et modo sufficiat, quando sacramenta quis dimittit non ex negligentia aut contemptu, sed ipsa fides tempore opportuno instigabat se demonstrari aliquibus exterioribus signis: et quando hujusmodi signa adhibebantur, efficacia remissionis culpæ non erat ex illis exterioribus, sed ex fide interiori. Sicque patet, qualiter intelligenda sint præinducta verba Gregorii. Innotescit quoque ex introductis intellectus verborum Hieronymi, qui effatur: Quæri solet, quomodo feminæ salvabantur, quæ non circumcidebantur. Fide utique et hostiarum oblatione, quemadmodum ante circumcisionem viri sancti mundabantur. Unde in Actorum legitur libro: Fide purificans corda eorum.
paras.en: Ninthly it is asked whether in adults, for the remission of original sin, a sacrifice or something of the kind was required besides their own faith. To this Thomas, on the fourth book, answers: The sacraments and sacrifices of the law of nature did not bind by divine precept, but were celebrated by a man's own vow or good pleasure, as his reason dictated to each, so that he might also profess his faith by an outward sign to the honour of God, according as the habit of charity inclines to outward acts. Just as, then, the inward act of charity suffices for salvation when there is no means of acting outwardly, so for adults in the law of nature the inward action of faith alone sufficed, as it suffices now too when someone omits the sacraments not out of negligence or contempt; but faith itself, at the fitting time, urged that it be shown by some outward signs; and when signs of this kind were used, the power of remitting guilt came not from those outward things but from the inward faith. And thus it is clear how the words of Gregory cited above are to be understood. From what has been said, the meaning of the words of Jerome also becomes known, who says: It is commonly asked how women were saved, who were not circumcised. By faith, surely, and the offering of victims, just as holy men were cleansed before circumcision. Whence we read in the book of Acts: [[Acts 15:9|purifying their hearts by faith|Fide purificans corda eorum]] [the margin gives Acts xv; the words are from v. 9].

paras.t: Decimo quæritur circa illud in textu: Masculus cujus præputii caro circumcisa non fuerit, delebitur anima illa de populo suo, quia pactum meum irritum fecit, quomodo verum sit illud, quum hoc contingere possit absque omni culpa infantis, nec puer ille irritum fecit pactum Dei, sed qui eum circumcidere neglexerunt. Hanc quæstionem Augustinus tangit et solvit, dicendo quod hoc ideo dictum est, quoniam omnes peccaverunt in primo parente. Alia solutio in expositione est tacta.
paras.en: Tenthly it is asked, concerning that in the text, [[17:14|The male whose flesh of his foreskin shall not be circumcised, that soul shall be destroyed out of his people: because he hath broken my covenant|Masculus cujus præputii caro circumcisa non fuerit, delebitur anima illa de populo suo, quia pactum meum irritum fecit]], how that can be true, since this may happen without any fault of the infant, and that child has not broken the covenant of God, but those who neglected to circumcise him. Augustine touches on this question and solves it, saying that it was said for this reason: because all sinned in the first parent. Another solution was touched on in the exposition.

paras.t: Postremo quæritur circa idem, an corporali morte fuerat puniendus qui circumcisionem neglexit. Ad hoc Lyra respondet, quod pater seu tutor pueri negligens puerum octavo circumcidere die, fuit morte ob hoc puniendus: similiter puer non circumcisus, si adultam ætatem adeptus, negligeret circumcisionem accipere. Sed his contradicit Rabbi Paulus, affirmans quod circumcisionem omittens, non erat morte puniendus, etiam secundum Hebræos. Non enim hic dicitur, morte moriatur, sicut in aliis criminibus quæ lex morte punivit. Verumtamen prima responsio verior esse videtur: primo, quoniam lex peccata multo minora transgressione hujus præcepti, morte punivit, ut patet in multis, et de eo qui fuerat lapidatus, quia ligna collegit in sabbato. Secundo, quia Apostolus loquitur ad Hebræos: Irritam quis faciens legem Moysis, absque ulla contradictione duobus aut tribus testibus moritur. Alia multa possent de ista inquiri materia, quæ circa quartum Sententiarum, distinctione 1, potius locum habent.
paras.en: Lastly it is asked, concerning the same, whether he who neglected circumcision was to be punished by bodily death. To this Lyra answers that the father or guardian of the child who neglected to circumcise the child on the eighth day was to be punished with death for it; and likewise the uncircumcised child, if on reaching adult age he neglected to receive circumcision. But Rabbi Paul [Paul of Burgos, a convert from Judaism, whose Additions accompany Lyra's Postil] contradicts this, affirming that one who omitted circumcision was not to be punished with death, even according to the Hebrews. For it is not said here, *Let him die the death*, as in the other crimes which the law punished with death. Yet the first answer seems the truer: first, because the law punished with death sins much less than the transgression of this precept, as is plain in many cases, and in that of the man who was stoned[[Num 15:36||]] because he gathered sticks on the sabbath[[Num 15:32||]]. Secondly, because the Apostle says to the Hebrews: [[Heb 10:28|A man making void the law of Moses dieth without any mercy under two or three witnesses|Irritam quis faciens legem Moysis, absque ulla contradictione duobus aut tribus testibus moritur]] [Denis reads "without any contradiction" where the Vulgate has "without any mercy"]. Many other things could be inquired into on this matter, which have their place rather on the fourth book of the Sentences, distinction 1.

17.title: Spiritualis expositio ejusdem capituli septimidecimi
17.title_en: Spiritual exposition of the same seventeenth chapter

paras.t: Abraham (sicut præhabitum est) figura exstitit Christi. Unde promissiones quæ in isto capitulo Abrahæ factæ leguntur, et cetera hic contenta, possunt allegorice exponi de Christo, cui secundum naturam assumptam loquitur Deus Pater: Ambula coram me, obediendo voluntati meæ in omnibus, atque humanæ redemptionis mysteria adimplendo, et esto perfectus. Unde Salvator testatur: Sicut mandatum dedit mihi Pater, sic facio. Et rursus: Opus, inquit, consummavi quod dedisti mihi ut facerem. Denique Christus homo, ab incarnationis exordio fuit confirmatus in bono, et in omni virtute perfectus. Idcirco quod dicitur ei, Esto perfectus, non dicitur ei hortando ut proficiat, nisi forte quantum ad manifestationem, quemadmodum ait Evangelista: Jesus proficiebat ætate, sapientia et gratia coram Deo et hominibus, sed suæ perfectioni congratulando.
paras.en: Abraham (as was said before) was a figure of Christ. Hence the promises which we read were made to Abraham in this chapter, and the other things contained here, can be expounded allegorically of Christ, to whom, according to the nature He assumed, God the Father says: [[17:1|walk before me|Ambula coram me]], by obeying my will in all things and by fulfilling the mysteries of human redemption, [[17:1|and be perfect|et esto perfectus]]. Hence the Saviour testifies: [[John 14:31|as the Father hath given me commandments, so do I|Sicut mandatum dedit mihi Pater, sic facio]]. And again: [[John 17:4|the work|Opus]], He says, [[John 17:4|I have finished|consummavi]] [[John 17:4|which thou gavest me to do|quod dedisti mihi ut facerem]]. Moreover, Christ as man was confirmed in good from the first moment of the Incarnation, and perfect in every virtue. Therefore when it is said to Him, [[17:1|be perfect|Esto perfectus]], it is not said to Him by way of urging Him to make progress (unless perhaps as regards the showing of it, as the Evangelist says: [[Luke 2:52|Jesus advanced in wisdom and age and grace with God and men|Jesus proficiebat ætate, sapientia et gratia coram Deo et hominibus]]), but by way of rejoicing with Him in His perfection.

paras.t: Pactumque fœdus meum inter me et te. Hoc fœdus est fœdus summæ dilectionis et promissionis inter Patrem et Filium incarnatum: quia et Filium secundum naturam humanam assumptam Pater plus diligit quam totum mundum, cui et promisit et dedit super omnia principatum, quemadmodum Christus testatur: Data est mihi omnis potestas in cœlo et in terra: posuitque Pater fœdus evangelicæ legis in Christo, ut eam per se et suos Apostolos omnibus prædicaret. Insuper multiplicavit Christum vehementissime, totum pene mundum convertendo ad ipsum, ita quod innumerabiles genuit filios ex aqua et Spiritu Sancto.
paras.en: [[17:2|And I will make my covenant between me and thee|Pactumque fœdus meum inter me et te]] [Denis's text reads *Pactumque fœdus*, "and the pact, my covenant", where the Vulgate has *Ponamque fœdus*, "and I will make my covenant"]. This covenant is a covenant of the highest love and promise between the Father and the incarnate Son: for the Father loves the Son, according to the human nature He assumed, more than the whole world, and has both promised and given Him sovereignty over all things, as Christ testifies: [[Matt 28:18|All power is given to me in heaven and in earth|Data est mihi omnis potestas in cœlo et in terra]]. And the Father set the covenant of the Gospel law in Christ, that He might preach it to all men through Himself and His Apostles. Moreover He multiplied Christ exceedingly, converting almost the whole world to Him, so that He begot countless sons of water and the Holy Ghost.

paras.t: Cecidit Abram pronus in faciem, quoniam Christus homo Patri se humilians retulit grates super omni bono quod contulit sibi, et per se toti generi humano.
paras.en: [[17:3|Abram fell flat on his face|Cecidit Abram pronus in faciem]]: for Christ as man, humbling Himself before the Father, gave Him thanks for every good that He bestowed on Him, and through Him on the whole human race.

paras.t: Erisque pater multarum gentium: quoniam Christus est legislator, magister, rex et pontifex omnium gentium conversarum. Nec ultra vocabitur nomen tuum Abram, sed Abraham. Christus quamdiu solis prædicavit Judæis, quasi Abram dici valebat, hoc est pater excelsus Judæorum, quos instruxit et rexit: sed quum per Apostolos universis gentibus gratiam dedit conversionis, rite Abraham poterat appellari, utpote innumerabilium hominum pater; tunc et reges ac principes, prælati ac præsules prodierunt ex Christo ubique terrarum.
paras.en: [[17:4|and thou shalt be a father of many nations|Erisque pater multarum gentium]]: for Christ is the lawgiver, master, king and high priest of all the nations converted. [[17:5|Neither shall thy name be called any more Abram|Nec ultra vocabitur nomen tuum Abram]], [[17:5|but thou shalt be called Abraham|sed Abraham]]. So long as Christ preached to the Jews alone, He could be called, as it were, Abram, that is, the high father of the Jews, whom He taught and ruled; but when through the Apostles He gave the grace of conversion to all the nations, He could rightly be called Abraham, as being the father of countless men. Then too kings and princes, prelates and bishops came forth from Christ all over the earth.

paras.t: Et statuam pactum meum inter me et te, et inter semen tuum post te in generationibus suis, fœdere sempiterno, id est, evangelicam legem tibi et tuis discipulis prædicandam et observandam committam usque in finem mundi; ut sim Deus tuus, in quantum homo es, et seminis tui, videlicet populi christiani post tuam passionem et ascensionem. Daboque tibi et semini tuo terram peregrinationis tuæ. Omnia quippe climata terræ a christiano populo inhabitata sunt et possessa per plurimos annos, quamvis interdum et diu aliqua propter sua perdiderunt peccata.
paras.en: [[17:7|And I will establish my covenant between me and thee, and between thy seed after thee in their generations, by a perpetual covenant|Et statuam pactum meum inter me et te, et inter semen tuum post te in generationibus suis, fœdere sempiterno]], that is, I will entrust the Gospel law to thee and to thy disciples, to be preached and kept until the end of the world; [[17:7|to be a God to thee|ut sim Deus tuus]], inasmuch as thou art man, [[17:7|and to thy seed|et seminis tui]], namely, to the Christian people after thy Passion and Ascension. [[17:8|And I will give to thee, and to thy seed, the land of thy sojournment|Daboque tibi et semini tuo terram peregrinationis tuæ]]. For all the regions of the earth have been inhabited and possessed by the Christian people for very many years, although at times they have lost some of them, and for a long while, because of their sins.

paras.t: Tu ergo custodies pactum meum, etc. Circumcidetis carnem præputii vestri. Hoc Christus litteraliter adimplevit, et suis fidelibus spiritualiter adimplere præcepit, quia circumcisioni fecit succedere Baptismum, in quo fit purgatio ab originali infectione. Deinde docuit et præcepit totum corpus et animam ab omni inquinamento carnis ac spiritus spiritualiter circumcidere seu mundare, ita quod masculus cujus præputii caro circumcisa non fuerit, id est, qui carnalia desideria, fœdaque opera non amputaverit a se, peribit de populo suo.
paras.en: [[17:9|And thou therefore shalt keep my covenant|Tu ergo custodies pactum meum]], etc. [[17:11|And you shall circumcise the flesh of your foreskin|Circumcidetis carnem præputii vestri]]. This Christ fulfilled literally[[Luke 2:21||]], and He commanded His faithful to fulfil it spiritually, for He made Baptism succeed circumcision, and in Baptism there is a cleansing from the infection of original sin. Then He taught and commanded that the whole body and soul be spiritually circumcised, or cleansed, [[2 Cor 7:1|from all defilement of the flesh and of the spirit|ab omni inquinamento carnis ac spiritus]]; so that [[17:14|The male whose flesh of his foreskin shall not be circumcised|masculus cujus præputii caro circumcisa non fuerit]], that is, who has not cut away from himself carnal desires and foul works, shall perish [[17:14|out of his people|de populo suo]].

paras.t: Dixit quoque Deus ad Abraham: Sarai uxorem tuam non vocabis Sarai, sed Saram. Per uxorem Abrahæ designatur Christi Ecclesia, quæ Sarai dici poterat quamdiu vigebat in sola Judæa, quasi tunc Christi principissa. Quum vero toto orbe diffundi cœpit, et undique promulgari ac dominari, rite vocata est Sara, id est princeps absolute, quoniam juxta Isaiæ oraculum, Gens et regnum quod non servierit ei, peribit. Et benedicam ei. Deus enim implevit Ecclesiam Christi omni superno charismate abundantissime. Et ex illa dabo tibi filium cui benedicturus sum. Per filium istum intelligitur populus christianus, ex gentilitate per Ecclesiam primitivam conversus et spiritualiter genitus, cui ineffabilem gratiarum copiam largitus est Deus.
