Quemadmodum autem homo per unum peccatum meretur relinqui a Deo, ita ut incidat in aliud, sicque peccatum illud est peccatum et causa peccati ; sic homo per opera bona meretur præservari a Deo, ne peccet : meretur, inquam, de condigno aut congruo. Sicque fuit in isto Abimelech, ut constat ex textu. Præterea peccare in Deum, quandoque distinguitur contra peccare in proximum, ita quod peccata contra tria prima præcepta dicuntur peccata in Deum, quia sunt directe contra eum et contra præcepta quæ versantur circa ipsum. Peccata vero contra alia septem præcepta, vocantur peccata in proximum ; quia directe et immediate sunt contra eum, et ei nociva. Ex consequenti vero sunt contra Deum, quoniam contra ejus præcepta : sed nunc peccare in Deum, acceptum est, prout includit peccata in proximum.
paras.en: [[20:6|And God said to him: And I know that thou didst it with a sincere heart|Dixitque ad eum Deus : Et ego scio quod simplici corde feceris]]. It may be asked whether this whole conversation was completed in a vision and in sleep, or rather was finished while he was awake. And the whole of it could take place in sleep, just as in the third book of Kings we read that God appeared to Solomon[[3 Kings 3:5||]], and a conversation took place between them. And then it is added there: And Solomon [[3 Kings 3:15|perceived that it was a dream|intellexit Salomon quod somnium esset]]. Such a conversation was within the soul, spiritual and imaginary [that is, formed in the imagination, not heard with the bodily ears], to the ears of the heart, not of the body; and for it a man is more apt in sleep, because then the outward senses are at rest. For which reason it is written in Job: [[Job 33:15|By a dream in a vision by night, when deep sleep falleth upon men|Per somnium in visione nocturna, quando sopor irruit super homines]], God [[Job 33:16|openeth the ears of men|aperit Deus aures virorum]], and [[Job 33:16|instructeth them in what they are to learn|instruit disciplina]], [[Job 33:17|That he may withdraw a man|ut avertat hominem]] from impiety. [[20:6|and therefore I withheld thee from sinning against me, and I suffered thee not to touch her|Ideo custodivi te, ne peccares in me, et non dimisi ut tangeres eam]], that is, by this adversity I held thee back from unlawful intercourse, lest thou shouldst offend Me by sinning against thy neighbour. And this is the gift and the loving-kindness of God, that by adversities He thus keeps a man from sin. For just as a man by one sin deserves to be forsaken by God, so that he falls into another, and so that sin is both a sin and the cause of sin, so a man by good works deserves to be preserved by God from sinning: deserves it, I say, de condigno or de congruo [that is, by merit in strict justice, or by a merit of fittingness that God rewards out of His liberality]. And so it was with this Abimelech, as is clear from the text. Moreover, sinning against God is sometimes distinguished from sinning against one's neighbour, so that sins against the first three commandments are called sins against God, because they are directly against Him and against the commandments that concern Him; while sins against the other seven commandments are called sins against one's neighbour, because they are directly and immediately against him, and harmful to him. Consequently, however, they are against God, since they are against His commandments: but here sinning against God is taken as including sins against one's neighbour.

paras.t: Nunc ergo redde viro suo uxorem, quia propheta est, et orabit pro te, et vives : quum enim propheta sit et vir sanctus, gravius crimen esset ei suam auferri uxorem ; estque idoneus orare pro te, nec latet eum, conjugem suam esse intactam a te. Et orabit pro te : ex his patet, quod Abimelech aliquantulum erat culpabilis in tollendo Saram ab Abraham, non satis ordinate et caute procedendo et inquirendo de statu Saræ, aut amore pulchritudinis ejus sensualiter affectatus, quamvis juxta expositionem præhabitam simplici corde tulerit eam. Bonis enim operibus sæpe miscentur aliqua mala. Si autem nolueris reddere, scito quod morte morieris tu, et omnia quæ tua sunt. Circa hoc quæri posset, quare propter peccatum Abimelech Deus occidisset omnia ad ipsum spectantia, cur etiam ob hoc flagellavit omnes uxores ipsius : quorum responsio patet ex dictis in expositione duodecimi capituli, ubi habetur, qualiter rex Ægypti tulerit Saram, et qualiter propter hoc ipse et domus ejus fuerint maxime flagellati. Hæc namque historia quasi omnino cum illa coincidit.
paras.en: [[20:7|Now therefore restore the man his wife, for he is a prophet: and he shall pray for thee, and thou shalt live|Nunc ergo redde viro suo uxorem, quia propheta est, et orabit pro te, et vives]]: for since he is a prophet and a holy man, it would be the graver crime that his wife should be taken from him; and he is fit to pray for thee, nor is it hidden from him that his wife is untouched by thee. [[20:7|and he shall pray for thee|Et orabit pro te]]: from these words it is plain that Abimelech was somewhat to blame in taking Sara from Abraham, not proceeding orderly and cautiously enough and inquiring about Sara's state, or being sensually drawn by love of her beauty, although, according to the exposition given before, he took her with a sincere heart. For some evils are often mingled with good works. [[20:7|but if thou wilt not restore her, know that thou shalt surely die, thou and all that are thine|Si autem nolueris reddere, scito quod morte morieris tu, et omnia quæ tua sunt]]. Concerning this it could be asked why, for the sin of Abimelech, God would have slain everything belonging to him, and why too He scourged all his wives for this: the answer to which is plain from what was said in the exposition of the twelfth chapter, where it is told how the king of Egypt took Sara, and how for this he and his house were most grievously scourged. For this history agrees almost entirely with that one.

paras.t: Statimque de nocte consurgens Abimelech. Si tam infirmus erat quod medici de ejus desperaverant curatione, quomodo potuit tam cito consurgere ? Dici potest, quod statim quum obtemperare proposuit revelationi divinæ, cœperit melius sentire. Vel aliorum ope erexit se, et fuit valde perterritus. Timor autem facit hominem quandoque ardua attentare, ut evadat periculum. Vocavit omnes servos suos, etc. Timueruntque omnes viri valde, omnes scilicet domestici ejus, istis auditis. Vocavit autem Abimelech etiam Abraham, id est, die facta, fecit eum venire ad se, et dixit ei : Quid fecisti nobis ? quasi dicat, Exposuisti nos magno periculo, dicendo quod femina ista sit soror tua. Quid peccavimus in te, quia induxisti super me et super regnum meum peccatum grande ? id est, occasionem dedisti mihi magni excessus, et per consequens populo meo, qui mihi consentiendo aut me in similibus imitando, potuissent magnam incidere culpam. Ex quibus constat, quod ignorantia facti non excusat in toto, nisi debita adhibeatur diligentia, inquisitio, seu cautela. Rursusque expostulans causam verborum Abrahæ, ait : Quid vidisti ut hoc faceres ? id est, quid te movit ad ita loquendum, et quo intuitu dixisti quod sit soror tua ? Abimelech itaque vehementissime mirabatur, quod quum Abraham esset vir sanctus ac sapiens et propheta, dixit verba hujusmodi, ex quibus secutum fuit tale malum, et majus sequi potuerat.
paras.en: [[20:8|And Abimelech forthwith rising up in the night|Statimque de nocte consurgens Abimelech]]. If he was so ill that the physicians had despaired of his cure, how could he rise up so quickly? It can be said that as soon as he resolved to obey the divine revelation, he began to feel better. Or he raised himself up with the help of others, and was greatly terrified. And fear sometimes makes a man attempt hard things, so as to escape danger. [[20:8|called all his servants|Vocavit omnes servos suos]], etc. [[20:8|and all the men were exceedingly afraid|Timueruntque omnes viri valde]], that is, all his household, when they had heard these things. [[20:9|And Abimelech called also for Abraham|Vocavit autem Abimelech etiam Abraham]], that is, when day had come, he had him come to him, [[20:9|and said to him: What hast thou done to us|et dixit ei : Quid fecisti nobis]]? as if to say: Thou hast exposed us to great danger by saying that this woman is thy sister. [[20:9|what have we offended thee in, that thou hast brought upon me and upon my kingdom a great sin?|Quid peccavimus in te, quia induxisti super me et super regnum meum peccatum grande]]? that is, thou hast given me occasion of a great excess, and consequently to my people, who by consenting with me or imitating me in like things could have fallen into great guilt. From which it is clear that ignorance of the fact does not excuse wholly, unless due diligence, inquiry or caution is used. [[20:10|And again he expostulated with him|Rursusque expostulans]] over the reason for Abraham's words, [[20:10|and said: What sawest thou, that thou hast done this?|ait : Quid vidisti ut hoc faceres]] that is, what moved thee to speak so, and with what view didst thou say that she is thy sister? For Abimelech wondered most greatly that, since Abraham was a holy and wise man and a prophet, he had spoken such words, from which so great an evil had followed, and a greater could have followed.

paras.t: Respondit Abraham : Cogitavi mecum, dicens, hoc est tacitus intra me : Forsitan non est timor Dei in loco isto, id est in hominibus urbis hujus sive provinciæ, et interficient me propter uxorem meam, hoc est, ut eam liberius habeant ; idcirco inveni istud consilium atque remedium, nec Deum tentavi, sed eo inspirante cognovi, quod ipse meam conjugem præservaret in Palæstina, sicut fecerat in Ægypto. Quæ circa istud dicenda essent, introducta sunt in expositione præfati capituli duodecimi.
paras.en: [[20:11|Abraham answered: I thought with myself, saying|Respondit Abraham : Cogitavi mecum, dicens]], that is, silently within myself: [[20:11|Perhaps there is not the fear of God in this place|Forsitan non est timor Dei in loco isto]], that is, in the men of this city or province: [[20:11|and they will kill me for the sake of my wife|et interficient me propter uxorem meam]], that is, so as to have her more freely; therefore I devised this counsel and remedy, nor did I tempt God, but by His inspiration I knew that He would preserve my wife in Palestine, as He had done in Egypt. What there would be to say about this has been set down in the exposition of the aforesaid twelfth chapter.

paras.t: Alias autem, id est, hoc est secundum alium respectum et sensum, seu alio modo quam putas, vere soror mea est, filia patris mei, non quod ipsa sit filia patris mei, aut matris meæ, tanquam nata immediate ab illo aut illa, sed filia est patris mei, videlicet Thare, quia ille est avus ipsius. Avi autem sæpe patres vocantur eorum, quorum sunt avi. Et non filia matris meæ, etc. : quia ut dicitur, Thare pater Abrahæ, habuit plures uxores, ex quarum una genuit Abraham, ex alia Aram, qui fuit immediatus pater Saræ et Lot. Sicque Sara et Lot attinebant Abrahæ ex parte patris sui, non ex parte matris suæ. Porro in Scholastica historia tanguntur alii sensus horum verborum, ita quod Abraham vocavit fratrem suum Aram, patrem Saræ, patrem suum, quia senior eo erat. Vel, ut hoc quod ait, patris, mei, intelligatur divisim, ut sit sensus : Ipsa est filia patris, supple, sui : mei, hoc est, qui est meus frater. Alii vero dicunt, quod ipso Aram mortuo, pater suus Thare duxit uxorem ejus in conjugem, et genuit Saram ex illa, suscitans filio suo defuncto semen ex conjuge ejus, et ita Thare fuisset immediatus pater Saræ. Sed prima expositio planior est, ut scilicet Sara dicatur soror Abrahæ eo modo, quo frater suus Lot supra vocatus est Abrahæ frater.
paras.en: [[20:12|Howbeit, otherwise|Alias autem]], that is, in another respect and sense, or in another way than thou thinkest, [[20:12|she is truly my sister, the daughter of my father|vere soror mea est, filia patris mei]]; not that she is the daughter of my father or of my mother as born immediately of him or of her, but she is the daughter of my father, namely Thare, because he is her grandfather. And grandfathers are often called the fathers of those whose grandfathers they are. [[20:12|and not the daughter of my mother|Et non filia matris meæ]], etc.: because, as is said, Thare, the father of Abraham, had several wives, of one of whom he begot Abraham, of another Aran, who was the immediate father of Sara and of Lot. And so Sara and Lot were related to Abraham on his father's side, not on his mother's. Further, in the Scholastic History other senses of these words are touched on: that Abraham called his brother Aran, Sara's father, his own father, because he was older than he. Or that what he says, *of my father*, is understood divided, so that the sense is: She is the daughter of the father, supply, her own: *my*, that is, who is my brother [that is, reading *patris* and *mei* apart: the daughter of her father, who is mine, that is, my brother]. Others again say that when Aran himself had died, his father Thare took his wife in marriage and begot Sara of her, raising up seed to his dead son from his wife [as the levirate law later required of a brother], and so Thare would have been the immediate father of Sara. But the first exposition is plainer: namely that Sara is called Abraham's sister in the way in which Lot, his brother's son, was called Abraham's brother above.

paras.t: Postquam autem eduxit me Deus de domo patris mei, id est de terra et cognatione mea paterna. […] ad eam : Hæc misericordiam, hoc est hunc pium effectum, […] id est in omni populo alieno ad quem venimus, […] quod frater tuus […] ne occidant me desiderio te habendi. Nec hoc fuit mendosum, quia multum propinqui vocantur ad invicem frater et soror ; nec fuit illicitum, quia interdum licet veritatem prudenter abscondere, ne malum contingat, quamvis mentiri non liceat.
paras.en: [[20:13|And after God brought me out of my father's house|Postquam autem eduxit me Deus de domo patris mei]], that is, from my land and my father's kindred. […] [[20:13|to her|ad eam]]: [[20:13|this kindness|Hæc misericordiam]], that is, this loving service, […] that is, among every foreign people to which we have come, […] that [[20:13|thy brother|frater tuus]] […], lest they kill me out of desire to have thee. Nor was this a falsehood, because those who are close kin call one another brother and sister; nor was it unlawful, because it is sometimes lawful prudently to hide the truth so that evil may not befall, although it is not lawful to lie.

paras.t: Tulit ergo Abimelech oves et boves, et servos et ancillas, et dedit Abraham, id est ipsi Abrahæ, pro molestia seu injuria aut culpa circa eum commissa, atque ad honorandum eum tanquam Dei amicum ac vatem, et item ad captandum benevolentiam ac amicitiam ejus, ut etiam provocaret eum ad orandum pro se ac mulieribus suis, totaque domo sua. Reddiditque illi Saram uxorem suam, et ait : Terra coram vobis est, id est, tota hæc regio mea in vestro prospectu est, et ad usum ac placitum vestrum parata ; ubicumque tibi placuerit, habita cum tuis domesticis. Hoc singulariter dixit ad Abraham, tanquam ad patremfamilias, quem ceteros sequi oportet ad habitandum quo ipse elegerit.
paras.en: [[20:14|And Abimelech took sheep and oxen, and servants and handmaids, and gave to Abraham|Tulit ergo Abimelech oves et boves, et servos et ancillas, et dedit Abraham]], that is, to Abraham himself, for the trouble or wrong or fault committed against him, and to honour him as the friend of God and a prophet, and also to win his goodwill and friendship, so as also to move him to pray for himself and his women and his whole house. [[20:14|and restored to him Sara his wife|Reddiditque illi Saram uxorem suam]], [[20:15|And said: The land is before you|et ait : Terra coram vobis est]], that is, all this region of mine lies open to your view, and is ready for your use and pleasure: [[20:15|dwell wheresoever it shall please thee|ubicumque tibi placuerit, habita]], with thy household. This he said in the singular to Abraham, as to the father of the family, whom the others must follow to dwell wherever he chooses.

paras.t: Sar[…] autem dixit : Ecce mille argenteos dedi fratri tuo, hoc est Abrahæ tuo marito quem fratrem tuum vocasti. Ex hoc patet, quod Abimelech dedit Abrahæ tantam pecuniam præter oves et boves, servos ac famulas. Hoc erit tibi in velamen oculorum ad omnes qui tecum sunt : id est, donum istud pecuniarium sit tibi ad pepla emenda, quibus faciem tuam tegas usque ad oculos, inter omnes apud quos fueris, ne ex inspectione pulchritudinis tuæ te ament, et viro tuo te subtrahant. Vel, in velamen oculorum tuorum, id est, ad operiendum oculos tuos quum per mortem fuerint clausi, utpote in præparationem funeris tui : ut elegans exstet irrisio ; quasi dicat : Quum vetulam te esse jam noverim, potius te oportet cogitare de pertinentibus ad funebria, quam uti tali modo loquendi, per quem alii inducantur ad appetendum te pro uxore. Vel, Hoc erit tibi in velamen oculorum, id est pro memoriali verecundiæ quam nunc pateris, et ad operiendum oculos tuos ac faciem a pudore præsenti, seu ad relevandum et eripiendum te a confusione, quia per dona ista te etiam honoravi. Et quocumque perrexeris, memento te deprehensam. Hoc quidam exponit sic, id est, acceptam a me in uxorem. Sed non videtur quod Abimelech accepit Saram in conjugem, sicut nec Pharao, sed uterque eorum hoc facere intendebat. Est igitur sensus : Memento te deprehensam, hoc est, in modo loquendi illicito seu mendoso aut periculoso inventam, quia virum tuum vocasti fratrem tuum. Unde secundum Rabbi Paulum, dictio Hebraica hic posita, sonat redargutam.
paras.en: [[20:16|And to Sara he said|Sar[…] autem dixit]]: [[20:16|Behold I have given thy brother a thousand pieces of silver|Ecce mille argenteos dedi fratri tuo]], that is, to Abraham thy husband, whom thou didst call thy brother. From this it is plain that Abimelech gave Abraham so much money besides the sheep and oxen, menservants and maidservants. [[20:16|this shall serve thee for a covering of thy eyes to all that are with thee|Hoc erit tibi in velamen oculorum ad omnes qui tecum sunt]]: that is, let this gift of money be for thee to buy veils with which to cover thy face up to the eyes among all with whom thou shalt be, lest from looking on thy beauty they should love thee and draw thee away from thy husband. Or, *for a covering of thy eyes*, that is, for covering thy eyes when they have been closed by death, namely for the preparation of thy funeral: so that it is a neat piece of mockery; as if to say: Since I know now that thou art an old woman, thou oughtest rather to think of what pertains to funerals than to use such a manner of speech, by which others are led to desire thee as a wife. Or, *This shall serve thee for a covering of thy eyes*, that is, as a memorial of the shame that thou now sufferest, and to cover thy eyes and face from the present disgrace, or to relieve thee and rescue thee from confusion, because by these gifts I have also honoured thee. [[20:16|and whithersoever thou shalt go: and remember thou wast taken|Et quocumque perrexeris, memento te deprehensam]]. Someone explains this thus: that is, taken by me as a wife. But it does not seem that Abimelech took Sara in marriage, any more than Pharao did, but each of them intended to do so. The sense then is: Remember that thou wast *caught* [the Latin *deprehensam* means both taken and caught out], that is, found in an unlawful or false or dangerous manner of speaking, because thou didst call thy husband thy brother. Hence, according to Rabbi Paul [Paul of Burgos], the Hebrew word placed here means *reproved*.

paras.t: Orante autem Abraham pro Abimelech et mulieribus suæ domus, sanavit Deus Abimelech, reddendo eum sanitati perfectæ, et uxorem ancillasque ejus, et pepererunt. Concluserat enim Dominus omnem vulvam domus Abimelech propter Saram uxorem Abrahæ, hoc est pro culpa commissa in ablatione Saræ a suo marito. Per uxorem autem Abimelech, intelligitur uxor ejus vel principalis, vel unica. Et per ancillas illius, intelliguntur ejus concubinæ, aut conjuges servorum suorum.
paras.en: [[20:17|And when Abraham prayed|Orante autem Abraham]] for Abimelech and the women of his house, [[20:17|God healed Abimelech|sanavit Deus Abimelech]], restoring him to perfect health, [[20:17|and his wife, and his handmaids, and they bore children|et uxorem ancillasque ejus, et pepererunt]]. [[20:18|For the Lord had closed up every womb of the house of Abimelech, on account of Sara, Abraham's wife|Concluserat enim Dominus omnem vulvam domus Abimelech propter Saram uxorem Abrahæ]], that is, for the fault committed in taking Sara away from her husband. By Abimelech's wife is meant either his chief wife or his only one. And by his handmaids are meant his concubines, or the wives of his servants.

paras.t: Præterea, juxta spiritualem intelligentiam, per Abraham, ut dictum est sæpe, significatus est Christus ; per Saram, Ecclesia, quæ est soror Christi, et uxor seu sponsa ipsius. Dicitur autem soror Christi duplici ratione. Primo, propter communionem naturæ humanæ in utrisque. Secundo, propter spiritualem regenerationem et obedientiam præceptorum, sicut ait Salvator : Quicumque fecerit voluntatem Patris mei, ipse meus frater et soror et mater est. Per Abimelech quoque significantur principes mundi, seu invisibiles potestates, qui voluerunt Ecclesiam violare, nec potuerunt : quorum principum mundanorum quidam per inspirationem, aut alio modo correpti, conversi sunt, et ex ignorantia sua aliqualiter excusabantur, quemadmodum fatetur Paulus : Misericordiam consecutus sum, quia ignorans feci in incredulitate. Nam et aliqui principes tales, fuerunt corporaliter castigati propter excessus suos in Christi Sponsam, quos et Deus præservavit, ne gravius peccarent in eam. Denique principes sic conversi, retulerunt servis quæ ipsis acciderant, et quanta eis instarent supplicia, nisi pœniterent de sua transgressione contra Christi Ecclesiam, eamque Christo offerrent, et ita plures ministri perterriti, sunt conversi, quibus Christus advocatus interpellatorque hominum apud Patrem veniam impetravit, qui magna Domino munera obtulerunt, et suos ministros fecerunt Christo subjectos : sicque de cetero cum suis familiis spiritualiter fecundi effecti, semen, in quo cultus Dei ac fides catholica aucti sunt, genuerunt.
paras.en: Moreover, according to the spiritual understanding, Abraham, as has often been said, signifies Christ; Sara, the Church, who is the sister of Christ and His wife or bride. And she is called the sister of Christ for two reasons. First, because of the human nature common to both. Secondly, because of spiritual regeneration and obedience to the commandments, as the Saviour says: [[Matt 12:50|whosoever shall do the will of my Father|Quicumque fecerit voluntatem Patris mei]], [[Matt 12:50|he is my brother, and sister, and mother|ipse meus frater et soror et mater est]]. Abimelech too signifies the princes of the world, or the invisible powers, who wished to violate the Church and could not: and some of those worldly princes, reproved by inspiration or in some other way, were converted, and were in some measure excused by their ignorance, as Paul confesses: [[1 Tim 1:13|I obtained the mercy|Misericordiam consecutus sum]], [[1 Tim 1:13|because I did it ignorantly in unbelief|quia ignorans feci in incredulitate]]. For some such princes, too, were chastised in body for their excesses against the Bride of Christ, and God also preserved them from sinning more gravely against her. Lastly, the princes thus converted told their servants what had befallen them, and how great punishments threatened them unless they repented of their transgression against the Church of Christ and offered her to Christ; and so many of their ministers, terrified, were converted; for whom Christ, the advocate and intercessor of men, obtained pardon with the Father; and they offered great gifts to the Lord and made their ministers subject to Christ: and so thenceforth, made spiritually fruitful with their households, they begot a seed in which the worship of God and the Catholic faith were increased.

21.title: Expositio litteralis capituli vicesimi primi: Visitavit autem Dominus Saram, etc.
21.title_en: Literal exposition of the twenty-first chapter: And the Lord visited Sara, etc.

paras.t: Visitavit autem Dominus Saram, hoc est, supernaturalem fecunditatem tradidit ei, sicut promiserat ei per angelicam assertionem, et implevit quæ locutus est. Concepitque et peperit filium in senectute sua, videlicet nonagenaria, tempore quo prædixerat ei Deus, hoc est die eodem quo ei prædictum fuit ab angelo, anno scilicet revoluto ab illo die, juxta quod supra dictum est : Revertens veniam ad te tempore isto, et habebit filium Sara.
paras.en: [[21:1|And the Lord visited Sara|Visitavit autem Dominus Saram]], that is, he gave her a fruitfulness above nature, [[21:1|as he had promised|sicut promiserat]] her through the angel's assurance, [[21:1|and fulfilled what he had spoken|et implevit quæ locutus est]]. [[21:2|And she conceived and bore a son in her old age|Concepitque et peperit filium in senectute sua]], namely at ninety years, [[21:2|at the time that God had foretold her|tempore quo prædixerat ei Deus]], that is, on the same day on which it was foretold her by the angel, a year having come round from that day, as was said above: [[Gen 18:10|I will return and come to thee at this time|Revertens veniam ad te tempore isto]], [[Gen 18:10|and Sara, thy wife, shall have a son|et habebit filium Sara]] [the margin gives Gen. xviii, 19; the words are from Gen 18:10, repeated at 18:14].

paras.t: Vocavitque Abraham nomen filii sui, quem genuit ei Sara, Isaac. Hoc enim nomen prænuntiatum fuit ei ab angelo, quemadmodum supra legitur : Ait Dominus ad Abraham : Sara pariet tibi filium, vocabisque nomen ejus Isaac.
paras.en: [[21:3|And Abraham called the name of his son, whom Sara bore him, Isaac|Vocavitque Abraham nomen filii sui, quem genuit ei Sara, Isaac]]. For this name was foretold him by the angel, as we read above: [[Gen 17:19|And God said to Abraham|Ait Dominus ad Abraham]]: [[Gen 17:19|Sara thy wife shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name Isaac|Sara pariet tibi filium, vocabisque nomen ejus Isaac]].

paras.t: Et circumcidit eum octavo die, sicut præceperat ei Deus, prout superius habitum est : Infans octodierum circumcidetur in vobis. Porro, quod sequitur, quum centum esset annorum, non refertur ad verbum immediate præcedens, videlicet, Præceperat ; sed ad verbum istud, Circumcidit : quando enim præceptum circumcisionis accepit a Domino, fuit nonaginta annorum : sed dum illud implevit in Isaac, centenarius fuit. Ideo subditur : Hac quippe ætate patris, natus est Isaac, id est, quum pater suus Abraham erat centum annorum.
paras.en: [[21:4|And he circumcised him the eighth day, as God had commanded him|Et circumcidit eum octavo die, sicut præceperat ei Deus]], as was set down above: [[Gen 17:12|An infant of eight days old shall be circumcised among you|Infans octodierum circumcidetur in vobis]]. Further, what follows, [[21:5|When he was a hundred years old|quum centum esset annorum]], does not refer to the word immediately before it, namely *had commanded*, but to the word *circumcised*: for when he received the precept of circumcision from the Lord he was ninety years old [Gen 17:24 gives ninety-nine], but when he fulfilled it in Isaac he was a hundred. Therefore it is added: [[21:5|for at this age of his father, was Isaac born|Hac quippe ætate patris, natus est Isaac]], that is, when his father Abraham was a hundred years old.

paras.t: Dixitque Sara : Risum fecit mihi Deus : hoc est, causam ridendi et gloriandi ac admirandi de magnitudine beneficiorum suorum, præstitit mihi Deus, concedendo mihi hunc filium supra naturam. Quicumque audierit ista, non solum corporali, sed interiori auditu, corridebit, hoc est, congratulabitur mihi de beneficiis mihi desuper datis. Hinc puer ille vocatus est Isaac, quod risus interpretatur, ut dictum est.
paras.en: [[21:6|And Sara said: God hath made a laughter for me|Dixitque Sara : Risum fecit mihi Deus]]: that is, God has granted me cause to laugh, to glory and to marvel at the greatness of his benefits, by giving me this son above nature. [[21:6|whosoever shall hear of it|Quicumque audierit]], not only with bodily but with inward hearing, [[21:6|will laugh|corridebit]], that is, will rejoice [[21:6|with me|mihi]] over the benefits given me from above [*corridebit*, literally "will laugh with", glossed by *congratulabitur*, "will rejoice with"]. Hence that boy was called Isaac, which is interpreted *laughter*, as has been said.

paras.t: Rursumque ait Sara : Quis auditorum, id est eorum qui ista audierint, crederet Abraham, hoc est ipsi Abrahæ, quod Sara lactaret filium quem peperit ei, videlicet Abrahæ, jam seni? Ista sunt verba exsultantis. Quasi dicat : Partus iste tam supernaturalis ac mirus est, quia et ex naturali dispositione atque ex senio sterilis fui, quod vix aliquis crederet, si recitaretur ei res ista ab Abraham. Refert Lyra, quod in Hebræo habetur pluraliter, Filios. Deinde narrat fabulam Judæorum, dicentium quod Sara in die ablactationis filii sui Isaac, lactavit et filios vicinarum mulierum, quæ suspicando dicebant, quod Sara non accepisset filium illum ex Abraham, sed ab alia muliere pro pretio. Cui fabulæ obviat quod dictum est, Quem peperit ei jam seni. Certum est equidem, quod filios illos non peperit Abrahæ: Sara quoque tamdiu gravida fuit, quod vicini ejus eam concepisse noverunt.
paras.en: [[21:7|And again she said|Rursumque ait]] Sara: [[21:7|Who|Quis auditorum]] [Denis reads *Quis auditorum*, "who of the hearers", where the Vulgate has *auditurus*], that is, who of those who should hear these things, [[21:7|would believe that Abraham|crederet Abraham]], that is, would believe Abraham himself [Denis takes *Abraham* as the one who would tell it], [[21:7|that Sara gave suck to a son, whom she bore to him|quod Sara lactaret filium quem peperit ei]], namely to Abraham, [[21:7|in his old age|jam seni]]? These are the words of one exulting. As if she said: This birth is so far above nature and so wonderful (for I was barren both by natural disposition and from old age) that scarcely anyone would believe it, if this thing were told him by Abraham. Lyra reports that in the Hebrew it is in the plural, *sons*. Then he tells a fable of the Jews, who say that Sara, on the day her son Isaac was weaned, suckled also the sons of the neighbouring women, who in their suspicion were saying that Sara had not had that son by Abraham, but from another woman for a price. Against this fable stands what is said: [[21:7|whom she bore to him in his old age|Quem peperit ei jam seni]]. For it is certain that she did not bear those sons to Abraham; and Sara was so long with child that her neighbours knew she had conceived.

paras.t: Crevit igitur puer, scilicet Isaac, et ablactatus est, quum esset trimus, hoc est trium annorum, ut in Scholastica habetur historia. Et hoc erat magnæ dilectionis, quod Sara jam anus lactavit filium suum uberibus propriis, quasi cum lacte corporis cupiens et bonitatem infundere suæ mentis. Fecitque Abraham grande convivium suis domesticis, vicinis et amicis, in die ablactationis ejus, videlicet Isaac, qui in die illa puer primo accessit ad mensam patris, et quia extunc puer tanti roboris fuit, quod major spes apparebat de ejus perduratione in vita. Quumque vidisset Sara filium Agar Ægyptiæ ludentem cum Isaac filio suo, dixit ad Abraham: Ejice ancillam hanc, et filium ejus; non enim erit heres filius ancillæ cum filio meo Isaac.
paras.en: [[21:8|And the child grew|Crevit igitur puer]], namely Isaac, [[21:8|and was weaned|et ablactatus est]] when he was *trimus*, that is, three years old, as is found in the Scholastic History [the *Historia scholastica* of Peter Comestor]. And this was a sign of great love, that Sara, already an old woman, suckled her son at her own breasts, as though wishing to pour into him, with the milk of the body, the goodness of her own mind as well. [[21:8|and Abraham made a great feast|Fecitque Abraham grande convivium]] for his household, neighbours and friends, [[21:8|on the day of his weaning|in die ablactationis ejus]], namely of Isaac, because on that day the boy first came to his father's table, and because from then on the boy was so strong that there appeared greater hope of his lasting in life. [[21:9|And when Sara had seen the son of Agar, the Egyptian, playing with Isaac, her son, she said to Abraham|Quumque vidisset Sara filium Agar Ægyptiæ ludentem cum Isaac filio suo, dixit ad Abraham]]: [[21:10|Cast out this bondwoman and her son; for the son of the bondwoman shall not be heir with my son Isaac|Ejice ancillam hanc, et filium ejus; non enim erit heres filius ancillæ cum filio meo Isaac]].

paras.t: Secundum Lyram, pro Ludentem, in Hebræo habetur, Messahet, quod multa significat, videlicet ludentem, idololatrantem, occidentem, et coeuntem, seu lascivientem. Et dicit quod translator noster, videlicet S. Hieronymus, videtur hanc æquivocationem ignorasse, aut non advertisse: quod non censetur bene sonare, quum B. Hieronymus quamperitissimus fuerit in Hebræo, quamque diligentissimus in transferendo. Denique Rabbi Paulus hic scribit, quod prædictum verbum Hebraicum, significat ut frequenter ridentem, quandoque deridentem, interdum gaudentem, aliquando vero ludentem: nunquam vero significat idololatrantem, nec occidentem, nec coeuntem, seu lascivientem. Unde translator noster bene se habuit, transferendo præfatam dictionem quandoque per ludum, interdum per risum seu gaudium, aliquando per irrisionem, nunquam vero per alia significata prædicta. Hæc Rabbi Paulus. Verum, tam Paulus iste quam Lyra affirmant, quod istud complexum, Cum Isaac, non est in Hebræo, neque de textu.
paras.en: According to Lyra, for *playing* the Hebrew has *Messahet*, which signifies many things, namely playing, committing idolatry, killing, and coupling or wantoning. And he says that our translator, namely St Jerome, seems to have been ignorant of this equivocation, or not to have noticed it: which is not thought to sound well, since Blessed Jerome was most skilled in Hebrew and most careful in translating. Then Rabbi Paul [Paul of Burgos, the converted rabbi who wrote additions to Lyra] writes here that the aforesaid Hebrew word signifies most often laughing, sometimes mocking, at times rejoicing, and sometimes playing; but it never signifies committing idolatry, nor killing, nor coupling or wantoning. Hence our translator did well in rendering that word sometimes by *play*, sometimes by *laughter* or *joy*, sometimes by *mockery*, but never by the other meanings mentioned. Thus far Rabbi Paul. Yet both this Paul and Lyra affirm that the phrase *with Isaac* is not in the Hebrew, nor part of the text.

paras.t: Dicit itaque Lyra, quod secundum Hebræos dictio illa Hebraica, accipitur hic in triplici significatione. Primo, pro idololatrare, ut sit sensus, quod Sara vidit Ismaelem aliqua facientem quæ ad idololatriam pertinebant. Unde in Scholastica recitatur historia: Tradunt Hebræi, quod Ismael instigabat puerum Isaac, ut adoraret imagines luteas a se factas. Secundo, pro occidere, ut sit sensus, quod Sara consideravit, quod Ismael quærebat versute occidere Isaac, quatenus hereditatem acquireret. Tertio, pro lascivire, ita quod Sara perpendit Ismaelem esse lascivum: ideo timuit ne filium suum ad similia provocaret, idcirco dixit marito: Ejice ancillam hanc, etc. Verumtamen expositiones præfatæ non solum ab Hebræis, sed et a Catholicis sunt prolatæ. Dicitur enim in Glossa: Vidisset ludentem, etc. Dupliciter hoc exponitur: vel quod Ismael idolis lusum fecit, vel quod adversus Isaac vindicavit sibi primogenita tanquam major ætate. In Scholastica quoque historia dicitur: Quum pueri luderent simul, Ismael lædebat Isaac. Intellexitque Sara in ludo persecutionem, quod scilicet Ismael post Abrahæ dormitionem vellet dominari fratri suo Isaac, tanquam major et senior eo. His consonat illud Apostoli ad Galatas: Is qui secundum carnem natus est, persequebatur eum qui secundum spiritum, hoc est, Ismael Isaac fratrem suum. Rursus super illud, Ludentem, habetur in Glossa: Lubricum et lascivum esse docebat ipsum Isaac, sicut et ipse erat.
paras.en: So Lyra says that according to the Hebrews that Hebrew word is taken here in a threefold meaning. First, for committing idolatry, so that the sense is that Sara saw Ismael doing certain things that pertained to idolatry. Hence it is related in the Scholastic History: The Hebrews hand down that Ismael was urging the boy Isaac to adore images of clay that he had made. Second, for killing, so that the sense is that Sara observed that Ismael was craftily seeking to kill Isaac, so as to gain the inheritance. Third, for wantoning, so that Sara perceived Ismael to be wanton, and therefore feared that he would provoke her son to the like; and for that reason she said to her husband: [[21:10|Cast out this bondwoman|Ejice ancillam hanc]], etc. These explanations, however, were put forward not only by the Hebrews but also by Catholics. For it is said in the Gloss: [[21:9|had seen|Vidisset]] him [[21:9|playing|ludentem]], etc. This is explained in two ways: either that Ismael made sport with idols, or that against Isaac he claimed the birthright for himself, as the elder. In the Scholastic History too it is said: When the boys were playing together, Ismael was hurting Isaac. And Sara understood persecution in the play, namely that after Abraham's falling asleep Ismael would wish to lord it over his brother Isaac, as being greater and older than he. With these agrees that saying of the Apostle to the Galatians: [[Gal 4:29|he that was born according to the flesh persecuted him|Is qui secundum carnem natus est, persequebatur eum]] [[Gal 4:29|that was after the spirit|qui secundum spiritum]], that is, Ismael persecuted his brother Isaac. Again, on the word *playing* the Gloss has: He was teaching Isaac to be loose and wanton, as he himself was.

paras.t: Insuper Rabbi Paulus testatur, quod locus iste melius exponitur ab aliis Hebræorum doctoribus, quam a Rabbi Salomone. Nam dicunt, quod Ismael videns tam grande celebrari convivium in die ablactationis Isaac, irrisit: ad innuendum quod nihilo minus ipse fieret heres, tanquam major natu atque legitime natus. Quod Sara attendens, dixit: Ejice, etc. Dicitur autem Agar ancilla, quia ancilla erat Abrahæ, antequam duceretur in conjugem, et mansit ancilla Saræ. Præterea Sara ex divino instinctu dixit : Ejice ancillam, etc. Nam Deo revelante cognovit, quod Isaac esset præelectus, et principalis filius Abrahæ, cui primogenita debebantur ex ordinatione divina. Quæritur, quæ fuit hereditas Abrahæ, quam Sara voluit pertinere ad Isaac, non ad Ismaelem, quum Deus non dederit Abrahæ hereditatem in terra promissionis, nec passum pedis. Respondetur, quod per hereditatem potest intelligi principalis et major opulentia Abrahæ, quam (ut infra habetur) reliquit Isaac filio suo.
paras.en: Moreover Rabbi Paul testifies that this place is better explained by other doctors of the Hebrews than by Rabbi Solomon [Rashi]. For they say that Ismael, seeing so great a feast celebrated on the day of Isaac's weaning, mocked, to hint that he himself would none the less be the heir, as being older by birth and lawfully born. Sara, noticing this, said: [[21:10|Cast out|Ejice]], etc. Now Agar is called a bondwoman because she was Abraham's bondwoman before she was taken as his wife, and she remained Sara's bondwoman. Further, Sara said by divine instinct: [[21:10|Cast out this bondwoman|Ejice ancillam]], etc. For by God's revelation she knew that Isaac was the chosen one and the principal son of Abraham, to whom the birthright was due by divine ordinance. It is asked what was the inheritance of Abraham which Sara wished to belong to Isaac and not to Ismael, since God did not give Abraham an inheritance in the land of promise, not even the pace of a foot. The answer is that by inheritance can be understood Abraham's principal and greater wealth, which (as is found below) he left to his son Isaac.

paras.t: Dure accepit hoc Abraham pro filio suo : id est, verba Saræ de ejectione Ismaelis, displicuerunt Abrahæ tanquam inclementia. Multum enim dilexerat Ismaelem, præsertim quum diu habuerit atque dilexerit eum ut unicum filium qui valde amatur. Abraham autem non scivit quod Sara protulit verba illa desuper mota. Gravis etiam videbatur Abrahæ ejectio ancillæ, quæ erat conjux ejus : idcirco dissimulavit ad tempus verba Saræ.
paras.en: [[21:11|Abraham took this grievously for his son|Dure accepit hoc Abraham pro filio suo]]: that is, Sara's words about casting out Ismael displeased Abraham as unkind. For he had loved Ismael much, especially since he had long had him and loved him as an only son, who is greatly loved. And Abraham did not know that Sara spoke those words moved from above. The casting out of the bondwoman, who was his wife, also seemed hard to Abraham: therefore he let Sara's words pass for a time.

paras.t: Cui dixit Deus, in visione nocturna per angelum : Non tibi videatur asperum quod locuta est Sara super puero et super ancilla tua, etc., hoc est de amborum ejectione, quia in Isaac vocabitur tibi semen, id est, Isaac principalis filius tuus est, et ejus posteritas a te specialiter processisse dicetur, quia in eo et ejus posteritate complebuntur principalia illa quæ tibi feci promissa, et inde Christus nascetur. Sed et filium ancillæ faciam in gentem magnam, id est, grandem populum faciam nasci ex Ismaele, quia semen tuum est, hoc est meritis tuis.
paras.en: [[21:12|And God said to him|Cui dixit Deus]], in a vision by night through an angel: [[21:12|Let it not seem grievous to thee|Non tibi videatur asperum]], what Sara has said, [[21:12|for the boy, and for thy bondwoman|super puero et super ancilla tua]], etc., that is, about casting out both of them, [[21:12|for in Isaac shall thy seed be called|quia in Isaac vocabitur tibi semen]]: that is, Isaac is your principal son, and his posterity will be said to have come forth from you in a special way, because in him and his posterity will be fulfilled those chief promises I made to you, and from there Christ will be born. [[21:13|But I will make the son also of the bondwoman a great nation|Sed et filium ancillæ faciam in gentem magnam]], that is, I will cause a great people to be born of Ismael, [[21:13|because he is thy seed|quia semen tuum est]], that is, for your merits.

paras.t: Surrexit itaque Abraham mane : ex quo elicitur, quod in nocte præcedente facta sit ei revelatio ista ; et tollens panem et utrem, id est vas seu lagenam aquæ, imposuit scapulæ ejus, etc. Per panem et aquam intelliguntur quæcumque cibaria et pocula. Quæ quum abiisset, errabat in solitudine Bersabee, de qua dictum est ante.
paras.en: [[21:14|So Abraham rose up in the morning|Surrexit itaque Abraham mane]]: from which it is gathered that this revelation was made to him in the night before; [[21:14|and taking bread and a bottle|et tollens panem et utrem]], that is, a vessel or flask, [[21:14|of water, put it upon her shoulder|aquæ, imposuit scapulæ ejus]], etc. By bread and water are understood all kinds of food and drink. [[21:14|And she departed, and wandered in the wilderness of Bersabee|Quæ quum abiisset, errabat in solitudine Bersabee]], of which mention was made before.

paras.t: Quumque consumpta esset aqua, quæ erat in utre, abjecit, id est cum tristitia posuit, puerum Ismaelem subter, unam arborum, quæ ibi erat, puta abietem, ut habet translatio alia, forte ut puer siti deficiens, ad arborem reclinaretur, et ejus umbra a solis protegeretur ardore. Et abiit, seditque regione procul quantum potest arcus jacere; dixit enim, Non videbo morientem puerum : putabat enim Agar Ismaelem mox ibi periclitaturum : et sedens contra, levavit vocem suam, et flevit ex tristitia, compassione et timore afflictionum sui filii.
paras.en: [[21:15|And when the water in the bottle was spent|Quumque consumpta esset aqua, quæ erat in utre]], [[21:15|she cast|abjecit]], that is, she set down in sadness, [[21:15|the boy|puerum]] Ismael [[21:15|under one of the trees that were there|subter, unam arborum, quæ ibi erat]], perhaps a fir, as another translation has it, perhaps so that the boy, failing from thirst, might lean against the tree and be shielded by its shade from the heat of the sun. [[21:16|And she went her way, and sat over against him a great way off, as far as a bow can carry|Et abiit, seditque regione procul quantum potest arcus jacere]]; for she said: [[21:16|I will not see the boy die|Non videbo morientem puerum]]; for Agar thought that Ismael would soon perish there; [[21:16|and sitting over against, she lifted up her voice and wept|et sedens contra, levavit vocem suam, et flevit]] from sadness, compassion, and fear of her son's sufferings.

paras.t: Exaudivit autem Deus vocem pueri, id est fletum Agar pro filio suo ; vel, vocem pueri, quia et ipse Ismael flebat, atque ut aliqui dicunt, de peccatis suis pœnituit. Jam enim erat decem et septem annorum, aut circiter. Nam tredecim fuit annorum tempore circumcisionis. Et post hoc, anno sequenti natus est Isaac, qui etiam fuit ad minus trium annorum tempore suæ ablactationis, ut creditur. Imo quidam dicit, quod erat viginti annorum, quod non videtur.
paras.en: [[21:17|And God heard the voice of the boy|Exaudivit autem Deus vocem pueri]], that is, Agar's weeping for her son; or else [[21:17|the voice of the boy|vocem pueri]], because Ismael himself too was weeping, and, as some say, repented of his sins. For he was already seventeen years old or thereabouts: he was thirteen at the time of the circumcision, and after that, in the following year, Isaac was born, who was also at least three years old at the time of his weaning, as is believed. Indeed someone says that he was twenty years old, which does not seem right.

paras.t: Vocavitque angelus Domini Agar de cælo, hoc est, angelus de cœlo descendens, et in aere stans, vocavit ipsam Agar, dicens : Quid agis Agar ? Noli timere. Exaudivit enim Deus vocem pueri, etc. Omnia ista erant consolatoria verba. Tolle puerum, et tene manum ejus. Aperuitque Dominus oculos ejus, videlicet Agar, id est, fecit eam videre quod ante non vidit. Ideo subditur : Quæ videns puteum aquæ, abiit, et implevit utrem aqua, deditque puero bibere, etc. Factusque est juvenis sagittarius, habitavitque in deserto Pharan, id est urbis seu terræ sic dictæ. Factus est ergo ibi juvenis sagittarius, quia exercuit se ad sagittandum bestias, atque ut refert Lyra, Hebræi dicunt, quod exercuit prædas et latrocinia de transeuntibus. Unde de eo prædictum est : Manus ejus contra omnes. Et accepit illi mater sua uxorem de terra Ægypti, de qua erat et ipsa.
paras.en: [[21:17|and an angel of God called to Agar from heaven|Vocavitque angelus Domini Agar de cælo]], that is, an angel coming down from heaven and standing in the air called Agar herself, [[21:17|saying: What art thou doing, Agar? fear not|dicens : Quid agis Agar ? Noli timere]]. [[21:17|for God hath heard the voice of the boy|Exaudivit enim Deus vocem pueri]], etc. All these were words of comfort. [[21:18|take up the boy, and hold him by the hand|Tolle puerum, et tene manum ejus]]. [[21:19|And God opened her eyes|Aperuitque Dominus oculos ejus]], namely Agar's, that is, he made her see what she had not seen before. Therefore it is added: [[21:19|and she saw a well of water, and went and filled the bottle, and gave the boy to drink|Quæ videns puteum aquæ, abiit, et implevit utrem aqua, deditque puero bibere]], etc. [[21:20|and became a young man, an archer|Factusque est juvenis sagittarius]]. [[21:21|And he dwelt in the wilderness of Pharan|habitavitque in deserto Pharan]], that is, of the city or land so called. So he became there a young man, an archer, because he trained himself in shooting wild beasts; and, as Lyra reports, the Hebrews say that he practised plunder and robbery upon passers-by. Hence it was foretold of him: [[Gen 16:12|his hand will be against all men|Manus ejus contra omnes]]. [[21:21|and his mother took a wife for him out of the land of Egypt|Et accepit illi mater sua uxorem de terra Ægypti]], from which she herself also was.

paras.t: Eodem tempore dixit Abimelech rex Palestinæ, et Phicol princeps exercitus ejus, ad Abraham : Deus tecum est in universis quæ agis. Jura ergo per Deum, ne noceas mihi et posteris meis, etc. Abimelech iste sciens neminem posse Deo resistere, cognoscensque Abraham esse Dei amicum, cum timuit eum propter adsistentiam Dei, quæ et in omnibus adfuit : et forte Abimelech iste percepit, qualiter Abraham vicerat, Dei adjutus auxilio, quatuor reges, ut dictum est : idcirco init pactum pacis cum Abraham. Phicol autem verba regis approbando firmavit, et idem cum rege suo petebat.
paras.en: [[21:22|At the same time Abimelech|Eodem tempore dixit Abimelech]], king of Palestine, [[21:22|and Phicol the general of his army|et Phicol princeps exercitus ejus]], [[21:22|said to Abraham: God is with thee in all that thou dost|ad Abraham : Deus tecum est in universis quæ agis]]. [[21:23|Swear therefore by God, that thou wilt not hurt me, nor my posterity|Jura ergo per Deum, ne noceas mihi et posteris meis]], etc. This Abimelech, knowing that no one can resist God, and recognising that Abraham was the friend of God, feared him because of the help of God, who stood by him in all things; and perhaps this Abimelech had learned how Abraham, aided by God's help, had overcome four kings, as has been told[[Gen 14:15||]] [the margin note here cannot be read; the victory over the four kings is told in Gen 14:14–16]: therefore he makes a pact of peace with Abraham. And Phicol confirmed the king's words by approving them, and asked the same thing with his king.

paras.t: Dixitque Abraham : Ego jurabo. Et increpavit ipse Abraham Abimelech regem, propter puteum aquæ, quem vi abstulerant servi illius. Ille fuit puteus quem angelus ostendit Agar, quem puteum foderat Abraham ante Agar ejectionem. Servi autem Abimelech abstulerant puteum istum Abrahæ violenter pro gregibus aliis adaquandis, ut in Scholastica habetur historia. Responditque Abimelech : Nescivi quis fecerit hanc rem, sed et tu non indicasti mihi hucusque. In quo patet patientia Abrahæ, et quod querulosus non fuit, sed tantum damnum et vim pertulit patienter, quum tamen aqua sit illis in partibus pretiosa.
paras.en: [[21:24|And Abraham said: I will swear|Dixitque Abraham : Ego jurabo]]. [[21:25|And he reproved|Et increpavit]], Abraham himself, [[21:25|Abimelech|Abimelech]] the king, [[21:25|for a well of water, which his servants had taken away by force|propter puteum aquæ, quem vi abstulerant servi illius]]. That was the well which the angel showed to Agar, a well which Abraham had dug before Agar was cast out. And the servants of Abimelech had taken this well from Abraham by violence, to water other flocks, as is found in the Scholastic History. [[21:26|And Abimelech answered: I knew not who did this thing: and thou didst not tell me|Responditque Abimelech : Nescivi quis fecerit hanc rem, sed et tu non indicasti mihi]] until now. In this appears the patience of Abraham, and that he was not given to complaining, but bore so great a loss and violence patiently, although water is precious in those parts.

paras.t: Tulit itaque Abraham oves et boves, et dedit Abimelech, id est, de propriis bobus et ovibus dedit ipsi Abimelech munera, tanquam principi terræ. Percusseruntque ambo fœdus, id est, pactum amicitiæ inierunt cum juramento. Et statuit Abraham septem agnas seorsum, quas dedit regi in testimonium, et in memoriale quod ipse Abraham puteum illum fodisset, et pertineret ad se, ne sibi amplius auferretur.
paras.en: [[21:27|Then Abraham took sheep and oxen, and gave them to Abimelech|Tulit itaque Abraham oves et boves, et dedit Abimelech]], that is, from his own oxen and sheep he gave gifts to Abimelech himself, as to the prince of the land. [[21:27|and both of them made a league|Percusseruntque ambo fœdus]], that is, they entered into a pact of friendship with an oath. [[21:28|And Abraham set apart seven ewelambs|Et statuit Abraham septem agnas seorsum]], which he gave to the king for a testimony and a memorial that Abraham himself had dug that well and that it belonged to him, so that it might not be taken from him any more.

paras.t: Idcirco vocatus est locus ille Bersabee, id est puteus septem, propter septem præfatas agnas : vel puteus juramenti, quia Abraham et Abimelech ibi fœdus cum juramento firmarunt. BEER enim interpretatur puteus : SABA, septem aut juramentum. Quocirca scribit Hieronymus : Isaac non est natus in valle Mambre, sed in Geraris, ubi Bersabee usque hodie oppidulum est. In Scholastica vero historia continetur : A puteo illo circumstans regio dicta est Bersabee. In littera vero exprimitur ratio nominis putei, quum dicitur : Vocatus est locus ille Bersabee, quia ibi uterque juravit, et inierunt fœdus pro puteo Juramenti, etc., id est, pro hoc quod puteus ille pertineret ad Abraham, specialiter tamen pro causa alia jam dicta.
paras.en: [[21:31|Therefore that place was called Bersabee|Idcirco vocatus est locus ille Bersabee]], that is, *well of seven*, because of the seven lambs mentioned; or *well of the oath*, because Abraham and Abimelech confirmed a league there with an oath. For BEER is interpreted *well*, SABA *seven* or *oath*. Wherefore Jerome writes: Isaac was not born in the valley of Mambre but in Gerara, where Bersabee is a small town to this day. And in the Scholastic History it is contained: From that well the surrounding region was called Bersabee. But in the letter the reason for the well's name is expressed, when it is said: [[21:31|that place was called Bersabee|vocatus est locus ille Bersabee]], [[21:31|because there both of them did swear|quia ibi uterque juravit]], [[21:32|And they made a league for the well of oath|et inierunt fœdus pro puteo Juramenti]], etc., that is, on the terms that that well should belong to Abraham, but especially for the other cause already mentioned.

paras.t: Reversique sunt Abimelech et Phicol cum suis ministris in terram Philistinorum, quæ est terra Palæstinæ, seu pars ipsius : hoc est, ad urbem suæ habitationis, quæ fuit in terra Philistiim, quam tamen non erant in toto egressi, veniendo ad Abraham. Abraham vero plantavit nemus in Bersabee, etc., id est, copiam arborum circa puteum illum, forsan ut de fructibus arborum domestici et hospites sui reficerentur : et secundum Augustinum, ipse emerat spatium illud, in quo nemus plantavit. Et fuit colonus terræ Philistinorum vel ut alii habent, Palæstinorum, multis diebus, habitando in ea quasi in aliena : dicuntque aliqui, quod habitavit in ea annis viginti quinque. Postremo, quod Abraham dicitur non accepisse hereditatem in terra repromissionis, seu in ista, nec passum pedis, ut in Actis dicitur, Augustinus intelligit de hereditate sibi a Domino danda, non de hereditate pretio empta.
paras.en: [[21:33|returned|Reversique sunt]] [[21:33|Abimelech and Phicol|Abimelech et Phicol]] with their attendants [[21:33|to the land of the Palestines|in terram Philistinorum]] [Denis reads *Philistinorum*, "of the Philistines", where the Vulgate has *Palæstinorum*], which is the land of Palestine, or part of it: that is, to the city where they dwelt, which was in the land of the Philistines, which, however, they had not entirely left in coming to Abraham. [[21:33|But Abraham planted a grove in Bersabee|Abraham vero plantavit nemus in Bersabee]], etc., that is, a great number of trees around that well, perhaps so that his household and guests might be refreshed with the fruit of the trees; and according to Augustine he had bought that space in which he planted the grove. [[21:34|And he was a sojourner in the land of the Palestines|Et fuit colonus terræ Philistinorum]], or, as others have it, *of the Palæstines*, [[21:34|many days|multis diebus]], dwelling in it as in a land not his own; and some say that he dwelt in it twenty-five years. Lastly, as to Abraham being said not to have received an inheritance in the land of promise, that is, in this land, [[Acts 7:5|no, not the pace of a foot|nec passum pedis]], as is said in the Acts, Augustine understands it of an inheritance to be given him by the Lord, not of an inheritance bought for a price.

paras.t: Juxta mysticos sensus, per supernaturalem fecundationem partumque Sarræ, intelligitur superadmirabilis nativitas Christi de Virgine, a Sancto Spiritu fecundata. Christus quoque est risus et gaudium omnium electorum, quoniam ipse est Desideratus cunctis gentibus, eoque nato angeli cecinerunt : Gloria in altissimis Deo. Et angelus dixit pastoribus : Evangelizo vobis gaudium magnum, quia natus est vobis hodie Salvator. Per Abraham potest intelligi Deus Pater ; et per centenariam ejus ætatem, æternitas Dei Patris, qua invariabiliter perdurante, Virgo sacratissima genuit Filium ejus. Insuper Virgo dignissima dicere quivit cum Sara : Risum fecit mihi Deus, id est, materiam summæ exsultationis contulit mihi, faciendo me matrem Unigeniti sui inviolatam. Quicumque audierit, corridebit mihi : quia universi fideles congratulantur in hac beatissimæ Virgini. Quod autem hæc Virgo filium lactavit, tam supernaturale erat, quod quasi incredibile videbatur.
paras.en: In the mystical senses, by the fruitfulness and childbearing of Sara above nature is understood the more than wonderful birth of Christ from the Virgin, made fruitful by the Holy Ghost. Christ too is the laughter and joy of all the elect, since he is [[Agg 2:8|the desired of all nations|Desideratus cunctis gentibus]]; and when he was born the angels sang: [[Luke 2:14|Glory to God in the highest|Gloria in altissimis Deo]]. And the angel said to the shepherds: [[Luke 2:10|I bring you good tidings of great joy|Evangelizo vobis gaudium magnum]], [[Luke 2:11|For, this day is born to you a Saviour|quia natus est vobis hodie Salvator]]. By Abraham can be understood God the Father, and by his hundred years the eternity of God the Father, during which, abiding unchangeably, the most holy Virgin bore his Son. Moreover the most worthy Virgin could say with Sara: [[21:6|God hath made a laughter for me|Risum fecit mihi Deus]], that is, he has given me matter of the highest exultation, by making me the inviolate mother of his Only-begotten. [[21:6|whosoever shall hear of it will laugh with me|Quicumque audierit, corridebit mihi]]: because all the faithful rejoice with the most blessed Virgin in this. And that this Virgin suckled her son was so far above nature that it seemed as it were incredible.

paras.t: Præterea, quod Abraham fecit convivium in die ablactationis Isaac, hoc designat, quod Deo præcipue placet abstractio fidelium a carnalibus oblectamentis. Propter quod loquitur Isaias : Quem docebit Dominus scientiam ? et quem intelligere faciet auditum ? Ablactatos a lacte, avulsos ab ubere. Per crudelem vero lusum Ismaelis cum Isaac, figurata est derisio Christi et ejus fidelium, ab induratis atrocibusque Judæis, ac ceteris perfidis. Quod et Apostolus ad Galatas exponendo disseruit, quod electi et spirituales Israelitæ a carnalibus illis Judæis persecutionem sunt passi. Per ejectionem demum ancillæ et filii ejus de domo Abrahæ, significata est reprobatio perfidæ Synagogæ, et carnalium filiorum ipsius, ac omnium qui ex solo servili timore serviunt Christo, qui omnes ab electorum Ecclesia repelluntur.
paras.en: Further, that Abraham made a feast on the day of Isaac's weaning signifies that the withdrawal of the faithful from carnal delights is especially pleasing to God. For which reason Isaias says: [[Is 28:9|Whom shall he teach knowledge? and whom shall he make to understand the hearing? them that are weaned from the milk, that are drawn away from the breasts|Quem docebit Dominus scientiam ? et quem intelligere faciet auditum ? Ablactatos a lacte, avulsos ab ubere]]. And by the cruel play of Ismael with Isaac is figured the mockery of Christ and his faithful by the hardened and savage Jews and other faithless men. This the Apostle too set forth in expounding it to the Galatians[[Gal 4:29||]]: that the elect and spiritual Israelites suffered persecution from those carnal Jews. Lastly, by the casting out of the bondwoman and her son from Abraham's house is signified the rejection of the faithless Synagogue and of its carnal sons, and of all who serve Christ out of servile fear alone, all of whom are driven out of the Church of the elect.

paras.t: Insuper, per hoc quod Abraham imposuit ipsi Agar panes et utrem aquæ, datur intelligi, quod infideli Synagogæ Deus reliquit sua carnalia sacramenta, et litteralem atque insipidam Scripturarum expositionem. Propter quod errat in solitudine, tanquam deserta a Deo, et filiis suis in captivitatem redactis compatitur. Per hoc vero quod angelus hanc Agar vocavit, et filio ejus subvenit per putei aquam, notatur finalis conversio Judæorum, et eorum per Baptismum salvatio.
paras.en: Moreover, by Abraham's putting bread and a bottle of water upon Agar herself, we are given to understand that God left to the unbelieving Synagogue its carnal sacraments and a literal and tasteless exposition of the Scriptures. For which reason she wanders in the wilderness, as one forsaken by God, and suffers with her sons brought into captivity. And by the angel's calling this Agar and helping her son by the water of the well is signified the final conversion of the Jews and their salvation through Baptism.

paras.t: Insuper per hoc, quod Abimelech cum suis venit ad Abraham, eo quod videret Deum esse cum eo, signatum est, quod principes sæculi, gloriam Christi in ejus Ecclesia conspicientes, ad ipsum conversi sunt, et promiserunt obedientiam ei, abrenuntiando diabolo in Baptismo. Viderunt namque qualiter Christus per suos discipulos idololatriam undique dissipavit, et infinita, soloque omnipotenti Deo possibilia fecit miracula. Et increpavit Abimelech propter puteum aquæ, quem vi abstulerant servi illius : hoc est, Christus per suos ministros reprehendit principes conversos, saltem in sacramentali eorum confessione, pro hoc quod permiserunt infideles satellites suos impedire fideles ab usu Baptismi, gratiamque Baptismatis præripere seu auferre pro posse hominibus. Quod tamen aliquando contigit, ignorantibus ipsis principibus, nec cognoverunt quam enorme fuerit hoc peccatum, quousque illuminati fuerunt a Christo. At vero per hoc, quod Abraham tulit oves et boves, et dedit eas Abimelech, insinuatur quod conversis principibus Christus adjunxit fideles innocentes et onus divinorum præceptorum promptissime bajulantes, ad ædificandum et confortandum principes illos. Qui principes quandoque tam virtuose se habuerunt, quod Christus populo suo eos præfecit. Percusseruntque ambo fœdus : quia Salvator veniam et salutem eis promisit, ipsi quoque Christo se obtulerunt, et fidelitatem promiserunt eidem.
paras.en: Further, by Abimelech coming with his men to Abraham because he saw that God was with him, it is signified that the princes of the world, beholding the glory of Christ in his Church, were converted to him and promised him obedience, renouncing the devil in Baptism. For they saw how Christ through his disciples scattered idolatry everywhere and worked countless miracles, possible to almighty God alone. [[21:25|And he reproved Abimelech for a well of water, which his servants had taken away by force|Et increpavit Abimelech propter puteum aquæ, quem vi abstulerant servi illius]]: that is, Christ through his ministers rebuked the converted princes, at least in their sacramental confession, for allowing their unbelieving retainers to hinder the faithful from the use of Baptism, and, as far as they could, to snatch away or take from men the grace of Baptism. Yet this sometimes happened without those princes knowing it, nor did they know how enormous this sin was until they were enlightened by Christ. But by Abraham taking sheep and oxen and giving them to Abimelech it is suggested that Christ joined to the converted princes faithful men, innocent and most readily bearing the burden of the divine precepts, to edify and strengthen those princes. And those princes sometimes behaved so virtuously that Christ set them over his people. [[21:27|and both of them made a league|Percusseruntque ambo fœdus]]: because the Saviour promised them pardon and salvation, and they for their part offered themselves to Christ and promised him fidelity.

paras.t: Et statuit Abraham septem agnas seorsum. Per agnas has intelliguntur septem dona Spiritus Sancti, quæ in Ecclesia locum sortiuntur specialem atque præcipuum, quæ Christus largitur conversis, in testimonium quod ipse fodit puteum istum, hoc est, quatenus ipsi per dona illa clare cognoscant et fateantur, quod Dominus Jesus Christus sacramentum Baptismi primo instituit. Idcirco vocatus est locus ille Bersabee, hoc est puteus septem, seu puteus juramenti. In Baptismo etenim infunduntur his, qui baptizantur, septem dona Spiritus Sancti, et ipsi in Baptismo se obligant Deo. Abraham vero plantavit nemus in Bersabee, id est, circa fontem Baptismi in Ecclesia fundavit ac stabilivit multitudinem fidelium copiosam, qui sunt arbores fructuosæ simul locatæ.
paras.en: [[21:28|And Abraham set apart seven ewelambs|Et statuit Abraham septem agnas seorsum]]. By these lambs are understood the seven gifts of the Holy Ghost, which hold a special and chief place in the Church, and which Christ bestows on the converted, in testimony that he himself dug this well: that is, so that through those gifts they may clearly know and confess that the Lord Jesus Christ first instituted the sacrament of Baptism. [[21:31|Therefore that place was called Bersabee|Idcirco vocatus est locus ille Bersabee]], that is, *well of seven*, or *well of the oath*. For in Baptism the seven gifts of the Holy Ghost are poured into those who are baptized, and they in Baptism bind themselves to God. [[21:33|But Abraham planted a grove in Bersabee|Abraham vero plantavit nemus in Bersabee]], that is, around the font of Baptism in the Church he founded and established a copious multitude of the faithful, who are fruitful trees planted together.

22.title: Elucidatio litteralis capituli vicesimi secundi: Quæ postquam gesta sunt, tentavit Deus Abraham
22.title_en: Literal explanation of the twenty-second chapter: After these things, God tempted Abraham

paras.t: Recitatur deinde magnitudo perfectionis Abrahæ in obedientia et fide, excellentia quoque promissionum desuper sibi factarum. Quæ postquam gesta sunt, hoc est, post expletionem eorum quæ scripta sunt capitulo præcedenti, tentavit Deus Abraham. Aliter tentat Deus, aliter caro, aliter mundus, aliterque diabolus. Deus etenim tentat homines, ut probet, ut coronet, ut alios inde ædificet. Tentat, inquam, ut probet, non ut ipse aliquid discat, experiatur, aut sciat, sed ut eum quem tentat, ostendat probatum, fidelem, idoneum: sicque virtus ejus aliis ad eorum ædificationem patescat, sicque is quem tentat, gloriosius coronetur. Diabolus autem tentat ut fallat: caro titillat, et materialiter seu occasionaliter incitat. Qualiter vero intelligendum sit, quod scriptum est alibi, Deus neminem tentat, et de multiplici tentatione; qualiter etiam tentare diversimode conveniat Deo et mundo ac carni atque diabolo, super septem Canonicas, præsertim Jacobi, diffuse scripsi.
paras.en: Next is told the greatness of Abraham's perfection in obedience and faith, and also the excellence of the promises made to him from on high. [[22:1|After these things|Quæ postquam gesta sunt]], that is, after the fulfilment of what was written in the preceding chapter, [[22:1|God tempted Abraham|tentavit Deus Abraham]]. God tempts in one way, the flesh in another, the world in another, and the devil in another. For God tempts men to prove them, to crown them, and to edify others thereby. He tempts, I say, to prove: not that He Himself may learn, find out or know anything, but that He may show the one He tempts to be proven, faithful and fit; and so that his virtue may be made plain to others for their edification, and so that he whom He tempts may be crowned the more gloriously. But the devil tempts in order to deceive; the flesh entices, and stirs one up materially or by way of occasion. How we are to understand what is written elsewhere, that God [[Jas 1:13|tempteth no man|Deus neminem tentat]], and of the many kinds of temptation, and also how tempting belongs in different ways to God, to the world, to the flesh and to the devil, I have written at length on the seven Canonical Epistles, especially on James.

paras.t: Itaque Deus tentavit Abraham, id est, experimentum seu probationem sumpsit de fide et obedientia ejus; et dixit ad eum in visione nocturna, sive in somno factum sit hoc, sive in vigilia, et per angelicam apparitionem ac subministrationem locutus est: Abraham, Abraham. Repetitio nominis, indicium est amoris ac familiaritatis, atque excitandæ attentionis. Circa quod loquitur Origenes: Vir iste prius vocabatur Abram, et nusquam legimus, quod hoc nomine vocaverit eum Deus, aut dixerit ad eum, Abram. Non enim vocandus fuit a Deo nomine delendo, sed nomine quod ipse Deus donavit. At ille respondit: Adsum. Forsitan ex vocatione illa, et nominis sui ingeminatione evigilavit, quemadmodum primo Regum habetur de Samuele, qui Deo vocante eum atque dicente, Samuel, Samuel, surrexit de somno, et cucurrit ad Heli.
paras.en: So [[22:1|God tempted Abraham|Deus tentavit Abraham]], that is, He made trial or proof of his faith and obedience; [[22:1|and said to him|et dixit ad eum]] in a vision by night (whether this happened in sleep or awake), and He spoke through an angelic apparition and ministry: [[22:1|Abraham, Abraham|Abraham, Abraham]]. The repetition of the name is a sign of love and familiarity, and is meant to rouse attention. On this Origen says: This man was formerly called Abram, and nowhere do we read that God called him by this name or said to him: Abram. For he was not to be called by God by a name that was to be done away, but by the name which God Himself had given. [[22:1|And he answered: Here I am|At ille respondit: Adsum]]. Perhaps at that call and the doubling of his name he awoke, as is told in the first book of Kings of Samuel, who, when God called him and said, [[1 Kings 3:10|Samuel, Samuel|Samuel, Samuel]], rose from sleep and ran to Heli[[1 Kings 3:4||]][[1 Kings 3:5||]].

paras.t: Ait illi: Tolle, id est tecum accipe, filium tuum unigenitum quem diligis Isaac, et vade in terram Visionis, id est in Judæam, præsertim in illam Judææ partem, quæ inter montana est sita: quæ dicitur terra Visionis, quoniam ipsa a longe, et de ea a longe videri poterat, ut in Scholastica historia continetur; vel quia in ea habuit Abraham plures visiones seu apparitiones et revelationes divinas, quemadmodum ex præhabitis elucescit. Unde in Isaia Jerusalem seu Judæa vallis Visionis vocatur, quo scribitur, Onus vallis Visionis; quoniam fuit terra habitationis Prophetarum, quibus copiosissime factæ sunt revelationes et visiones cœlestes. Quidam per terram Visionis, intelligit montem qui fuit tunc prope Jerusalem, in quo monte Dominus jussit ipsum Isaac sibi offerri: qui mons dicitur terra Visionis, quia ab eo poterat terra promissionis in circuitu late ac longe videri. Sed hoc reprobat Rabbi Paulus, quoniam Deus primo non ostendit Abrahæ montem in quo Isaac immolari debebat, sed terram in qua erat mons ille: et istud apparet verum, præsertim quoniam Deus loquitur de terra Visionis, et de monte isto quasi de duobus locis distinctis, dicendo: Vade in terram Visionis, atque ibi offer eum in holocaustum super unum montium quem monstravero tibi. Reprobat quoque Rabbi Paulus, quod dictum est, terram promissionis potuisse in circuitu conspici a monte præfato: quia visio talis impediebatur per altos montes in circuitu Jerusalem exsistentes. Sed istud non videtur efficaciter dictum. Nam dici posset, quod mons ille fuit altior aliis montibus, imo in Scholastica fertur historia: In summitate montium Judææ, erat monticulus eminentior aliis, dictus mons Moria.
paras.en: [[22:2|He said to him: Take|Ait illi: Tolle]], that is, take with thee, [[22:2|thy only begotten son Isaac, whom thou lovest|filium tuum unigenitum quem diligis Isaac]], [[22:2|and go into the land of vision|et vade in terram Visionis]], that is, into Judea, and especially into that part of Judea which lies among the mountains. It is called the land of vision because it could be seen from afar, and from it one could see far off, as the Scholastic History has it; or because in it Abraham had many divine visions or apparitions and revelations, as is clear from what has gone before. Hence in Isaias Jerusalem, or Judea, is called the valley of vision, where it is written: [[Is 22:1|The burden of the valley of vision|Onus vallis Visionis]]; for it was the land where the Prophets dwelt, to whom heavenly revelations and visions were given in great abundance. Someone understands by the land of vision the mountain which was then near Jerusalem, on which the Lord commanded that Isaac be offered to Him: this mountain is called the land of vision because from it the land of promise could be seen far and wide all around. But Rabbi Paul rejects this, since God did not first show Abraham the mountain on which Isaac was to be sacrificed, but the land in which that mountain was. And this appears true, especially since God speaks of the land of vision and of that mountain as of two distinct places, saying: [[22:2|go into the land of vision; and there thou shalt offer him for an holocaust upon one of the mountains which I will shew thee|Vade in terram Visionis, atque ibi offer eum in holocaustum super unum montium quem monstravero tibi]]. Rabbi Paul also rejects the saying that the land of promise could be seen all around from that mountain, since such a view was blocked by the high mountains that stand round about Jerusalem. But this does not seem to be said convincingly. For one could say that that mountain was higher than the other mountains; indeed the Scholastic History says: On the summit of the mountains of Judea there was a hillock higher than the others, called mount Moria.

paras.t: Unde subjungitur: Atque offer eum in holocaustum, super unum montium quem monstravero tibi, id est, ad majestatis meæ honorem, filium tuum carissimum macta sive occide, atque occisum totum corpus ejus combure, ut cineres tantum de ipso remaneant. Istud erat difficillimum opus, in quo obedientia poterat perfecte examinari. Denique Deus volens fidem et obedientiam Abrahæ plene probare, jussit ei occidere filium, de quo jam sæpe promissiones a Deo accepit, quod in ipso vocaretur ei semen, et quod reges et nationes nascerentur ex filio illo. Ea quoque verba protulit Deus, quæ erant maxime inflammativa cordis paterni ad filium illum, dicens: Tolle filium tuum unigenitum quem diligis Isaac, ut ex hoc augeretur difficultas implendi præceptum, et Abrahæ obedientia plenius commendaretur. Hinc etiam jussit Deus, ut iret ad locum ita remotum. Unde Josephus refert: Abraham nimium diligebat ipsum Isaac, quum esset unigenitus, eique a Deo pro munere et in senectute concessus; et ipse puer parentes suos provocavit ad suum favorem atque amorem, eo quod omni virtuti studeret, et parentum haberet sollicitudinem, et affectum circa Dei religionem. Erat autem unigenitus Abrahæ ex Sara. Nec dubium quin Abraham diligebat Ismaelem; sed per verba illa, Quem diligis, datur intelligi, quod valde specialiter dilexit Isaac, quemadmodum Evangelista Joannes, de se ipso dicendo, Hic est discipulus ille, quem diligebat Jesus, insinuat se specialiter dilectum a Domino Jesu.
paras.en: Hence it is added: [[22:2|thou shalt offer him for an holocaust upon one of the mountains which I will shew thee|Atque offer eum in holocaustum, super unum montium quem monstravero tibi]]: that is, to the honour of My majesty slay or kill thy dearest son, and when he is slain burn his whole body, so that only ashes remain of him. This was a most difficult work, in which obedience could be perfectly tested. For God, wishing to prove Abraham's faith and obedience to the full, commanded him to kill the son concerning whom he had already often received promises from God: that in him his seed should be called, and that kings and nations should be born of that son. God also used the words that were most apt to inflame a father's heart towards that son, saying: [[22:2|Take thy only begotten son Isaac, whom thou lovest|Tolle filium tuum unigenitum quem diligis Isaac]], so that the difficulty of fulfilling the command might be increased by this, and Abraham's obedience more fully commended. It was for this reason too that God commanded him to go to so distant a place. Hence Josephus relates: Abraham loved Isaac exceedingly, since he was his only begotten, granted him by God as a gift and in his old age; and the boy himself drew his parents to favour and love him, because he applied himself to every virtue, was attentive to his parents, and was devoted to the worship of God. Now he was Abraham's only begotten by Sara. Nor is there any doubt that Abraham loved Ismael; but by the words [[22:2|whom thou lovest|Quem diligis]] we are given to understand that he loved Isaac in a quite special way, as John the Evangelist, saying of himself, This is the disciple [[John 21:7|whom Jesus loved|quem diligebat Jesus]][[John 13:23||]], suggests that he was specially loved by the Lord Jesus.

paras.t: Insuper, secundum Hieronymum, mons in quo Dominus jussit Isaac immolari, fuit mons Moria, qui postea additus est civitati Jerusalem, et in ea inclusus, in quo Salomon templum construxit, juxta illud: Cœperunt ædificare templum in monte Moria. Dicit autem Rabbi Paulus, quod in monte hoc celebrata est passio Christi, et quod in eo Christus se obtulit Patri: quod non est idonee dictum, quia in monte Calvariæ passus est Christus; tamen in monte isto aut prope fuit cænaculum, in quo Salvator cum Apostolis agnum comedit paschalem, et altaris instituit Sacramentum.
paras.en: Moreover, according to Jerome, the mountain on which the Lord commanded that Isaac be sacrificed was mount Moria, which was afterwards added to the city of Jerusalem and enclosed in it, and on which Solomon built the Temple, according to the words: They [[2 Par 3:1|began to build the house of the Lord in Jerusalem, in mount Moria|Cœperunt ædificare templum in monte Moria]] [the margin note here cannot be read; the words are from 2 Par 3:1, which has "the house of the Lord" where Denis has "the temple"]. Rabbi Paul says that the Passion of Christ took place on this mountain, and that on it Christ offered Himself to the Father. This is not rightly said, since Christ suffered on mount Calvary; yet on this mountain, or near it, was the upper room in which the Saviour ate the paschal lamb with the Apostles and instituted the Sacrament of the altar [a margin note here cannot be read].

paras.t: Igitur Abraham de nocte consurgens: in quo patet fervida suæ mentis promptitudo ad obediendum, quia non præstolabatur usque ad auroram: stravit asinum suum, id est, præparavit eum ad portandum ligna pro holocausto penitus comburendo. Ducens secum duos juvenes, etc., qui (secundum Hebræos) fuerunt Ismael atque Eliezer. Quod non videtur verum, quantum ad Ismaelem, qui (ut capitulo habetur præhabito) jam fuit de domo Abrahæ separatus, atque in deserto Pharan cœperat commorari.
