Sin autem mulier noluerit sequi te, non teneberis juramento, etc., quia per juramentum seu adjurationem nolo te ad impossibilia obligare. Hoc etenim esset contra proprietatem juramenti, cujus tres comites sunt, judicium, id est discretio, veritas atque justitia. Et si quidquam contra aliquid horum trium juratur sive promittitur, non tenet simpliciter, nec obligat absolute.
paras.en: Therefore he adds: [[24:7|The Lord God of heaven, who took|Deus cœli qui tulit]], that is, made to go out, [[24:7|me out of my father's house|me de domo patris mei]], etc., [[24:7|and swore to me, saying: To thy seed will I give this land|qui juravit mihi, dicens : Semini tuo dabo terram hanc]]: [[24:7|he will send his angel before thee|ipse mittet angelum suum coram te]], that is, he will make his holy angel go invisibly before thee, guide thee and keep thee, [[24:7|and thou shalt take from thence a wife for my son|et accipies inde uxorem filio meo]]. Abraham knew by God's revelation that this would come to pass, and seems to have foretold it prophetically; or else it was a word of good hope in God. [[24:8|But if the woman will not follow thee, thou shalt not be bound by the oath|Sin autem mulier noluerit sequi te, non teneberis juramento]], etc., because I do not wish to bind thee to impossibilities by an oath or adjuration. For this would be against the nature of an oath, whose three companions are judgment (that is, discretion), truth and justice. And if anything is sworn or promised against any of these three, it does not hold simply, nor bind absolutely.

paras.t: Posuit ergo servus manum sub femore Abraham domini sui, et juravit illi super sermone hoc, id est, juravit quod verba ista pro posse impleret. Tulitque decem camelos de grege domini sui, et abiit, ex omnibus bonis ejus portans secum. Cameli enim fortia animalia sunt, ad portandum homines et res eorum. Portavit itaque secum pretiosa clenodia, et præsertim ea quæ rara erant in Mesopotamia, ad dandum munuscula atque jocalia puellæ aptæ, et secum venire volenti, ac ejus propinquis. Portavit quoque copiam auri et argenti ac necessariarum rerum in via, tam propter viaticum longi itineris, quam ad ostendendum opulentiam Abrahæ, ut per hoc puella et ejus propinqui citius assentirent causæ propter quam venit. Profectusque perrexit in Mesopotamiam ad urbem Nachor : quæ urbs vocabatur Haran, in qua Nachor frater Abrahæ mansit habitans. Abraham inde egresso ad intrandum terram Chanaan, ut capitulo duodecimo patuit. Circa hoc Josephus ait : Multo labore ac tempore pervenit servus ille in Mesopotamiam, quoniam tempore hiemali est ibi luti profunditas, et tempore æstivali penuria aquæ. In saltibus quoque latrones sunt.
paras.en: [[24:9|The servant, therefore, put his hand under the thigh of Abraham, his lord, and swore to him upon his word|Posuit ergo servus manum sub femore Abraham domini sui, et juravit illi super sermone hoc]], that is, he swore that he would fulfil these words as far as he could. [[24:10|And he took ten camels of his master's herd, and departed, carrying something of all his goods with him|Tulitque decem camelos de grege domini sui, et abiit, ex omnibus bonis ejus portans secum]]. For camels are strong animals, for carrying men and their belongings. So he took with him precious jewels, especially such as were rare in Mesopotamia, to give as little gifts and trinkets to the maid who should be suitable and willing to come with him, and to her kinsfolk. He also took a store of gold and silver and of things needed on the way, both as provision for the long journey and to show Abraham's wealth, so that the maid and her kinsfolk might the sooner consent to the business on which he had come; [[24:10|and he set forward and went on to Mesopotamia, to the city of Nachor|Profectusque perrexit in Mesopotamiam ad urbem Nachor]]: this city was called Haran, and in it Nachor, Abraham's brother, stayed on and dwelt when Abraham had gone out from it to enter the land of Chanaan, as was shown in the twelfth chapter. On this Josephus says: That servant reached Mesopotamia with much labour and time, since in winter there is deep mud there, and in summer a want of water; and in the forests there are robbers.

paras.t: Quumque camelos fecisset accumbere, etc., id est quiescere ac refici, quos nolebat introducere impotens, oravit Dominum, dicens : Domine Deus domini mei Abraham : nam Deus omnium, erat tanto specialius Deus Abrahæ, quanto gratiosius habuit se circa eum, et quanto ipse Abraham devotius coluit Deum ; occurre, obsecro, mihi hodie, id est, pietatis tuæ effectum mihi nunc evidenter impende ac monstra, et fac misericordiam cum domino meo Abraham, providendo ejus filio de uxore idonea. Deinde describitur signum, quod servus iste in se excogitavit, per cujus eventum posset cognoscere quod Deus prosperum iter suum fecisset, et quæ esset puella filio Abrahæ divinitus prævisa ac præparata : utpote quod illa esset quæ sibi petenti porrigeret potum, et non sibi dumtaxat, sed et camelis, præsertim aliis mulieribus id sibi negantibus, ut adjecit Josephus, quamvis hoc non exprimatur in textu : alias non videtur fuisse in signo illo aliquid rarum aut magnum, quamvis quidam hoc reprobet. Ecce ego sto prope fontem aquæ, id est puteum, et filiæ habitatorum hujus civitatis egredientur ad hauriendam aquam. Fuit enim consuetudo ibi, ut pariter egrederentur pro aqua, quæ ibi non abundavit, sed cara fuit.
paras.en: [[24:11|And when he had made the camels lie down|Quumque camelos fecisset accumbere]], etc., that is, rest and be refreshed, which he was unwilling to bring in [the printed text reads *impotens*, "unable", which makes little sense here; perhaps it should be *in oppidum*, "into the town", the verse having "without the town"], he prayed to the Lord, saying: [[24:12|O Lord, the God of my master, Abraham|Domine Deus domini mei Abraham]]: for though he was the God of all, he was the more especially the God of Abraham, the more graciously he had dealt with him and the more devoutly Abraham himself worshipped God; [[24:12|meet me today, I beseech thee|occurre, obsecro, mihi hodie]], that is, bestow on me now and show plainly the effect of thy goodness, [[24:12|and shew kindness to my master, Abraham|et fac misericordiam cum domino meo Abraham]], by providing his son with a fitting wife. Then is described the sign which this servant devised within himself, by whose outcome he might know that God [[24:21|had made his journey prosperous|prosperum iter suum fecisset]], and which maid had been foreseen and prepared by God for Abraham's son: namely, that she should be the one who, when he asked, would offer him drink, and not only to him but to the camels too, and this while the other women refused him it, as Josephus adds, though this is not expressed in the text; otherwise there seems to have been nothing rare or great in that sign, though some reject this. [[24:13|Behold, I stand nigh the spring of water|Ecce ego sto prope fontem aquæ]], that is, the well, [[24:13|and the daughters of the inhabitants of this city will come out to draw water|et filiæ habitatorum hujus civitatis egredientur ad hauriendam aquam]]. For it was the custom there for them to go out together for water, which was not plentiful there but scarce [literally "dear"].

paras.t: Igitur puella cui ego dixero, Inclina hydriam tuam ut bibam, et illa responderit, Bibe, etc. Necdum intra se verba compleverat, id est, nondum ista plenarie cogitavit, et ecce Rebecca egrediebatur, filia Bathuel, etc., habens hydriam in scapula sua, etc., in qua jam hauserat aquam. Occurritque ei servus Abrahæ : ex quo apparet, quod interim dum Rebecca puteum accessit, et aquam hausit, servus Abrahæ parum discessit a puteo, et redire illuc incepit, quum ipsam Rebeccam viderat a puteo regredi ; et ait : Pauxillum aquæ mihi ad bibendum præbe de hydria tua, etc. Quumque ille bibisset, adjecit : Quin et camelis tuis hauriam aquam, etc. Effundensque hydriam in canalibus, id est receptaculis illis aquarum, ex quibus animalia bibebant, quæ receptacula erant magna ligna aut saxa cavata, quæ nunc canales vocantur, recurrit ad puteum, etc. Ex quibus patet magna obsequiositas, caritas, pietasque Rebeccæ, quod circa virum alienum ignotum tam amorose se habuit : imo, secundum Josephum, increpavit puellas tanquam inclementes, quæ potum aquæ negaverunt peregrino.
paras.en: [[24:14|Now, therefore, the maid to whom I shall say: Let down thy pitcher that I may drink|Igitur puella cui ego dixero, Inclina hydriam tuam ut bibam]], [[24:14|and she shall answer, Drink|et illa responderit, Bibe]], etc. [[24:15|He had not yet ended these words within himself|Necdum intra se verba compleverat]], that is, he had not yet fully thought these things through, [[24:15|and behold Rebecca came out, the daughter of Bathuel|et ecce Rebecca egrediebatur, filia Bathuel]], etc., [[24:15|having a pitcher on her shoulder|habens hydriam in scapula sua]], etc., in which she had already drawn water. [[24:17|And the servant ran to meet her|Occurritque ei servus]] of Abraham: from which it appears that, while Rebecca went to the well and drew water, Abraham's servant went a little way off from the well, and began to go back there when he saw Rebecca herself coming back from the well; [[24:17|and said: Give me a little water to drink of thy pitcher|et ait : Pauxillum aquæ mihi ad bibendum præbe de hydria tua]], etc. [[24:19|And when he had drunk, she said: I will draw water for thy camels also|Quumque ille bibisset, adjecit : Quin et camelis tuis hauriam aquam]], etc. [[24:20|And pouring out the pitcher into the troughs|Effundensque hydriam in canalibus]], that is, into those receptacles for water from which the animals drank, which were large hollowed logs or stones, now called *canales* [troughs, or channels], [[24:20|she ran back to the well|recurrit ad puteum]], etc. From all this appear the great obligingness, charity and kindness of Rebecca, in that she behaved so lovingly toward a strange man unknown to her; indeed, according to Josephus, she rebuked the other girls as unkind for refusing a drink of water to a stranger.

paras.t: Postquam autem […] […] […] protulit vir, scilicet servus Abrahæ […] […], id est valentes […], ita quod vel ambæ simul fuerunt tanti valoris aut unaquæque earum. Dedit equidem puellæ duas inaures, quæ sunt aurium ornamenta, ut in qualibet aure una penderet, et armillas totidem in […], pondo, id est pondere, siclorum decem. Sunt autem armillæ, brachiorum ornamenta. Porro secundum Hieronymum, siclus continet unciam. Verumtamen de istis ponderibus ignoramus, quanti valoris extiterint, secundum nostras computationes, quum certum sit, pondera ac mensuras re et nomine apud diversos diversimode variari.
paras.en: [[24:22|And after that|Postquam autem]] […] [[24:22|the man took out|protulit vir]], namely Abraham's servant, […], that is, worth […], so that either both together, or each of them, were of that value. So he gave the maid two earrings, which are ornaments of the ears, so that one might hang in each ear, [[24:22|and as many bracelets|et armillas totidem]] in […], *pondo* (that is, by weight) [[24:22|of ten sicles weight|siclorum decem]]. Now bracelets are ornaments of the arms. Further, according to Jerome, a sicle contains an ounce. Yet we do not know what these weights were worth by our reckoning, since it is certain that weights and measures vary, in substance and in name, among different peoples.

paras.t: Dixitque ad eam : Cujus es filia ? Probabile est, quod interrogavit hoc, et interrogationis suæ responsionem a puella audivit, antequam tam pretiosa clenodia ei præstabat. Attamen Rabbi Paulus dicit oppositum. Nam opinatur, quod sicut Rebecca habuit se curialiter, obsequiose ac humiliter circa virum, ita et ipse ex curialitate dedit ei hæc munera ; sed primum verius reor, et infra in isto capitulo insinuatur, quod prius interrogavit, et postea dedit. Scriptura autem recitando historias, non semper observat ordinem rei gestæ. Josephus quoque insinuat, quod primo interrogavit ; addit tamen, quod quasi pro præmio laboris ac poculi contulit prima munuscula, justum affirmans, ut talia acciperet, quæ præter ceteras fuit tam pia.
paras.en: [[24:23|And he said to her: Whose daughter art thou?|Dixitque ad eam : Cujus es filia]] It is probable that he asked this, and heard the maid's answer to his question, before he gave her such precious jewels. Yet Rabbi Paul [Paul of Burgos, a converted rabbi, author of the Additions to Lyra's Postill] says the opposite: for he thinks that, as Rebecca behaved courteously, obligingly and humbly toward the man, so he too, out of courtesy, gave her these gifts. But I think the first the truer view, and it is suggested below in this chapter that he first asked and afterwards gave; for Scripture, in recounting histories, does not always keep the order in which things were done. Josephus too suggests that he asked first; he adds, however, that he gave her the first little gifts as a reward, as it were, for her labour and the drink, saying that it was just that she should receive such things, who had been so kind beyond the others.

paras.t: Quæ respondit : Filia sum Bathuelis, etc. Inclinavit se homo, et adoravit Dominum, dicens : Benedictus Dominus Deus, etc., qui recto itinere me perduxit in domum fratris domini mei, hoc est ad domum et progeniem Nachor, qui fuit frater Abrahæ. Jam enim reputavit se vir iste esse quasi in domo Nachor, quia parum inde distabat, et facillime poterat eam attingere.
paras.en: [[24:24|And she answered: I am the daughter of Bathuel|Quæ respondit : Filia sum Bathuelis]], etc. [[24:26|The man bowed himself down, and adored the Lord|Inclinavit se homo, et adoravit Dominum]], [[24:27|Saying: Blessed be the Lord God|dicens : Benedictus Dominus Deus]], etc., [[24:27|and hath brought me the straight way into the house of my master's brother|qui recto itinere me perduxit in domum fratris domini mei]], that is, to the house and stock of Nachor, who was Abraham's brother. For the man already reckoned himself as good as in Nachor's house, because he was only a little way from it and could very easily reach it.

paras.t: Cucurrit itaque puella, et nuntiabat in domo matris suæ. Ex hoc verbo opinatus est Josephus, quod Bathuel pater Rebeccæ jam obiit ; alias potius dictum esset, Nuntiabat in domo patris. Alii vero dicunt oppositum, quia infra habetur, Responderunt Laban et Bathuel ; et quia mulieres habebant tabernacula quædam separata in domibus maritorum, in quibus cum filiabus et ancillis exercebant opera feminis competentia. Quid autem dicendum sit ad primum istorum, patebit in expositione verbi præallegati, nec istud est magni vigoris.
paras.en: [[24:28|Then the maid ran, and told in her mother's house|Cucurrit itaque puella, et nuntiabat in domo matris suæ]]. From this word Josephus supposed that Bathuel, Rebecca's father, was already dead; otherwise it would rather have been said: She told in her father's house. But others say the opposite, because we find below: [[24:50|And Laban and Bathuel answered|Responderunt Laban et Bathuel]]; and because women had certain separate tents in their husbands' houses, in which, with their daughters and handmaids, they did the work proper to women. What is to be said to the first of these will be plain in the exposition of the word just cited; nor is this second one of much force.

paras.t: Habebat autem Rebecca fratrem nomine Laban. Qui, etc., venit ad virum, dixitque ad eum : Ingredere, benedicte Domini, id est, tu qui es benedictus a Domino ; sicque Laban idololatra scivit aliquid loqui de Deo. Et introduxit eum in hospitium, ac destravit camelos, deponendo sellas et onera desuper posita, deditque paleas et fœnum in pabulum camelorum, et aquam ad lavandum pedes ejus et virorum qui venerant cum eo, scilicet servo Abrahæ principali : et forte juxta numerum camelorum fuit numerus virorum illorum, qui et ipsi fuerunt servi Abrahæ inferiores servo præfato, ut creditur.
paras.en: [[24:29|And Rebecca had a brother, named Laban|Habebat autem Rebecca fratrem nomine Laban]]. He, etc., [[24:30|came to the man|venit ad virum]], [[24:31|And said to him: Come in, thou blessed of the Lord|dixitque ad eum : Ingredere, benedicte Domini]], that is, thou who art blessed by the Lord; and so Laban, an idolater, knew how to say something of God. [[24:32|And he brought him into his lodging; and he unharnessed the camels|Et introduxit eum in hospitium, ac destravit camelos]], taking off the saddles and the loads laid on them, [[24:32|and gave straw and hay|deditque paleas et fœnum]] as fodder for the camels, [[24:32|and water to wash his feet, and the feet of the men that were come with him|et aquam ad lavandum pedes ejus et virorum qui venerant cum eo]], that is, with Abraham's chief servant; and perhaps the number of those men matched the number of the camels; they too were servants of Abraham, of lower rank than the said servant, as is believed.

paras.t: Et appositus est in conspectu ejus panis, id est, cibus et potus coram servo isto et viris istis sunt positi. Qui ait : Non comedam donec loquar sermones meos. Ex quo innotescunt fervor et fidelitas hujus servi, qui fuit legatus fidelis. Respondit ei Laban, qui videtur fuisse senior frater Rebeccæ : Loquere. At ille : Servus, inquit, Abraham sum, etc. Littera plana est. Deditque ei omnia quæ habuerat, etc., id est, Abraham ordinavit, ut omnia principalia bona sua devolvantur ad Isaac filium suum, qui est ei nunc unicus ex Sara principali conjuge sua.
paras.en: [[24:33|And bread was set before him|Et appositus est in conspectu ejus panis]], that is, food and drink were set before this servant and these men. [[24:33|But he said: I will not eat, till I tell my message|Qui ait : Non comedam donec loquar sermones meos]]. From this appear the zeal and faithfulness of this servant, who was a faithful envoy. [[24:33|He answered him|Respondit ei]] Laban, who seems to have been Rebecca's elder brother: [[24:33|Speak|Loquere]]. [[24:34|And he said: I am the servant of Abraham|At ille : Servus, inquit, Abraham sum]], etc. The letter is plain. [[24:36|and he hath given him all that he had|Deditque ei omnia quæ habuerat]], etc., that is, Abraham arranged that all his principal goods should pass to Isaac his son, who is now his only son by Sara, his principal wife.

paras.t: Innocens eris a maledictione mea, etc. Hoc est verbum Abrahæ ad servum istum : et est sensus, Non incurres culpam, aut pœnam violationis juramenti quod mihi præstitisti, de adducenda conjuge filio meo, si non poteris aliquam aptam adducere.
paras.en: [[24:41|But thou shalt be clear from my curse|Innocens eris a maledictione mea]], etc. This is Abraham's word to this servant, and the sense is: Thou shalt not incur the guilt, or the penalty, of breaking the oath thou hast sworn me about bringing a wife for my son, if thou canst not bring any suitable one.

paras.t: Deinde servus ait : Veni ergo hodie ad fontem aquæ : non quod uno die pervenerit a domo Abrahæ usque ad puteum istum, ut Judæi stolide fabulantur ; sed sensus est, Hodie viam meam continuando perduxi usque ad terminum istum. Et dixi : Domine Deus, etc., virgo quæ egredietur ad hauriendam aquam, et audierit a me, Da mihi paululum aquæ, etc., ipsa est, quam præparavit Dominus universorum, filio domini mei, id est Isaac.
paras.en: Then the servant says: [[24:42|And I came today to the well of water|Veni ergo hodie ad fontem aquæ]]: not that he came in one day from Abraham's house to this well, as the Jews foolishly fable; but the sense is: Today, continuing my journey, I have brought it to this goal. [[24:42|and said: O Lord God|Et dixi : Domine Deus]], etc., [[24:43|and the virgin, that shall come out to draw water|virgo quæ egredietur ad hauriendam aquam]], [[24:43|who shall hear me say: Give me a little water|et audierit a me, Da mihi paululum aquæ]], etc., [[24:44|let the same be the woman, whom the Lord hath prepared|ipsa est, quam præparavit Dominus]] of all, [[24:44|for my master's son|filio domini mei]], that is, Isaac.

paras.t: Circa hoc loquitur Augustinus: Quærendum est, quid differant augurationes illicitæ ab ista petitione servi, petentis sibi a Domino ostendi futuram ipsius Isaac conjugem, a qua sibi potum petenti diceretur, Bibe, quin et camelis tuis potum tribuam. Sed aliud est, petere quod ipso miraculo signum sit: aliud, observare ea quæ ita fiunt, ut mira non sint, sed a conjectoribus superstitiosa vanitate interpretentur. Sed et non parva quæstio est, utrum sit audendum hoc ipsum quod mirum aliquid postuletur, quo significetur, quod quis appetit nosse. Ad hoc namque pertinet, quod dicuntur Deum tentare, qui non recte hoc faciunt: contra quod dicitur, Non tentabis Dominum Deum tuum. Suggerebatur namque Christo, tanquam homini, ut signo aliquo exploraret, quantum apud Deum posset: quod fit utique vitiose. Ab hoc autem discernitur, quod Gedeon fecit, imminente pugnæ periculo. Consultatio namque Dei magis, quam ejus tentatio, fuit quod fecit. Unde Achaz timuit signum petere, ne videretur Deum tentare, quum Dominus hoc per Prophetam moneret: forsitan æstimans ipse Achaz, quod a Propheta exploraretur, an memor esset præcepti, quo prohibetur Deum tentare. Hæc Augustinus. Hinc alii dicunt, quod servus iste non quæsivit signum per modum divinationis sive augurii, quod prohibetur; sed oratione præmissa, signum postulavit a Deo, quo experiretur, quod Deus ipse per angelum direxisset iter suum juxta Abrahæ verbum.
paras.en: On this Augustine says: It must be asked how unlawful auguries differ from this request of the servant, who asked the Lord to show him the future wife of Isaac himself, as the one who, when he asked her for drink, would say to him: [[24:14|Drink, and I will give thy camels drink also|Bibe, quin et camelis tuis potum tribuam]]. But it is one thing to ask for something that is a sign by being itself a miracle; another to watch for things that happen in such a way that they are not wonderful, but are interpreted by diviners with superstitious vanity. Yet it is also no small question whether one should dare to do even this: to ask for something wonderful by which may be signified what one desires to know. For to this belongs what is said of those who tempt God, who do this not rightly: against which it is said, [[Matt 4:7|Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God|Non tentabis Dominum Deum tuum]]. For it was suggested to Christ, as to a man, that he should find out by some sign how much he could do with God: which is certainly done sinfully. From this is distinguished what Gedeon did[[Judg 6:39||]] when the danger of battle hung over him; for what he did was a consulting of God rather than a tempting of him. Hence Achaz feared to ask a sign, lest he should seem to tempt God[[Is 7:12||]], although the Lord was urging him to it through the Prophet: Achaz himself thinking, perhaps, that he was being tested by the Prophet, whether he remembered the precept which forbids tempting God. Thus far Augustine. Hence others say that this servant did not seek a sign by way of divination or augury, which is forbidden; but, having first prayed, he asked of God a sign by which he might learn whether God himself had directed his journey through an angel, according to Abraham's word.

paras.t: Deinde Eliezer ait: Interrogavique eam, et dixi: Cujus es filia? Quæ respondit: Filia Bathuelis sum, etc. Suspendi itaque inaures in auribus ejus, ad ornandam faciem ejus: ad cujus decorem ordinatur præcipue, quidquid ornamenti circa caput apponitur; et armillas posui in manibus ejus: ut per eas sua brachia […].
paras.en: Then Eliezer says: [[24:47|And I asked her, and said: Whose daughter art thou? And she answered: I am the daughter of Bathuel|Interrogavique eam, et dixi: Cujus es filia? Quæ respondit: Filia Bathuelis sum]], etc. [[24:47|So I put earrings on her|Suspendi itaque inaures]] in her ears, [[24:47|to adorn her face|ad ornandam faciem ejus]], to whose comeliness is chiefly ordered whatever ornament is put about the head; [[24:47|and I put bracelets on her hands|et armillas posui in manibus ejus]]: so that by them her arms […].

paras.t: Quamobrem si facitis, misericordiam et veritatem cum domino meo, hoc est, si vultis Rebeccam tradere uxorem filio Abrahæ, sicut pium et justum est: pium, quia pro consolatione est Abrahæ, et pro relevamine doloris Isaac filii sui, de suæ matris morte graviter contristati; et quia accommodum est ad bona matrimonii obtinenda: justum quoque et decens est, quoniam ex divina inspiratione id petitur, et quia de una sunt genealogia, quos rectum est copulari. Itaque veritas capitur hic pro justitia, sicut in Psalmo: Universæ viæ Domini misericordia et veritas. Potest tamen veritas nunc sumi pro verificatione, ut sit sensus: Si facitis veritatem cum domino meo, id est, si verba Abrahæ verificatis, implendo quod dixit me sumpturum ex filiabus suæ cognationis puellam pro filio suo, indicate mihi; si autem aliud placet, et hoc dicite mihi, ut vadam ad dexteram sive ad sinistram, hoc est, per viam aptiorem qua potero, vel, ut quidam exponunt, alibi quæram puellam, quæ fiat uxor filii Abrahæ. Aliqui sic exponunt: Ut vadam ad dexteram, id est ad quærendum de filiabus Ismaelis, ad dexteram commorantibus, quantum ad locum istum; vel ad sinistram, hoc est ad quærendum de filiabus Lot, quæ tunc erant de cognatione Abrahæ et Isaac. Sed non videtur, quod Abraham conjunxisset Isaac filio suo aliquam filiarum Lot, quæ incestum cum patre proprio commiserunt.
paras.en: [[24:49|Wherefore, if you do according to mercy and truth with my master|Quamobrem si facitis, misericordiam et veritatem cum domino meo]]: that is, if you are willing to give Rebecca as wife to Abraham's son, as is kind and just [pium et justum: *pium*, kind or dutiful, answers to *mercy*, *justum* to *truth*]. Kind, because it is for the consolation of Abraham, and for the relief of the sorrow of Isaac his son, gravely saddened by his mother's death; and because it is suited to obtaining the goods of marriage [the goods of marriage, as the theologians name them after Augustine: offspring, fidelity and the sacrament]. Just also and fitting, since it is asked by divine inspiration, and because they are of one lineage, whom it is right to join together. So truth is taken here for justice, as in the Psalm: [[Ps 24:10|All the ways of the Lord are mercy and truth|Universæ viæ Domini misericordia et veritas]]. Yet truth may here be taken for verification [that is, the making good of a word], so that the sense is: If you do truth with my master, that is, if you make Abraham's words true by fulfilling what he said, that I would take a girl of the daughters of his kindred for his son, [[24:49|tell me: but if it please you otherwise, tell me that also, that I may go to the right hand, or to the left|indicate mihi; si autem aliud placet, et hoc dicite mihi, ut vadam ad dexteram sive ad sinistram]]: that is, by the more suitable way that I can; or, as some explain, that I may seek a girl elsewhere to become the wife of Abraham's son. Some explain it thus: [[24:49|that I may go to the right hand|Ut vadam ad dexteram]], that is, to seek among the daughters of Ismael, who dwell on the right hand as regards this place; or [[24:49|to the left|ad sinistram]], that is, to seek among the daughters of Lot, who were then of the kindred of Abraham and Isaac. But it does not seem that Abraham would have joined to his son Isaac any of the daughters of Lot, who committed incest with their own father.

paras.t: Responderuntque Laban et Bathuel. Iste Bathuel, secundum quosdam, fuit frater Rebeccæ, et junior ipso Laban: idcirco nominatur post eum. Porro in Scholastica historia tangitur, quod Bathuel in extremis positus, ordinavit ut filia sua Rebecca non traderetur alicui in uxorem, nisi exsistenti de sua progenie: idcirco nunc nomine Bathuelis, designatur mater Rebeccæ, in quantum viri sui mandatum detexit. Alii dicunt, quod pater Rebeccæ adhuc vixit, et nunc nominatur, quamvis filio suo postponatur. Itaque responderunt: A Domino egressus est sermo, id est, petitio qua petis dari Rebeccam in conjugium filio Abrahæ ex divina inspiratione ac ordinatione prolata est, ut patet ex signo quod recitasti. Vel, ut tangit Augustinus, ideo hoc dixerunt, quoniam crediderunt Abraham esse prophetam, qui servo suo prædixit, quod de sua cognatione acciperet unam pro filio suo. Non possumus bene aut de jure extra placitum ejus, scilicet Dei, quidquam aliud loqui tecum. En Rebecca coram te est, etc.
paras.en: [[24:50|And Laban and Bathuel answered|Responderuntque Laban et Bathuel]]. This Bathuel, according to some, was Rebecca's brother, and younger than Laban himself: that is why he is named after him. Moreover, the Scholastic History mentions that Bathuel, when at the point of death, ordained that his daughter Rebecca should not be given to anyone as wife unless he were of his own stock: so that here Rebecca's mother is designated by the name of Bathuel, inasmuch as she made known her husband's command. Others say that Rebecca's father was still living, and is named here although he is put after his son. So they answered: [[24:50|The word hath proceeded from the Lord|A Domino egressus est sermo]], that is, the request by which thou askest that Rebecca be given in marriage to Abraham's son has been put forth by divine inspiration and ordinance, as is clear from the sign thou hast related. Or, as Augustine mentions, they said this because they believed Abraham to be a prophet, who foretold to his servant that he would take one of his kindred for his son. They go on: [[24:50|we cannot|Non possumus]] rightly or lawfully [[24:50|speak any other thing to thee but his pleasure|extra placitum ejus, scilicet Dei, quidquam aliud loqui tecum]], that is, God's. [[24:51|Behold, Rebecca is before thee|En Rebecca coram te est]], etc.

paras.t: Quod quum audisset puer Abraham, id est Eliezer servus ipsius, qui Eliezer fuit jam grandævæ ætatis, ut patet ex præinductis. Quo constat, quam inconsiderate dixerit Rabbi Paulus, quod in Scripturis non vocetur aliquis puer, qui est ultra triginta annos. Iste quippe Eliezer habuit filium nomine Damascum, ante Isaac conceptionem, ut patuit supra, qui Isaac nunc fuit quadraginta annorum. Procedens adoravit in terra Dominum, regratiando ei, quod iter suum tam prospere direxisset: per quod patet viri hujus devotio, imo et fervor, quia in aliorum præsentia se ita in terram prosternere non erubescebat. Prolatisque vasis argenteis et aureis, ac vestibus, quæ sumpsit ex repositoriis seu marsupiis suis, dedit ea Rebeccæ pro munere, id est pro donis jocalibus, quæ dari solent puellis, quæ de novo conceduntur in sponsas. Fratribus quoque ejus et matri dona obtulit. Ex hoc apparentiam habet, quod præfatus Bathuel fuit frater Rebeccæ. Nam si et pater vixisset, et præsens fuisset, data fuissent et ei dona, ut matri ac fratribus, nec Scriptura hoc tacuisset.
paras.en: [[24:52|Which when Abraham's servant heard|Quod quum audisset puer Abraham]] [the Latin has *puer*, "boy", which also means a servant]: that is, Eliezer his servant, who was by now of great age, as is clear from what was brought forward earlier. From this it is plain how thoughtlessly Rabbi Paul said that in the Scriptures no one is called *puer* who is over thirty years old. For this Eliezer had a son named Damascus before Isaac was conceived[[Gen 15:2||]], as was shown above; and Isaac was now forty years old. Then, [[24:52|falling down to the ground, he adored the Lord|Procedens adoravit in terra Dominum]], thanking him for having directed his journey so prosperously: by which this man's devotion is plain, and indeed his fervour, since he did not blush to prostrate himself thus on the ground in the presence of others. [[24:53|And bringing forth vessels of silver and gold, and garments|Prolatisque vasis argenteis et aureis, ac vestibus]], which he took out of his stores or bags, [[24:53|he gave them to Rebecca, for a present|dedit ea Rebeccæ pro munere]], that is, as the gifts of jewellery that are wont to be given to girls newly given in betrothal. [[24:53|He offered gifts also to her brothers, and to her mother|Fratribus quoque ejus et matri dona obtulit]]. From this it appears that the aforesaid Bathuel was Rebecca's brother. For if her father too had been living and present, gifts would have been given to him as well, as to the mother and the brothers, nor would Scripture have kept silent about it.

paras.t: Surgens autem mane, locutus est puer, videlicet servus: Dimittite me, ut vadam ad dominum meum. Responderunt frater ejus, puta Rebeccæ, et mater: et nomine fratris possunt ambo fratres intelligi: Maneat puella saltem decem dies apud nos, etc. Hoc dixerunt ex naturali amore, ne tam cito et quodammodo inopinate separarentur a tam bona, pulchra, et cara propinqua, quam satis conjiciebant se postea aut raro, aut nunquam visuros. Unde quod Rabbi Salomon dicit, Bathuelem patrem Rebeccæ nunc pœnituisse de consensu suo priori, ut filia sua fieret uxor filii Abrahæ, et voluisse hoc impedire, atque ob hoc percussum ab angelo et mortuum, non videtur nisi fictitium, ut etiam Rabbi Paulus circa hæc ait. Nolite, ait servus, me retinere, quia Dominus direxit viam meam, etc.: idcirco non decet ut retardetis iter desuper prosperatum. Ex quo constat, quod voluerunt servum cum ceteris sibi adjunctis tenere secum per decem dies pariter cum Rebecca.
paras.en: [[24:54|And in the morning, the servant arose, and said|Surgens autem mane, locutus est puer]] [the Latin has *puer*, "boy"; Denis adds: namely the servant]: [[24:54|Let me depart, that I may go to my master|Dimittite me, ut vadam ad dominum meum]]. [[24:55|And her brother|Responderunt frater ejus]], that is, Rebecca's, [[24:55|and mother answered|et mater]]; and by the name of brother both brothers can be understood: [[24:55|Let the maid stay, at least, ten days with us|Maneat puella saltem decem dies apud nos]], etc. They said this out of natural love, lest they should be parted so soon and so unexpectedly from so good, fair and dear a kinswoman, whom they rightly guessed they would afterwards see seldom or never. Hence what Rabbi Solomon says, that Bathuel, Rebecca's father, now repented of his earlier consent that his daughter should become the wife of Abraham's son, and wished to prevent it, and for this was struck by an angel and died, seems nothing but a fiction, as Rabbi Paul also says on this passage. [[24:56|Stay me not|Nolite, ait servus, me retinere]], said the servant, [[24:56|because the Lord hath prospered my way|quia Dominus direxit viam meam]], etc.: therefore it is not fitting that you delay a journey prospered from above. From this it is clear that they wished to keep the servant, with the others who were with him, there with them for ten days, together with Rebecca.

paras.t: Et dixerunt: Vocamus puellam, et quæramus illius voluntatem. Hoc quidam exponunt de voluntate puellæ ad ipsum conjugium, quia ad matrimonium requiritur consensus expressus: sed verba sequentia non videntur ita sonare. Nam subditur: Quumque vocata venisset, sciscitati sunt: Vis ire cum homine isto? Sicque requisita videtur de profectione, non de sponsalibus aut consensu conjugii. Quod et S. Ambrosius protestatur. Verumtamen dici potest, quod ex consequenti per hæc verba requisita est de consensu, quia profectio illa ordinabatur ad matrimonium. Quæ ait: Vadam. Hoc non dixit ex carnalitate aut inverecundia, sed ex divino instinctu, quoniam totum istud fuit opus specialis providentiæ Dei. Præterea circa hæc in Scholastica historia dicitur: Hic primo legitur consensus mulieris requisitus, et exinde pro jure habitum est, ut requiratur.
paras.en: [[24:57|And they said: Let us call the maid, and ask her will|Et dixerunt: Vocamus puellam, et quæramus illius voluntatem]]. Some explain this of the girl's will to the marriage itself, since express consent is required for matrimony: but the words that follow do not seem to sound so. For it is added: [[24:58|And they called her, and when she was come, they asked: Wilt thou go with this man?|Quumque vocata venisset, sciscitati sunt: Vis ire cum homine isto?]] And so she seems to be asked about the departure, not about the betrothal or her consent to the marriage; and St Ambrose declares this too. Yet it can be said that by these words she was asked, by consequence, about her consent, since that departure was ordered to matrimony. [[24:58|She said: I will go|Quæ ait: Vadam]]. She did not say this out of carnal desire or immodesty, but by divine prompting, since that whole matter was a work of God's special providence. Furthermore, on this the Scholastic History says: Here for the first time we read that a woman's consent was asked, and from then on it was held as law that it should be asked.

paras.t: Dimiserunt ergo eam et nutricem illius, quæ infra Debora nuncupatur, quæ forte lactavit Rebeccam infantulam, et custodivit, erudivit, educavitque eam. Iverunt quoque et aliæ quædam puellæ et ancillæ cum Rebecca, ut paulo post subditur, et hoc propter solatium ejus. Servumque Abraham et comites ejus, id est socios servi, imprecantes prospera sorori suæ, id est Rebeccæ, quæ erat soror omnium propinquorum suorum, ibi tunc congregatorum, præsentium, et valefacientium ei, ut moris est in tali recessu, et cognata ipsorum eo modo, quo qui de eadem progenie sunt, fratres et sorores mutuo appellantur; atque dicentes: Soror nostra es; crescas in mille millia, id est, plurima seu innumerabilia millia ex semine tuo nascantur: ponitur enim hic numerus iste indeterminate; et possideat semen tuum portas inimicorum suorum, id est, hostibus suis prævaleat: quod tandem in Christo summe impletum est, qui omnes mundi nationes suæ subjecit legi ac fidei christianæ, cui Pater ait in Psalmo: Postula a me, et dabo tibi gentes hereditatem tuam, et possessionem tuam terminos terræ. Igitur Rebecca et puellæ illius, ascensis camelis, secutæ sunt virum, etc., scilicet servum Abrahæ, qui in via eis ducatum præbebat; et patet ex verbis his, quod et aliæ mulieres præter nutricem Rebeccæ processerunt cum ea.
paras.en: [[24:59|So they sent her away, and her nurse|Dimiserunt ergo eam et nutricem illius]], who further on is called Debora[[Gen 35:8||]], who perhaps suckled Rebecca as a little child, and watched over, taught and brought her up. Certain other girls and handmaids also went with Rebecca, as is said a little later, and this for her comfort. [[24:59|and Abraham's servant, and his company|Servumque Abraham et comites ejus]], that is, the servant's companions, [[24:60|Wishing prosperity to their sister|imprecantes prospera sorori suæ]], that is, to Rebecca, who was the sister of all her kinsfolk then gathered there, present and bidding her farewell, as is the custom at such a leave-taking, and their kinswoman, in the way that those who are of the same stock call one another brothers and sisters; [[24:60|and saying: Thou art our sister, mayst thou increase to thousands of thousands|atque dicentes: Soror nostra es; crescas in mille millia]]: that is, may very many or countless thousands be born of thy seed, for the number is put here without a fixed sense; [[24:60|and may thy seed possess the gates of their enemies|et possideat semen tuum portas inimicorum suorum]]: that is, may it prevail over its foes. This was at last fulfilled in the highest way in Christ, who subjected all the nations of the world to his law and to the Christian faith, and to whom the Father says in the Psalm: [[Ps 2:8|Ask of me, and I will give thee the Gentiles for thy inheritance, and the utmost parts of the earth for thy possession|Postula a me, et dabo tibi gentes hereditatem tuam, et possessionem tuam terminos terræ]]. [[24:61|So Rebecca and her maids, being set upon camels, followed the man|Igitur Rebecca et puellæ illius, ascensis camelis, secutæ sunt virum]], etc., namely Abraham's servant, who led them on the way; and it is plain from these words that other women besides Rebecca's nurse went with her.

paras.t: Eo autem tempore deambulabat Isaac per viam quæ ducit ad puteum, cujus nomen est Viventis et videntis: de quo puteo, et cur ita vocatus sit, dictum est capitulo sextodecimo. Habitabat enim in terra australi, puta in Gerara seu Bersabee, unde ductus fuit ad immolandum, qui locus est in parte australi respectu terræ Chanaan: ex quo videtur, quod post sepulturam Saræ Abraham cum filio suo Isaac redierit ad Bersabee. Et egressus fuerat ad meditandum in agro, inclinata jam die. In Scholastica historia dicitur, quod egressus fuit ad meditandum forte de mora servi. Alii dicunt, quod fuit egressus causa recreationis atque ad spatiandum; sed multo convenientius creditur, et magis consonat litteræ, quod egressus fuit ad meditandum intente de Deo et pertinentibus ad salutem, abstrahens se ab aliorum præsentia, strepitu ac tumultu, ut solus et in solitudine quadam consistens, tanto devotius et liberius insisteret meditationibus sanctis, quanto plus separatus erat ab aliis. Unde (secundum Hieronymum) in Hebræo habetur, Ad loquendum: quod exponit de locutione cum Deo in oratione devota, quia ante solis occasum spirituales victimas obtulit Deo. Lyra quoque affirmat, quod Hebræi dicunt, Egressus fuit ad orandum, quia consuetudo est Judæis, circa tempus vespertinum orare. Porro alia translatio continet, Egressus est ut exerceretur in campo: quod aptius explanatur de exercitatione interna ac spirituali, quam corporali. Egressus itaque fuit ad meditandum salubriter, et ad contemplandum divina: quod ei non casuale, sed consuetudinarium fuit, ut etiam in statutis ordinis Cartusiensis habetur.
paras.en: [[24:62|At the same time, Isaac was walking along the way to the well which is called Of the living and the seeing|Eo autem tempore deambulabat Isaac per viam quæ ducit ad puteum, cujus nomen est Viventis et videntis]]: of this well, and why it was so called, we spoke in the sixteenth chapter; [[24:62|for he dwelt in the south country|Habitabat enim in terra australi]], that is, in Gerara or Bersabee, whence he was led to be sacrificed, a place which lies in the southern part with respect to the land of Chanaan: from which it seems that after Sara's burial Abraham returned with his son Isaac to Bersabee. [[24:63|And he was gone forth to meditate in the field, the day being now well spent|Et egressus fuerat ad meditandum in agro, inclinata jam die]]. In the Scholastic History it is said that he went out to meditate, perhaps on the servant's delay. Others say that he went out for recreation and to take a walk; but it is believed much more fittingly, and it agrees better with the letter, that he went out to meditate intently on God and on the things that pertain to salvation, withdrawing from the presence, noise and bustle of others, so that, being alone and in a kind of solitude, he might give himself to holy meditations the more devoutly and freely, the more he was separated from others. Hence (according to Jerome) the Hebrew has, To speak: which he explains of speaking with God in devout prayer, because before sunset he offered spiritual victims to God. Lyra also affirms that the Hebrews say, He went out to pray, because it is the custom of the Jews to pray about the time of evening. Moreover, another translation has, He went out to exercise himself in the field: which is more fittingly explained of inward and spiritual exercise than of bodily. So he went out to meditate to his soul's profit and to contemplate divine things: and this was with him not a matter of chance but of custom, as is also found in the statutes of the Carthusian order.

paras.t: Circa hoc scribit Lyra: Forte egressus fuit ad videndum dispositionem cœli et aliquarum stellarum, quæ incipiebant tunc apparere, quia edoctus erat in astronomia a patre suo, qui eam primus docuit in Ægypto. Sed contra hoc Rabbi Paulus multipliciter arguit. Primo, quia in nulla Scriptura canonica legitur hoc de Abraham. Secundo, quia Apostoli fuerunt maxime illuminati a Deo, non tamen de mathematicis veritatibus, ergo multo minus Abraham. Tertio, quia scientia Ægyptiorum reprobatur in Scripturis, tanquam divinatio superstitiosa. Quarto, quia ex hoc daretur infidelibus occasio opinandi, quod mirabilia per Abraham vel circa aut propter eum facta, sint facta virtute astrorum influentiisque cœlorum. Sed argumentationes istæ nihil concludunt: idcirco dicendum ad primum, quod non sequitur, Hoc non est scriptum de Abraham in Scripturis, ergo non fuit; quia nec omnia ejus gesta conscripta sunt. Ad secundum dicendum, quod nullus dicit Abraham habuisse notitiam astronomiæ ex sola supernaturali et miraculosa illuminatione Spiritus Sancti, sicut Apostoli habuerunt suam scientiam. Ad tertium respondetur, quod scientia Ægyptiorum non reprobatur in Scripturis, quantum ad id quod continuit veritatis, quum de Moyse scriptum sit, quod eruditus est in omni sapientia Ægyptiorum, sed quantum ad abusum et præsumptionem ac superstitiones Ægyptiorum. Ad quartum dicendum, quod mira quæ de Abraham scripta sunt, talia sunt, quod non possunt virtuti aut influxui siderum et cœlorum adscribi. Quod autem in astronomia erat edoctus, eamque in Ægypto docuerit, Josephus et alii multi testantur, et supra inductum est.
paras.en: On this Lyra writes: Perhaps he went out to see the arrangement of the heaven and of certain stars which were then beginning to appear, since he had been taught astronomy by his father, who was the first to teach it in Egypt. But Rabbi Paul argues against this in many ways. First, because in no canonical Scripture is this read of Abraham. Second, because the Apostles were enlightened by God in the highest degree, yet not about mathematical truths [*mathematica*: the sciences of number and of the heavens, astronomy among them]; much less, then, Abraham. Third, because the science of the Egyptians is condemned in the Scriptures as superstitious divination. Fourth, because this would give unbelievers occasion to think that the wonders done by Abraham, or about him or for his sake, were done by the power of the stars and the influences of the heavens. But these arguments conclude nothing. So to the first it must be said that it does not follow: This is not written of Abraham in the Scriptures, therefore it did not happen; for not all his deeds are written down. To the second it must be said that no one says Abraham had his knowledge of astronomy from the supernatural and miraculous enlightenment of the Holy Ghost alone, as the Apostles had their knowledge. To the third the answer is that the science of the Egyptians is not condemned in the Scriptures as regards the truth it contained, since it is written of Moses that he [[Acts 7:22|was instructed in all the wisdom of the Egyptians|eruditus est in omni sapientia Ægyptiorum]], but as regards the abuse, presumption and superstitions of the Egyptians. To the fourth it must be said that the wonders written of Abraham are such that they cannot be ascribed to the power or influence of the stars and heavens. And that he was taught astronomy, and taught it in Egypt, Josephus and many others testify, and it was brought forward above.

paras.t: Quumque elevasset oculos, ipse Isaac, vidit camelos venientes procul, et protinus ivit obviam servo suo et ceteris. Rebecca quoque, conspecto Isaac, descendit de camelo, et ait ad puerum: Quis est ille homo, qui venit per agrum in occursum nobis? Dixitque ei: Ipse est dominus meus. Verisimile est, quod Rebecca istud interrogavit, et interrogationis suæ responsum audivit antequam de camelo descendit. Quumque audisset quod vir ille esset filius Abrahæ, sponsus suus futurus, descendit de camelo propter reverentiam ejus, quoniam filius fuit talis ac tanti Patriarchæ. At illa tollens cito pallium suum, operuit se: vel ex verecundia puellari, vel caput suum decenter ornando, ut coram sponso suo mox futuro appareret honestior. Nam alia littera habet, Theristrum, quod est vestis Arabica alba, qua mulieres provinciæ illius velantur.
paras.en: [[24:63|and when he had lifted up his eyes|Quumque elevasset oculos]], Isaac himself, [[24:63|he saw camels coming afar off|vidit camelos venientes procul]], and at once went to meet his servant and the rest. [[24:64|Rebecca also, when she saw Isaac, lighted off the camel|Rebecca quoque, conspecto Isaac, descendit de camelo]], [[24:65|And said to the servant: Who is that man who cometh towards us along the field? And he said to her: That man is my master|et ait ad puerum: Quis est ille homo, qui venit per agrum in occursum nobis? Dixitque ei: Ipse est dominus meus]]. It is likely that Rebecca asked this, and heard the answer to her question, before she got down from the camel; and when she had heard that the man was Abraham's son, her future spouse, she got down from the camel out of reverence for him, since he was the son of so great a Patriarch. [[24:65|But she quickly took her cloak, and covered herself|At illa tollens cito pallium suum, operuit se]]: either from maidenly modesty, or adorning her head becomingly, so as to appear more seemly before the one who was soon to be her spouse. For another text has *theristrum*, which is a white Arabian garment with which the women of that province veil themselves.

paras.t: Servus autem cuncta quæ gesserat, scilicet viæ suæ processum, prosperitatem et fructum, narravit domino suo, videlicet Isaac, deinde et Abrahæ. Qui introduxit eam in tabernaculum Saræ matris suæ, et accepit eam uxorem; et in tantum dilexit eam, non libidinoso, sed moderato, spirituali, naturali, sociali et conjugali amore: inter quas multiplices affectiones, sola spiritualis dilectio, fuit directe et per se meritoria vitæ beatæ: ut dolorem qui ex morte matris ejus acciderat, temperaret. Ex quo constat, quam ardentissime matrem suam dilexerat, quam jam per tres annos deflevit, nec dolorem quem ex ejus morte conceperat, sponsam carissimam accipiendo ac diligendo, prorsus exstinxit, sed temperavit.
paras.en: [[24:66|And the servant|Servus autem]] [[24:66|told|narravit]] his master, namely Isaac, and afterwards Abraham too [the Latin Denis reads has *narravit domino suo*, "told his master", where the Vulgate has "told Isaac"], [[24:66|all that he had done|cuncta quæ gesserat]], that is, the course of his journey, its success and its fruit. [[24:67|Who brought her into the tent of Sara his mother, and took her to wife|Qui introduxit eam in tabernaculum Saræ matris suæ, et accepit eam uxorem]]; [[24:67|and he loved her so much|et in tantum dilexit eam]], with a love not lustful but moderate, spiritual, natural, companionable and conjugal (and among these many affections, the spiritual love alone was directly and of itself meritorious of the life of bliss), [[24:67|that it moderated the sorrow which was occasioned by his mother's death|ut dolorem qui ex morte matris ejus acciderat, temperaret]]. From this it is clear how very ardently he had loved his mother, whom he had now mourned for three years; and that by taking and loving a most dear bride he did not altogether extinguish the sorrow he had conceived from her death, but moderated it.

paras.t: Itaque temperavit illum dolorem per istius amorem. Nam anima quanto plus occupatur atque dispergitur circa plura, tanto minus intenta est uni. Rursus, quanto affectio cordis circa plura dividitur, tanto minus in uno defigitur. Unumquodque oppositorum expellit reliquum: ideo quanto Isaac plus cœpit circa propriam conjugem affici, occupari, defigi ac delectari, tanto plus cœpit oblivisci matris interitum et memorare dolorem inde conceptum.
paras.en: So he moderated that sorrow by his love for her. For the more the soul is busied with and scattered among many things, the less it is intent on one. Again, the more the heart's affection is divided among many things, the less it is fixed on one. Each of two opposites drives out the other: so the more Isaac began to be moved by, busied with, fixed on and delighted in his own wife, the more he began to forget his mother's death and to call to mind the sorrow conceived from it [so the Latin, *memorare*; the sense seems to require "to forget to call to mind", or perhaps *minorare*, "to lessen", was meant].

24.title: Explanatio spiritualis ejusdem capituli vicesimi quarti
24.title_en: Spiritual explanation of the same twenty-fourth chapter

paras.t: Abraham senex, æternum Patrem designat. Quemadmodum itaque Abraham servo suo principali præcepit, ut filio suo carissimo adduceret puellam, acciperetque uxorem de genere suo, non alieno, nec Chananæo: sic Pater æternus unigenito Filio per Apostolorum prædicationem adduxit, atque in sponsam conjunxit electam gentilitatem, quæ secundum prædestinationem divinam vere ac spiritualiter fuit Israelitica plebs, et Abrahæ semen per fidei et obedientiæ imitationem. Quemadmodum etiam Abraham habuit servum suum excusatum, si mulier secum venire non vellet; sic Apostolorum chorus culpam non habet de pereuntibus incredulis, qui eorum prædicationi credere ac parere spreverunt. Insuper, sicut servus Abrahæ tulit secum decem camelos, portans secum ex omnibus bonis domini sui, sicque Mesopotamiam introivit; sic cœtus Apostolorum sumpsit in adjutorium quosdam ex Judaismo ac gentilitate conversos, qui instar camelorum, patientissime super se ferebant onus evangelicæ legis et pondus Decalogi: sed et sancti Apostoli in vasis cordium suorum deferebant ad gentium nationes pretiosissima et quasi innumerabilia charismata Spiritus Sancti, sapientiamque multiplicem; et universa dona quæ olim habuit Synagoga, ad Christi deportaverunt Ecclesiam, quæ per Mesopotamiam designatur sicut gentilitas.
paras.en: Abraham, old, signifies the eternal Father. Therefore, as Abraham commanded his chief servant to bring a maid to his dearest son, and to take him a wife of his own kindred, not of a stranger, nor of the Chanaanites: so the eternal Father, through the preaching of the Apostles, brought to his only-begotten Son, and joined to him as bride, the chosen gentile world, which, according to the divine predestination, was truly and spiritually the people of Israel and the seed of Abraham, by the imitation of his faith and obedience. And as Abraham held his servant excused if the woman would not come with him, so the choir of the Apostles bears no blame for the unbelievers who perish, who scorned to believe and obey their preaching. Further, as Abraham's servant took ten camels with him, carrying with him something of all his master's goods, and so entered Mesopotamia: so the company of the Apostles took to help them certain converts from Judaism and from the gentiles, who like camels bore most patiently upon themselves the burden of the Gospel law and the weight of the Decalogue. And the holy Apostles, too, carried in the vessels of their hearts to the nations of the gentiles the most precious and almost countless charisms of the Holy Ghost, and manifold wisdom; and all the gifts which the Synagogue once had they carried over to the Church of Christ, which is signified by Mesopotamia, as is the gentile world.

paras.t: Quumque camelos fecisset accumbere juxta puteum: nam gloriosissimi Christi Apostoli, juxta gratiam sacri Baptismi et profunditatem Scripturæ atque fluenta supernorum charismatum, quiescere et spiritualiter epulari fecerunt conversos a se. Unde Salvator disseruit: Aqua quam ego dabo credenti, fiet in eo fons aquæ salientis in vitam æternam. Iterum, sicut servus Abrahæ Dominum invocavit, ut iter suum dirigeret, ac filio Abrahæ de conjuge provideret, signum quoque in se ipso excogitavit, quod ista fieret uxor domini sui, quæ sibi potum petenti, præberet mox poculum, imo et suis camelis: sic sancti Apostoli et coadjutores eorum, omnem spem suam in Deo ponentes, ejus auxilium et directionem jugiter invocabant, sine cujus ope et gratia se nihil posse penitus fatebantur. Hinc Paulus in suis epistolis toties pro suis intercessit discipulis. Illas quoque personas consideraverunt Apostoli magis aptas ad fidem et spirituales nuptias Christi, quæ magis benigne se habuerant ad ipsos, et eorum cooperatores, atque ad pietatis et misericordiæ opera fuerant proniores.
paras.en: [[24:11|And when he had made the camels lie down|Quumque camelos fecisset accumbere]] [[24:11|near a well|juxta puteum]]: for the most glorious Apostles of Christ made those they had converted rest and feast spiritually beside the grace of holy Baptism, the depth of Scripture and the streams of heavenly charisms. Hence the Saviour said: [[John 4:14|the water that I will give|Aqua quam ego dabo]] to him that believeth [[John 4:14|shall become in him a fountain of water, springing up into life everlasting|fiet in eo fons aquæ salientis in vitam æternam]]. Again, as Abraham's servant called upon the Lord to direct his journey and to provide a wife for Abraham's son, and also devised a sign within himself, that she should be his master's wife who, when he asked for drink, would at once offer him a cup, and to his camels too: so the holy Apostles and their helpers, putting all their hope in God, called without ceasing for his help and guidance, confessing that without his aid and grace they could do nothing at all. Hence Paul in his epistles so often interceded for his disciples. The Apostles also judged those persons fitter for the faith and the spiritual marriage of Christ who had behaved more kindly towards them and their fellow workers[[Rom 16:1||]][[1 Cor 16:15||]], and were more inclined to works of piety and mercy.

paras.t: Quumque ita orassent et prædicare cœpissent Apostoli, protinus eis occurrit Rebecca virgo pulcherrima, id est gentilitas, quantum ad naturalem imaginem et similitudinem Dei decora, et in natura specifica valde pura, quæ statim ad fidei susceptionem obtulit se paratam. Apostolisque beneficam, ex cujus hydria petierunt Apostoli bibere, id est, de illius conversione appetebant mentaliter refici, scientiam quoque sæcularem et philosophicam voluerunt evangelicæ sapientiæ deservire ac subdi. Denique Rebecca camelis tribuit potum, quando conversa gentilitas misit sanctis qui in Jerusalem erant, eleemosynam largam: de qua re sæpius meminit Paulus. Rursus, sicut Rebecca hausit aquam quam dedit camelis, ita Ecclesia gratiam impetravit a Spiritu Sancto, et ex Evangelio cepit doctrinam, quam rudibus communicavit. Illa autem contemplabatur eum tacitus, etc. Sic et Apostoli vigilantissime intuebantur eos quos converterunt, an perseverarent in fide.
paras.en: When the Apostles had thus prayed and had begun to preach, at once there came to meet them Rebecca, a most beautiful virgin, that is, the gentile world, comely as to the natural image and likeness of God, and very pure in its specific nature [that is, in the nature of man as such], which straightway offered itself ready to receive the faith, and kindly to the Apostles. From her pitcher the Apostles asked to drink, that is, they longed to be refreshed in mind by her conversion; and they willed that secular and philosophical knowledge too should serve and be subject to the wisdom of the Gospel. Then Rebecca gave drink to the camels when the converted gentiles sent a large alms to the saints who were in Jerusalem, a thing Paul often mentions. Again, as Rebecca drew the water which she gave to the camels, so the Church obtained grace from the Holy Ghost and took from the Gospel the teaching which she imparted to the unlearned. [[24:21|But he musing, beheld her with silence|Illa autem contemplabatur eum tacitus]], etc. [the printed text reads "she beheld him"; the Vulgate has "he beheld her", which Denis's gloss follows]. So too the Apostles watched most vigilantly those they had converted, whether they would persevere in the faith.

paras.t: Insuper, sicut servus dedit Rebeccæ varia ornamenta, inaures, armillas, vasa aurea atque argentea, vestesque pretiosas; sic plane Apostoli dispositive ac ministerialiter ornaverunt credentes et ipsam Ecclesiam. Accipiebant etenim Spiritum Sanctum et præclarissima ipsius charismata hi quibus Apostoli manus suas imposuerunt. Potest autem per inaurem obedientia, per armillam operatio virtuosa intelligi: per aurea vasa, donum sapientiæ, caritatisque fervor; per vasa argentea, donum linguarum, seu efficacia prædicandi, aut ipsa prudentia accipi; vestes vero, virtutes sunt. Hæc gentilitas sic conversa, dixit se in temporalibus satis habere, et spatiosum sibi locum esse pro recipiendis ac sustentandis prædicatoribus sanctis. Hinc sancti illi prædicatores Deo grates retulerunt humillimas, omnem fructum suæ prædicationis atque laboris pietati adscribentes divinæ.
paras.en: Further, as the servant gave Rebecca various ornaments, earrings, bracelets, vessels of gold and silver, and costly garments, so plainly the Apostles, by disposing and ministering [that is, as instruments and ministers, not as the source of grace], adorned the believers and the Church herself. For those on whom the Apostles laid their hands received the Holy Ghost and his most excellent charisms. Now by the earring obedience may be understood, by the bracelet virtuous working; by the vessels of gold the gift of wisdom and the fervour of charity; by the vessels of silver the gift of tongues, or power in preaching, or prudence itself; and the garments are the virtues. This gentile world, thus converted, said that she had enough in temporal things, and room enough to receive and maintain the holy preachers. Hence those holy preachers gave most humble thanks to God, ascribing all the fruit of their preaching and labour to the divine goodness.

paras.t: Cucurrit puella, et nuntiabat in domo matris suæ. Sic conversa gentilitas gratiam sibi concessam studuit mox suis proximis intimare et communicare, quorum nonnulli fidem adhibuerunt, et considerantes supernaturalia dona conversis ex paganismo collata, acceperunt Apostolos sanctosque prædicatores, eosdem rogando, ut ad se dignarentur divertere; quibus libenter acquieverunt benedicti Apostoli, sed ante omnia retulerunt illis, cur missi essent a Deo, scilicet ut gentilitatem Christo conjungerent, quem Virgo mundissima peperit in natura humana, cui Pater dedit omnia sua, sive per generationem æternam, sive per plenissimam fruitionem, et quoniam omni creaturæ prætulit eum, totamque animæ suæ capacitatem donis gratiæ adimplevit ac gloriæ.
paras.en: [[24:28|Then the maid ran, and told in her mother's house|Cucurrit puella, et nuntiabat in domo matris suæ]]. So the converted gentile world was eager at once to make known and to share with her neighbours the grace granted her; some of whom believed and, considering the supernatural gifts bestowed on those converted from paganism, received the Apostles and holy preachers, asking them to deign to turn in to them. To these the blessed Apostles gladly consented; but before all things they told them why they had been sent by God: namely, to join the gentile world to Christ, whom the most pure Virgin bore in human nature, to whom the Father gave all that is his[[John 17:10||]], whether by eternal generation or by the fullest fruition, and because he set him above every creature and filled the whole capacity of his soul with the gifts of grace and of glory.

paras.t: Quamobrem si facitis misericordiam et veritatem cum domino meo: hoc est, si Salvatori et Creatori vestro vere grati ac subditi esse vultis, ejusque servis ac membris, imo et animabus propriis misereri, hoc nobis insinuate. Si autem aliud placet, hoc dicite nobis: quia non est nostræ institutionis, aliquem ad fidem compellere: ut eamus ad dexteram sive sinistram, eundo quocumque ad aliorum conversionem.
paras.en: [[24:49|Wherefore, if you do according to mercy and truth with my master|Quamobrem si facitis misericordiam et veritatem cum domino meo]]: that is, if you wish to be truly grateful and subject to your Saviour and Creator, and to have mercy on his servants and members, and indeed on your own souls, let us know it. [[24:49|But if it please you otherwise, tell me that also|Si autem aliud placet, hoc dicite]] (to us, that is): for it is not of our rule to compel anyone to the faith; [[24:49|that I may go to the right hand, or to the left|ut eamus ad dexteram sive sinistram]], going wherever we may for the conversion of others.

paras.t: Responderunt Laban et Bathuel: A Domino egressus est sermo. Sic plane gentiles frequenter convicti evidentia signorum ac sanctitatis et mirabilium, quæ in Apostolis et apostolicis viris viderunt, reniti non poterant, nec valebant; sed Rebeccam, id est, quamcumque personam gentilem ad eos pertinentem, seu propriam animam, resignaverunt ac tradiderunt prædicatoribus sanctis, ut conversa fieret sponsa Christi: propter quod sancti Apostoli non solum sic conversis, sed et eorum propinquis ita consentientibus, munera gratiarum procuraverunt cœlestium. Initoque convivio, pariter epulabantur: facti commensales et domestici in Ecclesia Christi, atque in mensa Sapientiæ consedentes, frumentum electorum et vinum germinans virgines, hoc est, corpus et sanguinem Salvatoris simul sumpserunt.
paras.en: [[24:50|And Laban and Bathuel answered: The word hath proceeded from the Lord|Responderunt Laban et Bathuel: A Domino egressus est sermo]]. So plainly the gentiles, often convinced by the evidence of the signs, of the holiness and of the wonders which they saw in the Apostles and apostolic men, could not and were not able to resist; but they gave up and handed over Rebecca, that is, any gentile person belonging to them, or their own soul, to the holy preachers, that being converted she might become the bride of Christ. For which reason the holy Apostles obtained gifts of heavenly graces not only for those thus converted, but also for their kinsfolk who so consented. [[24:54|And a banquet was made|Initoque convivio]], they feasted together: made table companions and members of the household in the Church of Christ, and sitting together at the table of Wisdom, they received together [[Zach 9:17|the corn of the elect, and wine springing forth virgins|frumentum electorum et vinum germinans virgines]], that is, the body and blood of the Saviour.

paras.t: Surgens autem mane, locutus est puer: Dimittite me, etc. Sic sancti Apostoli et cooperatores eorum jugiter conabantur in anteriora se ipsos extendere, et ad cœlestia properare; imo et quosdam a se conversos, non solum ad observantiam mandatorum, sed ad evangelicorum quoque impletionem consiliorum traxerunt, ut parentes et fratres ac omnia quæ sunt mundi relinquendo, separatam et quasi monasticam vitam assumpserint: quod propinqui eorum, quamvis credentes, tamen adhuc imperfecti, conati sunt saltem ad tempus impedire sive differre, dicentes: Maneat saltem decem dies apud nos: quibus non consenserunt Apostoli, prædicatoresque sancti, eo quod Christus petenti dilationem, quousque sepeliret proprium patrem, locutus sit, Dimitte mortuos sepelire mortuos suos. Et dixerunt: Vocemus puellam, et quæramus illius voluntatem: quoniam nemo cogendus est ad religionis ingressum, sive ad opera supererogationis, nisi aliunde sit obligatus ad ea. Quæ ait: Vadam. Sic enim fideles ac fervidæ animæ responderunt.
paras.en: [[24:54|And in the morning, the servant arose, and said: Let me depart|Surgens autem mane, locutus est puer: Dimittite me]], etc. So the holy Apostles and their fellow workers strove without ceasing to stretch themselves forth to the things that are before, and to hasten to heavenly things[[Phil 3:13||]]; and they even drew some of their converts not only to the keeping of the commandments, but also to the fulfilling of the evangelical counsels, so that, leaving parents and brothers and all that is of the world, they took up a separate and as it were monastic life. This their kinsfolk, though believers, yet still imperfect, tried at least for a time to hinder or delay, saying: [[24:55|Let the maid stay, at least, ten days with us|Maneat saltem decem dies apud nos]]. To them the Apostles and holy preachers did not consent, because Christ said to one who asked for a delay until he should bury his own father: [[Matt 8:22|let the dead bury their dead|Dimitte mortuos sepelire mortuos suos]]. [[24:57|And they said: Let us call the maid, and ask her will|Et dixerunt: Vocemus puellam, et quæramus illius voluntatem]]: for no one is to be compelled to enter religion, or to works of supererogation [that is, works beyond what the commandments require], unless he is bound to them on some other ground. [[24:58|She said: I will go|Quæ ait: Vadam]]. For so faithful and fervent souls have answered.

paras.t: Dimiserunt ergo eam et nutricem illius. Sæpe enim contingit, ut aliqua persona viam perfectionis aggrediens, aliam sibi magis familiarem, aut etiam quasi magistram aut institutricem secum alliciat et perducat: quibus propinqui eorum prospera imprecantur, cupiendo eorum spiritualem profectum, ut crescant in mille millia, exercendo quotidie opera virtuosa sine numero et mensura, ita ut universis suæ salutis prævaleant hostibus, et eorum possideant portas, id est tentationum introitus, atque suggestionum pravarum initia vincant. Igitur Rebecca et puellæ illius, ascensis camelis, secutæ sunt virum, id est, animæ ferventes in fide, ac patientes, propriis corporibus conculcatis, refrenatis, et rationi subjectis, apostolicam perfectionem sectatæ sunt.
paras.en: [[24:59|So they sent her away, and her nurse|Dimiserunt ergo eam et nutricem illius]]. For it often happens that a person setting out on the way of perfection draws and brings along another who is closer to him, or even one who is as it were his mistress or teacher; and their kinsfolk wish them prosperity, desiring their spiritual progress, that they may grow to thousands of thousands, practising daily works of virtue without number or measure, so that they may prevail over all the enemies of their salvation and possess their gates, that is, overcome the entries of temptations and the first beginnings of evil suggestions. [[24:61|So Rebecca and her maids, being set upon camels, followed the man|Igitur Rebecca et puellæ illius, ascensis camelis, secutæ sunt virum]], that is, souls fervent in faith and patient, their own bodies trodden down, bridled and subject to reason, followed apostolic perfection.

paras.t: Eo autem tempore deambulabat Isaac per viam quæ ducit ad puteum Viventis et videntis: hoc est, tempore primitivæ Ecclesiæ prædicantibus sanctis Apostolis, post Salvatoris ascensionem, ipse Salvator per gratiam morabatur, et per credentium indesinentem profectum deambulabat in cordibus eorumdem per viam perfectionis, quæ ducit ad profundissimam contemplationem ejus qui essentialiter vivit, et omnia intuetur, utpote ad beatificam et fruitivam ipsius inspectionem, in qua Beati torrente voluptatis immensæ potantur, et fluminis impetus eos lætificat. Habitabat in terra australi, id est, in mentibus fervidorum, qui frigora Aquilonis abhorrent, et calore Solis justitiæ perfunduntur; et egressus fuerat ad meditandum in agro: nam et ipse Christus ante suam ascensionem, egressus fuit a Patre, et per Incarnationis mysterium intraverat hujus sæculi campum, ad meditandum et exercendum humanæ redemptionis negotium: inclinata jam die, id est, luce gratiæ ac virtutum splendore in hominibus pro maxima parte deficiente, atque instante jam fine durationis Mosaicæ legis. Quumque elevasset oculos, vidit camelos venientes. Christus namque oculo pietatis clementissime intuebatur, quemadmodum sancti Apostoli et adjutores eorum, jugum Dei super se bajulantes, fructificaverunt in gentilium conversione, et quidquid boni egerunt, retulerunt ad ipsum, a quo jam ante audierant, Sine me nihil potestis facere, sicque grata mente redierunt ad eum quotidie.
paras.en: [[24:62|At the same time, Isaac was walking along the way to the well which is called Of the living and the seeing|Eo autem tempore deambulabat Isaac per viam quæ ducit ad puteum Viventis et videntis]]: that is, in the time of the early Church, while the holy Apostles were preaching after the Saviour's ascension, the Saviour himself dwelt by grace, and through the unceasing progress of the believers walked in their hearts along the way of perfection which leads to the deepest contemplation of him who lives by his essence and beholds all things, that is, to the beatific vision and enjoyment of him, in which the Blessed are given to drink of the torrent of boundless pleasure[[Ps 35:9||]], and the stream of the river makes them joyful[[Ps 45:5||]]. [[24:62|He dwelt in the south country|Habitabat in terra australi]], that is, in the minds of the fervent, who shrink from the cold of the North and are bathed in the heat of the Sun of justice. [[24:63|And he was gone forth to meditate in the field|et egressus fuerat ad meditandum in agro]]: for Christ himself too, before his ascension, went forth from the Father and through the mystery of the Incarnation had entered the field of this world, to meditate and carry out the business of man's redemption; [[24:63|the day being now well spent|inclinata jam die]], that is, when the light of grace and the splendour of the virtues were for the most part failing among men, and the end of the time of the Mosaic law was now at hand. [[24:63|And when he had lifted up his eyes, he saw camels coming|Quumque elevasset oculos, vidit camelos venientes]]. For Christ beheld most mercifully, with the eye of loving kindness, how the holy Apostles and their helpers, bearing the yoke of God upon themselves, bore fruit in the conversion of the gentiles, and referred whatever good they did to him, from whom they had already heard: [[John 15:5|without me you can do nothing|Sine me nihil potestis facere]]; and so with grateful minds they returned to him daily.

paras.t: Rebecca quoque, conspecto Isaac, descendit de camelo: hoc est, conversa gentilitas, Salvatore plenius cognito, carnalia cuncta transcendit, atque per contempla[…]ionem deseruit, et edocta qualiter Christus venit per agrum mundi hujus in occursum suis electis, ut eos constringeret et brachiis caritatis in patibulo crucis, ulnas suas extendens in eorum amplexum, ornavit se intus per virtutes et dona Spiritus Sancti, hujusque mundi vanitatibus se abscondit; pallio quoque suo operuit se, dum confessionis tegumento peccata sua texit et abstulit, ut Sponso cœlesti præsentaretur purgata. Qui introduxit eam in tabernaculum Saræ matris suæ. Christus, ipsa Synagoga, de qua secundum carnem natus fuerat, jam per infidelitatem defuncta, induxit conversam gentilitatem in gradum et gratiam, quam aliquando habuit Synagoga: cui dato libello repudii, Ecclesiam gentium duxit sponsam, et eam tam intense amavit, quod temperavit dolorem, quem de Synagogæ perditione conceperat, de cujus ingratitudine et damnatione tempore suæ passionis ineffabiliter doluit, imo et ante frequenter.
paras.en: [[24:64|Rebecca also, when she saw Isaac, lighted off the camel|Rebecca quoque, conspecto Isaac, descendit de camelo]]: that is, the converted gentile world, having come to know the Saviour more fully, rose above all carnal things, and through contempla[…] forsook […]; and, taught how Christ came through the field of this world to meet his elect, to bind them with the arms of charity on the gibbet of the cross, stretching out his arms to embrace them, she adorned herself within with the virtues and gifts of the Holy Ghost, and hid herself from the vanities of this world. And she covered herself with her cloak when she covered her sins with the veil of confession and took them away, that she might be presented cleansed to the heavenly Bridegroom. [[24:67|Who brought her into the tent of Sara his mother|Qui introduxit eam in tabernaculum Saræ matris suæ]]. Christ, the Synagogue, of which he had been born according to the flesh, being now dead through unbelief, brought the converted gentile world into the rank and grace which the Synagogue once had; and having given that one a bill of divorce, he took the Church of the gentiles as his bride, and loved her so intensely that it moderated the sorrow he had conceived at the loss of the Synagogue, over whose ingratitude and damnation he grieved unspeakably at the time of his passion, and often before.

25.title: Explanatio capituli vicesimi quinti: Abraham vero aliam duxit uxorem
25.title_en: Explanation of the twenty-fifth chapter: And Abraham married another wife

paras.t: Præsenti capitulo describuntur novæ […] nuptiæ veteris Patriarchæ, et propagatio filiorum ex conjuge ista, felix quoque consummatio Abrahæ, et generationes filiorum ipsius.
paras.en: In the present chapter are described the new […] nuptials of the aged Patriarch, and the begetting of sons from this wife, and also the happy end of Abraham, and the generations of his sons.

paras.t: Abraham vero aliam duxit uxorem. Hoc maligni hæretici irriserunt, qui vetus Testamentum dixerunt non esse a vero Deo, quibus visum est, plenum fuisse lasciviæ, quod Abraham in tanta senectute duxit uxorem. Quibus dicendum, quod sanctus Patriarcha non fecit hoc ex incontinentia aliqua, et tripliciter excusatur. Primo, quia desiderio prolis copiosioris hoc fecit. Secundo, propter mysticam significationem, videlicet propter significandum futura, quemadmodum Osee propheta Deo jubente accepit fornicariam in uxorem, ad præsignandum quod terra seu plebs Israelitica fornicans fornicaretur a Domino, id est, per idololatriam a Deo vero recederet. Prophetæ etenim aliquando verbis, aliquando factis prophetaverunt: sic et Abraham, qui Deo testante fuit propheta, in senio suo duxit uxorem, ad præfigurandum re ipsa, quod ex Christo et Ecclesia militante generantur in fonte Baptismatis, et tamen non pertinent vere ad ipsam Ecclesiam, puta hæretici atque schismatici, qui per istam Abrahæ uxorem nomine Ceturam, ejusque filios designantur, quemadmodum per Agar et filium ejus, carnales ac perfidi veteris Testamenti sunt designati. Tertio, quia Deo inspirante hoc fecit, ad reprobandum quorumdam hæreticorum perfidiam, qui secundas nuptias damnaverunt, quæ tamen tanti Patriarchæ roborantur exemplo. Hanc rationem, sicut et præcedentem, tangit Augustinus.
paras.en: [[25:1|And Abraham married another wife|Abraham vero aliam duxit uxorem]]. Wicked heretics mocked at this, those who said that the Old Testament is not from the true God, and who thought it a thing full of wantonness that Abraham took a wife in so great an old age. To them it must be said that the holy Patriarch did not do this out of any incontinence, and he is excused on three counts. First, because he did it from the desire of a more numerous offspring. Second, on account of a mystical signification, that is, in order to signify things to come; just as Osee the prophet at God's command took a harlot to wife[[Osee 1:2||]] [the margin also gives Osee ii, 1, which does not fit here], to foreshadow that [[Osee 1:2|the land|terra]], or the people of Israel, [[Osee 1:2|by fornication shall depart from the Lord|fornicans fornicaretur a Domino]], that is, would fall away from the true God by idolatry. For the prophets prophesied sometimes by words, sometimes by deeds: so Abraham too, who by God's own testimony was a prophet, took a wife in his old age, to prefigure by the very deed that some are begotten of Christ and the Church militant in the font of Baptism, and yet do not truly belong to the Church herself, for instance heretics and schismatics, who are signified by this wife of Abraham named Cetura and by her sons; just as by Agar and her son the carnal and faithless of the Old Testament are signified. Third, because he did this at God's inspiration, to condemn the faithlessness of certain heretics who condemned second marriages, which nevertheless are confirmed by the example of so great a Patriarch. This reason, like the one before it, Augustine touches on [a margin note here, probably the reference to Augustine, could not be read].
