Alii dicunt, quod Esau jam ante oblitus fuit injuriæ, quam aliquando reputavit sibi a Jacob illatam, et quod venit obviam non ad lædendum, sed ad suscipiendum ipsum Jacob pacifice ac honeste.
paras.en: [[33:4|Then Esau ran to meet his brother, and embraced him|Currens itaque Esau obviam fratri suo, amplexatus est eum]], that is, Jacob his brother. Some say that, by God's ordering and working with it, Esau's heart was changed from wrath and indignation to kindness and brotherly love. For the heart of men is [[Prov 21:1|in the hand of the Lord: whithersoever he will, he shall turn it|in manu Dei est: et quocumque voluerit, vertet illud]] [Prov. xxi, 1 speaks of the heart of the king; Denis widens it to the heart of men]; and it is proper to God to act immediately upon the very will of man, and to change it at his pleasure. Others say that Esau had already forgotten the wrong which he once reckoned Jacob had done him, and that he came to meet him not to harm him, but to receive Jacob peaceably and honourably.

paras.t: Et appropinquantes ancillæ et filii earum, incurvati sunt, etc., id est, profunde inclinaverunt ipsi Esau: extremi Joseph et Rachel adoraverunt, adoratione duliæ. Sed quæri potest, qualiter Joseph adhuc infantulus potuit adorare. Et respondendum, quod Joseph jam erat quasi septennis, quoniam natus est quartodecimo anno servitii quo Jacob servivit Laban, post quos adhuc servivit eidem sex annis; quibus elapsis, recessit: sicque poterat Joseph a parentibus informari, ut inclinaret suo avunculo Esau.
paras.en: [[33:6|Then the handmaids and their children came near and bowed themselves|Et appropinquantes ancillæ et filii earum, incurvati sunt]], etc., that is, they bowed low to Esau: [[33:7|and last of all, Joseph and Rachel bowed down|extremi Joseph et Rachel adoraverunt]], with the adoration of dulia. But it may be asked how Joseph, still a little child, could bow down. The answer is that Joseph was already about seven years old, since he was born in the fourteenth year of the service with which Jacob served Laban, after which he served him six years more; and when these were over he departed. And so Joseph could be taught by his parents to bow to his uncle Esau.

paras.t: Dixitque Esau: Quænam sunt istæ turmæ, quas obviam habui? Hoc interrogavit de servis et pecoribus quos Jacob præmisit per ordinem. Respondit Jacob: Ut invenirem gratiam coram domino meo, etc., hoc est, ad me pertinent, et præmisi eas, ut dignareris pecora ista pro munere de mea manu accipere, quatenus per hoc tibi acceptus fiam, et pietatem tuam promerear, cui quasi domino me sponte subjicio.
paras.en: [[33:8|And Esau said: What are the droves that I met?|Dixitque Esau: Quænam sunt istæ turmæ, quas obviam habui?]]? He asked this about the servants and cattle which Jacob had sent ahead in order. [[33:8|He answered: That I might find favour before my lord|Respondit Jacob: Ut invenirem gratiam coram domino meo]], etc.; that is: They belong to me, and I sent them ahead so that thou mightest deign to accept these cattle as a gift from my hand, that by this I may become acceptable to thee and win thy kindness, for I submit myself to thee of my own accord as to a lord.

paras.t: Sic enim vidi faciem tuam, quasi viderim vultum Dei. Circa hoc loquitur Augustinus: Utrum verba animi Jacob paventis ac perturbati usque ad hanc adulationem proruperunt: an sine peccato dici potuerunt? Et forsan, quod imo: quia et dii gentium dicti sunt, qui dæmonia appellantur, et Apostolus ait, Siquidem sunt dii multi et domini multi; maxime quia in Græco dictum est sine articulo, quo evidentissime solet verus Deus significari: quod facile capiunt qui Græcum intelligunt. Est itaque sensus: Vidi te cum ingenti reverentia, quasi quemdam deum, eo modo quo judices et prælati dii vocantur, juxta illud: Diis non detrahes. Et Moysi dictum est: Constitui te deum Pharaonis.
paras.en: [[33:10|for I have seen thy face, as if I should have seen the countenance of God|Sic enim vidi faciem tuam, quasi viderim vultum Dei]]. On this Augustine says: Did these words break forth from the mind of Jacob, fearful and troubled, so far as this flattery, or could they be said without sin? And perhaps rather the latter [that is, that they could be said without sin]: for those too are called gods of the Gentiles who are named devils[[Ps 95:5||]], and the Apostle says, [[1 Cor 8:5|for there be gods many and lords many|Siquidem sunt dii multi et domini multi]]; above all because in the Greek it is said without the article, by which the true God is most plainly wont to be signified: which those who understand Greek easily grasp. So the sense is: I have seen thee with great reverence, as a kind of god, in the way in which judges and prelates are called gods, according to that saying: [[Ex 22:28|Thou shalt not speak ill of the gods|Diis non detrahes]]. And it was said to Moses: [[Ex 7:1|I have appointed thee the god of Pharao|Constitui te deum Pharaonis]].

paras.t: Esto mihi propitius, et suscipe benedictionem, etc., id est dona et encænia quæ attuli. Vix a fratre compellente suscipiens, etc., id est, Esau dona ista vix capiens ex instantissima et quodammodo importuna prece ipsius Jacob.
paras.en: [[33:10|be gracious to me|Esto mihi propitius]], [[33:11|And take the blessing|et suscipe benedictionem]], etc., that is, the gifts and presents which I have brought. [[33:11|He took it with much ado at his brother's earnest pressing him|Vix a fratre compellente suscipiens]], etc., that is, Esau hardly taking these gifts, at the most urgent and in a manner importunate entreaty of Jacob.

paras.t: Dixitque Jacob, etc. Sequar paulatim vestigia ejus, scilicet Esau, sicut videro parvulos meos posse, donec veniam ad dominum meum in Seir, etc. Hoc dixit Jacob, ut persuaderet fratri suo Esau, quod præcederet eum, asserens se velle eum sequi morose. Non enim fuit libenter diu cum Esau, ne forte Esau inciperet recordari præteritorum quæ Jacob fecerat ei. Verumtamen Jacob non sequebatur eum usque in Seir, vel quia ex meliori deliberatione mutavit propositum, vel occurrit ei aliunde obstaculum. Potest tamen a mendacio excusari, dicendo quod intendebat eum sequi, quando protulit verba hæc.
paras.en: [[33:13|And Jacob said|Dixitque Jacob]], etc. [[33:14|I will follow softly after him|Sequar paulatim vestigia ejus]], that is, Esau, [[33:14|as I shall see my children to be able, until I come to my lord in Seir|sicut videro parvulos meos posse, donec veniam ad dominum meum in Seir]], etc. Jacob said this to persuade his brother Esau to go on before him, declaring that he meant to follow him slowly. For he was not glad to be long with Esau, lest Esau might begin to remember the things Jacob had done to him in the past. Yet Jacob did not follow him as far as Seir, either because on better deliberation he changed his purpose, or because some obstacle met him from elsewhere. He can, however, be excused from lying by saying that he meant to follow him when he spoke these words.

paras.t: Hoc uno tantum indigeo, id est, inter ea quæ tu mihi impendere potes, et quæ ego a te cupio, hoc solo indigeo, ut inveniam gratiam in conspectu tuo, domine mi. Quasi diceret: Non cupio tuas divitias, neque honorem, neque comitatum, sed bonum favorem.
paras.en: [[33:15|I want nothing else but only|Hoc uno tantum indigeo]], that is, among the things which thou canst bestow on me and which I desire of thee, I need this one thing only, [[33:15|to find favour, my lord, in thy sight|ut inveniam gratiam in conspectu tuo, domine mi]]. As if he said: I do not desire thy riches, nor honour, nor company, but good favour.

paras.t: Reversus est itaque illo die Esau itinere quo venerat in Seir, id est in terram Edom seu Idumæam, a nomine suo sic appellatam; tamen aliqui dicunt, quod Seir sit hic nomen villæ, in qua Esau habitavit, et eam suo nomine nuncupavit.
paras.en: [[33:16|So Esau returned that day, the way that he came, to Seir|Reversus est itaque illo die Esau itinere quo venerat in Seir]], that is, into the land of Edom or Idumea, so called from his name; though some say that Seir here is the name of a town in which Esau dwelt, and which he called by his own name.

paras.t: Et Jacob venit in Socoth, ad urbem sic dictam. Unde Hieronymus scribit: Socoth usque hodie civitas est trans Jordanem, de qua in libro Judicum legitur: Locutus est Gedeon ad viros Socoth. Dicit quoque Hieronymus, quod Socoth interpretatur tabernaculum. Hinc Jacob imposuit nomen hoc urbi illi, quoniam ipse fixit ibi tabernacula sua, sicut subjungitur. Ubi ædificata domo et fixis tentoriis, appellavit nomen illius Socoth, id est tabernacula. Sed quare ædificavit ibi domum, quum soleret in tabernaculis seu tentoriis et papilionibus commorari? Ad hoc, ut Lyra refert, respondent Judæi, quod per annum cum medio habitavit ibidem, ideo fecit etiam domum ibi.
paras.en: [[33:17|And Jacob came to Socoth|Et Jacob venit in Socoth]], to the city so called. Hence Jerome writes: Socoth is to this day a city beyond the Jordan, of which we read in the book of Judges: Gedeon spoke [[Judg 8:5|to the men of Soccoth|ad viros Socoth]]. Jerome also says that Socoth is interpreted tabernacle. Hence Jacob gave this name to that city, because he pitched his tabernacles there, as is added: [[33:17|where having built a house, and pitched tents, he called the name of the place Socoth, that is, Tents|Ubi ædificata domo et fixis tentoriis, appellavit nomen illius Socoth, id est tabernacula]]. But why did he build a house there, when he was wont to dwell in tabernacles, that is, tents and pavilions? To this, as Lyra relates, the Jews answer that he dwelt there a year and a half, and therefore made a house there as well.

paras.t: Transivitque in Salem urbem Sichimorum, etc. Circa hoc quærit Hieronymus, quæ fuerit ista urbs nomine Salem, ad Sichimos pertinens, quum Jerusalem, in qua regnavit Melchisedech, ante vocata sit Salem. Ad quod respondet, quod vel utraque civitas idem nomen sortita est: quod de aliis multis Judææ locis et oppidis invenitur, quod scilicet idem nomen loci et urbis, in alia et alia tribu est. Aut Salem, de qua nunc sermo, interpretatur perfecta seu consummata: alia vero, puta Jerusalem, interpretatur pacifica. Tradunt enim Hebræi, quod femur claudicantis Jacob, in Salem urbe Sichimorum sanatum sit: ideoque urbem illam esse Salem vocatam, quæ etiam dicta est Sichem, ita quod erat binomia. Et apud Joannem dicitur Salim, et istud verius æstimatur, quam quod Lyra refert, dicendo: Secundum Hebræos, Salem non est hic nomen proprium civitatis, sed nomen commune, significans integritatem seu pacem, ut sit sensus: Transivit Jacob salem, hoc est integer atque pacificus, in urbem Sichem, quia videlicet nihil de rebus suis amisit in via.
paras.en: [[33:18|And he passed over to Salem, a city of the Sichemites|Transivitque in Salem urbem Sichimorum]], etc. On this Jerome asks what this city named Salem was, belonging to the Sichemites, since Jerusalem, in which Melchisedech reigned, was formerly called Salem. To which he answers that either both cities were given the same name, as is found of many other places and towns of Judea, namely that the same name of a place or city occurs in one tribe and in another; or else the Salem now spoken of is interpreted perfect or consummated, while the other, that is, Jerusalem, is interpreted peaceful. For the Hebrews hand down that the thigh of the limping Jacob was healed in Salem, the city of the Sichemites, and that this is why that city was called Salem; it was also called Sichem, so that it had two names. And in John it is called Salim[[John 3:23||]], and this is thought truer than what Lyra relates, saying: According to the Hebrews, Salem here is not the proper name of a city but a common noun, meaning wholeness or peace, so that the sense is: Jacob passed over salem, that is, whole and peaceable, to the city of Sichem, because, namely, he lost nothing of his goods on the way [the Hebrew shalem means whole, safe].

paras.t: Et habitavit juxta oppidum illud. Et dicit quidam, quod noluit habitare in urbe illa, quia idololatræ habitabant in ea. Verumtamen certum est, quod Jacob et etiam Abraham et Isaac, sæpius commorati sunt in urbibus idololatrarum: imo Jacob viginti annis habitavit cum Laban idololatra. Fortassis autem magis conveniebat ipsi Jacob, juxta urbem illam quam in ea morari, propter pecora sua.
paras.en: [[33:18|and he dwelt by the town|Et habitavit juxta oppidum]], that town. And someone says that he would not dwell in that city because idolaters dwelt in it. Yet it is certain that Jacob, and Abraham and Isaac too, often stayed in cities of idolaters: indeed Jacob dwelt twenty years with Laban, an idolater. But perhaps it suited Jacob better to stay near that city than in it, because of his cattle.

paras.t: Emitque partem agri in qua fixerat tabernacula, id est tentoria sua juxta urbem præfatam, a filiis Hemor patris Sichem: qui Hemor fuit rex Sichimorum, et pater viri nomine Sichem, a quo Sichimi seu Sichimitæ vocati sunt; centum agnis. Circa hoc dicit Lyra: Hebræi dicunt, centum obolis: ex quo concludit, Ideo nostra translatio deficit, aut dictio Hebraica est æquivoca. Ad quod dicendum, quod conclusio illa, quantum ad primam ejus partem, non valet; quoniam magis credendum est sancto Hieronymo, quam Hebræis. Tamen si verbum illud Hebræum æquivocum est ad agnum et obolum, non magis habetur in Hebræo, centum obolis, quam centum agnis. Divitiæ autem antiquorum pecora erant: idcirco frequenter emerunt per pecora, sicut nunc per pecunias: propter quod a pecus pecunia nomen sumpsit, ut asserit Augustinus, et in Decreto habetur.
paras.en: [[33:19|And he bought that part of the field, in which he pitched his tents|Emitque partem agri in qua fixerat tabernacula]], that is, his tents beside the city mentioned, [[33:19|of the children of Hemor, the father of Sichem|a filiis Hemor patris Sichem]]: this Hemor was king of the Sichemites, and father of the man named Sichem, from whom the Sichemites or Sichimites were named; [[33:19|for a hundred lambs|centum agnis]]. On this Lyra says: The Hebrews say, for a hundred obols [small coins]: from which he concludes: Therefore either our translation is at fault, or the Hebrew word is equivocal. To which it must be said that this conclusion, as to its first part, does not hold; for Saint Jerome is more to be believed than the Hebrews. Yet if that Hebrew word is equivocal, meaning both lamb and obol, the Hebrew no more has "a hundred obols" than "a hundred lambs". Now the riches of the ancients were cattle: therefore they often bought with cattle, as now with money: for which reason pecunia [money] took its name from pecus [cattle], as Augustine asserts, and as is found in the Decree [Gratian's Decretum, the standard collection of canon law].

paras.t: Et erecto, id est constructo, ibi altari, invocavit super illud fortissimum Deum Israel, id est, orando obtulit super altare hoc hostias omnipotenti Deo Israelis, videlicet sui ipsius, qui Israel est vocatus, seu suæ posteritatis, quæ sæpe hoc nomine designatur. Et recte nunc dicitur, Fortissimum Deum Israel, quoniam Deus omnipotentiam suam demonstravit in Jacob, protegendo eum a Laban et Esau, ceterisque adversis: quod et Jacob recognoscens, sacrificavit ei ibi cum gratiarum actione devota.
paras.en: [[33:20|And raising|Et erecto]], that is, building, [[33:20|an altar there|ibi altari]], [[33:20|he invoked upon it the most mighty God of Israel|invocavit super illud fortissimum Deum Israel]], that is, praying, he offered victims upon this altar to the almighty God of Israel: namely of himself, who was called Israel, or of his posterity, which is often designated by this name. And rightly is it now said, the most mighty God of Israel, since God showed his almighty power in Jacob, protecting him from Laban and Esau and other adversities: which Jacob also acknowledging, sacrificed to him there with devout thanksgiving.

paras.t: Itaque sancti hujus Patriarchæ exemplo discamus nos ipsos in omnibus humiliare, nec aliquis de sua quasi virtuositate, sapientia et electione præsumens, alteri se præponat, aut offensum placare ac veniam petere dedignetur, quum Jacob, qui tot habuit revelationes, cui et factæ erant tot et tantæ a Deo promissiones, quam profundissime atque sæpissime humiliaverit se coram reprobo fratre; nec bono caritatis et pacis aliquid præferamus, imo ob ea libenter despiciamus seu aliis condividamus transitoria bona, quæ et Jacob quam liberalissime ac promptissime præstitit suo fratri desiderio amicitiæ atque concordiæ.
paras.en: Let us therefore learn by the example of this holy Patriarch to humble ourselves in all things; and let no one, presuming on his own supposed virtue, wisdom and election, set himself above another, or disdain to appease one he has offended and to ask pardon, since Jacob, who had so many revelations, and to whom so many and so great promises had been made by God, humbled himself so very deeply and so very often before his reprobate brother. And let us prefer nothing to the good of charity and peace, but rather for their sake willingly despise transitory goods, or share them with others, as Jacob too most liberally and most readily bestowed them on his brother, out of desire for friendship and concord.

34.title: Expositio litteralis capituli tricesimi quarti: Egressa est autem Dina filia Liæ
34.title_en: Literal exposition of the thirty-fourth chapter: “And Dina the daughter of Lia went out”

paras.t: CAPITULO nunc elucidando describitur, quid contigerit ipsi Jacob, ac soboli ejus circa Sichimitas. Egressa est autem Dina filia Liæ et ultima proles ejus, ut videret mulieres regionis illius. Mulieres quippe naturaliter leves sunt animo et curiosæ. Unde libenter vident aliquid novi, quum tamen deceat esse eas valde pudicas et taciturnas, ac domi manere, quantum congrue fieri potest, præsertim virgines atque juvenculas.
paras.en: The chapter now to be explained describes what befell Jacob and his offspring in regard to the Sichemites. [[34:1|And Dina the daughter of Lia went out|Egressa est autem Dina filia Liæ]], and her last child, [[34:1|to see the women of that country|ut videret mulieres regionis illius]]. For women are by nature light of mind and curious; hence they like to see something new; though it befits them to be very modest and silent, and to stay at home as far as can fittingly be done, especially maidens and young girls.

paras.t: Egressa est itaque Dina ex domo parentum, et introivit præfatum oppidum Sichimorum, juxta quod habitavit, atque ut Josephus refert, tunc erat solemnitas illa in urbe, et Dina sola transivit illuc ad emendum ornamenta mulierum terræ illius, et forsitan ad videndum ornatus et mores, festa ac gestus civium loci illius.
paras.en: So Dina [[34:1|went out|Egressa est]] from her parents' house, and entered the aforesaid town of the Sichemites, near which they dwelt; and, as Josephus relates, there was then a festival in the city, and Dina went over there alone to buy the ornaments of the women of that country, and perhaps to see the finery and the manners, the feasts and the bearing of the citizens of that place.

paras.t: Quam quum vidisset Sichem filius Hemor Hevæi, princeps terræ illius. Sichem iste fuit primogenitus ipsius Hemor, qui pro tunc fuit rex et princeps urbis illius, et quorumdam circumjacentium locorum : sicque Sichem non fuit adhuc princeps terræ illius, nisi in quantum hereditario jure successurus fuit patri suo in principatu. Vel forsitan pater suus jam ei commisit quædam dominia. Dicitur autem Hemor Hevæus, quoniam fuit de stirpe Hevæi, qui fuit filius Cham filii Noe, ut dictum est supra. Adamavit eam amore libidinoso ac prædominante, et rapuit eam violenter, adjutorio suorum servorum, et forte per eos : et dormivit cum illa, cognoscendo ipsam carnaliter, vi opprimens virginem, id est eam quæ virgo fuit antequam taliter cognosceretur : et ita in fornicatione illa fuit raptus et stuprum, utpote violentia et violatio virginis. Et conglutinata est anima ejus cum ea, id est, amore intensissimo (qui amor ἔρως appellatur) ei adhæsit ; qui amor est pessimus, subjiciens hominem carni totaliter, ita ut vix valeat aliud cogitare, nisi quod taliter amat, multaque mala sequuntur ex eo ; tristemque delinivit blanditiis, etc., hoc est, blandis ac dulcibus verbis conatus est consolari ac mitigare Dinam, de sua injuriatione et constupratione mœrentem, quia et parentum ac fratrum suorum metuebat indignationem atque offensam ; doluit quoque de hoc, quod a juvene idololatra et incircumciso cognita fuit. Denique probabile est, quod Sichem dixit ad eam : Ego sum primogenitus patris mei, et ero rex hujus loci, et accipiam te uxorem, eroque tibi bonus maritus, nec parentes tui potuissent te taliter sublimare.
paras.en: [[34:2|And when Sichem the son of Hemor the Hevite, the prince of that land, saw her|Quam quum vidisset Sichem filius Hemor Hevæi, princeps terræ illius]]. This Sichem was the firstborn of Hemor, who was then king and prince of that city and of certain places round about: and so Sichem was not yet prince of that land, except inasmuch as he was to succeed his father in the principality by hereditary right. Or perhaps his father had already committed certain lordships to him. Hemor is called the Hevite because he was of the stock of the Hevite[[Gen 10:17||]], who was a son of Chanaan [Denis writes *filius Cham*, son of Cham; in Gen 10:15–17 the Hevite is a son of Chanaan, Cham's son] the son of Noe, as was said above. [[34:2|he was in love with her|Adamavit eam]] with a lustful and overmastering love, [[34:2|and took her away|et rapuit eam]] by force, with the help of his servants, and perhaps through them: [[34:2|and lay with her|et dormivit cum illa]], knowing her carnally, [[34:2|ravishing the virgin|vi opprimens virginem]], that is, her who was a virgin before she was so known: and so in that fornication there were both rape and defilement, namely violence and the violation of a virgin. [[34:3|And his soul was fast knit unto her|Et conglutinata est anima ejus cum ea]], that is, he clung to her with a most intense love (which love is called *eros*), which is the worst love, subjecting a man wholly to the flesh, so that he can scarcely think of anything but what he so loves, and many evils follow from it; [[34:3|and whereas she was sad, he comforted her with sweet words|tristemque delinivit blanditiis]], etc., that is, with coaxing and sweet words he tried to console and soothe Dina, who was grieving over the wrong and defilement done to her, since she feared the anger and displeasure of her parents and brothers; she grieved too that she had been known by an idolatrous and uncircumcised youth. Lastly, it is probable that Sichem said to her: I am my father's firstborn, and I shall be king of this place, and I will take thee to wife, and I will be a good husband to thee; nor could thy parents have raised thee so high.

paras.t: Quod quum audisset Jacob, etc., scilicet filiam suam esse raptam et corruptam, siluit donec filii sui redirent, etc., qui tunc erant in pastu pecorum occupati. Siluit autem dissimulando injuriam, non ut filios suos incitaret ad inordinatam vindictam, sed ut conferret cum eis quid esset agendum : quia nec regi Hemor audebat negare quod petiit, nec filio ejus alienigenæ libenter tradidit filiam suam, ut Josephus refert.
paras.en: [[34:5|But when Jacob had heard this|Quod quum audisset Jacob]], etc., namely that his daughter had been carried off and defiled, [[34:5|he held his peace till they came back|siluit donec filii sui redirent]], etc., that is, his sons, who were then busy feeding the cattle. He held his peace, hiding the wrong, not so as to stir his sons to disorderly revenge, but to confer with them about what was to be done: since he neither dared refuse King Hemor what he asked, nor willingly gave his daughter to his son, a foreigner, as Josephus relates.

paras.t: Locutus est itaque Hemor ad eos, videlicet ad Jacob ac filios ejus : Sichem filii mei anima adhæsit filiæ vestræ, etc. Loquitur autem pluraliter, Filiæ vestræ, quamvis filia esset ipsius Jacob, non filiorum ejus, eo modo quo aliquid adscribitur toti multitudini propter partem ipsius. Sed et Sichem ad patrem et fratres ejus, id est ad Jacob et filios ejus, ait : Inveniam gratiam, etc. Augete dotem, id est, exigite a me pro dote quantum vultis ; et munera postulate, etc., hoc est, non solum paratus sum huic puellæ assignare pro dote quod vultis, sed vobis quoque munera volo largiri ad libitum vestrum.
paras.en: [[34:8|And Hemor spoke to them|Locutus est itaque Hemor ad eos]], namely to Jacob and his sons: [[34:8|The soul of my son Sichem has a longing for your daughter|Sichem filii mei anima adhæsit filiæ vestræ]], etc. He speaks in the plural, *your daughter*, though she was Jacob's daughter and not his sons', in the way in which something is ascribed to a whole company because of a part of it. [[34:11|Sichem also said to her father and to her brethren|Sed et Sichem ad patrem et fratres ejus]], that is, to Jacob and his sons, [[34:11|Let me find favour|ait : Inveniam gratiam]], etc. [[34:12|Raise the dowry|Augete dotem]], that is, ask of me for the dowry as much as you will; [[34:12|and ask gifts|et munera postulate]], etc., that is: not only am I ready to assign to this girl for her dowry whatever you will, but I also wish to bestow gifts on you at your pleasure.

paras.t: Responderunt filii Jacob, Sichem et patri ejus in dolo, sævientes ob stuprum sororis, etc., id est, pacatos se finxerunt ex verbis Hemor et filii ejus, et velle facere quod postulabant, dummodo ipsi circumciderentur, quum tamen corde sævirent in illos, et sororis suæ violationem proponerent ferociter vindicare, atque ut aliqui dicunt, proposuerunt ipsos invadere, quando jam essent circumcisi, quatenus tunc non possent resistere ex circumcisionis dolore. Vel dixerunt hoc, ut sic evaderent quod Hemor et Sichem ipsis proposuerunt, quos putabant non consensuros circumcisionis conditioni ac pacto. Placuit oblatio eorum, etc., id est, conditio ista, quam filii Jacob obtulerunt Hemor et filio ejus, placuit eis, quamvis videretur multum difficilis. Sed mirum quod hic non ponitur responsio Jacob : et forte id quod filii sui responderunt, venit ex ejus consilio ; non tamen ipse intendebat dolum quem filii intendebant.
paras.en: [[34:13|The sons of Jacob answered Sichem and his father deceitfully, being enraged at the deflowering of their sister|Responderunt filii Jacob, Sichem et patri ejus in dolo, sævientes ob stuprum sororis]], etc., that is, they pretended to be appeased by the words of Hemor and his son, and to be willing to do what they asked, provided they were circumcised, while yet in their hearts they raged against them and purposed fiercely to avenge the violation of their sister; and, as some say, they purposed to attack them when they had been circumcised, so that they could not then resist because of the pain of circumcision. Or they said this so as to escape what Hemor and Sichem proposed to them, thinking they would not consent to the condition and pact of circumcision. [[34:18|Their offer pleased|Placuit oblatio eorum]], etc., that is, this condition which the sons of Jacob offered to Hemor and his son pleased them, though it seemed very hard. But it is strange that Jacob's answer is not given here: and perhaps what his sons answered came from his counsel; yet he did not intend the guile his sons intended.

paras.t: Deinde in textu describitur, qualiter Hemor et filii ejus persuaserunt populo civitatis circumcisionem accipere. Si circumcidamus masculos nostros, id est, infantulos jam natos et etiam nascituros, imo et nos ipsi jam circumcidamur, ritum gentis imitantes, hoc est, observationi et consuetudini Hebræorum istorum nos conformantes per circumcisionis assumptionem ; substantia eorum et pecora, et cuncta quæ possident, nostra erunt, id est, per mutua matrimonia inter nos et eos devolventur ad nos, sicut et e converso, bona nostra ad eos per mutuam associationem. Tantum in hoc acquiescamus, et simul habitantes, unum efficiamus populum per observantiam ejusdem ritus et conjugalis conjunctionis et cognationis ac affinitatis. Assensique sunt omnes, etc., juxta antiquam grammaticam, id est, omnes cives urbis illius consenserunt conditioni et pactioni propositæ.
paras.en: Then the text describes how Hemor and his son persuaded the people of the city to accept circumcision. [[34:22|We must circumcise every male among us|Si circumcidamus masculos nostros]], that is, the little children already born, and those yet to be born, and let us too be circumcised ourselves, [[34:22|following the manner of the nation|ritum gentis imitantes]], that is, conforming ourselves to the observance and custom of these Hebrews by taking up circumcision; [[34:23|And their substance, and cattle, and all that they possess, shall be ours|substantia eorum et pecora, et cuncta quæ possident, nostra erunt]], that is, by intermarriage between us and them these will pass to us, as, conversely, our goods to them through our mutual fellowship. [[34:23|only in this let us condescend, and by dwelling together, we shall make one people|Tantum in hoc acquiescamus, et simul habitantes, unum efficiamus populum]], by the observance of the same rite, and by the union of marriage, and by kinship and affinity. [[34:24|And they all agreed|Assensique sunt omnes]], etc., according to the old grammar, that is, all the citizens of that city consented to the condition and pact proposed [*assensi sunt*, a deponent form of the older Latin, where later usage has *assenserunt*].

paras.t: Præterea, ut recitat Lyra, Hebræorum doctores aliter passum istum exponunt, dicentes quod filii Jacob sincera intentione dixerunt ad Hemor et Sichem, Si circumcidamini, dabitur soror nostra in conjugem Sichem, ut petitis ; et quod dictio Hebraica, quam Hieronymus interpretatus est dolum, sit æquivoca ad fraudem, et ad bonam cautelam : sicque filii Jacob intenderunt Sichimitas ad circumcisionem recta intentione inducere : sed Hemor et Sichem dolum fecerunt, dicentes civibus suis, Si circumcidamus masculos nostros, omnia quæ possident, erunt nostra, id est, habebimus eos nobis omnino subjectos, et erunt servilis conditionis sub nobis : quo dolo percepto, filii Jacob ruperunt pactum : quoniam violantibus fidem, non est fides servanda ; et interfecerunt Sichimitas. Hæc autem expositio falsa censetur, quoniam dato quod dictio illa Hebraica interdum significet bonam cautelam, quod tamen Rabbi Paulus negat, attamen hoc loco non posset sic accipi, quia immediate subjungitur, Sævientes ob stuprum sororis. Si autem filii Jacob dixissent bona intentione et prudenti cautela, Si circumcidamini, non dixissent verba quæ in textu habentur sævientes, sed placati et ignoscentes. Denique paulo post in isto habetur capitulo, quod dum Jacob reprehendisset filios suos de interfectione Sichimitarum, nullam aliam excusationem tangebant, quam sororis suæ violationem, dicendo : Numquid ut scorto abuti debuerunt sorore nostra ? Si autem Sichimitæ commisissent dolum prætactum, allegassent eum pro sua excusatione. Infra quoque habetur, quemadmodum Jacob mox moriturus, locutus sit : Simeon et Levi vasa iniquitatis bellantia, etc. ; ubi reprehendit eos de fraudulenta et atroci interfectione Sichimitarum ; nec possunt verba illa exponi de peccato eorum in Joseph commisso, ut in expositione capituli quadragesimi noni ostendetur.
paras.en: Further, as Lyra relates, the doctors of the Hebrews expound this passage otherwise, saying that the sons of Jacob said to Hemor and Sichem with a sincere intention, If you are circumcised, our sister shall be given in marriage to Sichem, as you ask; and that the Hebrew word which Jerome translated *guile* is equivocal between fraud and good caution: and so the sons of Jacob meant to lead the Sichemites to circumcision with a right intention: but Hemor and Sichem used guile, saying to their citizens, [[34:22|We must circumcise every male among us|Si circumcidamus masculos nostros]], [[34:23|all that they possess, shall be ours|omnia quæ possident, erunt nostra]], that is, we shall have them wholly subject to us, and they shall be of servile condition under us: and when this guile was perceived, the sons of Jacob broke the pact, since faith need not be kept with those who break faith; and they killed the Sichemites. But this exposition is judged false, since, granted that that Hebrew word sometimes means good caution (which Rabbi Paul nevertheless denies), yet in this place it could not be so taken, because there follows at once, [[34:13|being enraged at the deflowering of their sister|Sævientes ob stuprum sororis]]. For if the sons of Jacob had said, If you are circumcised, with a good intention and prudent caution, the words of the text would not have said *enraged*, but *appeased and forgiving*. Further, a little later in this chapter we read that when Jacob had rebuked his sons for the slaughter of the Sichemites, they touched on no other excuse than the violation of their sister, saying: [[34:31|Should they abuse our sister as a strumpet|Numquid ut scorto abuti debuerunt sorore nostra]]? But if the Sichemites had committed the aforesaid guile, they would have alleged it in their own excuse. Below, too, we have how Jacob, about to die, said: [[Gen 49:5|Simeon and Levi brethren: vessels of iniquity waging war|Simeon et Levi vasa iniquitatis bellantia]], etc.; where he rebukes them for the treacherous and savage slaughter of the Sichemites; nor can those words be explained of their sin committed against Joseph, as will be shown in the exposition of the forty-ninth chapter.

paras.t: Verumtamen Rabbi Paulus dicit, quod præinducta Hebræorum expositio potest salvari, quia (ut asserit) Sichimitæ non petierunt veniam aliquam de tanta injuria illata Jacob ac filiis ejus, nec filii Jacob promiserunt pacem Sichimitis, sed concesserunt solum quod possent confœderari, si circumciderentur : ideo non videntur peccasse, abscondendo suum propositum Sichimitis, quoniam licitum est contra inimicos uti insidiis. Sed omnia ista istius Pauli verba, sunt valde imperite prolata. Quod enim affirmat Sichimitas nullam veniam postulasse, est contra textum quo dicitur : Sichem ad patrem ejus, scilicet Dinæ, et ad fratres ejus ait : Inveniam gratiam coram vobis ; et quæcumque statueritis, dabo ; munera postulate, libens tribuam quod petieritis. Insuper quamvis filii Jacob non promiserunt Sichimitis pacem absolute, promiserunt tamen eam sub conditione, dicentes : In hoc valebimus fœderari, si similes nostri esse volueritis, et circumcidatur in vobis omnis masculini sexus ; tunc dabimus et accipiemus mutuo filias nostras ac vestras, et habitabimus vobiscum, erimusque unus populus. Ideo postquam Sichimitæ conditionem hanc impleverunt, filii Jacob obligati fuerunt pacem servare cum eis, ac si absolute promisissent hanc illis : stante quoque illa conditione, et præsertim ea impleta, non potuerunt filii Jacob uti insidiis contra Sichimitas, nec habuerunt contra eos prælium justum, in quo solo licet insidiis uti. Præterea falsum est, quod Paulus iste affirmat, Jacob patriarcham non increpasse filios suos de injustitia in hoc facto. Nam (ut paulo post inducetur) dixit ad eos, Turbastis me : per quod insinuavit, eos injuste egisse.
paras.en: Yet Rabbi Paul says that the aforesaid exposition of the Hebrews can be saved, since (as he asserts) the Sichemites asked no pardon for so great a wrong done to Jacob and his sons, nor did the sons of Jacob promise the Sichemites peace, but granted only that they might be allied with them if they were circumcised: so they do not seem to have sinned by hiding their purpose from the Sichemites, since it is lawful to use stratagems against enemies. But all these words of this Paul are very unskilfully put forward. For his claim that the Sichemites asked no pardon is against the text, where it is said: [[34:11|Sichem also said to her father and to her brethren|Sichem ad patrem ejus, scilicet Dinæ, et ad fratres ejus ait]], namely Dina's: [[34:11|Let me find favour in your sight, and whatsoever you shall appoint I will give|Inveniam gratiam coram vobis ; et quæcumque statueritis, dabo]]; [[34:12|and ask gifts, and I will gladly give what you shall demand|munera postulate, libens tribuam quod petieritis]]. Moreover, though the sons of Jacob did not promise the Sichemites peace absolutely, they promised it under a condition, saying: [[34:15|But in this we may be allied with you, if you will be like us, and all the male sex among you be circumcised|In hoc valebimus fœderari, si similes nostri esse volueritis, et circumcidatur in vobis omnis masculini sexus]]; [[34:16|Then will we mutually give and take your daughters, and ours; and we will dwell with you, and will be one people|tunc dabimus et accipiemus mutuo filias nostras ac vestras, et habitabimus vobiscum, erimusque unus populus]]. Therefore, after the Sichemites had fulfilled this condition, the sons of Jacob were bound to keep peace with them as if they had promised it absolutely: and while that condition stood, and especially once it was fulfilled, the sons of Jacob could not use stratagems against the Sichemites, nor did they have a just war against them, in which alone it is lawful to use stratagems. Further, what this Paul affirms is false, that the patriarch Jacob did not rebuke his sons for injustice in this deed. For (as will be brought in a little later) he said to them, [[34:30|You have troubled me|Turbastis me]]: by which he hinted that they had acted unjustly.

paras.t: Et ecce die tertio quando gravissimus vulnerum dolor est, id est, quando circumcisi magis affliguntur ex vulnere circumcisionis, quia (ut dicitur) tertio die inde amplius cruciantur, sicut et vulnera quædam magis affligunt post certum tempus, quam dum recentia exstant : Simeon et Levi, fratres Dinæ uterini, arreptis gladiis, ingressi sunt urbem confidenter, id est audacter, interfectisque omnibus masculis adultæ ætatis, quia (ut statim dicetur) parvulos duxerunt captivos : Hemor et Sichem pariter necaverunt, etc. Quibus egressis de domo Hemor, irruerunt super occisos ceteri filii Jacob, et depopulati sunt urbem in ultionem stupri, etc., non in vindictam præfatæ fraudis confictæ.
paras.en: [[34:25|And behold the third day, when the pain of the wound was greatest|Et ecce die tertio quando gravissimus vulnerum dolor est]], that is, when the circumcised are most afflicted by the wound of circumcision, since (as is said) on the third day they are tormented more by it, as certain wounds too give more pain after a certain time than while they are fresh: [[34:25|Simeon and Levi, the brothers of Dina|Simeon et Levi, fratres Dinæ]], born of the same mother, [[34:25|taking their swords, entered boldly into the city and slew all the men|arreptis gladiis, ingressi sunt urbem confidenter, id est audacter, interfectisque omnibus masculis]] of grown age, since (as will be said at once) they led away the little ones captive: [[34:26|And they killed also Hemor and Sichem|Hemor et Sichem pariter necaverunt]], etc. [[34:27|And when they were gone out|Quibus egressis]] from Hemor's house, [[34:27|the other sons of Jacob came upon the slain; and plundered the city in revenge of the rape|irruerunt super occisos ceteri filii Jacob, et depopulati sunt urbem in ultionem stupri]], etc., not in revenge for the aforesaid feigned fraud.

paras.t: Quibus patratis audacter, audacia excessiva, quæ fortitudini et rationi contrariatur : fortitudo namque est virtus moralis et cardinalis, media inter duo vitiosa extrema, quæ sunt timor atque audacia, quamvis timor et audacia interdum accipiantur extense in bono ; Jacob dixit ad Simeon et Levi : Turbastis me, id est, per hæc opera vestra mala ad magnam me induxistis tristitiam, inquietudinem ac timorem. Fuerunt enim in gestis his filiorum Jacob violatio pacti, crudelitas, furor, immansivus dolus, et indignatio gravis, homicidium et injustitia prorsus enormis : quoniam et multos occidisse censentur, qui in raptu violationeque Dinæ, culpam non habuerunt. Propter quod Jacob dixit postea de eisdem : Maledictus furor eorum, quia pertinax : et indignatio, quia dura. In consilium eorum non veniat anima mea, et in cœtu eorum non sit gloria mea. Et odiosum fecistis me, etc., habitatoribus terræ hujus, quoniam factum vestrum mihi imponetur ab illis. Nos pauci sumus comparatione illorum ; illi congregati percutient me, id est occident, et delebor ego et domus mea, hoc est, ego et soboles atque familia mea, auferemur de superficie terræ per interfectionem ab illis. Videtur Jacob ita dicendo esse mentitus, quia non contigit ita, et de veritate divinarum promissionum ei sæpe factarum dubitasse. Frequenter etenim Deus ei promisit copiosissimam posteritatis suæ multiplicationem. Dicendum, quod Jacob protulit verba illa, non simpliciter asserendo, sed avisando ac formidando, secundum considerationem inferiorum causarum, secundum quas sic factum fuisset, nisi Deus omnipotens aliter subvenisset.
paras.en: [[34:30|And when they had boldly perpetrated these things|Quibus patratis audacter]], with excessive daring, which is contrary to fortitude and to reason: for fortitude is a moral and cardinal virtue, a mean between two vicious extremes, which are fear and daring, though fear and daring are sometimes taken broadly in a good sense; [[34:30|Jacob said to Simeon and Levi: You have troubled me|Jacob dixit ad Simeon et Levi : Turbastis me]], that is, by these evil deeds of yours you have brought me into great sadness, disquiet and fear. For in these deeds of the sons of Jacob there were the breaking of a pact, cruelty, fury, savage guile, grievous wrath, manslaughter and wholly enormous injustice: since they are reckoned to have killed many who had no guilt in the rape and violation of Dina. For which reason Jacob afterwards said of them: [[Gen 49:7|Cursed be their fury, because it was stubborn: and their wrath, because it was cruel|Maledictus furor eorum, quia pertinax : et indignatio, quia dura]]. [[Gen 49:6|Let not my soul go into their counsel, nor my glory be in their assembly|In consilium eorum non veniat anima mea, et in cœtu eorum non sit gloria mea]]. [[34:30|and made me hateful|Et odiosum fecistis me]], etc., [[34:30|the inhabitants of this land|habitatoribus terræ hujus]], since your deed will be laid to my charge by them. [[34:30|We are few|Nos pauci sumus]] compared with them; [[34:30|they will gather themselves together and kill me|illi congregati percutient me]], that is, slay me, [[34:30|and both I, and my house shall be destroyed|et delebor ego et domus mea]], that is, I and my offspring and household shall be taken from the face of the earth by being slain by them. In saying this Jacob seems to have lied, since it did not so happen, and to have doubted the truth of the divine promises often made to him. For God had often promised him a most plentiful multiplying of his posterity. The answer is that Jacob uttered those words not asserting them absolutely, but in warning and in fear, according to the consideration of lower causes, according to which it would have so happened, had not almighty God helped otherwise.

paras.t: Responderunt : Numquid ut scorto, id est quasi meretrice, abuti debuere sorore nostra ? Non utique : imo graviter peccaverunt ea abutendo, hoc est rapiendo et illicite cognoscendo, quæ tamen carnalis cognitio a solo Sichem peracta est : et quamvis Sichimitæ non debuerunt sic agere, iste tamen non fuit justus ultionis modus ac ordo, præsertim quoniam Hemor et Sichem emendationem præbuerunt tam magnam, et propter alias causas præhabitas.
paras.en: [[34:31|They answered: Should they abuse our sister as a strumpet?|Responderunt : Numquid ut scorto]] *strumpet*, that is, a harlot. Surely not: indeed they sinned grievously in abusing her, that is, in carrying her off and knowing her unlawfully, though that carnal knowledge was done by Sichem alone: and although the Sichemites ought not so to have acted, this was nevertheless not a just manner and order of vengeance, especially since Hemor and Sichem offered so great an amends, and for the other reasons given above.

paras.t: Præterea objici potest prædictis, quod historia ista incredibiliter sonat : quomodo enim tam pauci qui ad sobolem ac familiam Jacob pertinuerunt, poterant multitudinem occidere tantam ? præsertim quia senior filius Jacob, adhuc vix erat viginti quinque annorum, vel parum plus. Jacob enim habitavit in Mesopotamia solum viginti annis, et septem annis moratus est ibi antequam genuit Ruben primogenitum suum, imo quasi octo annis, ita quod Ruben in exitu a Mesopotamia erat duodecim annorum aut circiter : propter quod Jacob rediens, de filiis suis ad Esau dixit : Parvuli sunt. Ad istud Augustinus respondet, quod multi fuerunt cum Simeone et Levi adjuvantes eosdem, et quod Jacob diu habitavit in terra illa post reditum a Mesopotamia, antequam filii sui istud fecerunt. Habuit autem Jacob grandem familiam, sicut de Abraham et Isaac dictum est. Sichimitæ quoque fuerunt ad resistendum imparati, imo et ex dolore circumcisionis infirmi. Porro Josephus protestatur : Quum esset in urbe illa festivitas, et Sichimitæ requie ac epulis uterentur, filii Jacob primis custodiis incunctanter adsistentes, occiderunt dormientes.
paras.en: Further, it can be objected to what has been said that this history sounds incredible: for how could so few, belonging to the offspring and household of Jacob, kill so great a multitude? especially since Jacob's eldest son was as yet scarcely twenty-five years old, or a little more. For Jacob dwelt in Mesopotamia only twenty years, and he stayed there seven years before he begot Ruben his firstborn, indeed almost eight, so that Ruben was about twelve years old at the departure from Mesopotamia: for which reason Jacob, on his return, said of his sons to Esau: They are little ones. To this Augustine answers that there were many with Simeon and Levi helping them, and that Jacob dwelt a long time in that land after his return from Mesopotamia before his sons did this. Jacob, too, had a great household, as was said of Abraham and Isaac. The Sichemites, also, were unprepared to resist, and indeed weak from the pain of circumcision. Josephus, moreover, declares: While there was a festival in that city, and the Sichemites were given to rest and feasting, the sons of Jacob, falling without delay upon the first guards, killed them as they slept.

paras.t: Rursus contra prædicta objicitur, quod sancta vidua Judith ait : Domine, Deus patris mei Simeon, qui dedisti ei gladium in defensionem, id est ultionem alienigenarum, qui violatores exstiterunt in coinquinatione, et denudaverunt femur virginis, et dedisti mulieres eorum in prædam, et parvulos eorum in captivitatem, et omnem prædam in divisionem servis tuis qui zelaverunt zelum tuum. Ex quibus videtur, quod filii Jacob justo ac divino zelo id peregerunt, et factum illud Deo sit adscribendum, ejusque adjutorio factum. Ad hoc breviter aliqui dicunt, quod liber Judith non est in canone sacræ Scripturæ, et ab Hebræis inter apocrypha computatur, idcirco non habet auctoritatem contra Scripturam canonicam. In Scholastica vero historia respondetur, quod Judith non commendavit factum Simeonis, quod detestatus est Jacob, sed ultionem Domini factam per manum iniquam. Cui solutioni objicitur, quod Judith dicit deprædatores Sichimitarum zelo Dei permotos. Ad quod dici potest, sicut de Judæis ait Apostolus, quod habuerunt zelum Dei, sed non secundum scientiam.
paras.en: Again, it is objected against what has been said that the holy widow Judith says: [[Jdt 9:2|Lord God of my father Simeon, who gavest him a sword|Domine, Deus patris mei Simeon, qui dedisti ei gladium]] in defence, that is, [[Jdt 9:2|to execute vengeance against strangers|ultionem alienigenarum]], [[Jdt 9:2|who had defiled by their uncleanness, and uncovered the virgin|qui violatores exstiterunt in coinquinatione, et denudaverunt femur virginis]] [Denis's text: *uncovered the thigh of the virgin*], [[Jdt 9:3|And who gavest their wives to be made a prey|et dedisti mulieres eorum in prædam]], [[Jdt 9:3|and their daughters into captivity|et parvulos eorum in captivitatem]] [Denis's text has *parvulos*, their little ones], [[Jdt 9:3|and all their spoils to be divided to the servants, who were zealous with thy zeal|et omnem prædam in divisionem servis tuis qui zelaverunt zelum tuum]]. From which it seems that the sons of Jacob did this with a just and divine zeal, and that the deed is to be ascribed to God and was done with His help. To this some say briefly that the book of Judith is not in the canon of sacred Scripture and is counted among the apocrypha by the Hebrews, and so it has no authority against canonical Scripture [the Council of Trent later defined Judith as canonical]. But in the Scholastic History it is answered that Judith did not commend the deed of Simeon, which Jacob detested, but the vengeance of the Lord done by a wicked hand. Against this solution it is objected that Judith says that the plunderers of the Sichemites were moved by the zeal of God. To which it can be said, as the Apostle says of the Jews, that they had [[Rom 10:2|a zeal of God, but not according to knowledge|zelum Dei, sed non secundum scientiam]].

paras.t: Postremo moraliter per Dinam foris egressam ac violatam, intelligitur anima curiosa, quæ sui ipsius discussione et custodia derelictis, per inania evagatur, aliorumque vitam et defectus scrutatur : ideo a diabolo constupratur, fitque illius adultera, corruendo in mortalia peccata. Grave quippe curiositatis est vitium, quod dum hominem aliorum observationi facit intentum, reddit eum ad considerandum proprias culpas cæcum. Quumque anima talis ad horam de suis dolet peccatis, diabolus tristem delinit blanditiis, persuadens ei ad pristina mala redire ; ejus quoque prælato conatur suggerere, ut eum non increpet inde, sed sibi cohærere permittat. Boni autem prælati non acquiescunt suggestioni hujusmodi, sed arreptis gladiis verborum cœlestium ac virtutum, impugnant diabolum, et de ejus domo, quæ est ecclesia malignorum, animam ita deceptam ac eis commissam, reducunt, convertendo eamdem, Satanamque sub pedibus suis velociter conterunt.
paras.en: Lastly, in the moral sense, by Dina going out and being violated is understood the curious soul which, neglecting the examination and guarding of itself, wanders about through vain things and pries into the life and failings of others: therefore it is defiled by the devil and becomes his adulteress, falling into mortal sins. For grievous is the vice of curiosity, which, while it makes a man intent on observing others, makes him blind to considering his own faults. And when such a soul grieves for a while over its sins, the devil soothes the sad soul with blandishments, persuading it to return to its former evils; he also tries to suggest to its prelate that he should not rebuke it for this, but let it cleave to him. But good prelates do not yield to such a suggestion, but, taking up the swords of heavenly words and of virtues, they attack the devil, and lead back from his house, which is the church of the wicked, the soul so deceived and committed to them, converting it, and swiftly crush Satan under their feet.

35.title: Expositio capituli tricesimi quinti: Interea locutus est Deus ad Jacob
35.title_en: Exposition of the thirty-fifth chapter: “In the mean time God said to Jacob”

paras.t: RECITANTUR in isto capitulo actus quidam et peregrinationes sancti Jacob, et beneficia ei a Deo collata. Interea locutus est Deus ad Jacob per angelum, consolando eum in timore quem habuit propter causam in fine præcedentis capituli expressam, et consulendo ei quid ageret. Surge de loco isto, et a tua formidine, et ascende Bethel, id est ad locum in quo vidisti scalam in somnis, puta ad montem Moria prope Jerusalem, et habita ibi cum tuis domesticis, facque ibi altare Deo qui apparuit tibi quando fugiebas Esau, quando vidisti Dominum scalæ innixum, ut dictum est supra. Loquitur autem Deus per angelum de se ipso, quasi de alio, vel ad insinuandam pluralitatem Personarum in simplici deitate sic loquitur. Est tamen consuetudo Scripturæ veteris Testamenti sic loqui.
paras.en: This chapter relates certain acts and journeyings of holy Jacob, and the benefits God bestowed on him. [[35:1|In the mean time God said to Jacob|Interea locutus est Deus ad Jacob]] through an angel, consoling him in the fear he had for the reason stated at the end of the preceding chapter, and counselling him what to do. [[35:1|Arise|Surge]] from this place, and from thy dread, [[35:1|and go up to Bethel|et ascende Bethel]], that is, to the place where thou sawest the ladder in thy sleep, namely to Mount Moria near Jerusalem, [[35:1|and dwell there|et habita ibi]] with thy household, [[35:1|and make there an altar to God|facque ibi altare Deo]], [[35:1|who appeared to thee when thou didst flee from Esau|qui apparuit tibi quando fugiebas Esau]], when thou sawest the Lord leaning on the ladder, as was said above. God speaks through the angel of Himself as of another; or He speaks so to suggest the plurality of Persons in the simple Godhead. Yet it is the custom of the Scripture of the Old Testament to speak so.

paras.t: Jacob vero convocata omni domo, id est sobole ac familia sua, ait: Abjicite deos alienos qui in medio vestri sunt, id est idola quæ habetis. Probabile est, quod in domo Jacob nemo aperte coluit idola, et forte nec clam: quod de ejus uxoribus et filiis ac filia certius est. Sed ex urbe Sichimorum asportarunt idola quædam, ut dicitur. Josephus quoque fatetur, quod dum Jacob purgaret suos domesticos, invenit idola Laban. Et mundamini a vestris peccatis quæ commisistis in Sichimitas, et a ceteris vitiis vestris per pœnitentiam veram, ac mutate vestimenta vestra sanguine adspersa, aut a Sichimitis injuste sublata, quatenus per exterioris vestitus mutationem admoneamini, et curetis interiorem cordis vestri dispositionem mutare in melius. Faciamus ibi altare Domino, ad offerendum ei sacrificia laudis et gratiarum actionis, qui exaudivit me in die tribulationis meæ, et socius fuit itineris mei, id est, gratiose ac familiariter adfuit mihi in peregrinationibus meis, in quibus etiam per angelos visibiliter comitatus est me. At ille, scilicet Jacob, infodit eos, utpote deos alienos cum inauribus et armillis, idolorum illorum ornamentis, subter terebinthum. Est autem terebinthus quercus quædam nigra. Quumque profecti essent, id est, quum Jacob et ejus domestici recessissent a loco prope Sichem seu Salem, terror Dei invasit omnes per circuitum civitates, hoc est, Deus omnipotens perterruit habitatores urbium quæ erant in gyro Sichem; et non sunt ausi persequi recedentes: et hoc fecit Deus meritis Jacob, qui idola illa tanquam spurcitias fodit sub terra, et quia domestici ejus jam purgaverunt se, ut divina protectione essent condigni. Qualiter vero Deus perterruit urbium illarum habitatores, an scilicet per aliqua exteriora visa sive audita, an corda eorum alterando ab audacia ad pavorem, Scriptura non exprimit.
paras.en: [[35:2|And Jacob having called together all his household|Jacob vero convocata omni domo]], that is, his offspring and family, [[35:2|said: Cast away the strange gods that are among you|ait: Abjicite deos alienos qui in medio vestri sunt]], that is, the idols you have. It is probable that in Jacob's house no one worshipped idols openly, and perhaps not even in secret: which is more certain of his wives, his sons and his daughter. But they carried off certain idols from the city of the Sichemites, as is said. Josephus too states that when Jacob was purifying his household he found Laban's idols. [[35:2|and be cleansed|Et mundamini]] from your sins which you committed against the Sichemites, and from your other vices, by true penance, [[35:2|and change your garments|ac mutate vestimenta vestra]], sprinkled with blood, or unjustly taken from the Sichemites, so that by the change of your outward clothing you may be reminded, and take care, to change the inward disposition of your heart for the better. [[35:3|that we may make there an altar to God|Faciamus ibi altare Domino]], to offer Him sacrifices of praise and thanksgiving, [[35:3|who heard me in the day of my affliction, and accompained me in my journey|qui exaudivit me in die tribulationis meæ, et socius fuit itineris mei]] [the Latin has *socius fuit itineris mei*, was the companion of my journey], that is, was graciously and familiarly present with me in my wanderings, in which He also accompanied me visibly through angels. [[35:4|and he buried them|At ille, scilicet Jacob, infodit eos]], namely Jacob, that is, the strange gods with the earrings and bracelets, the ornaments of those idols, [[35:4|under the turpentine tree|subter terebinthum]]. Now the terebinth is a kind of black oak. [[35:5|And when they were departed|Quumque profecti essent]], that is, when Jacob and his household had withdrawn from the place near Sichem or Salem, [[35:5|the terror of God fell upon all the cities round about|terror Dei invasit omnes per circuitum civitates]], that is, almighty God terrified the inhabitants of the cities that were round about Sichem; [[35:5|and they durst not pursue after them as they went away|et non sunt ausi persequi recedentes]]: and God did this by the merits of Jacob, who buried those idols under the earth as filth, and because his household had now purified themselves, so as to be worthy of divine protection. But how God terrified the inhabitants of those cities, whether by some outward things seen or heard, or by changing their hearts from daring to fear, Scripture does not say.

paras.t: Venit igitur Jacob Luzam, etc., cognomento Bethel, etc., id est ad urbem Jerusalem, quæ his aliisque nominibus appellatur, ut dictum est. Et appellavit nomen loci illius, Domus Dei, etc., hoc enim significat Bethel, et ita vocavit locum illum quando fugit ad Mesopotamiam; nunc quoque ita vocavit, nomen prius a se impositum confirmando. Tunc etiam adimplevit quod Domino vovit in visione præfata, sibi in monte Moria facta, dicendo: Cunctorumque quæ dederis mihi, decimas offeram tibi.
paras.en: [[35:6|And Jacob came to Luza|Venit igitur Jacob Luzam]], etc., [[35:6|surnamed Bethel|cognomento Bethel]], etc., that is, to the city of Jerusalem, which is called by these and other names, as has been said [Denis here follows his earlier identification of Bethel with Jerusalem and Mount Moria]. [[35:7|and called the name of that place, The house of God|Et appellavit nomen loci illius, Domus Dei]], etc.: for this is what Bethel means; and he so named that place when he fled to Mesopotamia; now too he so named it, confirming the name he had given before. Then too he fulfilled what he vowed to the Lord in the aforesaid vision made to him on Mount Moria, saying: [[Gen 28:22|of all things that thou shalt give to me, I will offer tithes to thee|Cunctorumque quæ dederis mihi, decimas offeram tibi]].

paras.t: Eodem autem tempore mortua est Debora nutrix Rebeccæ, et sepulta est ad radices Bethel, id est prope urbem illam seu in pede montis Moria, subter quercum, quatenus ex arbore illa famosior esset sepultura ipsius; vocatumque est nomen loci illius, Quercus fletus: et hoc propter magnitudinem tristitiæ ac ploratus, quos Jacob et ejus domestici habuerunt de morte Deboræ, quæ fuit matrona valde antiqua, et (sicut ex verbis his conjicitur) virtuosa. Apparet quoque ex his, quod Debora obiit in domo Jacob. Dicuntque aliqui, quod Rebecca diu ante hæc misit eam cum aliis in Mesopotamiam, ut inde reduceret Jacob, et quod exinde mansit cum Jacob: quod si verum esset, probabile est quod Jacob non mansisset tot annis cum Laban; vel quando exposuit uxoribus suis causas suæ reversionis ad terram natalem, expressisset et causam hanc, quod scilicet mater sua ita misisset pro eo. Ideo dici potest, quod ex domo Isaac ivit ad visitandum Jacob, quem valde dilexit; et manens cum eo, defuncta sit.
paras.en: [[35:8|At the same time Debora, the nurse of Rebecca, died, and was buried at the foot of Bethel|Eodem autem tempore mortua est Debora nutrix Rebeccæ, et sepulta est ad radices Bethel]], that is, near that city, or at the foot of Mount Moria, [[35:8|under an oak|subter quercum]], so that her burial might be better known from that tree; [[35:8|and the name of that place was called, The oak of weeping|vocatumque est nomen loci illius, Quercus fletus]]: and this because of the greatness of the sorrow and weeping which Jacob and his household had over the death of Debora, who was a very old matron and (as is gathered from these words) a virtuous one. It appears from this, too, that Debora died in Jacob's house. And some say that Rebecca long before this sent her with others into Mesopotamia to bring Jacob back from there, and that from then on she stayed with Jacob: but if this were true, it is probable that Jacob would not have stayed so many years with Laban; or, when he set out to his wives the reasons for his return to his native land, he would have given this reason too, namely that his mother had so sent for him. So it can be said that she went from Isaac's house to visit Jacob, whom she greatly loved, and died while staying with him.

paras.t: Apparuit autem iterum Deus Jacob, etc., benedixitque ei, dicens: Non vocaberis ultra Jacob, id est, non solum nec principaliter Jacob vocaberis, sed Israel erit nomen tuum, quod nomen competit tibi tanquam viro contemplativo et perfecto. Et appellavit eum Israel: et ita nomen istud est ei modo impositum, quod ante prænuntiatum fuerat imponendum. Dixitque ei : Ego Deus omnipotens sum ; idcirco de meis promissionibus non est ambigendum quin possim eas implere. Cresce in virtutibus, et in sobole tua ac posteris, et multiplicare in successoribus tuæ propagationis : Jacob quoque post hæc genuit Benjamin. Gentes et populi nationum ex te erunt, videlicet duodecim tribus Israel, omnes quoque fideles erunt filii tui per fidei imitationem : reges de lumbis tuis egredientur, id est, ex semine posterorum tuorum nascentur, quia de tribu Juda fuerunt reges, ex tribu etiam Ephraim fuerunt multi decem tribuum reges. Terramque quam dedi Abraham et Isaac, id est, quam eis pro eorum posteris suo tempore dare promisi, dabo tibi, et, pro id est, semini tuo post te. Et recessit ab eo, hoc est, Deus per angelum loquens et apparens ipsi Jacob, disparuit.
paras.en: [[35:9|And God appeared again to Jacob|Apparuit autem iterum Deus Jacob]], etc., [[35:9|and he blessed him|benedixitque ei]], [[35:10|Saying: Thou shalt not be called any more Jacob|dicens: Non vocaberis ultra Jacob]], that is, thou shalt not be called Jacob only, nor chiefly, [[35:10|but Israel shall be thy name|sed Israel erit nomen tuum]], which name befits thee as a contemplative and perfect man. [[35:10|And he called him Israel|Et appellavit eum Israel]]: and so this name, which had been foretold as to be given him, is now given him. [[35:11|And said to him: I am God almighty|Dixitque ei : Ego Deus omnipotens sum]]; therefore there is no doubting about my promises, that I can fulfil them. [[35:11|increase thou|Cresce]] in virtues, and in thy offspring and descendants, [[35:11|and be multiplied|et multiplicare]] in the successors of thy line: Jacob also begot Benjamin after this. [[35:11|Nations and peoples of nations shall be from thee|Gentes et populi nationum ex te erunt]], namely the twelve tribes of Israel; all the faithful too shall be thy sons by imitation of thy faith: [[35:11|and kings shall come out of thy loins|reges de lumbis tuis egredientur]], that is, they shall be born of the seed of thy descendants: for from the tribe of Juda there were kings, and from the tribe of Ephraim too there were many kings of the ten tribes. [[35:12|And the land which I gave to Abraham and Isaac|Terramque quam dedi Abraham et Isaac]], that is, which I promised to give them for their descendants in their time, [[35:12|I will give to thee, and|dabo tibi, et]] (*and* standing for *that is*) [[35:12|to thy seed after thee|semini tuo post te]]. [[35:13|And he departed from him|Et recessit ab eo]], that is, God, who spoke and appeared to Jacob through an angel, vanished.

paras.t: Ille vero erexit titulum lapideum, id est, lapidem statuit pro signo et memoriali revelationis divinæ sibi factæ, in loco quo locutus ei fuerat Deus ; libans super eum libamina, id est, super lapidem illum Deo offerens oblationes de materiis liquidis, et effundens oleum, quod etiam Domino immolavit, vocansque nomen loci illius, id est urbis situatæ prope hunc montem seu titulum, Bethel. Ista quoque fecit quando ad Mesopotamiam fugit, et scalam in somno conspexit. Unde capitulo vicesimo octavo scriptum est : Surgens mane, tulit lapidem et erexit in titulum, fundens oleum desuper, appellavitque nomen urbis Bethel, quæ prius Luza vocabatur.
paras.en: [[35:14|But he set up a monument of stone|Ille vero erexit titulum lapideum]], that is, he set up a stone as a sign and memorial of the divine revelation made to him, [[35:14|in the place where God had spoken to him|in loco quo locutus ei fuerat Deus]]; [[35:14|pouring drink-offerings upon it|libans super eum libamina]], that is, offering to God on that stone oblations of liquid things, [[35:14|and pouring oil thereon|et effundens oleum]], which he also offered to the Lord, [[35:15|And calling the name of that place|vocansque nomen loci illius]], that is, of the city lying near this mount or monument, [[35:15|Bethel|Bethel]]. These things too he did when he fled to Mesopotamia and saw the ladder in his sleep. Hence it is written in the twenty-eighth chapter: [[Gen 28:18|And Jacob arising in the morning, took the stone|Surgens mane, tulit lapidem]] [[Gen 28:18|and set it up for a title, pouring oil upon the top of it|et erexit in titulum, fundens oleum desuper]], [[Gen 28:19|And he called the name of the city Bethel, which before was called Luza|appellavitque nomen urbis Bethel, quæ prius Luza vocabatur]].

paras.t: Egressus autem inde Jacob cum suis domesticis, venit verno tempore, scilicet tempore veris, quod ad ambulandum est aptum, ad terram quæ ducit Ephratam, hoc est ad Bethlehem ; in qua terra seu via, non ipsa urbe, quum parturiret, id est, cum vehementi dolore inciperet parere Rachel, ob difficultatem partus periclitari cœpit, hoc est morti appropinquare. Dixitque ei obstetrix : Noli timere, quia et hunc habebis filium, id est, post hujus infantuli nativitatem adhuc vivere : quasi diceret, Non morieris : quod dixit ad confortandum et consolandum Rachelem.
paras.en: [[35:16|And going forth from thence|Egressus autem inde]] Jacob with his household, [[35:16|he came in the spring time|venit verno tempore]], namely the season of spring, which is suited to travelling, [[35:16|to the land which leadeth to Ephrata|ad terram quæ ducit Ephratam]], that is, to Bethlehem; [[35:16|wherein|in qua]] land or road, not in the city itself, [[35:16|when Rachel was in travail|quum parturiret, id est, cum vehementi dolore inciperet parere Rachel]], that is, began to give birth with violent pain, [[35:17|By reason of her hard labour, she began to be in danger|ob difficultatem partus periclitari cœpit]], that is, to draw near to death. [[35:17|and the midwife said to her: Fear not, for thou shalt have this son also|Dixitque ei obstetrix : Noli timere, quia et hunc habebis filium]], that is, thou shalt still live after this little one's birth: as if she said, Thou shalt not die: which she said to strengthen and console Rachel.

paras.t: Egrediente autem anima Rachelis de corpore suo præ dolore, hoc est, disponente se ad egrediendum, ita quod vita animalis in aliquibus membris quasi defecit, et morte jam imminente, vocavit nomen filii sui Benoni, id est filius doloris mei, hoc est filius quem cum tanto dolore peperi, et qui mihi occasio est hujus doloris mortiferi. Pater vero appellavit eum Benjamin, id est filius dextræ, hoc est constantiæ seu virtutis, quam Jacob in ejus generatione ac nominatione monstravit. Mortua est ergo Rachel, et sepulta est in via quæ ducit Ephratam, hæc est Bethlehem : quæ primo vocata est Ephrata ex nomine uxoris Caleb, quæ Ephrata vocabatur, et ibi sepulta est, ut primo Paralipomenon et in Scholastica fertur historia ; postmodum vero dicta est Bethlehem, quod interpretatur domus panis, quia post grandem caristiam ibi factam tempore Elimelech, fuit ibi abundantia victualium magna. Erexitque Jacob titulum, hoc est notabile, memorialeque signum sepulturæ Rachelis, super sepulcrum ejus. Hebræi autem semper fuerunt specialiter diligentes de honorifica sepultura suorum, tanquam fidem habentes vitæ sequentis et resurrectionis futuræ, atque ut vivi haberent mortuorum memoriam, ad sequendum bonorum exempla, et ad orandum pro ipsis, imo et pro honoratione ipsorum. Hic est titulus monumenti Rachel usque in præsentem diem : quia duravit usque ad tempus quo Moyses scripsit hæc, diuque postea.
paras.en: [[35:18|And when her soul was departing for pain|Egrediente autem anima]], Rachel's soul from her body, that is, preparing to go out, so that the life of the senses had as it were failed in some members, [[35:18|and death was now at hand, she called the name of her son Benoni|et morte jam imminente, vocavit nomen filii sui Benoni]], [[35:18|that is, the son of my pain|id est filius doloris mei]], that is, the son whom I bore with such pain, and who is the occasion of this deadly pain to me. [[35:18|but his father called him Benjamin, that is, the son of the right hand|Pater vero appellavit eum Benjamin, id est filius dextræ]], that is, of constancy or strength, which Jacob showed in begetting and naming him. [[35:19|So Rachel died, and was buried in the highway that leadeth to Ephrata, this is Bethlehem|Mortua est ergo Rachel, et sepulta est in via quæ ducit Ephratam, hæc est Bethlehem]]: which was first called Ephrata from the name of Caleb's wife, who was called Ephrata and was buried there, as is said in the first book of Paralipomenon[[1 Par 2:19||]] [the margin note here is unreadable in the transcription; Caleb's wife Ephrata is in 1 Par 2:19] and in the Scholastic History; but afterwards it was called Bethlehem, which is interpreted *house of bread*, since after a great dearth there in the time of Elimelech there was a great plenty of victuals there. [[35:20|And Jacob erected a pillar|Erexitque Jacob titulum]], that is, a notable and memorial sign of Rachel's burial, [[35:20|over her sepulchre|super sepulcrum ejus]]. Now the Hebrews were always especially careful about the honourable burial of their own, as having faith in the life to come and in the future resurrection, and so that the living might have the dead in memory, to follow the examples of the good and to pray for them, and indeed to honour them. [[35:20|this is the pillar of Rachel's monument, to this day|Hic est titulus monumenti Rachel usque in præsentem diem]]: since it lasted until the time when Moses wrote these things, and long after.

paras.t: Egressus inde Jacob cum suis, fixit tabernaculum trans turrem Gregis. Circa hoc dicit Hieronymus : Hunc locum dicunt Hebræi, ubi postea ædificatum est templum, et per turrim Gregis significari turrim Ader, id est congregationis et cœtus, de qua ait Michæas : Et tu turris Gregis nebulosa filiæ Sion ; et Jacob fixisse tentoria illo tempore trans locum, ubi postea ædificatum est templum. Sed si sequimur ordinem viæ pastorum, locus est juxta Bethlehem, ubi vel angelorum grex in Christi nativitate cecinit; vel Jacob sua pecora pavit, nomen loco illi imponens: et quod verius est, tunc quoddam vaticinio præmonstrabatur, quod futurum erat mysterio. Itaque secundum Hebræos, turris Gregis significat locum ubi postea constructum est templum, qui locus vocatus est turris Gregis, quoniam templum factum fuit instar turris, illucque congregabatur populus, et pecora adducebantur ad immolandum. Porro secundum Hieronymum, locus est non remote a Bethlehem, ubi Christo nato angeli cecinerunt, Gloria in excelsis Deo; quem locum vocaverunt postea Christiani, Angelus ad pastores. Sicque secundum intentionem beati Hieronymi, locus ille vocatus est turris Gregis quodam vaticinio futurorum.
paras.en: [[35:21|Departing thence|Egressus inde]] Jacob with his people, [[35:21|he pitched his tent beyond the Flock tower|fixit tabernaculum trans turrem Gregis]]. On this Jerome says: The Hebrews say that this is the place where the temple was afterwards built, and that by the Flock tower is signified the tower of Ader, that is, of the gathering and assembly, of which Micheas says: [[Mich 4:8|And thou, O cloudy tower of the flock, of the daughter of Sion|Et tu turris Gregis nebulosa filiæ Sion]]; and that Jacob pitched his tents at that time beyond the place where the temple was afterwards built. But if we follow the order of the shepherds' way, the place is near Bethlehem, where either the flock of angels sang at Christ's birth[[Luke 2:11||]], or Jacob fed his cattle, giving the place its name: and, what is truer, something was then foreshown by a prophecy that was to come about in mystery. So, according to the Hebrews, the Flock tower signifies the place where the temple was afterwards built, which place was called the Flock tower because the temple was made like a tower, and the people gathered there, and cattle were brought there to be sacrificed. But according to Jerome, it is a place not far from Bethlehem, where, when Christ was born, the angels sang, [[Luke 2:14|Glory to God in the highest|Gloria in excelsis Deo]]; which place the Christians afterwards called *The Angel to the shepherds*. And so, according to the mind of blessed Jerome, that place was called the Flock tower by a certain prophecy of things to come.

paras.t: Quumque habitaret in illa regione, abiit Ruben, per enormem mentis suæ a Deo aversionem, et a loco in quo iniquitatem concepit, et dormivit cum Bala concubina patris sui. Bala illa, ancilla fuit Rachelis, et uxor legitima Jacob; attamen ejus concubina vocatur, quia erat uxor minus principalis, ut dictum est plenius: quod illum minime latuit, quia vel angelo revelante, vel homine recitante percepit: et hoc crimen Ruben fuit detestabilis prorsus incestus. Recitat tamen Lyra, quod secundum Hebræorum doctores Ruben non cognovit Balam carnaliter; sed mortua Rachele dum Jacob transtulisset lectum Balæ de tabernaculo Rachelis, in quo Bala jacere solebat, tanquam Rachelis ancilla, ad tabernaculum Liæ, Ruben ejecit lectum inde, quia displicuit sibi quod lectus Balæ jaceret in tabernaculo Liæ matris suæ. Sed istud fabulosum censetur, nec consonat litteræ, nec ob talem ejectionem aut culpam sanctus Moyses scripsisset ipsum Ruben dormivisse cum concubina patris sui, nec solet Scriptura peccata hominum minora ita exaggerare. Denique fabula illa, est contra id quod Jacob in extremis positus dixit ad Ruben: Effusus es sicut aqua, non crescas, quia ascendisti cubile patris tui, et maculasti stratum ejus. Hinc Rabbi Paulus refert quod alii dicunt ipsum Jacob in tantum abhorruisse tam enormem filii sui incestum, quod ipse de cetero ab actu generationis cessavit.
paras.en: [[35:22|And when he dwelt in that country, Ruben went|Quumque habitaret in illa regione, abiit Ruben]], by an enormous turning away of his mind from God, and from the place in which he conceived the iniquity, [[35:22|and slept with Bala the concubine of his father|et dormivit cum Bala concubina patris sui]]. That Bala was Rachel's handmaid and Jacob's lawful wife; yet she is called his concubine because she was a less principal wife, as has been said more fully: [[35:22|which he was not ignorant of|quod illum minime latuit]], since he learned it either by an angel's revealing or by a man's telling: and this crime of Ruben was an altogether detestable incest. Lyra relates, however, that according to the doctors of the Hebrews Ruben did not know Bala carnally; but that when, after Rachel's death, Jacob had moved Bala's bed from Rachel's tent, in which Bala used to lie as Rachel's handmaid, to Lia's tent, Ruben threw the bed out from there, because it displeased him that Bala's bed should lie in the tent of Lia his mother. But this is judged a fable, and it does not agree with the letter; nor would holy Moses have written, for such a throwing out or fault, that Ruben slept with his father's concubine; nor is Scripture wont to exaggerate men's lesser sins so. Lastly, that fable is against what Jacob, at the point of death, said to Ruben: [[Gen 49:4|Thou art poured out as water, grow thou not|Effusus es sicut aqua, non crescas]]; [[Gen 49:4|because thou wentest up to thy father's bed, and didst defile his couch|quia ascendisti cubile patris tui, et maculasti stratum ejus]]. Hence Rabbi Paul relates that others say that Jacob so abhorred his son's enormous incest that he ceased thenceforth from the act of generation.

paras.t: Deinde in littera nominantur duodecim filii Jacob, quia post Benjamin non genuit aliquam prolem; et additur: Hi sunt filii Jacob, qui nati sunt ei in Mesopotamia, quæ est pars ac regio Syriæ. Sed objici potest, quod Benjamin non est in Mesopotamia, sed in terra Chanaan natus. Ad quod Augustinus respondet, quod etiam Benjamin pro tanto dicitur in Mesopotamia natus, quoniam inde habuit causam suæ nativitatis. Ibi enim mater sua patri suo est matrimonio juncta. Additque Augustinus: Nulla autem est facilior hujus quæstionis solutio, quam ut verba Moysis, dicentis hos duodecim filios Jacob in Mesopotamia genitos, per synecdochen accipiantur, sumendo videlicet majorem partem pro toto.
paras.en: Then the letter names the twelve sons of Jacob, since after Benjamin he begot no more offspring; and there is added: [[35:26|these are the sons of Jacob, that were born to him in Mesopotamia|Hi sunt filii Jacob, qui nati sunt ei in Mesopotamia]], which is a part and region of Syria [Denis's gloss on *Syriæ* in the verse]. But it can be objected that Benjamin was not born in Mesopotamia, but in the land of Chanaan. To which Augustine answers that Benjamin too is said to have been born in Mesopotamia inasmuch as he had from there the cause of his birth: for there his mother was joined in marriage to his father. And Augustine adds: But there is no easier solution of this question than to take the words of Moses, saying that these twelve sons of Jacob were born in Mesopotamia, by synecdoche, namely taking the greater part for the whole.

paras.t: Venit etiam Jacob ad Isaac patrem suum. An hic servetur ordo historiæ, nescio. Non enim videtur, quod Jacob post reditum suum a Mesopotamia, non visitaverit patrem suum, senem, cæcum, atque carissimum, ante ea quæ modo sunt recitata, sed forte diu ante quædam eorum ac sæpius: sed nunc describitur suum patrem visitasse, quia Moyses voluit hic mortem et sepulturam Isaac enarrare. Venit ergo ad patrem suum in Mambre civitatem Arbee. Civitas Arbee seu Arbea nomine, ipsa est quæ alio nomine vocata est Hebron, atque ut scribit Hieronymus, eadem urbs antiquitus dicta est Mambre, ab amico Abrahæ nomine Mambre, de quo supra dictum est. Ideo non apparet verum, quod quidam hic scribit, Mambre nomen esse regionis in qua erat Hebron. In qua peregrinatus est Abraham et Isaac, id est, in civitate illa habitaverunt tanquam alieni et peregrini ac advenæ. Et completi sunt dies Isaac centum octoginta annorum : sicque quinque annis diutius vixit quam Abraham. Josephus tamen dicit eum vixisse centum octoginta quinque annis, ut aliqui referunt, quod tamen non inveni in Josepho, sed sicut in textu habetur.
paras.en: [[35:27|And he came to Isaac his father|Venit etiam Jacob ad Isaac patrem suum]], Jacob. Whether the order of the history is kept here I do not know.
